Q: What is the difference between HEX and RGB?
A: None in the colour itself. Both describe the same red, green and blue values from 0 to 255. HEX writes each value as two hexadecimal digits, so rgb(255, 153, 51) becomes #FF9933. HEX is compact for CSS and design tools; RGB is easier to read and adjust by hand.

Q: Why should I use HSL in CSS?
A: HSL describes colour as hue, saturation and lightness, which matches how people think. To make a button darker on hover, you lower the lightness and keep the hue the same. Building a consistent palette is much easier than guessing new HEX values, and all modern browsers support it.

Q: Is the CMYK value accurate for printing?
A: It is a straightforward mathematical conversion, useful as a starting point. Real print colours depend on the printer, paper and colour profile, so a professional printer may give different values. For brand-critical printing, such as visiting cards or packaging, ask your printer for a proof or use their recommended profile.

Q: What contrast ratio do I need for readable text?
A: WCAG 2.1 level AA asks for at least 4.5:1 between normal body text and its background, and 3:1 for large text, roughly 18.66px bold or 24px regular and above. Level AAA raises these to 7:1 and 4.5:1. The converter shows the ratio against white and black for any colour.

Q: How do I pick a colour from a logo or website?
A: In Chrome and Edge on a computer, click Pick from screen and then click anywhere on your screen to capture that colour. In browsers without the EyeDropper feature, use the BISCS India Image Color Picker on a screenshot or image file instead.

## Compound Interest Calculator: Formula, Frequency and Examples

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/compound-interest-formula-calculator/
Tool: Compound Interest (https://biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/)

Quick answer: Compound interest is calculated as A = P × (1 + r ÷ n)^(n × t), where n is how often interest is added each year. ₹1 lakh at 8% for 10 years grows to about ₹2.16 lakh with yearly compounding and ₹2.21 lakh with quarterly compounding. BISCS India's free Compound Interest calculator also handles monthly contributions.

Compound interest is interest earned on both your original money and the interest already added to it. The standard formula is **A = P × (1 + r ÷ n)^(n × t)**, where P is the principal, r the annual rate as a decimal, n the number of times interest is added each year and t the number of years.

₹1,00,000 at 8% for 10 years becomes about ₹2,15,892 if interest is added once a year, and about ₹2,20,804 if it is added every quarter. The free [Compound Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/) calculator on BISCS India works this out for any frequency and can include a fixed monthly top-up.

## Why does compounding grow money faster?

With simple interest, ₹1 lakh at 8% earns ₹8,000 every year, no more. With yearly compounding, year one earns ₹8,000, year two earns 8% of ₹1,08,000, which is ₹8,640, and year three earns 8% of ₹1,16,640. Each year's interest is a little larger than the last.

Over short periods the difference is small. Over decades it becomes the main source of growth. That is why the same 8% looks modest over three years and powerful over thirty.

## How compounding frequency changes the result

Here is ₹1,00,000 at 8% for 10 years, calculated with the tool:

| Compounding | Future value | Interest earned | Effective annual rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yearly | ₹2,15,892 | ₹1,15,892 | 8.00% |
| Half-yearly | ₹2,19,112 | ₹1,19,112 | 8.16% |
| Quarterly | ₹2,20,804 | ₹1,20,804 | 8.24% |
| Monthly | ₹2,21,964 | ₹1,21,964 | 8.30% |
| Daily | ₹2,22,535 | ₹1,22,535 | 8.33% |

More frequent compounding always helps, but with diminishing returns. Quarterly is the common convention for bank fixed deposits in India, which is why it is the default in the calculator.

## How to use the BISCS Compound Interest calculator

1. Open the [Compound Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/) calculator.
2. Enter the **principal amount** you are starting with.
3. Set the **interest rate** per year.
4. Choose the **time period** in years.
5. Select the **compounding frequency**: yearly, half-yearly, quarterly, monthly or daily.
6. Optionally add a **monthly contribution**, which is added at the end of each month.
7. Read the future value, total invested, interest earned and effective annual rate, then explore the growth chart and year-by-year table.

The tool converts your chosen frequency into an equivalent monthly rate so that monthly contributions and compounding line up neatly. All calculations happen in your browser.

## Example: adding ₹2,000 a month

Kavya starts with ₹1 lakh at 8%, compounded quarterly, and adds ₹2,000 at the end of every month for 10 years.

- Total invested: ₹1,00,000 + (₹2,000 × 120) = ₹3,40,000
- Estimated value after 10 years: about ₹5,85,621
- Interest earned: about ₹2,45,621

Without the monthly top-ups, her ₹1 lakh would have grown to about ₹2.21 lakh. Regular additions more than double the final amount, and they earn compound interest too. For market-linked monthly investing, the [SIP Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sip-calculator/) uses a similar idea with start-of-month instalments.

## Time matters more than frequency

Compare the frequency table above with what happens when you simply leave the money longer. ₹1,00,000 at 8% compounded yearly grows to:

| Years | Value | Growth multiple |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | ₹2,15,892 | 2.16× |
| 20 | ₹4,66,096 | 4.66× |
| 30 | ₹10,06,266 | 10.06× |

Switching from yearly to daily compounding over 10 years added under ₹7,000. Staying invested for 30 years instead of 10 adds nearly ₹8 lakh. The last ten years alone add more than the first twenty combined, because each year's growth is calculated on a much bigger base. If you are deciding between chasing a slightly better compounding frequency and starting a year earlier, start earlier.

## When compounding works against you

The same maths applies to debt. As a purely hypothetical illustration, if an unpaid balance of ₹50,000 grew at 3% a month with nothing repaid, after 12 months it would be about ₹71,288, which is over 42% more in a single year. Real card and loan charges depend on your agreement, fees and repayments, but the lesson is clear: high-interest debt that compounds monthly should usually be cleared before you invest for modest returns.

## How to compare two offers with different compounding

Suppose one deposit pays 7.9% compounded yearly and another 7.75% compounded quarterly. Put each into the calculator and read the effective annual rate: the quarterly one works out to about 7.98%, so it edges ahead despite the lower headline rate. Comparing effective rates, or the final amounts over the same period, is the fair way to choose.

## Where you meet compound interest in real life

- **Fixed deposits:** banks commonly compound quarterly. The [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/) adds tenure in years, months and days.
- **Recurring deposits and PPF:** both grow by compounding, with their own rules.
- **Loans and credit cards:** compounding works against you. Unpaid credit card balances can grow very quickly because interest is charged on interest.
- **Inflation:** prices compound too, which is why ₹1 lakh today buys less each year.

## Common mistakes with compound interest

1. **Mixing up nominal and effective rates.** A product quoting 8% compounded monthly actually yields about 8.30% a year.
2. **Using compound formulas where simple interest applies.** Some loans and short deposits use simple interest. Check with the [Simple Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/simple-interest-calculator/) calculator when that is the case.
3. **Forgetting tax.** Interest on deposits is taxable each year, which reduces the amount that actually compounds.
4. **Overestimating with high rates.** Small changes in rate make big differences over long periods, so test a lower rate too.
5. **Treating contributions as start-of-month.** This tool adds them at month end; a start-of-month assumption gives a slightly higher number.

## Limits of the calculation

The calculator assumes a constant rate, regular contributions and no withdrawals or taxes. Real products may change rates, apply TDS or round interest at each step. Use the result as a clear illustration of how compounding works and a reasonable estimate for planning.

This article is general information, not financial advice. For the terms that actually apply to a deposit or loan, rely on your bank's documents and RBI guidance, and consult a qualified adviser for significant decisions.

Q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
A: Simple interest is charged or earned only on the original principal. Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus interest already added. On ₹1 lakh at 8% for 5 years, simple interest gives ₹40,000, while yearly compounding gives about ₹46,933, and the gap widens every year.

Q: Does more frequent compounding make a big difference?
A: It helps, but less than people expect. At 8% for 10 years on ₹1 lakh, moving from yearly to quarterly compounding adds about ₹4,900, and from quarterly to daily adds under ₹1,800 more. The rate and the length of time matter far more than the compounding frequency.

Q: What is the effective annual rate?
A: It is the yearly rate that would give the same result with compounding just once a year. At a nominal 8%, quarterly compounding gives an effective rate of about 8.24%, monthly about 8.30% and daily about 8.33%. It lets you compare products that compound at different frequencies.

Q: How long will it take to double my money with compound interest?
A: Divide 72 by the annual rate for a quick estimate. At 8%, money roughly doubles in nine years; at 6%, in about twelve. For an exact answer, enter your figures in the calculator and look at the year-by-year table to see when the value first passes twice the principal.

## How to Reduce PDF File Size for Email and Upload Portals

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/reduce-pdf-file-size-free/
Tool: Compress PDF (https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/)

Quick answer: To reduce a PDF’s file size, open a PDF compressor, choose a compression level and download the smaller file. Lossless compression keeps text perfect but saves less; image-based compression shrinks scanned PDFs much more. BISCS India’s Compress PDF offers both and works in your browser, so files are never uploaded.

To reduce a PDF's file size, open [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/), choose a level (Basic, Strong or Extreme) and download the smaller file. Basic is lossless and keeps text perfect; Strong and Extreme turn pages into compressed images, which shrinks scanned PDFs dramatically.

Everything happens in your browser, so even a bank statement or an Aadhaar scan is compressed without being uploaded anywhere.

## Why PDFs are often too big

PDF size mostly comes from images. A typed 20-page document might be 200 KB, while a 3-page scan from a phone or copier can easily be several MB, because each page is a high-resolution photo.

That becomes a problem when:

- An email bounces because the attachment is over the provider's limit.
- A government, university or recruitment portal rejects your upload for being "too large".
- A WhatsApp group admin asks you to stop sending 20 MB files.
- Your cloud storage or phone fills up with old scans.

## The three compression levels explained

| Level | What it does | Text stays selectable? | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic (lossless) | Re-packs the file structure; content untouched | Yes | Digital PDFs, already-optimised files, when quality must not change |
| Strong | Each page becomes a 150 DPI image at 70% JPEG quality | No | Scans, phone photos, image-heavy PDFs |
| Extreme | Each page becomes a 100 DPI image at 50% JPEG quality | No | When you must hit a very small size and quality is secondary |

Basic also offers an option to **remove document metadata** (title, author, software names), which shaves a little more and removes details you may not want to share.

With Strong and Extreme, the tool warns you clearly that text will no longer be selectable or searchable and that links and form fields are removed. That trade-off is fine for a scanned mark sheet, but not for a contract someone needs to search.

## How to compress a PDF step by step

1. Open [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) and choose your PDF.
2. Pick a level. Start with **Basic** for digital documents, or **Strong** for scans.
3. For Basic, decide whether to also strip metadata.
4. Click compress. A progress bar shows each page being processed.
5. Compare the **Original**, **Compressed** and **Saved** figures on the result screen.
6. Open the file and zoom in on small text to make sure it is still legible.
7. If it is still too large, try the next level, or remove unneeded pages first.

## Meeting government portal limits

Indian portals for exams, scholarships, recruitment, passports, tax and company filings commonly cap file sizes, and the caps differ widely. Some allow only a few hundred KB per document, others a few MB, and many also specify the format (PDF only, or JPG for photos and signatures). There is no national standard, and limits can change, so always check the instructions on the exact portal and upload field you are using.

A practical approach:

1. Note the exact limit and format from the portal.
2. Remove pages you do not need with [Remove PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/).
3. Compress with Strong if the document is a scan.
4. Aim for a size comfortably below the limit, not just under it.
5. Open the result and check that stamps, signatures and small print are readable.

If a portal wants an image rather than a PDF, convert a page with [PDF to Images](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-jpg/) and then use the image tools.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Using Extreme by default.** It can make fine print blurry. A rejected document because a seal is unreadable is worse than a slightly larger file.
- **Compressing a document that must stay searchable.** Use Basic for contracts, reports and anything others will copy text from.
- **Compressing the same file repeatedly.** Each image-based pass lowers quality again. Always compress from the original.
- **Ignoring a larger result.** If the tool says the output is bigger, keep your original.
- **Compressing fillable forms with Strong.** Form fields are removed. Fill the form first with Fill PDF Form, or compress with Basic only.

## Tips for the smallest file with readable text

- Scan at a sensible resolution in the first place. For forms and letters, very high scanner settings mostly add size.
- Black-and-white documents compress well. If colour is not required, [Grayscale PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/grayscale-pdf/) can help, and it also redraws pages as images, so compare results.
- Split very large documents if the portal allows multiple uploads.
- Remove blank pages from double-sided scans before compressing.

## Example: fitting a scanned certificate under a portal limit

Sneha in Jaipur is applying for a state government job. The portal asks for her graduation certificate as a PDF, with a maximum size stated on the upload page. Her phone scan of the two-page certificate is 3.8 MB, well over the limit.

She tries Basic first. It saves only a little, because almost all of the file is two large photos. She then tries Strong, which redraws each page at 150 DPI, and the file drops to a fraction of the original size. She opens the result, zooms in on the university seal and the registration number, and both are clear. She uploads it with room to spare.

Had Strong still been too large, she could have tried Extreme and checked readability again, or re-scanned the certificate with better lighting and a plain background, which compresses far better than a shadowy photo.

## Basic or Strong: a quick way to decide

Open your PDF in any reader and try to select a word of text. If you can select it, the PDF is digital, and Basic is the safe first choice. If the whole page selects as a single picture, or nothing selects at all, it is a scan, and Strong will usually save much more. Many real-world files are a mix, such as a typed form with a scanned photo attached, so do not hesitate to try both and compare the numbers on the result screen.

## What happens on your device

The compressor uses a PDF library and your browser's own image engine. Basic re-saves the file structure; Strong and Extreme render each page and save it as a JPEG inside a new PDF. All of this happens in the browser tab, which is why big scanned files take longer on a phone than on a laptop, and why nothing is ever uploaded.

Q: How do I compress a PDF to under 200 KB or 500 KB?
A: Try the Basic level first. If the file is still too big and it is a scan or photo-heavy, use Strong, which usually brings scanned pages down a lot. If you still need less, Extreme gives the smallest size at visibly lower quality. Removing unneeded pages also helps a great deal.

Q: Why did my PDF get bigger after compression?
A: This can happen when a PDF is already well optimised, or when a text-only document is converted to images by the Strong or Extreme levels. The tool shows the before and after sizes and recommends keeping your original whenever the result is larger.

Q: Will the text still be searchable after compression?
A: With Basic (lossless), yes, everything stays exactly as it was. Strong and Extreme redraw each page as an image, so text can no longer be selected or searched, and links and form fields are removed. Use those levels for scans or when size matters more.

Q: What is the file size limit on government portals?
A: There is no single limit. Each portal, and sometimes each upload field, sets its own maximum size and accepted format. Always read the instructions on the specific portal page, compress to comfortably below the stated limit, and preview the result before submitting.

Q: Is it safe to compress confidential PDFs online?
A: With this tool, the PDF is processed inside your browser and never uploaded, so it is suitable for bank statements, ITRs and ID documents. Upload-based compressors send your file to a remote server, which is worth avoiding for anything personal.

## How to Crop PDF Pages and Trim Margins Online for Free

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/crop-pdf-margins-online-free/
Tool: Crop PDF (https://biscsindia.com/tools/crop-pdf/)

Quick answer: To crop a PDF, open a PDF cropper, drag the box on the page preview or type the margins to trim in millimetres, choose whether to apply it to all pages or only the current one, and download. BISCS India’s Crop PDF does this in your browser without uploading. Cropping hides content outside the box rather than deleting it.

To crop a PDF, open [Crop PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/crop-pdf/), drag the handles of the crop box on the page preview (or type the margins to trim in millimetres), choose **All pages** or **This page only**, and download. The pages are trimmed to the area you kept.

Everything happens in your browser, so the document stays on your device. One thing to know up front: cropping **hides** what is outside the box; it does not securely delete it.

## Why crop a PDF?

Cropping is about making pages look right. Typical reasons:

- **Scanner and phone borders.** Dark edges, a bit of the desk, or the shadow of the scanner lid around every page.
- **Wide white margins.** Some PDFs, especially exported slides and old e-books, have huge margins that make text tiny on a phone.
- **Focusing on one part.** You need just the table from a report page, or one receipt from a page of several.
- **Fitting a page for printing or slides.** A tighter page enlarges the content when printed "fit to page".
- **Removing printer marks** around the edges of design proofs.

## How to crop a PDF step by step

1. Open [Crop PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/crop-pdf/) and choose your PDF.
2. The first page appears with a crop box. Drag the corner and edge handles, or drag the whole box. Drag on the dark area to draw a new box from scratch.
3. Or type exact values in **Top**, **Bottom**, **Left** and **Right** (in millimetres).
4. Use the page arrows to check other pages with the same box.
5. Choose **Apply to**: All pages, or This page only.
6. Decide whether to keep **Also shrink the page size (MediaBox)** switched on (it is on by default).
7. Crop and download. The result shows the new page size in millimetres.

## CropBox vs MediaBox, in plain words

Every PDF page has a few "boxes". Two matter here:

| Box | What it means | When the tool changes it |
|---|---|---|
| CropBox | The visible area a reader shows | Always |
| MediaBox | The physical page size | Only when "Also shrink the page size" is on |

Changing both gives the most predictable result: the page is smaller in every viewer and prints at the new size. Changing only the CropBox can be useful when you want to keep the original page size information for some later step, but a few readers and printers treat CropBox differently, so the default is to change both.

In both cases, the content outside the box usually remains in the file. It is simply out of view.

## Cropping is not redaction

This deserves its own section, because it is a common and risky misunderstanding. If a bank statement page shows your account number in a corner and you crop it off, someone with PDF software may still be able to reveal or extract it. The same applies to covering text with a white box.

If you need to withhold information:

- Drop whole pages with [Remove PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/), which genuinely excludes them from the new file.
- Or convert the cropped page to an image with [PDF to Images](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-jpg/), since an image contains only what is visible, and then turn it back into a PDF if needed.
- For formal or legal redaction, use dedicated redaction software or ask for a fresh document from the source.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Cropping into the text.** Check every page in the preview, especially pages where text runs closer to the edge than on page 1.
- **Applying one crop to mixed page sizes.** A crop that fits A4 pages may be too large for a smaller receipt page in the same file. The tool stops with a clear error if the margins exceed a page; crop those pages separately.
- **Expecting a smaller file.** Cropping changes appearance, not storage. Compress afterwards if size matters.
- **Cropping before rotating.** Fix orientation first with [Rotate PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-pdf/) so that "top" means what you think it means. The tool does account for rotation, but working on upright pages is less confusing.

## Example: cleaning up phone scans for a portal

Lakshmi photographed her four-page Class 12 mark sheet bundle on a wooden table and turned the photos into a PDF. Each page now has a brown border of tabletop around it. She opens the PDF in the cropper, drags the box in to the paper's edges on page 1, flips through the other pages to confirm the box fits them too, and crops all pages at once. The result looks like a proper scan.

For future documents, she could use Scan to PDF instead, which detects the paper edges and straightens the page automatically while capturing.

## Tips for precise crops

- Use the typed millimetre values when you need the same crop on several documents, such as a monthly report with fixed margins.
- A small margin of 3–5 mm around the content looks more professional than cropping tight to the text.
- For slides exported as PDF, trimming large side margins makes the content much more readable on phones.
- After cropping, a document printed with "fit to page" will appear larger on paper, which can help small print.

## Checklist before you download

- The crop box fits every page, not just the first one.
- No text, signature, stamp or page number is cut off at the edges.
- "Also shrink the page size" is on, unless you have a specific reason to keep the original page size.
- Nothing sensitive is merely hidden outside the crop area.
- Your original file is safely kept in case you need a different crop later.

## Private processing

The crop is applied by a PDF library running in your browser. Your document is never uploaded, which matters because the pages people crop are often scans of personal papers. The cropped copy is saved to your device, and your original file is untouched.

Q: Does cropping a PDF delete the content outside the crop area?
A: No. Cropping changes the visible page area, so the trimmed parts are hidden, but the underlying content usually remains inside the file. Do not rely on cropping to remove sensitive information. Use Remove PDF Pages for whole pages, or recreate the document without the sensitive part.

Q: What does Also shrink the page size do?
A: With it on, both the visible area (CropBox) and the page size (MediaBox) are reduced, so the page really becomes smaller when printed or viewed in any reader. With it off, only the visible area changes. Leaving it on gives the most consistent result across PDF readers.

Q: Can I crop different pages differently?
A: Yes. Choose This page only, crop the current page, download, then open the result and crop the next page that needs a different box. For most documents, one crop applied to all pages is enough because scanner borders tend to be similar.

Q: Will cropping make the PDF file smaller?
A: Usually not by much, because the hidden content is still stored in the file. Cropping is about how the page looks, not its size in KB. To reduce the file size, use Compress PDF after cropping.

Q: Why do I get an error that the margins are too large?
A: The margins you entered add up to more than the page’s width or height on at least one page, which often happens when a document mixes page sizes. Reduce the margins, or crop only the current page.

## CSS Gradient Generator: Linear, Radial and Conic Made Easy

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/css-gradient-generator-linear-radial/
Tool: CSS Gradient Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/css-gradient-generator/)

Quick answer: A CSS gradient is a smooth blend between colours created entirely in code with linear-gradient, radial-gradient or conic-gradient, so no image file is needed. BISCS India's CSS Gradient Generator lets you choose the type, angle and up to five colour stops visually, then copy ready-to-use CSS with a fallback colour.

A CSS gradient is a background that blends smoothly from one colour to another, drawn by the browser from a single line of code. No image file, no extra download, and it stays crisp on every screen from a budget Android phone to a 4K monitor.

The [CSS Gradient Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/css-gradient-generator/) on BISCS India lets you build one visually. Choose linear, radial or conic, drag the angle and colour stops, and copy the finished `background` CSS. A live preview shows exactly what you will get.

## The three kinds of CSS gradient

**Linear gradients** blend along a straight line at an angle you choose. They are the most common, used for hero sections, buttons and cards.

```css
background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4f46e5 0%, #ec4899 100%);
```

**Radial gradients** spread outward from a point, as a circle or ellipse. They are good for spotlights, soft glows and vignettes.

```css
background: radial-gradient(circle at center, #fde68a 0%, #fb7185 70%, #9d174d 100%);
```

**Conic gradients** sweep around a centre point like the hands of a clock. They are useful for colour wheels, pie-chart style indicators and eye-catching abstract backgrounds.

```css
background: conic-gradient(from 0deg at center, #22d3ee 0%, #a78bfa 33%, #f472b6 66%, #22d3ee 100%);
```

All three also have **repeating** versions, such as `repeating-linear-gradient`, which tile the pattern to create stripes.

## How to make a gradient with BISCS India

1. Open the [CSS Gradient Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/css-gradient-generator/).
2. Start from a preset if you like. There are eight, including Indigo dusk, Ocean, Sunset, Mint and a tricolour-inspired Saffron. Or start from scratch.
3. Choose the **Type**: **Linear**, **Radial** or **Conic**.
4. For linear and conic, set the **Angle** with the slider. For radial, choose the **Shape** (circle or ellipse). For radial and conic, choose the **Position**, such as center, top left or bottom right.
5. Edit the **Colour stops**. Each stop has a colour picker, a HEX field and a position slider from 0% to 100%. Use **Add stop** for up to five colours, or the bin icon to remove one (a gradient always keeps at least two).
6. Tick **Repeating gradient** for striped or ring patterns.
7. Click **Random** for inspiration, then **Copy CSS** when you are happy.

The copied code includes two lines:

```css
background: #4f46e5;
background: linear-gradient(135deg, #4f46e5 0%, #ec4899 100%);
```

The first line is a solid-colour fallback. Browsers that understand the gradient use the second line; anything older keeps the first.

## Understanding angles

Angles trip people up because CSS measures them differently from school geometry. In `linear-gradient`, the angle is the direction the colours **travel towards**:

| Angle | Direction | Keyword equivalent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0deg` | Bottom to top | `to top` |
| `90deg` | Left to right | `to right` |
| `135deg` | Top-left to bottom-right | (diagonal) |
| `180deg` | Top to bottom (the default) | `to bottom` |
| `270deg` | Right to left | `to left` |

For conic gradients, the angle sets where the sweep starts, measured clockwise from the top.

## Colour stops and hard edges

A colour stop is a colour plus a position. The browser blends smoothly between consecutive stops. If two stops share the same position, there is no blend at all, just a sharp line:

```css
background: linear-gradient(90deg, #ff9933 0% 33%, #ffffff 33% 66%, #138808 66% 100%);
```

That example draws three solid bands, an easy way to make flag-style stripes without images. In the generator, you get a similar effect by dragging two stops close together.

## Two popular tricks: overlays and gradient text

**Image overlays.** Text placed directly on a photo is often hard to read. Layering a semi-transparent gradient over the image fixes this without editing the photo. CSS lets you stack a gradient and an image in one `background` declaration, with the gradient listed first so it sits on top:

```css
background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(0,0,0,0) 40%, rgba(0,0,0,0.7) 100%), url(hero.jpg) center / cover;
```

The bottom of the photo darkens gently, so a white headline there stays readable.

**Gradient text.** Headlines filled with a gradient are eye-catching. Apply the gradient as the background of the text element, then clip it to the letters with `background-clip: text` and make the text colour transparent. Use it sparingly, on large headings only, and keep a plain fallback colour so the text never disappears in a browser that does not support clipping.

## Design tips for gradients that look good

- **Stay close on the colour wheel.** Blues to purples, or oranges to pinks, usually look smoother than opposites like red to green, which pass through a muddy middle.
- **Add a middle stop to avoid greyness.** If the centre of your gradient looks dull, add a third stop with a brighter, more saturated colour.
- **Use subtle gradients for large areas.** A gentle shift between two close shades feels modern and does not fight with text.
- **Check text contrast at both ends.** White text may pass on the dark end and fail on the light end. Test stop colours in the [Color Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/color-converter/).
- **Match your brand.** Start from your brand colour and a lighter or darker version of it, rather than random hues.

## Common mistakes

- **Using `background-color` for a gradient.** Gradients are images in CSS terms, so they belong in `background` or `background-image`, not `background-color`.
- **Forgetting the element has no height.** An empty `div` with a gradient background is zero pixels tall. Give it content, padding or a height.
- **Gradient on `body` that stops halfway.** On short pages, add `min-height: 100vh` to the element, or the gradient may repeat or end early.
- **Too many colours.** Five stops is plenty for almost any design. More usually looks busy.
- **Exporting a gradient as a PNG.** Code is smaller, sharper and easier to change than an image.

## Where gradients work well

Gradients suit landing page hero sections, call-to-action buttons, card headers, app splash screens and social media graphics. For more depth, pair a gradient card with a soft shadow from the [Box Shadow Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/box-shadow-generator/). And if the gradient is headed for social media rather than a web page, the [Instagram Grid & Story Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/social-post-maker/) helps you design posts and stories at the right sizes.

## Privacy

The preview is drawn by your own browser and nothing is sent to a server. You can design and copy as many gradients as you like with no account and no watermark.

Q: Do CSS gradients work in all browsers?
A: Linear and radial gradients without vendor prefixes work in all current browsers. Conic gradients are supported in all modern browsers too, but not in very old ones. The generated code starts with a plain background colour, so if a browser cannot draw the gradient, it still shows a sensible solid colour.

Q: Are gradients better than background images?
A: For simple colour blends, yes. A gradient is a few dozen bytes of CSS, scales perfectly to any screen size and resolution, needs no extra download and is easy to change. Use an image only when you need texture, photographs or effects CSS cannot produce.

Q: Why does my gradient look banded or stripy?
A: Banding appears when two similar colours are stretched across a very large area, because screens can show only a limited number of steps between them. Use colours that differ more, add a middle stop, or overlay a very subtle noise texture. Some displays and compressed screenshots make banding more visible.

Q: What does 90deg mean in linear-gradient?
A: The angle sets the direction the gradient travels. 0deg goes from bottom to top, 90deg from left to right, 180deg from top to bottom and 270deg from right to left. The keyword form to right is equivalent to 90deg for a linear gradient.

Q: Can I put text on top of a gradient?
A: Yes, but check contrast at both ends of the gradient, not just in the middle. Text that is readable on the dark end may disappear on the light end. Use the BISCS India Color Converter to test each stop colour against your text colour for a WCAG contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

## How to Convert CSV to JSON Online (Quotes, Types, Headers)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/convert-csv-to-json-online/
Tool: CSV to JSON (https://biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/)

Quick answer: To convert CSV to JSON, paste the CSV into a converter that reads the first row as headers and turns each following row into a JSON object. BISCS India's CSV to JSON tool auto-detects the delimiter, handles quoted commas and line breaks, optionally converts numbers and booleans, and runs fully in your browser.

Converting CSV to JSON means reading a table and writing each row out as an object whose keys come from the header row. A two-line CSV like `name,city` / `Asha,Delhi` becomes `[{"name": "Asha", "city": "Delhi"}]`.

That sounds simple, until you meet a value with a comma in it, a note that spans two lines, or a semicolon-separated file from a European tool. The [CSV to JSON](https://biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/) converter on BISCS India follows the CSV standard (RFC 4180) closely, so those cases come out right, and it all happens in your browser.

## Why convert CSV to JSON?

Spreadsheets are where data is born in most offices. JSON is what applications want. You might need to:

- Seed a database or a test fixture from a list someone maintained in Excel.
- Feed a product catalogue or price list into a website or app.
- Send records to an API that accepts JSON only.
- Load a lookup table, such as state codes or HSN categories, into JavaScript.

Writing that JSON by hand is slow and error-prone. A converter does it in a second.

## A worked example

Here is a small CSV with a few awkward values:

```text
id,name,city,amount,paid,notes
1,Asha Verma,Delhi,2500.50,true,
2,"Das, Rohan",Kolkata,1200,false,"Said ""call later"""
```

With the default settings, the output is:

```json
[
  { "id": 1, "name": "Asha Verma", "city": "Delhi", "amount": 2500.5, "paid": true, "notes": "" },
  { "id": 2, "name": "Das, Rohan", "city": "Kolkata", "amount": 1200, "paid": false, "notes": "Said \"call later\"" }
]
```

The quoted `"Das, Rohan"` stays a single value. The doubled quotes `""` turn into a literal quote, which JSON then escapes as `\"`. And because type detection is on, `2500.50` is a number and `true` is a boolean rather than strings.

## How to convert CSV to JSON with BISCS India

1. Open [CSV to JSON](https://biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/).
2. Paste your CSV, drag a `.csv`, `.tsv` or `.txt` file onto the box, or click **Upload**.
3. Leave **Delimiter** on **Auto-detect** unless the result looks wrong. It checks comma, semicolon, tab and pipe and picks the one that gives the most consistent column count.
4. Choose the **Output**: **Array of objects** (most common) or **Array of arrays** (smaller, positional).
5. Set the options: **First row is header**, **Detect numbers, booleans & null**, **Empty cells as null**, **Skip empty lines** and **Minify**.
6. Check the table in **Preview** and the status line, which reports rows, columns, the delimiter used and any rows with missing cells.
7. Click **Copy** or **Download .json**.

### Tab-separated files

TSV files, where values are separated by tabs, are common when data is copied straight out of a spreadsheet or exported from analytics tools. Paste them in exactly like CSV; auto-detect recognises the tab delimiter. You can even select a range of cells in Excel or Google Sheets, copy, and paste directly into the input box, because spreadsheets put tabs between cells on the clipboard.

## Array of objects or array of arrays?

| Output | Looks like | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Array of objects | `[{"name":"Asha","city":"Delhi"}]` | Sending to APIs, databases, most code |
| Array of arrays | `[["name","city"],["Asha","Delhi"]]` | Charts, compact storage, column order matters |

Objects are self-describing and easier to work with in code. Arrays repeat no key names, so they are smaller for large tables.

## When should you turn off type detection?

Type detection is convenient, but some values only look like numbers. Switch it off, or check the output carefully, for:

- **Account numbers, Aadhaar-style IDs and long reference numbers.** The tool only converts numbers up to 15 significant digits, so longer IDs stay as strings. Shorter IDs still become numbers, which may not be what your system expects.
- **Codes with leading zeros.** `0042` is kept as a string, because `0042` is not a valid JSON number. Good, but be aware the column then has mixed types if other rows are plain numbers.
- **Version numbers and phone numbers.** `10.20` becomes the number `10.2`, losing the trailing zero.

If in doubt, keep everything as strings and convert the specific fields you need in your own code.

## Common mistakes and how to spot them

- **Unquoted commas.** `Mumbai, Maharashtra` without quotes splits into two cells. The status bar warns about rows with a different number of columns.
- **An unclosed quote.** One stray `"` can swallow the rest of the file into a single value. The converter flags "Unclosed quote at the end of the file" when this happens.
- **Duplicate or blank headers.** Two columns both called `phone` would overwrite each other in an object. The tool renames the second one `phone_2`, and blank headers become `column_1`, `column_2` and so on.
- **The wrong delimiter.** If everything lands in a single column, the file probably uses semicolons or tabs. Auto-detect usually catches this; otherwise choose manually.
- **Excel’s hidden encoding.** Save as "CSV UTF-8" in Excel so that Indian-language text and the ₹ sign survive. A byte order mark at the start of the file is removed automatically.

## Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The CSV is parsed by JavaScript running on the page, and the JSON is built in memory on your device. Text files up to 50 MB can be loaded, though very large files will take longer on a phone. Because nothing leaves your computer, you can safely convert staff lists, customer exports or price sheets.

## Related tools

To check or prettify the resulting JSON, open it in the [JSON Formatter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/), which also offers a collapsible tree view. Going the other direction, [JSON to CSV](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) turns API data back into a spreadsheet-ready file. If your source is an `.xlsx` workbook rather than a CSV, start with the [Excel & CSV Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/excel-csv-converter/).

## A quick checklist before you use the JSON

- Row count in the status line matches what you expect.
- No warning about rows with missing cells or unclosed quotes.
- IDs and codes are strings if your system treats them as text.
- Empty cells are `""` or `null`, whichever your application expects.
- Key names are clean: no stray spaces, no duplicates.

Five seconds spent on this list saves a lot of head-scratching when the import fails later.

Q: How do I convert an Excel sheet to JSON?
A: Save or export the sheet as CSV first (File, Save As, CSV UTF-8 in Excel, or File, Download, CSV in Google Sheets). Then paste or upload the CSV into the converter. If you have an .xlsx file and no Excel, the BISCS India Excel and CSV Converter can produce the CSV for you.

Q: Why did my PIN code or phone number lose its leading zero?
A: With type detection on, a value like 0042 is kept as a string because numbers with leading zeros are not valid JSON numbers. However, the source CSV may already have lost the zero if Excel saved it as a number. Format such columns as Text in Excel before exporting.

Q: What does “Detect numbers, booleans & null” do?
A: CSV has no data types; every value is text. With this option on, values like 2500.50 become JSON numbers, true and false become booleans, and the word null becomes null. Turn it off when you need every value kept exactly as a string, for example IDs or codes.

Q: Can the converter handle commas inside a value?
A: Yes, as long as the value is wrapped in double quotes in the CSV, which is the standard. For example, "Das, Rohan" stays one value. Double quotes inside a quoted value are written as two quotes, and line breaks inside quotes are also preserved.

Q: What if some rows have fewer columns than the header?
A: The missing cells are filled with empty strings, or null if you tick Empty cells as null. The status line warns you how many rows were short, which often signals an unquoted comma or a broken line in the source file.

## How to Add or Subtract Days From a Date (With Business Days)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/add-days-to-date-calculator-guide/
Tool: Add or Subtract Days (https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/)

Quick answer: To add days to a date, count forward that many calendar days; for months or years, move the month or year and keep the same day where possible. BISCS India’s free Add or Subtract Days calculator does this instantly, handles month-end dates, and can count business days that skip Saturdays and Sundays.

To add days to a date, count forward that many calendar days. 90 days after 2 November 2026 is 31 January 2027. To add months or years, move the month or year forward and keep the same day of the month where it exists.

Doing this on a calendar is slow and easy to get wrong across month ends. The free [Add or Subtract Days](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/) calculator gives you the exact date and weekday instantly, and can count business days that skip weekends.

## Why add or subtract days?

Most deadlines in work and personal life are written as "within N days" or "N months from". Common examples in India include:

- Replying to a legal or tax notice within a stated number of days.
- A 30, 60 or 90-day notice period at work.
- Product warranties of one or two years from the purchase date.
- Payment terms such as "Net 30" on invoices.
- Cheque validity, which is three months from the date on the cheque under current RBI rules.
- Planning backwards: sending wedding invitations 45 days before the event.

## How to use the calculator

1. Open [Add or Subtract Days](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/).
2. Choose a **start date**. It defaults to today.
3. Choose **Add** or **Subtract**.
4. Fill in any combination of **years, months, weeks and days**. Leave the others at zero.
5. Tick **Count days as business days** if weekends should be skipped.
6. Read the result date and weekday. The stats show the ISO date, the number of calendar days, weeks and working days in between.

If the result falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the tool shows a warning, which is handy when a deadline lands on a weekend. All calculations run in your browser.

## Worked examples

### 90 days from a date

Start: Monday, 2 November 2026. Add 90 days. Result: **Sunday, 31 January 2027**. Because it is a Sunday, you might plan to finish the task by Friday, 29 January.

### 30 days for payment terms

An invoice dated 2 November 2026 with "Net 30" terms is due on **Wednesday, 2 December 2026**.

### Counting back from an event

A wedding is on Sunday, 20 December 2026, and you want invitations out 45 days before. Choose Subtract and 45 days. The answer is **Thursday, 5 November 2026**.

### Ten business days

A vendor promises delivery in 10 business days from Friday, 6 November 2026. With business days ticked, the result is **Friday, 20 November 2026**, because the two weekends in between are skipped. Subtract any holidays yourself.

### Adding a month at month-end

31 January 2027 plus one month gives **28 February 2027**, since February 2027 has 28 days. In a leap year such as 2028, the result would be 29 February.

## How months, weeks and days are combined

When you fill in more than one box, the tool applies them in a fixed order:

1. **Years and months first.** It moves the month forward and keeps the day number. If that day does not exist in the new month, it uses the last day of the month.
2. **Then weeks**, as blocks of 7 days.
3. **Then days**, either as calendar days or as business days if you ticked that option.

This order matters. "1 month and 1 day" from 31 January becomes 28 February, then 1 March. Doing the day first would give a different answer.

## Days, months or business days: which to use?

| Wording you see | What to enter | Note |
|---|---|---|
| "within 30 days" | 30 in Days | Calendar days, weekends included |
| "within one month" | 1 in Months | Same date next month, or month-end |
| "within 10 working days" | 10 in Days, business days ticked | Remove holidays separately |
| "valid for 1 year" | 1 in Years | 29 February start dates move to 28 February |
| "6 weeks from" | 6 in Weeks | Exactly 42 days |

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Treating 30 days as a month.** They differ in most months.
- **Counting the start date as day one.** Usually, "within 7 days of 1 March" means up to 8 March. Check the wording of your document.
- **Forgetting weekends** for working-day promises.
- **Ignoring holidays,** especially around Diwali, Durga Puja, Eid, Christmas and regional festivals, when offices and banks may be closed.
- **Assuming the deadline moves** if it falls on a weekend. Some rules extend to the next working day, others do not. Read the rule that applies to you.

## What about leap years and long durations?

Leap years add a 29 February every four years, with the century rule that 1900 and 2100 are not leap years but 2000 was. The calculator follows the real calendar, so adding 365 days does not always land on the same date next year. From 1 March 2027, 365 days later is 29 February 2028, while adding 1 year gives 1 March 2028.

For long plans, such as a five-year bond maturity or a ten-year document renewal, use the Years box rather than converting to days. It keeps the same calendar date, which is what most agreements mean. If you started on 29 February, a year later the tool uses 28 February.

## Practical tips

- For legal, tax or banking deadlines, use the calculator to plan, then confirm the exact rule with the official source or your advisor.
- Add the result date to your phone calendar straight away, with a reminder a few days earlier.
- When you share a deadline, write the weekday and the date together, such as "Thursday, 5 November", to avoid confusion.
- Note whether the count used calendar or business days.

If you already have two dates and want the gap between them, use the [Date Difference calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-difference-calculator/). To check an exact age on a cut-off date, try the [Age Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/). And when you have tasks timed to the minute, the [Stopwatch & Timer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/stopwatch-timer/) handles countdowns.

Deadlines are easier to meet when you know exactly when they are. Bookmark [Add or Subtract Days](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/) for the next time someone says "within 45 days".

Q: What date is 90 days from today?
A: Enter today’s date as the start, type 90 in the Days box and leave the operation on Add. The calculator shows the exact result date and its weekday. For example, 90 days after 2 November 2026 is Sunday, 31 January 2027.

Q: What happens when I add one month to 31 January?
A: There is no 31 February, so the calculator moves to the last day of February instead: 28 February, or 29 February in a leap year. This end-of-month rule is the convention used by most software and banks.

Q: Does the business days option skip public holidays?
A: No. Business days skip Saturdays and Sundays only. Holidays differ between states, banks and companies, so if a holiday falls in your range, add one more business day for each holiday yourself.

Q: Is 30 days the same as one month?
A: No. Adding one month keeps the same date in the next month, so 15 March plus one month is 15 April, which is 31 days later. Adding 30 days to 15 March gives 14 April. Contracts and notices usually say which they mean, so follow that wording.

## How to Count Days Between Two Dates (Including Working Days)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/count-days-between-two-dates/
Tool: Date Difference (https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-difference-calculator/)

Quick answer: To count days between two dates, subtract the start date from the end date in calendar days, and add one if both the first and last day should count. BISCS India’s free Date Difference calculator does this instantly and also shows weeks, months, Monday-to-Friday working days and weekend days.

To find the number of days between two dates, count the calendar days from the start date to the end date. If both the first and the last day should be counted, add one. From 1 January 2026 to 31 March 2026 is 89 days, or 90 days if you include 31 March.

That "plus one" question is where most counting mistakes happen. The free [Date Difference calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-difference-calculator/) gives you a tick box for it, and shows the answer in days, weeks, months and working days at the same time.

## When do you need to count days between dates?

Day counts turn up in everyday Indian life more often than you might expect:

- **Notice periods** at work, often 30, 60 or 90 days.
- **Leave applications**, where both the first and last day are counted.
- **Interest calculations** on fixed deposits or short loans, which are based on the number of days.
- **Deadlines** for returns, replies to notices, refunds or warranty claims.
- **Project timelines** and how many working days a task really has.
- **Countdowns** to a wedding, exam or festival trip.

## Worked examples

### A quarter of the year
