- Without the end date: 89 days, which reads as 2 months and 30 days. There are 63 working days.
- With the end date: 90 days, exactly 3 months, with 64 working days (31 March 2026 is a Tuesday).

### A financial year

India's financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March. From 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 is 364 days exclusive, or 365 days when you include the last day. Since February 2027 has 28 days, the inclusive count is a normal 365-day year.

### A notice period

You resign on 2 November 2026 and your last working day is 31 January 2027. That is 90 days between the dates, with 65 Monday-to-Friday days. Your HR policy decides whether the notice is measured in calendar days or working days, so check which one your contract uses.

### A countdown

From 2 November 2026 to Christmas Day, 25 December 2026, is 53 days.

## Inclusive or exclusive: which should you use?

| Situation | Count the end date? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| "How many days until…" | No | You want the gap between today and the event |
| Leave from 10 to 14 March | Yes | Both the 10th and 14th are days off |
| Hotel nights | No | Checking out on the last day is not a night stayed |
| Interest on a deposit | Usually no | Banks typically count the days money was held; check your bank's method |
| Event that runs "from … to …" | Yes | Both dates are part of the event |
| Age or tenure | No | Measured as elapsed time |

When in doubt, read the wording: "from X to Y inclusive" means both days count, while "within N days of X" normally starts counting the day after X. For legal or tax deadlines, follow the rule stated in the relevant law or notice.

## How working days are counted

The calculator counts **Monday to Friday** as working days and Saturday and Sunday as weekend days. It does not know about holidays, because national, state and company holidays vary across India. To get an accurate figure:

1. Note the working days shown by the tool.
2. Subtract public or company holidays that fall on weekdays in your range.
3. If your office works on Saturdays, or on alternate Saturdays, add those days back.

This is still much faster and safer than counting on a wall calendar.

## Common date-counting mistakes

- **Forgetting the plus one** for inclusive periods like leave or event days.
- **Assuming 30 days per month.** A "one month" notice from 31 January ends on a different day from one starting on 1 March.
- **Missing leap years.** 2028 has a 29 February, so spans crossing it gain a day.
- **Counting weekends as working days** in project plans.
- **Ignoring holidays** when estimating delivery or processing times.
- **Mixing date formats.** 03/04 can be 3 April or 4 March. A date picker avoids this.

## Tips for planning with date differences

- Use the **weeks** figure for things measured in weeks, such as pregnancy check-ups or course schedules.
- Use **total months** when billing or rent is monthly, but check how part-months are charged.
- For SLAs and turnaround times, rely on **working days**, then subtract holidays.
- Keep a note of whether a figure is inclusive or exclusive when you share it, so others read it the same way.

If you know the start date and the number of days but need the end date, use [Add or Subtract Days](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/) instead, which can also skip weekends. For someone's exact age on a date, the [Age Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/) shows years, months and days with a birthday countdown. And if your deadline involves another country, the [Time Zone Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/time-zone-converter/) helps you line up the right local time.

Counting days sounds simple until a deadline depends on it. The [Date Difference calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/date-difference-calculator/) takes the guesswork out, so you can focus on the plan rather than the calendar.

Q: Should I include the end date when counting days?
A: It depends on what you are measuring. For a duration such as “how long until” or interest periods, the end date is usually not counted. For inclusive spans like leave from 10 to 14 March or a hotel stay counted in days, include it. The calculator has a tick box that adds that extra day.

Q: Does the working days count include public holidays?
A: No. Working days are counted as Monday to Friday only. National, state and company holidays differ, so subtract any holidays that fall in your range yourself. If your office works on Saturdays, add those back as well.

Q: Why do two websites give different month counts for the same dates?
A: Months have 28 to 31 days, so “months between dates” depends on the method. The BISCS calculator counts whole calendar months first, then the remaining days. Other tools may divide total days by 30 or 30.44, which gives slightly different answers.

Q: Can I count days backwards, if the end date is earlier?
A: Yes. If the end date is before the start date, the calculator swaps them for the maths and shows a note that the end date is earlier. You can also use the Swap dates button to reverse them yourself.

## Discount Calculator: Final Price After Stacked Discounts

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/discount-calculator-stacked-offers/
Tool: Discount Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/)

Quick answer: To find a sale price, multiply the original price by (1 − discount ÷ 100). Two discounts apply one after the other, so 20% plus an extra 10% on ₹2,999 gives ₹2,159.28, an effective 28% off rather than 30%. BISCS India's free Discount Calculator shows the final price, total savings and effective discount instantly.

To find the price after a discount, multiply the original price by (1 − discount ÷ 100). A ₹1,499 shirt at 40% off costs 1,499 × 0.60 = ₹899.40. Your saving is the original price minus the final price.

When a shop offers an "extra" discount on top of a sale price, the second discount applies to the reduced price, not the original. So 20% off followed by an extra 10% off is **28% off in total, not 30%**. The free [Discount Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) on BISCS India handles one or two discounts and can add GST for prices quoted before tax.

## Worked example: a festive sale

A pair of running shoes has an MRP of ₹2,999. The store offers 20% off, and your bank card gives an extra 10% off.

1. After 20% off: 2,999 × 0.80 = ₹2,399.20
2. After the extra 10%: 2,399.20 × 0.90 = ₹2,159.28
3. Total saving: 2,999 − 2,159.28 = ₹839.72
4. Effective discount: 839.72 ÷ 2,999 × 100 = **28%**

A straight 30% discount would have cost ₹2,099.30, about ₹60 less. That gap grows with bigger discounts.

## The stacked discount formula

For two discounts a% and b%, the effective discount is:

**Effective % = 1 − (1 − a ÷ 100) × (1 − b ÷ 100)**, then × 100

| Offer | Looks like | Actual effective discount |
|---|---|---|
| 10% + 10% | 20% | 19% |
| 20% + 10% | 30% | 28% |
| 30% + 20% | 50% | 44% |
| 50% + 20% | 70% | 60% |
| 50% + 50% | 100% | 75% |

On a ₹4,000 item, "50% + extra 20% off" means paying ₹1,600, while a true 70% off would mean ₹1,200. Reading offers this way helps you compare deals across stores and apps.

## How do you find the original price from a sale price?

Sometimes you only see the sale price and the percentage. Divide the sale price by (1 − discount ÷ 100). A dress tagged ₹1,799 "after 40% off" should have an original price of 1,799 ÷ 0.60 = ₹2,998.33, so roughly ₹2,999. If the tag claims an MRP far above that, the advertised discount does not add up.

## Are "buy one get one" offers really 50% off?

Only if you wanted two of the item. Buy one get one free on two items priced the same is a 50% discount per item. "Buy 2 get 1 free" is one free item in three, or 33.33% off. "Buy 3 get 1 free" is 25% off. If you only needed one, a straight 20% discount may save you more money than a bigger-sounding multi-buy deal. To compare, work out the price per item you actually need and run the straight-discount option through the calculator.

| Offer | Equivalent discount per item |
|---|---|
| Buy 1 get 1 free | 50% |
| Buy 2 get 1 free | 33.33% |
| Buy 3 get 1 free | 25% |

## How to use the BISCS Discount Calculator

1. Open the [Discount Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/).
2. Enter the **original price (MRP)**.
3. Enter the first **discount** percentage.
4. If there is a second offer, enter it as the **extra discount**. Leave it at 0 if there is none.
5. If the price is quoted before tax, tick **Add GST on the final price** and pick the rate (5%, 12%, 18%, 28% or 40%).
6. Read the final price, total savings and effective discount, with the price after each step shown separately.

The calculator updates as you type and runs entirely in your browser.

## Where does GST come in?

For goods sold in shops and online to consumers, the MRP printed on the pack is inclusive of all taxes, and the sale price you pay is also tax-inclusive. You do not add GST on top.

The GST option is useful in other situations: a supplier quoting "₹50,000 less 10%, plus GST", or a service priced before tax. In those cases, GST is generally charged on the discounted value shown on the invoice. With 18% GST, the shoes in our example would come to ₹2,159.28 + ₹388.67 = ₹2,547.95. For more GST arithmetic, use the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/).

## Smart shopping checklist

- Is the discount on the MRP or on an already-inflated "original" price? Compare with the price a few weeks earlier if you can.
- Are the two offers stacked or combined? Most "extra" discounts are stacked.
- Is a bank or wallet discount capped at a maximum amount? A "10% up to ₹500" offer gives only ₹500 off a ₹10,000 purchase, which is 5%.
- Do delivery charges, convenience fees or cash-on-delivery fees reduce the saving?
- Is the item returnable at the sale price, and are exchange terms the same?

## Tips for shop owners running a sale

Discounts cut directly into profit. If your margin on a product is 25%, a 20% discount leaves you with very little. Before announcing a sale, check the new margin in the [Profit Margin Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/). For quick percentage checks, such as what share of last month's sales came from discounted items, the [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) is handy.

## Common mistakes

1. **Adding discounts together.** 20% + 10% is 28% off, not 30%.
2. **Ignoring caps on card offers.** The headline percentage may apply only up to a small rupee limit.
3. **Adding GST to an MRP-based price.** MRP already includes tax.
4. **Comparing deals by percentage alone.** Compare the final rupee price, including fees.
5. **Rounding the first step.** Keep paise until the end for an accurate final price.

## A note on accuracy

The calculator applies discounts in the order entered and GST on the final discounted amount. Actual offers can include caps, minimum order values, or conditions that change the result. This guide is general information for everyday arithmetic, not legal or tax advice. If you think a retailer has charged above MRP or misrepresented an offer, the National Consumer Helpline and the Legal Metrology department in your state are the right places to raise it.

Q: Is 20% plus 10% off the same as 30% off?
A: No. The second discount applies to the already-reduced price. On ₹1,000, 20% off leaves ₹800, and a further 10% off leaves ₹720, which is 28% off in total. A straight 30% discount would leave ₹700. The effective discount is 1 − (0.8 × 0.9) = 28%.

Q: How do I calculate the discount percentage from two prices?
A: Subtract the sale price from the original price, divide by the original price and multiply by 100. If a jacket marked ₹2,500 is selling for ₹1,750, the discount is 750 ÷ 2,500 × 100 = 30%. This helps you check whether a sale tag's claim is accurate.

Q: Is GST added on top of the discounted price?
A: In shops, MRP already includes all taxes, so the discounted price you pay normally includes GST too. GST is added separately mainly on business quotes and some services priced before tax. Where it is added, it is generally charged on the price after any discount shown on the invoice.

Q: Does the order of two discounts matter?
A: No. Because each discount multiplies the price, 20% then 10% gives the same final price as 10% then 20%. What matters is whether the discounts are stacked, as most extra offers are, or added together into one bigger percentage, which is rarer. Check the offer's terms.

## EMI Calculator: Formula, Examples and Amortisation Explained

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/emi-calculator-formula-home-loan/
Tool: EMI Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/)

Quick answer: EMI is calculated as P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan, r the monthly interest rate and n the number of months. A ₹25 lakh home loan at 8.5% for 20 years costs about ₹21,696 a month. BISCS India's free EMI Calculator also shows total interest and a yearly amortisation table.

An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount you pay every month to repay a loan with interest. It is calculated with the formula **EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1)**, where P is the loan amount, r is the annual rate divided by 12 and by 100, and n is the tenure in months.

For example, a ₹25 lakh home loan at 8.5% a year for 20 years works out to about ₹21,696 a month. Over 240 months you repay roughly ₹52.07 lakh, so about ₹27.07 lakh of that is interest. The free [EMI Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/) shows these numbers instantly and breaks them down year by year.

## How is EMI calculated, step by step?

Take the same ₹25 lakh loan:

1. **Monthly rate:** 8.5 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0070833
2. **Months:** 20 × 12 = 240
3. **Growth factor:** (1.0070833)^240 ≈ 5.44
4. **EMI:** 25,00,000 × 0.0070833 × 5.44 ÷ (5.44 − 1) ≈ ₹21,696

You do not need to do this by hand, but seeing the steps helps you understand why the rate and tenure matter so much. The factor (1 + r)^n grows quickly with both, which is why small changes have a big effect over 20 years.

## How to use the BISCS EMI Calculator

1. Go to the [EMI Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/).
2. Enter or slide the **loan amount** (the slider covers ₹50,000 to ₹2 crore; you can type other amounts).
3. Set the **interest rate** per year as quoted by your lender.
4. Choose whether to enter the tenure in **years** or **months**, then set it.
5. Read the monthly EMI, total interest and total payment, with a donut chart showing principal versus interest.
6. Scroll to the **amortisation schedule** for a chart of principal and interest paid each year, and open the table to see the closing balance and the percentage of the loan repaid.

The calculation runs entirely in your browser, so nothing about your loan is stored or uploaded.

## How do rate and tenure change your EMI?

Here is the same ₹25 lakh loan under three scenarios, calculated with the tool:

| Scenario | Monthly EMI | Total interest | Total paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.5% for 20 years | ₹21,696 | ₹27.07 lakh | ₹52.07 lakh |
| 8.5% for 15 years | ₹24,618 | ₹19.31 lakh | ₹44.31 lakh |
| 9.0% for 20 years | ₹22,493 | ₹28.98 lakh | ₹53.98 lakh |

Two lessons stand out. Cutting five years off the tenure raises the EMI by about ₹2,900 but saves nearly ₹7.8 lakh of interest. And a half-percent higher rate adds about ₹800 to each EMI, which becomes almost ₹1.9 lakh over 20 years.

For a shorter loan, such as a ₹5 lakh personal loan at 10.5% for 5 years, the EMI is about ₹10,747 and total interest about ₹1.45 lakh.

## Reading the amortisation schedule

In the early years, most of each EMI pays interest. In month one of the home loan above, interest is about ₹17,708 and only about ₹3,987 reduces the principal. The balance falls slowly at first and then faster, because each month a little less interest is due.

This is why **prepayments early in the loan** have the biggest effect. Every rupee of principal you clear in year two stops attracting interest for the remaining 18 years. The schedule's "Loan paid" column shows how far along you are; on the ₹25 lakh example, only about 12% of the principal has been repaid after the first five years.

## When should you use an EMI calculator?

- **Before applying:** to check what loan size your monthly budget can carry. Many lenders look at how much of your income goes to EMIs, so a lower EMI can affect eligibility.
- **When comparing offers:** enter each lender's rate and tenure to compare total interest, not just the EMI.
- **After a rate change:** enter the outstanding balance, new rate and remaining months to see the new EMI.
- **When planning a prepayment:** reduce the loan amount by your prepayment and compare the outcomes of keeping the EMI or the tenure the same.

## Mistakes people make with loan EMIs

1. **Looking only at the EMI.** A lower EMI from a longer tenure usually means far more interest.
2. **Ignoring fees.** Processing fees, insurance bundled with the loan and GST on fees add to the real cost but are not part of the EMI formula.
3. **Assuming a floating rate stays fixed.** Model a rate rise of 1% or so to see if you could still manage.
4. **Forgetting the tax angle.** For a self-occupied home, interest on a home loan may be deductible up to ₹2 lakh a year under the old tax regime. Try the numbers in the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/) before assuming a benefit.
5. **Comparing flat-rate and reducing-balance quotes directly.** Some lenders quote a flat rate, which charges interest on the original amount throughout. The [Simple Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/simple-interest-calculator/) tool shows how flat interest is worked out, and it is usually much costlier than the same reducing-balance rate.

## What the calculator does not cover

The tool assumes a fixed rate for the whole term and equal monthly instalments starting one month after disbursement. It does not model step-up EMIs, moratoriums, part-prepayments in the middle of the schedule or broken-period interest. For a full picture of how money grows or costs compound, the [Compound Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/) calculator is a useful companion.

Treat these results as estimates for planning, not as a loan offer or financial advice. Your sanction letter and the lender's repayment schedule are the official figures, and RBI rules and your loan agreement govern rate resets and charges. If a decision is significant, discuss it with your bank or a qualified adviser.

Q: Does a longer tenure reduce the total cost of a loan?
A: No. A longer tenure lowers each EMI but increases total interest, because you borrow the money for longer. On ₹25 lakh at 8.5%, a 15-year term costs about ₹19.3 lakh in interest while a 20-year term costs about ₹27.1 lakh, even though the EMI drops by roughly ₹2,900.

Q: Why is most of my early EMI going towards interest?
A: Interest each month is charged on the outstanding balance, which is highest at the start. As the balance falls, the interest part shrinks and the principal part grows. In the first month of a ₹25 lakh, 8.5%, 20-year loan, about ₹17,708 of the ₹21,696 EMI is interest.

Q: Will my bank's EMI match this calculator exactly?
A: It should be very close for a fixed-rate loan, but small differences are normal. Banks may round the EMI, charge broken-period interest from the disbursement date, or use a slightly different day count. Processing fees, insurance and floating-rate resets are not included in a standard EMI formula.

Q: What happens to my EMI if the interest rate rises on a floating loan?
A: Lenders usually either increase the EMI or keep it the same and extend the tenure. Extending the tenure can add many months and a lot of interest. You can model a rate change by entering the outstanding balance, the new rate and the remaining months in the calculator.

Q: Is a zero-interest EMI really free?
A: Not always. Some no-cost EMI offers build the interest into the product price or pass on a discount you would otherwise have received, and processing fees or GST on interest may apply. Compare the total amount you will pay with the price for an outright purchase before deciding.

## Entity SEO: Organization and Author Schema With sameAs

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/organization-author-schema-entity-seo/
Tool: Entity & Author Schema Builder (https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/)

Quick answer: Entity SEO means helping search engines and AI systems recognise your business and authors as distinct, real entities, using consistent details and structured data. BISCS India’s free Entity & Author Schema Builder creates linked Organization, WebSite and Person JSON-LD with sameAs profiles, stable @id references and expertise fields, in your browser.

Entity SEO is about making sure search engines and AI systems understand **who** is behind a website: which organisation runs it, who writes its content, and which social profiles and listings belong to them. When those facts are consistent and clearly stated, it is easier for Google, Bing and AI assistants to connect your site with your brand and trust it as a source.

The [Entity & Author Schema Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/) from BISCS India creates the structured data for this: a linked set of Organization, WebSite and Person JSON-LD, with sameAs profiles and stable @id references that other pages can point to.

## What is an entity, and why does it matter?

To a search engine, an entity is a distinct thing it can recognise: a company, a person, a place, a product. "BISCS India, an IT company in Kolkata" is an entity; the words "biscs india" on a page are just text until the search engine links them to that thing.

Entities matter more as search becomes answer-driven. When an AI assistant names a recommended accountant or quotes a guide, it needs confidence about who the source is. Consistent names, addresses, logos and profiles across the web, plus clear structured data on your own site, give it that confidence.

## What the builder generates

The output is a single JSON-LD block using an `@graph` with up to three connected items:

| Item | Key properties | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Organization | Type, official name, other names, URL, logo, description, founding date, email, phone, address, contact point, sameAs, knowsAbout | States who you are and links your official profiles |
| WebSite | URL, name, publisher | Ties the website to the organisation |
| Person (optional) | Name, job title, works for, author page URL, photo, sameAs, alumniOf, knowsAbout | Describes an author or founder and their expertise |

Each item gets a stable `@id`, such as `https://www.example.com/#organization` and `https://www.example.com/#founder`. Articles elsewhere on your site can then reference the same publisher and author by `@id`, rather than repeating the details.

The organisation type can be Organization, LocalBusiness, ProfessionalService, Corporation, EducationalOrganization or NGO. For a detailed local business listing with opening hours and map coordinates, the [Schema Markup Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) has a dedicated Local Business form.

## How to build your entity schema

1. Open the [Entity & Author Schema Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/).
2. Under **Organisation**, choose the type and enter your **official name** exactly as it appears on your registration, signboard and Google Business Profile. Add **other names** such as abbreviations.
3. Enter your **website URL** (it must be a full `https://` address) and a **logo URL** for a square logo at least 112 px wide.
4. Add a short **description**, the **founding date**, **email**, **phone with country code** (for example +91), and your **city, state, PIN code and country code**.
5. List your **official profiles** in sameAs, one URL per line: LinkedIn company page, Facebook page, Instagram, YouTube channel and similar.
6. Add **topics you are known for**, such as "GST compliance, payroll, company registration".
7. Under **Author (person)**, keep "Include an author / founder" ticked if you want a Person entry. Add the name, job title, author page URL, photo, profiles, where they studied and their expertise.
8. Read the warnings, then press **Copy** or **Download** and add the code to your home page, and optionally your About page.
9. Test the page with Google's Rich Results Test or the Schema.org validator.

Everything is generated in your browser; no details are sent anywhere.

## Getting sameAs right

sameAs is the heart of entity markup, and it is easy to misuse:

- **Do** list official profiles you control: LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X, YouTube.
- **Do** include reputable reference pages that are genuinely about you, such as a Wikipedia article if one exists.
- **Do not** list directory pages, review sites or other people's pages just to add links.
- **Do not** include profiles you have abandoned with outdated information. Update them first.
- **Use the same name, logo and description** on every profile as on your site.

## Author pages and E-E-A-T

Google's quality rater guidelines describe E-E-A-T: experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness. Schema does not create E-E-A-T, but it helps describe evidence that already exists.

A strong setup looks like this:

- A real **About page** describing the business, its team and how to contact it.
- An **author page** for each regular writer, with a photo, role, relevant qualifications (for example a chartered accountant writing about tax) and links to their profiles.
- Articles with a visible **byline** linking to that author page, and, for finance, health or legal topics, a "reviewed by" credit where appropriate.
- Person markup on the author page that matches all of the above.

## An example: a CA firm in Ahmedabad

Imagine a chartered accountancy firm. Its Organization entry uses the type ProfessionalService, the registered firm name, the logo from its website, its Ahmedabad address with PIN code, a +91 phone number and links to its LinkedIn company page and YouTube channel of tax explainer videos. Under "known for", it lists GST compliance, income tax filing and company incorporation.

The managing partner gets a Person entry with the job title "Managing Partner", a link to her author page on the firm's website, her LinkedIn profile, the institute she studied at and her areas of expertise. Every article she writes shows her byline, links to that page and, in its own Article markup, references her `@id` as the author and the firm's `@id` as publisher. The result is a small, consistent web of facts that search engines can connect with confidence.

## Common entity SEO mistakes

- **Inconsistent names**: "Sharma & Sons", "Sharma and Sons Pvt Ltd" and "Sharma Sons Traders" across different platforms.
- **Old addresses or phone numbers** on listings after a move.
- **Fake authors** or stock photos presented as experts. This undermines trust badly if discovered.
- **Several conflicting Organization blocks** from different plugins. Check your HTML with the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/).
- **Changing @id URLs** later, which breaks references from other pages.

## Bringing it together

Entity markup works best alongside good content and consistent listings. Once your organisation and authors are described clearly, check that your articles are structured to be quoted using the [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/). Revisit the [Entity & Author Schema Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/) whenever your logo, address, team or profiles change.

Q: What does sameAs mean in schema markup?
A: sameAs lists URLs of other pages that represent the same entity, such as your official LinkedIn, Facebook or Instagram profile, or a reputable reference page about you. It helps search engines connect those profiles to your website. List only official profiles you control or that genuinely describe you.

Q: Will Organization schema get me a knowledge panel?
A: Not by itself. Knowledge panels are generated automatically when Google has enough consistent, trusted information about an entity. Organization markup helps by stating your official name, logo, website and profiles clearly, but there is no markup that guarantees a panel.

Q: Where should I add Organization and author schema?
A: Add the Organization and WebSite markup to your home page, and optionally your About page. Author or Person markup belongs on the author’s profile page. Articles can then reference the same author and publisher using their @id URLs instead of repeating every detail.

Q: Is author schema the same as E-E-A-T?
A: No. E-E-A-T, which stands for experience, expertise, authoritativeness and trustworthiness, is a concept from Google’s quality rater guidelines, not a markup type. Author schema simply describes who wrote the content. Real author pages, credentials and accurate content are what demonstrate E-E-A-T.

Q: Is my business information uploaded when I use the builder?
A: No. The form is processed in your browser and the JSON-LD is generated on your device. Nothing is sent to a server. You copy or download the code and add it to your own site.

An Excel and CSV converter changes spreadsheet data from one format to another: Excel workbook (.xlsx) to CSV, CSV to Excel, or either one to JSON. You open the file, check the data, and download it in the format the next system wants.

It sounds trivial until you hit the real-world snags: a bank portal that wants a pipe-separated file, a CSV where every Hindi name turns into question marks, or a phone with no spreadsheet app. This guide covers those too.

## When do you need to convert spreadsheet formats?

## Which format should you choose?

| Format | Holds | Best for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| XLSX | Multiple sheets, formatting, formulas | People working in Excel or Sheets | Not readable by many upload portals |
| CSV | One sheet of plain values | Imports, portals, simple data exchange | Encoding and delimiter issues; no formatting |
| JSON | Structured records | Developers, apps, APIs | Less friendly for non-technical users |
| HTML table | A formatted table | Pasting into emails and documents | Not meant for re-importing |

## Fixing garbled Hindi, Bengali and ₹ symbols in CSV files

A very common problem in India: you open a CSV in Excel and names like "राम" or "সুমিত" appear as strings of odd symbols, and ₹ turns into "â‚¹".

The cause is encoding. CSV files do not say which character set they use, and Excel on Windows does not always assume UTF-8. Adding a small marker at the start of the file, called a byte order mark (BOM), tells Excel to read it as UTF-8.

The converter's **UTF-8 BOM (for Excel)** option is ticked by default for this reason. Untick it only if the system you are uploading to rejects files with a BOM, which some older portals do.

## Detect numbers and dates: what it does

When building an Excel file from a CSV, **Detect numbers & dates** turns text that looks like a plain number or an ISO date into real numeric and date cells, so you can sum columns, filter by date and sort properly.

The detection is deliberately cautious, because spreadsheets are notorious for damaging Indian data:

- **Leading zeros are kept.** A value like "0712345" or a PIN-style code starting with zero stays as text, so it is not shortened.
- **Long numbers stay as text.** Values of 16 digits or more, such as some bank account or card-style numbers, are not converted, which avoids Excel's scientific notation and lost digits.
- **Only unambiguous dates are converted.** Dates written as YYYY-MM-DD, like 2025-04-01, become date cells. Formats such as 01/04/2025 stay as text, because they could mean 1 April or 4 January.
- **The header row is never converted**, so a column called "2025" stays a label.

Even so, IDs such as mobile numbers, Aadhaar-style numbers and employee codes are safest kept as text. If your file is mostly identifiers, untick the option and every value stays exactly as written.

## A worked example: a bank statement export

Suppose your bank lets you download a statement as a pipe-separated text file, and your accountant wants an Excel file.

1. Open the `.txt` file in the converter. The pipe delimiter is detected automatically.
2. Check that the columns line up: date, narration, withdrawal, deposit, balance.
3. Search for a party name, such as a supplier, to check a few entries quickly.
4. Click **Download .xlsx**. Amounts become numbers you can total, and the header row stays bold and frozen.

Going the other way, a payroll team can open a salary workbook, pick the sheet the portal needs, choose the delimiter the portal specifies, and download a CSV ready to upload.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting CSV to keep every sheet.** A CSV holds one sheet. Export each sheet separately, or use XLSX.
- **Expecting formatting in CSV.** Colours, bold text, merged cells and formulas are lost; only values remain.
- **Uploading the wrong delimiter.** If a portal shows all your data in one column, it expected a different delimiter.
- **Exporting filtered rows by accident.** The export options can include only rows matching your search, in your sorted order. Clear the search if you want everything.
- **Opening old .xls files.** Save them as .xlsx first.

## Tips for cleaner data

- Search to find a specific invoice, GSTIN or customer in a large file without scrolling.
- Sort by amount or date before exporting a report.
- Developers converting between CSV and JSON for small snippets of pasted text may prefer [CSV to JSON](https://biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/) and [JSON to CSV](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/), which work on text rather than files. To check or tidy a JSON file, use the [JSON Formatter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/).

## Is it safe to open business spreadsheets here?

Yes. The [Excel & CSV Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/excel-csv-converter/) reads and writes files inside your browser. Salary sheets, customer lists and sales data are not uploaded to BISCS India. The spreadsheet library is downloaded once when you first open an Excel file; after that, the conversion happens on your device.

Q: Why does Hindi or Bengali text look garbled when I open a CSV in Excel?
A: Excel sometimes guesses the wrong text encoding for CSV files and shows Indian-language characters as symbols. Saving the CSV with a UTF-8 byte order mark tells Excel the correct encoding. The converter’s UTF-8 BOM (for Excel) option is on by default for this reason.

Q: Can the converter open old .xls files?
A: No. Only the modern .xlsx and .xlsm formats are supported, along with CSV, TSV, text and JSON. Open the old file in Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets, save it as .xlsx or .csv, and then open it here.

Q: Are formulas kept when I convert?
A: The converter reads the last calculated value of each formula cell, not the formula itself. That is what you want for CSV and JSON, which cannot hold formulas anyway. If you need the formulas, keep working in the original Excel file and use this tool only for exports.

Q: What is a CSV delimiter and which one should I use?
A: The delimiter is the character that separates columns. Comma is the most common. Semicolon is used in many European settings where the comma is a decimal mark, tab avoids clashes with commas in addresses, and pipe is used by some bank and accounting exports. Choose whatever the receiving system expects.

Q: Can it handle large files?
A: Yes. Files with 50,000 or more rows open comfortably on a computer because the table only draws the rows you can see. Very large workbooks take longer to read on phones and older laptops, but nothing is uploaded, so there is no server size limit.

- **Sending a single payslip.** HR sent a 12-month PDF, and the landlord's agent needs only the latest one.
- **Sharing one chapter.** A teacher wants pages 45 to 60 of a textbook PDF for a class worksheet.
- **Proof for a claim.** An insurance claim needs only the discharge summary and the final bill, not the full 30-page hospital file.
- **A single property document page.** A society office asks for the page showing the flat number and owner names, not the entire sale deed.
- **Interview preparation.** Pull the two relevant pages from a long company report to read on your phone.

## How to extract PDF pages step by step

1. Open [Extract PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/extract-pdf-pages/) and choose the PDF.
2. Click the thumbnails of the pages you want. Shift-click to select a whole run between two pages.
3. Or type page numbers and ranges in **Pages to extract**, for example `2, 5-9, 14`.
4. Use **Quick select** if helpful: All, None, Odd or Even.
5. Decide on the output: one combined PDF (default) or each page as a separate PDF in a ZIP.
6. Click **Extract pages** and download the result.

## Extract vs split vs remove

All three tools rebuild a PDF from chosen pages, but they suit different ways of thinking.

| Tool | You tell it… | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Extract PDF Pages | Which pages to **keep** | One new PDF, or one PDF per page |
| [Remove PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/) | Which pages to **drop** | One new PDF |
| [Split PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/) | Where to **cut** the document | Several PDFs covering the whole document |

If you need 3 pages out of 80, extract. If you need 77 out of 80, remove. If you need all 80 broken into sections, split.

## Combining extract with other tools

Extraction is often the first step in a bigger task.

**Building an application bundle.** Extract the relevant pages from several long documents (one page from your passport scan, two pages from a bank statement), then join them with [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/).

**Making a printable handout.** Extract the pages, then add numbering with [Add Page Numbers](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-page-numbers/) so the new handout starts at page 1.

**Reordering.** Extracted pages are saved in document order. If you need a different order, open the new file in Organize PDF and drag the pages around.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Going by printed footer numbers.** Many reports start numbering after the cover and contents pages. Always use the position shown under each thumbnail.
- **Forgetting the separate-files option.** If you need ten pages as ten separate attachments, tick the option instead of extracting ten times.
- **Assuming click order sets page order.** The output follows the original document order.
- **Extracting part of a signed agreement as "proof".** A single page cut from a contract may not be accepted as the full document. Ask what the receiver actually needs.

## Privacy: share less, and keep it local

Extracting is itself a privacy tool. A loan document, a medical file or a property paper usually contains far more personal information than any single recipient needs. Sending only the relevant pages reduces what is exposed if an email is forwarded or a phone is lost.

The tool adds a second layer of privacy: processing happens in your browser. Your PDF is not uploaded, so there is no copy sitting on a server somewhere. This is particularly reassuring for documents downloaded from DigiLocker or other sources that carry Aadhaar or PAN details.

## Example: sending just the right pages to an employer

Karthik is switching jobs, and his new employer's HR team asks for "the last three months' payslips and your relieving letter". His old company's portal let him download the whole year's payslips as one 12-page PDF, and the relieving letter came as page 3 of a 5-page exit document.

He opens the payslip PDF, types `10-12` to select the last three months, and extracts them into a new file. Then he opens the exit document and extracts page 3 alone. Finally he merges the two results so HR receives a single, four-page PDF with exactly what they asked for and nothing else, no annual salary breakup, no tax projections, no personal exit feedback.

This is a small thing, but it is the kind of care that makes paperwork go smoothly, and it keeps the rest of your financial details to yourself.

## What happens to links, bookmarks and forms?

The extracted pages look exactly like the originals. However, document-level extras such as the bookmark panel, which point to the whole original file, are not rebuilt for the new document. For most everyday uses (payslips, bills, certificates), this makes no difference, because those files rarely have bookmarks to begin with.

## Tips for neat results

- Rename the extracted file before sending, for example `Payslip-October.pdf` rather than `salary-extracted.pdf`.
- For very large PDFs, typing ranges is faster than scrolling through hundreds of thumbnails.

## Fancy Text Generator: Stylish Fonts for Instagram and WhatsApp

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/fancy-text-generator-instagram-whatsapp-fonts/
Tool: Fancy Text Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/fancy-text-generator/)

Quick answer: A fancy text generator converts ordinary letters into look-alike Unicode characters, such as bold, script or bubble letters, that you can copy into apps that do not offer fonts. BISCS India’s Fancy Text Generator shows 25 styles at once; click any style to copy it for your Instagram bio, WhatsApp status or post.

A fancy text generator turns plain letters into stylish look-alikes, like 𝐛𝐨𝐥𝐝, 𝘪𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘤, 𝓈𝒸𝓇𝒾𝓅𝓉 or ⓑⓤⓑⓑⓛⓔ, that you can copy and paste into apps without font options. Type your text once, see it in many styles, and tap the one you like to copy it.

It is popular for Instagram bios, WhatsApp statuses, YouTube channel descriptions and gaming names. But there is an important catch about accessibility and search that every user should know, covered below.

## How does fancy text actually work?

Instagram, WhatsApp and most apps do not let you choose fonts. Fancy text gets around that by swapping each letter for a **different Unicode character** that looks like a styled version.

Unicode, the standard that defines every character your phone can display, includes several complete alphabets originally intended for mathematical notation: bold, italic, script, fraktur, double-struck, monospace and sans-serif letters. There are also circled letters, squared letters, small capitals and full-width characters from East Asian typography.

So 𝐀 in bold is not the letter A with bold formatting. It is a separate character called "Mathematical Bold Capital A". That is why it survives copy and paste, and also why it causes the problems described later.

## How to create fancy text

1. Open the [Fancy Text Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fancy-text-generator/).
2. Type your text into the box at the top, up to 500 characters.
3. Scroll through the list of 25 styles, all updated live.
4. Tap or click any style to copy it.
5. Paste it into your Instagram bio, WhatsApp status, post or profile.

The styles include Bold, Italic, Bold italic, Script, Bold script, Fraktur, Bold fraktur, Double-struck, Monospace, four Sans-serif variants, Bubble, Bubble filled, Squared, Squared filled, Small caps, Wide, Upside down, Strikethrough, Underline, Double underline, Slashed and Spaced out.

## Which styles work best where?

| Style | Looks like | Support | Good for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bold / Sans bold | 𝐁𝐈𝐒𝐂𝐒 / 𝗕𝗜𝗦𝗖𝗦 | Very wide | Short headlines in bios and posts |
| Italic | 𝘉𝘐𝘚𝘊𝘚 | Very wide | Emphasis on a word or two |
| Script | 𝒮𝓉𝓎𝓁𝑒 | Wide | Names, wedding or boutique pages |
| Small caps | ꜱᴍᴀʟʟ ᴄᴀᴘꜱ | Wide | Subtle styling for taglines |
| Bubble | ⓑⓤⓑⓑⓛⓔ | Wide | Playful profiles |
| Fraktur | 𝔉𝔯𝔞𝔨𝔱𝔲𝔯 | Moderate | Gaming names, gothic look |
| Squared | Capital letters inside boxes | Patchy on older devices | Decorative one-word labels |
| Strikethrough | s̶t̶r̶i̶k̶e̶ | Wide, but spacing varies | Jokes, "old price" style |

Support depends on the fonts installed on the viewer's device, not yours. If you see empty boxes on someone else's phone, that device lacks the characters.

## The accessibility catch: screen readers

This is the part most fancy text sites leave out. Screen readers, the software that reads the screen aloud for blind and low-vision users, do not see "bold text". They see unusual mathematical characters. Depending on the app and device, they might:

- read each letter by its full name, such as "mathematical bold capital B, mathematical bold capital I…";
- spell the word out one letter at a time;
- skip the characters entirely, leaving silence.

A bio that says "𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐡 𝐇𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐝𝐞 𝐒𝐰𝐞𝐞𝐭𝐬 · 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐨𝐧 𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭𝐬𝐀𝐩𝐩" may be unreadable for a visually impaired customer. For a business, that is a lost order; for anyone, it shuts people out.

**A good rule:** use fancy letters for a small decorative touch, and keep your name, contact details, prices and key information in normal text.

## Other limits to know

- **Search.** Platforms may not match fancy letters to normal ones, so a profile name written entirely in script may not appear when people search for it.
- **Hashtags and mentions.** A hashtag in fancy letters will not become a clickable tag. Keep hashtags and @usernames plain.
- **Only A–Z and 0–9.** The styled alphabets exist only for English letters and digits. Hindi, Bengali and other scripts stay unchanged, though effects like strikethrough, underline and spaced out work with any text.
- **Character limits.** Many fancy characters count as two characters internally, so a styled bio can hit Instagram's limit sooner than you expect.
- **Professional settings.** Avoid fancy text in CVs, LinkedIn headlines, email subject lines and official forms. It can look unprofessional, and automated systems may not read it.

## Tips for using fancy text well

- **Style one line, not everything.** A bold name or headline stands out more when the rest is plain.
- **Preview on another phone.** Check how it looks on an older Android device if your audience uses them.
- **Mix with emoji sparingly.** Too much decoration makes text hard to scan.
- **Use upside-down text for fun only.** It is a good joke, but nobody can read it quickly. The [Reverse Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/reverse-text/) tool has more flipping options.
- **Prefer real formatting where it exists.** WhatsApp supports genuine bold with asterisks around words, which screen readers handle far better than fancy characters.

## Example: an accessible Instagram bio

Imagine a home bakery in Lucknow writing its bio. A version written entirely in script looks pretty but is hard to read, may not show up in search, and is silent or garbled for screen reader users.

A better approach uses fancy text for just one element:

1. First line: the brand name in a single fancy style, such as bold sans, for visual impact.
2. Second line, in plain text: "Eggless cakes and cookies, Gomti Nagar".
3. Third line, in plain text: "Order on WhatsApp: 98XXX XXXXX".
4. Hashtag in plain text, such as #LucknowBakery, so it stays clickable.

Better still, keep the brand name plain in the profile's name field, which is the field search relies on most, and use the styled version only in the bio itself. Everyone can find the shop, and every customer can read how to order.

If you want a post that stands out visually, an image often works better than stylised letters, because you can use any real font and add alt text for accessibility. The [Social Post Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/social-post-maker/) helps you design one. Q: Why do fancy fonts work in Instagram when it has no font options?
A: They are not really fonts. Each styled letter is a separate Unicode character, originally created for maths and other symbols, that happens to look like a bold, italic or script letter. Because they are characters rather than formatting, they paste into any app that supports Unicode text.

Q: Can screen readers read fancy text?
A: Often not well. Screen readers used by blind and low-vision people may read each letter as its full technical name, such as mathematical bold capital A, spell it letter by letter, or skip it entirely. Keep your name, key information and calls to action in normal text, and use fancy letters only for decoration.

Q: Why do some fancy letters show as boxes?
A: The device or app viewing the text does not have a font that includes those particular Unicode characters. Older phones and some desktop apps are most affected. Bold, italic and small caps styles are widely supported; rarer styles such as squared or fraktur letters are more likely to appear as empty boxes.

Q: Do fancy letters work in hashtags and usernames?
A: Generally no. Hashtags and usernames on most platforms accept only standard letters, numbers and underscores, so a hashtag written in fancy letters will not link or be searchable. Keep hashtags and @mentions in plain text even if the rest of your caption is styled.

Q: Does the generator support Hindi or other Indian scripts?
A: The styled alphabets exist only for the English letters A to Z and digits 0 to 9, so Hindi, Bengali and other scripts pass through unchanged. Effects such as strikethrough, underline and spaced out add marks or spaces around any character, so those also work with Indian scripts.

## FAQ Schema Generator: Build an FAQ Section With FAQPage JSON-LD

An FAQ schema generator turns a list of questions and answers into two things: a visible FAQ section for your page, and FAQPage JSON-LD structured data that describes the same content to search engines. Getting both from one source matters, because the markup must match what visitors actually see.

The [FAQ Schema Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/faq-schema-generator/) from BISCS India does exactly that. You type or paste your questions and answers, and it produces accessible HTML, valid JSON-LD, or both combined, with a live preview and checks for common problems.

## What FAQ rich results look like today

It is important to start with expectations. In August 2023, Google limited FAQ rich results (the expandable questions under a search result) to well-known, authoritative government and health websites. For almost every business, blog or shop, valid FAQPage markup will no longer produce that visual enhancement in Google.

So why bother? Because a good FAQ section is still valuable on its own:

- It answers real customer questions, reducing calls and WhatsApp messages.
- It gives search engines and AI answer tools clearly structured question-and-answer pairs to understand and quote.
- It covers the long-tail questions people type or speak into search.
- The markup remains valid schema.org that other search engines and AI systems can read.

The honest view: add FAQ schema when you have a genuine FAQ section, not as a ranking trick.

## How to build an FAQ section with schema

1. Open the [FAQ Schema Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/faq-schema-generator/). Press **Sample** to see a filled-in example.
2. Set the **Section heading**, such as "Frequently asked questions" or "GST registration: your questions answered".
3. Type each question and its answer. Use **Add question** for more, and the arrow buttons to reorder them.
4. In answers, you can use simple formatting: bold, italics, links and bullet lists.
5. Already have questions in a document? Open the import panel and paste **Q&A text**, either as "Q: … A: …" pairs or as question lines ending in "?" followed by the answer. Choose **Append** or **Replace all**.
6. Read the messages: empty questions or answers, duplicates, questions without a question mark, and very long answers are flagged.
7. Choose the output: **HTML**, **JSON-LD**, **Combined** or **Preview**. Tick **First answer open** if you want the first answer expanded by default.

## Writing questions people actually ask

The best FAQ sections come from real conversations, not from guessing. Good sources include:

- Questions customers ask on calls, at the counter or on WhatsApp.
- Emails and support tickets.
- The People Also Ask box in Google for your main topic.
- Your sales team's most common objections.

The [Question & Topic Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/question-generator/) can also suggest who, what, how, cost and comparison questions for a keyword, which you can then check against real demand.

Write each question the way a customer would say it: "Do you deliver to Howrah?" rather than "Delivery coverage information".

## Writing answers that stand alone

Each answer may be read without the rest of the page, by a person skimming or by an AI tool quoting it. So:

- **Answer in the first sentence.** "Yes, we deliver across Kolkata and Howrah within two working days."
- **Name the subject**, rather than starting with "It" or "This".
- **Be specific.** Prices with ₹ and the date they apply, timelines in days, clear conditions.
- **Keep it short.** Around 40–80 words usually works. Link to a full guide for complex topics.
- **Stay accurate.** For rules that change, such as tax rates or government fees, say "currently" and link to the official source.

To polish individual answers for snippets and voice search, the [AEO Answer Optimizer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/aeo-answer-optimizer/) checks length, structure and readability.

## FAQ schema rules to follow

| Do | Do not |
|---|---|
| Mark up questions and answers visible on the page | Put content in JSON-LD that is hidden or different |
| Use FAQPage for questions answered by you, the site owner | Use FAQPage for forums or user-submitted Q&A (use QAPage) |
| Keep one official answer per question | Add the same FAQ block to every page of the site |
| Write genuine informational answers | Use questions purely as advertising |
| Keep answers up to date | Leave old prices, dates or policies in place |

## Common FAQ mistakes

- **Duplicate FAQs across many pages.** A copy of the same ten questions on every service page adds little value. Tailor each page's FAQ to its topic.
- **Answers that dodge the question.** "Contact us for details" is not an answer.
- **Very long answers.** If an answer needs 400 words, it probably deserves its own article.
- **Markup without the section.** Pasting JSON-LD into a page with no visible FAQ goes against Google's guidelines.
- **Two FAQPage blocks on one page**, often from a plugin plus manual code. Check your final HTML with the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/), which lists structured data types it finds.

## An example FAQ for a local business

A dental clinic in Bhubaneswar might answer questions such as "Do you accept walk-in patients?", "How much does a root canal cost?", "Is parking available near the clinic?" and "Do you treat children?". Each answer is two or three sentences: a direct reply, the key condition, and a link to book or to a detailed treatment page. Prices are shown as a range with "currently" and a note that the final cost depends on the examination.

That section helps anxious patients decide, reduces repeated phone calls, and gives search engines clean question-and-answer pairs, whether or not a rich result ever appears.

## Where to place your FAQ section

Put it near the end of a service or product page, after the main content, or on a dedicated help page. Keep the heading clear, use your own brand voice, and link from answers to the pages that explain more.

Then build or update it whenever customer questions change. The [FAQ Schema Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/faq-schema-generator/) keeps your visible section and markup in step, so you only have to edit one list.

Q: Does Google still show FAQ rich results?
A: Since August 2023, Google shows FAQ rich results only for well-known, authoritative government and health websites. Most business sites will not get the expandable questions in search results, even with valid markup. The markup is still valid schema.org and can help other systems understand your content.

Q: Is FAQ schema still worth adding?
A: It is worth adding when the page genuinely has a visible FAQ section, because it costs little and describes the content precisely for search engines and AI tools. It is not worth adding to pages without real questions, and it should never be added just to chase a rich result.

Q: Must the FAQ content be visible on the page?
A: Yes. Google’s guidelines require the questions and answers in FAQPage markup to be visible to users on the same page. Hidden or different content in the JSON-LD is treated as misleading. Generating the HTML and markup from the same list avoids mismatches.

Q: Can I use FAQPage schema for customer questions in a forum?
A: No. FAQPage is for questions and answers written by the site owner, where each question has one official answer. Pages where users submit questions and several people answer, such as forums or product Q&A, should use QAPage markup instead.

Q: How long should FAQ answers be?
A: Short and complete is best. Most answers work well at 40–80 words, enough to answer properly on their own. The generator flags answers over about 150 words as long and over 300 as very long; link to a full guide when a topic needs more depth.

A favicon is the small icon that appears in a browser tab, in bookmarks, in search results on some devices and on a phone’s home screen when someone saves your site. Creating one means producing the same icon in several sizes and formats, then adding a few lines of HTML so browsers can find them.

## Designing an icon that works at 16 pixels

The hardest part of a favicon is not making the files, it is making something recognisable at the size of a fingernail.

### Simplify ruthlessly

A full logo with a company name will turn into a smudge at 16 pixels. Use just the symbol, or the first letter of your brand. A Kolkata bakery called “Mitra Sweets” might use a bold “M” on a warm orange square, and that will be clearer than a tiny drawing of a sweet box.

### Use strong contrast

Light grey on white disappears in a light-themed browser, and dark navy on black disappears in dark mode. A solid background with a contrasting letter is readable on any tab bar.

### Fill the space

Too much padding makes the icon look tiny next to other tabs. Start around 10% padding and reduce it if the preview looks small.

### Think about the round versions

Phones often mask icons into circles or rounded squares. Keep the important part of the design near the centre so nothing is cut off.

## Adding the favicon to your website

For a hand-built site, copy the files into the same folder as your home page and paste the snippet before the closing head tag. The snippet links the ICO, the 16 and 32 pixel PNGs, the Apple touch icon, the manifest and a theme-colour meta tag.

Website builders and content management systems often have their own “site icon” setting. In that case, upload the 512 pixel PNG there, as most builders generate the smaller sizes themselves.

## Why a favicon is worth five minutes of effort

A favicon is small, but it does a lot of quiet work. People with many tabs open scan the icons, not the titles, to find your page again. Bookmarks and browser history show it next to your site name. When someone adds your website to an Android or iPhone home screen, the larger icons become the app-style tile they tap every day.

Google also shows site icons beside results in its search pages on many devices, using the favicon your site declares. Google publishes its own favicon guidelines, so if search appearance matters to you, read their current documentation. In general, a square, clearly visible icon at a stable address is what search engines expect.

Without a favicon, browsers show a generic blank page symbol, which makes even a well-designed site look unfinished. For a small business, a coaching institute or a freelancer’s portfolio, that is an easy credibility point to win.

## Common mistakes

- **Using a wide, rectangular logo.** It gets squashed or shrunk into a tiny strip. Crop it to a square first with [Crop Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/).
- **Starting from a small source image.** A 64 pixel logo cannot produce a sharp 512 pixel icon. Use the largest version you have.
- **Uploading files to the wrong folder.** The snippet uses root paths such as `/favicon.ico`, so the files must sit at the root of the domain unless you edit the paths.
- **Forgetting the cache.** If the old icon keeps appearing, it is almost always the browser cache rather than a problem with the files.
- **Leaving the manifest name as the default.** Update the website name so Android shows the right label when someone adds your site to their home screen.

Yes. Your logo is drawn and resized on your own device using the browser’s canvas, and the ZIP is assembled locally. Nothing is uploaded, which is useful when you are working on a client’s brand before launch.

Q: What size should a favicon be?
A: There is no single size. Browser tabs use 16 and 32 pixel icons, Windows shortcuts may use 48 pixels, iPhones and iPads use a 180 pixel Apple touch icon, and Android home screens use 192 and 512 pixel icons. The generator creates all of them from one source image.

Q: Do I still need a favicon.ico file?
A: It is still worth including. Many browsers and tools look for favicon.ico at the root of a website automatically, even without any HTML tag. The generated ICO contains 16, 32 and 48 pixel versions, while modern browsers also use the PNG files listed in the HTML snippet.

Q: Why does my favicon look blurry or unreadable?
A: Usually because a detailed logo has been shrunk to 16 pixels, where fine text and thin lines disappear. Use a simplified mark, a single letter or a bold symbol, reduce padding so it fills the space, and choose strong contrast between the icon and its background.

Q: Why is my new favicon not showing after I uploaded it?
A: Browsers cache favicons aggressively. Check that the files are in your site’s root folder and the HTML is inside the head section, then hard-refresh the page or open it in a private window. It can take a while for every browser and search engine to pick up the change.

Q: Can I make a favicon without a logo?
A: Yes. Choose Create from text or emoji, type one to three characters such as your initials, pick a font, text colour and background colour, and round the corners or make it a circle. Many small businesses and personal sites use exactly this approach.

## FD Calculator: Fixed Deposit Maturity and Interest Explained

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/fd-calculator-maturity-interest/
Tool: FD Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/)

Quick answer: FD maturity is worked out as P × (1 + r ÷ n)^(n × t), where n is the number of compounding periods a year. ₹1 lakh at 7% for 5 years, compounded quarterly as most Indian banks do, matures to about ₹1,41,478. BISCS India's free FD Calculator shows maturity, interest earned and effective yield for any tenure.

A fixed deposit (FD) calculator works out how much you will receive at maturity when you lock in a sum at a fixed interest rate. Banks in India usually compound FD interest every quarter, so the formula is **A = P × (1 + r ÷ 4)^(4 × t)**, with r as the annual rate in decimal and t in years.

₹1,00,000 at 7% for 5 years, compounded quarterly, matures to about ₹1,41,478, so you earn ₹41,478 in interest. The free [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/) on BISCS India does this for any amount, tenure and compounding frequency, and shows the year-by-year growth.

## How is FD interest calculated?

Each quarter, the bank adds a quarter of the annual rate to your balance, and the next quarter's interest is calculated on that higher balance. For the example above:

- Quarterly rate: 7% ÷ 4 = 1.75%
- Number of quarters: 5 × 4 = 20
- Maturity: 1,00,000 × (1.0175)^20 ≈ ₹1,41,478

Compounding frequency makes a modest difference over five years:

| Compounding | Maturity on ₹1 lakh at 7% for 5 years | Interest |
|---|---|---|
| Yearly | ₹1,40,255 | ₹40,255 |
| Quarterly | ₹1,41,478 | ₹41,478 |
| Monthly | ₹1,41,763 | ₹41,763 |

The tool also shows the **effective yield**, which turns compounding into a single annual figure. At 7% compounded quarterly, that is about 7.19% a year.

## How to use the BISCS FD Calculator

1. Open the [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/).
2. Enter the **deposit amount** (the slider runs from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore, and you can type any value).
3. Set the **interest rate** offered by your bank for your tenure.
4. Enter the tenure in **years, months and days**. For a 444-day special FD, for example, type 1 year, 0 months and 79 days.
5. Choose the **compounding frequency**: monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly. Leave it on quarterly unless your bank says otherwise.
6. Read the maturity amount, total interest and effective yield, and check the year-wise table for opening balance, interest and closing balance each year.

Your numbers stay in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

## Example: comparing two FD offers

Ramesh, a retired teacher in Chennai, has ₹2 lakh to deposit for one year. Bank A offers 7.25% compounded quarterly. Bank B advertises 7.40% but pays simple interest at maturity for one-year deposits.

- Bank A: about ₹2,14,899 at maturity (₹14,899 interest)
- Bank B: 2,00,000 × 7.40% = ₹14,800 interest

The higher headline rate is not automatically better once compounding is considered, although the gap here is small. Over longer tenures, compounding matters more. Always compare the maturity amount, not just the rate. (Bank names here are illustrative.)

## How FD interest is taxed

FD interest is taxable at your income tax slab rate in the year it accrues, even if you choose a cumulative FD and receive everything at maturity. Banks deduct TDS once the interest you earn from them in a financial year crosses a threshold, currently ₹50,000 for most people and ₹1 lakh for senior citizens, generally at 10% if your PAN is on record.

TDS is not the final tax. If your slab rate is higher, you pay the difference when filing your return; if your total income is below the taxable limit, you can submit Form 15G (or 15H for seniors) to avoid deduction. To see how FD interest affects your overall tax, add it as "other income" in the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/).

## Common FD mistakes

1. **Comparing rates without the compounding basis.** Ask whether the rate is compounded quarterly or paid as simple interest.
2. **Forgetting post-tax returns.** For someone in the 30% slab, a 7% FD yields only about 4.8% after tax and cess.
3. **Breaking an FD early without checking the penalty.** Premature withdrawal usually means a lower rate and a penalty, which can wipe out much of the interest.
4. **Ignoring inflation.** If inflation is close to your FD rate, your real return after tax may be near zero or negative.
5. **Putting everything in one bank above the insurance limit.** DICGC cover is ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

## Tips for getting more from fixed deposits

- **Ladder your deposits.** Instead of one ₹5 lakh FD for five years, split it into five FDs of ₹1 lakh maturing in years one to five. Something always matures soon, so you rarely need to break an FD early, and you can reinvest at whatever rates are on offer then.
- **Check senior citizen rates.** Many banks pay senior citizens an extra margin on FDs. If a parent is above 60, an FD in their name may earn more, though the interest is then their income for tax purposes.
- **Match the tenure to the need.** Some banks have special tenures, such as 400 or 444 days, with slightly higher rates. Use the days field in the calculator to compare them with a standard one-year FD.
- **Use a nominee.** Adding a nominee makes it much easier for your family to claim the deposit if something happens to you.
- **Keep TDS in view.** If you expect interest above the TDS threshold at one bank, spreading deposits does not change your tax, but it can change when tax is deducted. Plan your advance tax and return accordingly.

## FD, RD or something else?

If you have a lump sum, an FD is the natural fit. If you want to save a fixed amount every month, the [RD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rd-calculator/) shows how a recurring deposit grows with quarterly compounding. And to see compounding over longer periods or with regular top-ups, the [Compound Interest](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/) calculator gives more flexibility.

## Limits of this calculator

The tool computes a cumulative (reinvestment) FD. For monthly or quarterly payout FDs, interest is paid out rather than compounded, so your maturity value is just the principal. It also treats part-years using the same compounding formula, while banks may apply simple interest to a final broken quarter or to short deposits. Expect small differences from your bank's figure.

Treat this as an estimate and general information, not financial or tax advice. Your bank's deposit advice is the binding document, and RBI and Income Tax Department rules on TDS and insurance can change, so confirm current limits on their official websites.

Q: Do banks compound FD interest quarterly?
A: Most Indian banks compound cumulative fixed deposits quarterly, which is why the calculator defaults to quarterly. Very short deposits are often paid simple interest at maturity instead. The exact method is in your bank's deposit terms, so check them if you need the figure to the rupee.

Q: What is the difference between the FD rate and the effective yield?
A: The FD rate is the nominal annual rate. The effective yield includes the effect of compounding within the year. At 7% compounded quarterly, the effective yield is about 7.19% a year. Banks sometimes advertise this annualised yield alongside the card rate.

Q: Is TDS deducted on fixed deposit interest?
A: Banks deduct TDS when your total interest from that bank in a financial year crosses the threshold, currently ₹50,000 for most depositors and ₹1 lakh for senior citizens. The rate is generally 10% if your PAN is linked. If your income is below the taxable limit, you can submit Form 15G or 15H to the bank.

Q: Is FD interest tax-free?
A: No. FD interest is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate, whether or not TDS was deducted. Only specific products, such as five-year tax-saver FDs under Section 80C in the old regime, offer a deduction on the deposit, and even then the interest is taxable.

Q: Is my fixed deposit insured?
A: Deposits in banks covered by DICGC are insured up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, including principal and interest, at the time of writing. Amounts above that are not covered by the insurance. Corporate deposits and NBFC deposits are not covered by DICGC.

## How to Fill a PDF Form Online for Free and Flatten It

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/fill-pdf-form-online-free/
Tool: Fill PDF Form (https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/)

Quick answer: To fill a PDF form, open a form filler, type into the text fields, tick checkboxes, choose radio and dropdown options, optionally flatten the form so values become permanent, and download. BISCS India’s Fill PDF Form works in your browser without uploading. Forms without interactive fields can be filled with the PDF editor instead.

To fill a PDF form for free, open [Fill PDF Form](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/), choose your PDF, type into the text fields, tick the checkboxes and pick options from radio buttons and dropdowns, then download. Tick **Flatten** if you want the answers fixed permanently on the page.

The form is filled in your browser and never uploaded, which matters when it asks for your PAN, Aadhaar number, bank details or salary.

## Fillable form or flat PDF?

PDF forms come in two kinds, and knowing which you have saves time.

| | Fillable (interactive) form | Flat PDF |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | The PDF contains real form fields (AcroForm) | Just a picture or layout of a form |
| How to spot it | Clicking in a box in a PDF reader lets you type | Clicking does nothing; you can only print |
| Best tool | Fill PDF Form | [Edit PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-editor/) (add text and ticks anywhere) |

When you open a flat PDF in the form filler, it tells you no fillable fields were found and offers a link to the editor. Many bank, insurance and HR forms are fillable; many scanned government forms are flat.

## How to fill a PDF form step by step

1. Open [Fill PDF Form](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/) and choose your PDF.
2. The tool lists every field it finds, with a count of fields. Field names are tidied up to be readable.
3. Fill in the text fields. Multi-line fields accept longer answers.
4. Tick checkboxes and choose options for radio buttons and dropdowns.
5. Fields marked **read-only** are locked by the form's author and cannot be changed.
6. Decide whether to **Flatten** the form (see below).
7. Download the filled PDF and open it to check every answer.

## To flatten or not to flatten?

Flattening "prints" your answers onto the page, removing the interactive fields.

**Flatten when:**

- You are submitting the final version and want nobody (including you, by accident) to change the answers.
- The recipient may open the file in a viewer that displays form fields badly, such as some mobile apps.
- You are going to merge, compress or convert the form, because some of those steps remove form fields.

**Do not flatten when:**

- You may need to edit the answers later.
- The organisation asks for the form to stay fillable, for example so their system can read the field values.

A sensible habit: keep an unflattened copy for yourself and send the flattened one.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Typing in Indian scripts or using ₹.** The standard PDF fonts cannot display them, and they turn into "?". Use English and write "Rs. 25,000" instead of "₹25,000".
- **Overflowing text boxes.** Long answers in a small single-line field can be cut off or shrunk. Abbreviate sensibly or use an attached sheet if the form allows it.
- **Forgetting the signature.** Interactive signature fields are digital-signature fields and are skipped here. For a signature image, open the filled form in [Sign PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sign-pdf/) afterwards.
- **Flattening too early.** If you notice a mistake after flattening, you have to start again from the original form.
- **Compressing a fillable form with image-based levels.** Strong and Extreme compression remove form fields. Flatten first, or use the Basic level.

## Example: a reimbursement claim form

Sunita works for a company in Gurugram that uses a fillable PDF for medical reimbursement claims. She opens the form in the filler and sees 24 fields: employee code, name, department, a date of treatment, the hospital name, amounts, a dropdown for relationship of the patient, and checkboxes for attached documents. She fills everything in, writing amounts as "Rs. 4,350", ticks the boxes for bills and prescription, and flattens the form.

Then she opens the flattened PDF in Sign PDF, adds her signature image and the date, and finally merges the form with her scanned bills using [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/). HR receives one tidy file, and the answers cannot be accidentally changed in transit.

## Government and office forms

Fillable forms are common in HR onboarding packs, bank account updates, insurance claims and some government and tax-related downloads. Requirements vary: some offices want a printed and hand-signed copy, some accept a signed PDF by email, and online portals often have their own web forms instead of PDFs. Follow the instructions given with the form, and when a document must be signed with a Digital Signature Certificate, use the appropriate DSC software for that step.

| Field type | What you can do |
|---|---|
| Text field (single or multi-line) | Type names, addresses, amounts, dates |
| Checkbox | Tick or untick |
| Radio group | Choose one option, such as Male / Female / Other |
| Dropdown and list | Pick from the options the form provides |

If the tool reports that some fields could not be updated, the form may use an unusual structure. In that case, check those fields in the downloaded PDF and, if needed, add the missing answers with Edit PDF.

## Dates, amounts and formatting tips

Forms rarely validate what you type in this tool, so be consistent. Use the date format the form shows (DD/MM/YYYY is most common in India), write amounts with "Rs." and Indian digit grouping if the form expects it (for example Rs. 1,25,000), and match capital letters if the form says "IN BLOCK LETTERS".

## Checklist before you submit

- Every mandatory field filled, including dates and codes.
- Checkboxes and radio options double-checked.
- No "?" characters where you typed special symbols.
- Signature added where required, in the format the recipient accepts.
- Flattened copy for sending, unflattened copy saved for yourself.

## Privacy

Forms collect precisely the information you should be careful with: identity numbers, bank accounts, addresses, health details. Here, the form is read and filled by a PDF library running in your browser, and the completed file is saved straight to your device. Nothing is uploaded or kept anywhere else, and closing the tab clears everything.

Q: How do I know if my PDF form is fillable?
A: Open it in the form filler. If it has interactive fields, they appear as a list of inputs with the field count shown. If the tool says no fillable form fields were found, the PDF is a flat document, and you can type on it using the Edit PDF tool instead.

Q: What does flattening a PDF form mean?
A: Flattening prints the field values onto the page so they become part of the document and can no longer be edited. It is useful for final submissions, so nobody can change your answers, and it makes the form look the same in every PDF reader.

Q: Can I sign a PDF form with this tool?
A: Signature fields in a PDF form need a digital signature and are skipped here. To add a drawn, typed or uploaded signature image, fill the form first, then open the result in Sign PDF and place your signature on the signature line.

Q: Why do some characters appear as question marks?
A: Form values are drawn with a standard PDF font that covers English and Western characters. Hindi, other Indian scripts and the rupee symbol are not supported, so they become question marks, and the tool tells you how many were replaced. Write Rs. instead of the rupee sign.

Q: Can I edit the form again later?
A: Yes, if you do not flatten it. The downloaded PDF keeps its interactive fields with your values filled in, so you can open it again and change answers. Once flattened, the values are fixed, so keep an unflattened copy if you may need to edit.

## Find and Replace Text Online, With Optional Regex Support

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/find-and-replace-text-online-regex/
Tool: Find and Replace (https://biscsindia.com/tools/find-and-replace/)

Quick answer: To find and replace text online, paste your text, type the word to find and its replacement, preview the highlighted matches and click Replace all. BISCS India’s Find and Replace tool adds match case, whole-word and regular expression options with capture groups, plus undo, all running in your browser.
