Find and replace lets you change every occurrence of a word or phrase in one go. Type what to find, type what to replace it with, check the highlighted matches, and click **Replace all**. It is the fastest way to fix a misspelt name, update a price throughout a document, or reformat data copied from somewhere else.

Word processors have this built in, but an online tool is handy when your text lives somewhere else: a WhatsApp export, a CSV file, code, an email draft or a website's content.

## How to find and replace text online

1. Open [Find and Replace](https://biscsindia.com/tools/find-and-replace/).
2. Paste your text into the **Text** box on the left.
3. Type the word or phrase in **Find**. Matches are highlighted on the right, and a badge shows how many there are.
4. Type the new text in **Replace with**. Leave it empty if you want to delete the matches.
5. Switch the preview from **Matches** to **Result** to see exactly how the text will look.
6. Click **Replace all**. If something looks wrong, click **Undo**.
7. **Copy result** or **Download** the final text.

The preview updates as you type, so you can refine the search before changing anything.

## What do the three options do?

| Option | What it changes | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Match case | Only matches the exact capitals you typed | "GST" will not match "gst" |
| Whole words only | Ignores matches inside longer words | "rate" will not match "corporate" |
| Regular expression | Treats Find as a pattern, not plain text | `\d{10}` matches any 10-digit number |

By default the search ignores case and matches anywhere, which is what you want most of the time. Whole words is the option people forget, and it prevents embarrassing results like replacing "Ram" and accidentally changing "Ramesh" and "program".

## Everyday examples

**Correcting a name throughout a document.** A contract mentions "Mr. Sharma" 40 times but should say "Mr. Verma". Find "Sharma", replace with "Verma", tick Whole words, and check the preview.

**Updating a city or branch.** Moving an office from Mumbai to Pune? Paste the brochure text and replace every "Mumbai" in seconds. Watch for addresses that should stay unchanged.

**Removing a repeated phrase.** Text copied from a PDF often includes "Page 3 of 12" lines. With regex on, find `Page \d+ of \d+` and leave the replacement empty.

**Cleaning phone numbers.** Remove "+91 " from a contact list by finding "+91 " and replacing with nothing. Then use [Remove Duplicate Lines](https://biscsindia.com/tools/remove-duplicate-lines/) to drop repeats.

**Changing separators.** Turn a comma-separated list into one item per line: with regex on, find `,\s*` and replace with `\n`.

## Using regular expressions: a gentle introduction

Regex is a mini-language for describing text patterns. You do not need to master it, but a few patterns go a long way.

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `\d` | Any digit 0–9 |
| `\d{6}` | Exactly six digits, such as a PIN code |
| `\s+` | One or more spaces, tabs or line breaks |
| `[A-Z]{5}\d{4}[A-Z]` | Text shaped like a PAN number |
| `^` and `$` | Start and end of a line |
| `(…)` | A group you can reuse in the replacement |

In the **Replace with** box, regex mode understands:

- `$1`, `$2` and so on for the first, second captured group;
- `$<name>` for a named group;
- `$&` for the whole match;
- `\n` for a new line and `\t` for a tab.

### Example: reformatting dates

Suppose your text has dates like 15/03/2025 and you need 2025-03-15 for a spreadsheet import.

- Find: `(\d{2})/(\d{2})/(\d{4})`
- Replace with: `$3-$2-$1`

Each group captures one part of the date, and the replacement puts them back in a new order. Check the **Result** preview before applying.

If you want to build and test more complex patterns step by step, the [Regex Tester](https://biscsindia.com/tools/regex-tester/) shows every match and group in detail.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Replacing inside other words.** Searching "in" and replacing with "IN" changes "India", "invoice" and "begin". Use Whole words only.
- **Forgetting special characters in regex.** A full stop in regex means "any character", so `Rs.` also matches "Rs5" or "Rsx". Write `Rs\.` to match the dot itself, or turn regex off.
- **Not checking the count.** If you expected 5 matches and the badge says 37, stop and look before replacing.
- **Replacing over and over.** Running "Replace all" twice with a replacement that contains the search word, for example "Ltd" to "Ltd.", can double things up. Use the preview and Undo.
- **Working on the only copy.** For important files, keep the original text safe until you have checked the result.

## Tips for larger documents

- Replacing in a Word or PDF file? Copy the text out, replace here, and paste it back. For PDFs, extract text first with [PDF to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-text/).
- The match badge counts up to 10,000 matches, which covers almost any real document.
- To compare the original and replaced versions line by line, paste both into [Text Compare](https://biscsindia.com/tools/text-diff/).
- Use the **Matches** view with alternating highlight colours to spot neighbouring matches that run together.

## Online tool or your word processor?

Microsoft Word (Ctrl + H), Google Docs and most code editors have their own find and replace. If your text is already in one of them and you only need a plain word swap, use it there.

An online tool earns its place in a few situations:

- **On a phone.** Mobile apps often hide replace options or lack them entirely. Here you paste, replace and copy in a few taps.
- **Text without a home.** A WhatsApp chat export, a list copied from a website or an email draft is quicker to fix here than in a new document.
- **Regex without setup.** Google Docs supports regular expressions, but Word uses its own wildcard system. This tool uses standard JavaScript regex, the same syntax you will find in most tutorials.
- **Seeing everything first.** The live highlight and match count let you check every hit before anything changes.

## Is it safe for confidential text?

Yes. [Find and Replace](https://biscsindia.com/tools/find-and-replace/) runs in your browser, and the text you paste is not uploaded to or stored by BISCS India. That makes it suitable for contracts, salary sheets and customer lists. The undo history exists only while the page is open, and closing the tab clears everything.

Q: How do I replace a word only when it appears on its own?
A: Tick Whole words only. Then searching for art will match art but not part, start or article. The check understands letters in Hindi and other scripts too, so a whole-word search for a Hindi word will not match it inside a longer word.

Q: How do I delete every match instead of replacing it?
A: Leave the Replace with box empty and click Replace all. Every match is removed from the text. This is a quick way to strip a repeated footer line, a prefix such as +91, or a symbol you do not want.

Q: What is a regular expression and do I need one?
A: A regular expression, or regex, is a pattern language for matching text by shape rather than exact words, for example any 10-digit number. Most everyday jobs only need plain text replacement. Turn on regex when you need patterns, such as reformatting dates or removing all numbers.

Q: Can I undo a Replace all?
A: Yes. Click Undo above the text box to restore the version before the replacement. The tool keeps several earlier versions while the page is open, so you can try a replacement, check it and step back if it went wrong.

Q: Why does my regex show an error?
A: The pattern has a syntax problem, such as an unclosed bracket or a stray special character like a plus or question mark. The error message explains what went wrong. To search for those characters literally, put a backslash in front of them, or switch regex off and search as plain text.

## What Is GEO? How to Write Content AI Answer Engines Cite

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/generative-engine-optimization-content-checklist/
Tool: GEO Content Analyzer (https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/)

Quick answer: Generative engine optimisation (GEO) is the practice of making content easy for AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews to understand, trust and cite in their answers. BISCS India’s free GEO Content Analyzer scores an article on fifteen research-informed checks, from direct answers to sources and statistics, and lists the top fixes.

Generative engine optimisation, usually shortened to GEO, is the practice of shaping your content so that AI systems can understand it, trust it and cite it when they generate answers. When someone asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity or Google's AI Overviews a question, the answer is assembled from sources. GEO is about making your page one of those sources.

The [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/) from BISCS India checks an article against fifteen practical signals drawn from published GEO research and long-standing content good practice, and gives you a score with a prioritised list of fixes. It is a checklist, not a promise: no tool can guarantee citations.

## Why GEO matters now

More searches end with an AI-written summary rather than a list of blue links. For a business, that changes the question from "do we rank?" to "are we the source the answer is built from, and are we named or linked?"

The good news is that GEO is not a separate discipline that replaces SEO. A page that AI systems like to cite is usually one that people like to read: it answers the question quickly, explains clearly, shows evidence and is kept up to date. GEO simply puts more emphasis on making each passage easy to lift and quote accurately.

## What does the research say?

The term was popularised by a 2023 academic paper, "GEO: Generative Engine Optimization", by researchers from institutions including Princeton University and IIT Delhi. They tested different ways of rewriting web content and measured how visible each version became in AI-generated answers.

In broad terms, the methods that helped most were:

- **Citing sources**: adding references to credible sources.
- **Adding quotations** from relevant, named people or bodies.
- **Adding statistics**: specific, concrete numbers instead of vague claims.
- **Improving fluency and readability.**

Keyword stuffing, by contrast, did not perform well. The study used its own test set and AI setups, so treat it as useful direction rather than a formula; real-world AI systems change frequently.

## What the GEO Content Analyzer checks

| Check | Why it helps AI answers |
|---|---|
| Direct answer in the first 80 words | AI systems often lift a crisp, self-contained answer from the opening |
| Question-style subheadings | They match how people phrase queries |
| Lists or tables | Structured blocks are easy to extract and quote |
| Statistics and specific numbers | Concrete figures (₹, %, years) are quotable facts |
| Sources and citations | Attribution signals reliability |
| Quotations | Named expert or official statements add authority |
| Clear entities | Naming products, places and organisations removes ambiguity |
| Freshness | Recent years and an update date matter for time-sensitive topics |
| Short paragraphs and sentences | Each idea can stand alone as an answer |
| Readability (Flesch score) | Plain language is easier to summarise correctly |
| Depth (word count) | Thorough coverage answers follow-up questions |
| FAQ section | Real question-and-answer pairs match conversational queries |
| Author and expertise signals | Shows who wrote it and why they are qualified |
| Jargon density | Unexplained acronyms and long words reduce clarity |

Each check is weighted, and the score shows full credit for a pass and half for a warning.

## How to analyse your content

1. Open the [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/). Press **Sample** to see an example report.
2. Paste your article as plain text, Markdown or full HTML. For HTML, the tool removes navigation, forms and footers and focuses on the main article.
3. Enter the **Main topic or keyword**, such as "GST registration". This lets the tool check that your opening and headings actually name the subject.
4. Read the overall score, the verdict and the **Top fixes** list.
5. Look at the **Opening paragraph** panel. It highlights the definition sentence, figures and named entities, and marks where the first 80 words end.
6. Switch the checks list to **Issues only** and work through failures first.
7. Edit your draft and paste it again to see the improvement.

Your text is analysed in your browser and never sent to a server or an AI service.

## How to write content that AI systems quote

**Answer first, explain second.** Start with one or two sentences that answer the main question and name the subject. "GST registration is mandatory for most businesses whose annual turnover crosses the threshold set for their state and type of supply" is quotable. "In this article, we will explore..." is not.

**Make every section self-contained.** AI systems often pull a single passage. If a paragraph begins with "It also..." the quote makes no sense on its own. Name the subject again.

**Back claims with evidence.** Cite the official source by name, for example the CBIC or the Income Tax Department, and link to it. Add real figures with dates. Never invent statistics to look authoritative; inaccurate numbers damage trust far more than missing ones.

**Show who is behind the content.** A byline, a short author bio with relevant credentials, and "reviewed by" for financial, legal or health topics all help. The [Entity & Author Schema Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/) can add matching structured data.

**Keep it current.** Show a "last updated" date and refresh rates, fees and rules when they change.

## Common GEO mistakes

- **Long, story-style introductions** before the actual answer.
- **Vague claims** such as "many people" or "huge savings" without figures.
- **Walls of text** with no headings, lists or tables.
- **Undefined jargon**, like using "ITC" without ever writing "input tax credit".
- **Anonymous content** on topics where expertise matters.
- **Blocking AI search crawlers** in robots.txt while hoping to be cited. Check your settings with the [AI Crawler Access Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ai-crawler-checker/).

## Where GEO fits in your workflow

Use the analyzer on your most important guides and service pages before publishing, and on older pages that get impressions but little traffic. To polish individual answers for featured snippets and voice search, use the [AEO Answer Optimizer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/aeo-answer-optimizer/). To find the questions your audience actually asks, start with the [Question & Topic Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/question-generator/).

Good GEO is mostly good writing made explicit. Paste your next draft into the [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/) and fix the top three issues it finds.

Q: What is the difference between GEO and SEO?
A: SEO aims to rank pages in traditional search results. GEO aims to have your content selected, summarised and cited inside AI-generated answers. They overlap heavily: crawlable, helpful, well-structured and trustworthy pages serve both. GEO places extra weight on quotable passages, clear facts and cited sources.

Q: Can any tool guarantee my page will be cited by ChatGPT or Google AI Overviews?
A: No. AI systems decide what to cite using their own retrieval and ranking methods, which are not public and change often. A GEO score is a checklist of good practices drawn from research and content guidelines, not a prediction or promise of citations.

Q: What did the GEO research actually find?
A: A 2023 academic paper titled GEO: Generative Engine Optimization tested ways of rewriting content and measured visibility in AI-generated answers. Adding citations to sources, quotations from relevant people and statistics were among the most effective methods, while traditional keyword stuffing performed poorly.

Q: Do I need to write differently for AI answer engines?
A: Mostly you need to write more clearly. Answer the main question early, use descriptive headings, keep paragraphs focused, name people, places and products explicitly, support claims with sources and numbers, and keep information current. These habits also help human readers.

Q: Is my article uploaded when I analyse it?
A: No. The text or HTML you paste is analysed in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server or an AI service, so you can safely check unpublished drafts and client work.

## Gratuity Calculator: The 15/26 Formula, Eligibility and Tax

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/gratuity-calculation-formula-india/
Tool: Gratuity Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/gratuity-calculator/)

Quick answer: For employees covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act, gratuity = 15 × last drawn monthly basic plus DA × years of service ÷ 26, with a final part-year of six months or more counted as a full year. ₹60,000 a month for 10 years 7 months gives about ₹3.81 lakh. BISCS India's free Gratuity Calculator also shows the tax-exempt part.

Gratuity is a lump sum an employer pays when you leave after long service, as a thank-you for the years you worked there. If your employer is covered by the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the formula is:

**Gratuity = 15 × last drawn monthly (basic + DA) × years of service ÷ 26**

A final part-year of six months or more counts as a full year. So someone earning ₹60,000 a month in basic plus DA who leaves after 10 years and 7 months is credited with 11 years, and their gratuity is about ₹3,80,769. The free [Gratuity Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gratuity-calculator/) does this sum and shows how much is tax-exempt.

## Why 15 and 26?

The Act grants **15 days' wages for every completed year** of service. It treats a month as **26 working days**. So one year's gratuity equals 15 ÷ 26 of a month's basic plus DA, about 57.7% of it.

If your employer is not covered by the Act, gratuity is often calculated with half a month's salary per completed year, based on a 30-day month (15 ÷ 30), and part-years are ignored. That gives a lower figure, as the examples below show.

## How to use the BISCS Gratuity Calculator

1. Open the [Gratuity Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gratuity-calculator/).
2. Enter your **last drawn monthly salary (basic + DA)**. Do not use gross or CTC.
3. Enter your **years of service** and any **additional months** (0 to 11).
4. Choose whether your employer is **covered under the Gratuity Act**. Most establishments with ten or more employees are.
5. Read the gratuity payable, the number of years counted, and the tax-exempt and taxable parts. The exact formula used is printed under the result so you can check it.

The tool reminds you if your service is under five years, and runs entirely in your browser.

## Worked examples

| Situation | Years counted | Calculation | Gratuity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Covered, ₹60,000, 10 years 7 months | 11 | 15 × 60,000 × 11 ÷ 26 | ₹3,80,769 |
| Covered, ₹60,000, 10 years 5 months | 10 | 15 × 60,000 × 10 ÷ 26 | ₹3,46,154 |
| Not covered, ₹60,000, 10 years 7 months | 10 | 15 × 60,000 × 10 ÷ 30 | ₹3,00,000 |
| Covered, ₹1,50,000, 25 years | 25 | 15 × 1,50,000 × 25 ÷ 26 | ₹21,63,462 |

The first two rows show why timing matters. Leaving at 10 years 7 months instead of 10 years 5 months adds a full year, about ₹34,600 here. If you are close to a six-month mark, it may be worth knowing before you hand in your notice.

For a feel of the scale, here is gratuity after exactly 20 years of service with a covered employer at different levels of basic plus DA: ₹30,000 gives about ₹3,46,154; ₹50,000 gives about ₹5,76,923; and ₹1,00,000 gives about ₹11,53,846. Gratuity rises in direct proportion to both salary and years, so a pay rise late in your career lifts the whole amount, because the last drawn salary is used for every year of service.

## Who is eligible for gratuity?

- You must normally complete **five years of continuous service** with the same employer.
- The five-year condition does not apply on **death or disablement**; gratuity is then paid to you or your nominee.
- Some court rulings have treated **four years and 240 days** as five years, especially where the employer works a six-day week, but this is not automatic.
- The Act applies to factories, mines, plantations, shops and establishments with **ten or more employees** on any day in the previous twelve months.

The Code on Social Security, 2020 consolidates the Gratuity Act with other labour laws and brings changes such as gratuity for fixed-term employees after one year. Check how its provisions apply to your job on the Ministry of Labour and Employment's website.

## How is gratuity taxed?

For private-sector employees, gratuity is tax-free up to **₹20 lakh** across their whole career, and the calculator applies this limit. Anything above it is taxed as salary income in the year you receive it. Gratuity received by **central and state government employees is fully exempt**.

In the last example in the table, ₹20 lakh is exempt and about ₹1,63,462 would be taxable. Note too that the Act caps the gratuity an employer is legally required to pay at ₹20 lakh, although some employers pay more under their own schemes. To see how a taxable portion affects your overall tax, try the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/).

## Common gratuity mistakes

1. **Using CTC or gross salary.** Only basic plus DA counts. A ₹1 lakh gross salary might have only ₹40,000 basic.
2. **Rounding up every part-year.** Only six months or more rounds up, and only for covered employers.
3. **Forgetting the nominee form.** Keep your gratuity nomination up to date so your family can claim without delay.
4. **Assuming gratuity is in your PF.** It is a separate benefit, paid by the employer.
5. **Not following up.** The employer must pay within a set time after it becomes payable; delays can attract interest under the Act.

## Tips before you resign or retire

- Check your appointment letter and HR policy to see whether your employer follows the Act or a more generous scheme.
- Look at your last few [salary slips](https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/) to confirm basic and DA.
- Plan what to do with the lump sum. The [Lumpsum Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/lumpsum-calculator/) shows how it might grow if invested.

## A word of caution

This calculator follows the standard statutory formula and the ₹20 lakh tax exemption, but it does not know your employer's policy, any disputes over continuity of service, or how labour-code changes apply to your role. Treat the result as an estimate and general information, not legal or tax advice. For an exact figure, ask your HR or payroll team for their calculation, and check tax treatment with the Income Tax Department or a qualified professional.

Q: Is gratuity paid if I resign before 5 years?
A: Normally gratuity becomes payable only after five years of continuous service, except on death or disablement, where the five-year condition does not apply. Some court rulings have treated four years and 240 working days as meeting the requirement. Changes under the newer labour codes may also affect certain categories, so check your case.

Q: Why is the formula divided by 26?
A: The Act treats a month as 26 working days, excluding four Sundays. Fifteen days' wages are therefore 15 ÷ 26 of a monthly salary. For employers not covered by the Act, a 30-day month is commonly used, which gives a smaller amount, and only completed years are counted.

Q: Which salary is used to calculate gratuity?
A: The last drawn monthly basic salary plus dearness allowance. Other allowances such as HRA, special allowance, bonus and overtime are not included. If your basic is a small share of your total pay, your gratuity will be correspondingly lower than a calculation on gross salary would suggest.

Q: How much gratuity is tax-free?
A: For private-sector employees, gratuity is exempt up to ₹20 lakh over their working life, subject to the formula limits under the Income-tax law. Any excess is taxed as salary. Gratuity received by central and state government employees is fully exempt. Check the current limit with the Income Tax Department before planning around it.

Q: Does the employer pay gratuity or is it deducted from my salary?
A: Gratuity is a benefit paid by the employer and is not deducted from your salary. Some companies show it as part of cost to company (CTC), which is why your gross salary is lower than CTC. Many employers fund it through a group gratuity policy with an insurer.

## How to Convert a Colour PDF to Black and White (Grayscale)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/convert-pdf-to-black-and-white/
Tool: Grayscale PDF (https://biscsindia.com/tools/grayscale-pdf/)

Quick answer: To convert a PDF to black and white, open a grayscale converter, choose a resolution such as 150 DPI and an image quality, then convert and download. BISCS India’s Grayscale PDF previews pages in grey before you start and runs in your browser, so your document is never uploaded. Text becomes non-selectable.

To convert a colour PDF to black and white, open [Grayscale PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/grayscale-pdf/), choose a resolution (150 DPI suits most uses) and an image quality, then convert and download. The page thumbnails already preview in grey, so you can see the result before you start.

The conversion runs entirely in your browser, so the document is never uploaded. One trade-off to know: each page becomes a grayscale image, so the text is no longer selectable or searchable.

## Why convert a PDF to grayscale?

There are practical reasons beyond saving colour ink:

- **Cheaper printing.** Print shops and office printers often charge more for colour pages. A grayscale file makes sure no page is accidentally printed in colour.
- **Portal or office requirements.** Some forms and submission instructions ask for black-and-white copies. Requirements vary, so check the specific instructions.
- **Consistent look.** A bundle of documents from different sources (blue bank statements, red-stamped certificates, green tax forms) looks uniform in grayscale.
- **Better readability of some scans.** Yellowed paper and colour casts from phone photos often look cleaner in grey.
- **Smaller files for colourful scans.** Colour photos of documents carry a lot of data; grayscale images usually need less.

## How to convert a PDF to grayscale step by step

1. Open [Grayscale PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/grayscale-pdf/) and choose your PDF.
2. Look at the page grid; thumbnails are shown in grayscale as a preview.
3. Choose the **Resolution (DPI)**: 100, 150, 200 or 300.
4. Set the **Image quality** slider (the default is 80%).
5. Read the notice: pages will become images and text will not be selectable.
6. Convert and download. The result screen shows the page count and the original size so you can compare.

## Choosing resolution and quality

| Document type | Resolution | Quality | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typed letters, forms, statements | 150 DPI | 75–80% | Clear text, moderate size |
| Small print, legal fine print, tables | 200–300 DPI | 80–90% | Keeps small characters sharp |
| Photo-heavy brochures | 150 DPI | 70–80% | Photos look fine, file stays reasonable |
| Quick draft for internal reading | 100 DPI | 70% | Smallest file, check legibility |

Higher DPI and quality give sharper pages and larger files. If the result is too big, try 150 DPI before reducing quality heavily.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Converting the only copy.** Grayscale is a one-way trip for practical purposes, and text becomes an image. Always keep the colour original.
- **Converting before filling forms.** Fillable form fields are flattened into the image. Fill the form first with [Fill PDF Form](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/), then convert.
- **Using grayscale where colour carries meaning.** Charts with colour-coded lines, maps and medical images can become hard to read. Check the preview carefully.
- **Expecting a smaller file every time.** Text-only digital PDFs can get bigger, because vector text is replaced by pictures of text. Compare sizes on the result screen.
- **Choosing a low DPI for small print.** At 100 DPI, footnotes and fine print can blur. Zoom in on the result before submitting.

## Grayscale vs compress: which one do you need?

Both tools redraw pages as images, so they overlap. The difference is the goal:

- Use **Grayscale PDF** when colour must go, for printing or a black-and-white requirement.
- Use [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) when you only need a smaller file and colour is fine. Its Basic level keeps text selectable, which grayscale cannot do.

If you need both (a black-and-white file under a size limit), convert to grayscale at 150 DPI first; the result is often small enough. If not, try a lower DPI or quality rather than running a second image-based compression on top.

## Example: printing a 200-page study pack

A coaching institute in Patna wants to print a 200-page colour PDF of study material for 60 students. Printing in colour would be costly, and the colour adds little to the text-heavy content. The administrator converts the PDF to grayscale at 150 DPI and 80% quality, checks a few pages with diagrams to make sure labels are readable, and sends the grayscale file to the print shop. Because the file contains no colour at all, there is no risk of any page being billed as colour.

## Tips for the best result

- Faint pencil marks, light stamps and pale signatures may become lighter in grey. If they matter, raise the DPI and quality and check those pages.
- Coloured highlights turn into grey bands. They usually remain visible, but very light yellow can almost disappear.
- For documents photographed on a phone, a proper scan with [Scan to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/) and its Gray or B&W filter often gives a cleaner page than converting a colour photo afterwards.

## Checklist before you print or submit

- Zoom in on the smallest text in the grayscale file and confirm it is crisp.
- Check pages with signatures, seals and stamps; they should still be clearly visible.
- Look at charts and diagrams to make sure lines that relied on colour are still distinguishable.
- Compare the new file size with the original if a portal limit applies.
- Keep the colour original saved separately for future edits.

## What about documents that must stay searchable?

If someone needs to search or copy text from the final document, grayscale conversion is not ideal, because the output is image-based. In that case, print the colour PDF using your printer's "grayscale" or "black and white" setting instead, which saves ink without changing the file. Use Grayscale PDF when the file itself must be black and white, for example when you hand it over to a print shop or submit it somewhere.

## Privacy and performance

Each page is rendered and converted to grey using your browser's own graphics engine, then reassembled into a new PDF on your device. Nothing is uploaded. Long documents at 300 DPI are processed page by page with a progress bar, and they take noticeably longer on a phone than on a computer, so for big files a laptop is the comfortable choice.

Q: Will the text still be selectable after converting to grayscale?
A: No. Each page is redrawn as a grayscale image, so text can no longer be selected, copied or searched, and links stop working. Keep your original colour PDF as the master copy and use the grayscale version for printing or submission.

Q: Which resolution should I choose?
A: 150 DPI suits most printing and on-screen reading. Choose 300 DPI if the document has very small print, fine lines or detailed drawings. Lower settings such as 100 DPI make smaller files but can blur small text, so check the result.

Q: Does grayscale make a PDF smaller?
A: Often, especially for colourful scans and photo-heavy documents. But because pages become images, a text-only PDF can grow larger. Compare the size shown on the result screen with the original, and keep whichever suits your needs.

Q: Is grayscale the same as pure black and white?
A: Not quite. Grayscale keeps shades of grey, so photos, stamps and logos still show detail. Pure black and white uses only two tones. For printing on an office laser printer, grayscale usually looks better and keeps faint signatures and seals visible.

## How to Calculate GST: Add or Remove GST with CGST/SGST Split

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/gst-calculator-add-remove-gst/
Tool: GST Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/)

Quick answer: To add GST, multiply the net price by the rate and add the result: ₹10,000 at 18% becomes ₹11,800. To remove GST from an inclusive price, divide by (1 + rate ÷ 100): ₹11,800 ÷ 1.18 = ₹10,000. BISCS India's free GST Calculator does both and shows the CGST/SGST or IGST split.

GST is calculated as a percentage of the taxable value of a sale. If a price excludes GST, multiply it by the rate and add that amount on top. If a price already includes GST, divide it by (1 + rate ÷ 100) to get the value before tax, then subtract to find the GST inside it.

For a sale within one state, the tax is split equally into CGST and SGST. For a sale from one state to another, the whole amount is charged as IGST. The free [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/) on BISCS India does all of this as you type and shows the same amount at every common rate.

## What is the formula to add GST to a price?

When you quote a price "plus GST", the arithmetic is simple:

- **GST amount** = net price × rate ÷ 100
- **Total** = net price + GST amount

**Example:** A Pune-based designer bills a client in Pune ₹10,000 for a logo, at 18%.

- GST = 10,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = ₹1,800
- Total = ₹11,800
- Split: CGST 9% = ₹900, SGST 9% = ₹900

If the same client were in Bengaluru, the designer would charge IGST of ₹1,800 instead of the CGST/SGST pair. The total stays ₹11,800.

## How do you remove GST from an inclusive amount?

Retail prices, restaurant menus and many online listings already include GST. To find the taxable value, divide rather than subtract a percentage:

- **Net price** = inclusive total ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100)
- **GST included** = inclusive total − net price

**Example:** A box of stationery costs ₹5,250 including 5% GST.

- Net price = 5,250 ÷ 1.05 = ₹5,000
- GST included = ₹250 (₹125 CGST + ₹125 SGST)

The most common error is taking 18% of the total and subtracting it. On ₹11,800 that gives 11,800 − 2,124 = ₹9,676, which is wrong by more than ₹300, because the 18% was originally calculated on ₹10,000, not on ₹11,800.

## How to use the BISCS GST Calculator

1. Open the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/).
2. Choose **Add GST (exclusive)** if your amount is before tax, or **Remove GST (inclusive)** if it already contains tax.
3. Type the amount in rupees. Commas are fine, and the field reformats when you leave it.
4. Pick a rate: 0.25%, 3%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% or 40%, or choose **Custom** and enter any rate up to 100%.
5. Select **Within state** for a CGST + SGST split or **Inter-state** for IGST.
6. Read the result card for the net amount, GST, the split and the total. Scroll down to the table to see the same amount worked out at every listed rate side by side.

Everything is calculated in your browser. The figures you enter are not sent anywhere, so you can check client invoices or supplier bills without sharing them.

## Which GST rate should you use?

The rate depends on the goods or services and is set by the GST Council through notifications. With effect from 22 September 2025, the structure was rationalised (often called "GST 2.0"): most goods and services now sit in the 5% and 18% slabs, and a 40% rate applies to certain luxury and sin goods. Special rates continue for a few categories, such as 3% on gold and jewellery and 0.25% on rough diamonds.

The calculator still offers 12% and 28% because older invoices, credit notes for earlier periods and some exceptions may need them. Treat the rate list as a convenience, not a ruling. Before you bill, look up your product's HSN or service's SAC code with the [HSN & SAC Code Finder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hsn-code-finder/) and confirm the current rate on the CBIC GST rate pages.

| Situation | Tax charged | Example on ₹10,000 at 18% |
|---|---|---|
| Seller and buyer in the same state | CGST + SGST, half each | ₹900 + ₹900 |
| Seller in a Union Territory without legislature, buyer in the same UT | CGST + UTGST | ₹900 + ₹900 |
| Seller and buyer in different states | IGST, full rate | ₹1,800 |
| Imports | IGST (plus customs duty) | ₹1,800 on the assessable value |

## When is a GST calculator most useful?

- **Quoting prices.** Freelancers and small businesses can check that "₹40,000 + GST" means ₹47,200 to the client at 18%.
- **Checking bills.** Restaurant, hotel and electronics bills sometimes mix inclusive and exclusive prices. Reverse calculation shows how much tax you actually paid.
- **Setting MRP.** If you want a shelf price of ₹999 inclusive of 5% GST, the taxable value is 999 ÷ 1.05 = ₹951.43, which helps you plan margins.
- **Reconciling purchases.** Before you claim input tax credit, a quick check of each supplier invoice can catch arithmetic slips.

## Common mistakes to avoid

1. **Subtracting the rate from an inclusive total.** Always divide by 1.18, 1.05 and so on.
2. **Charging CGST/SGST on an inter-state sale.** The place of supply decides the tax type. Charging the wrong one can mean paying the right tax again under the correct head and then claiming a refund of the wrong one.
3. **Splitting IGST.** IGST is never split; it is the full rate under one head.
4. **Using an outdated rate.** Rates for many items changed in September 2025. Copying a rate from an old invoice is risky.
5. **Ignoring rounding on high-volume billing.** Round each invoice consistently. Tiny paisa differences add up across thousands of bills.
6. **Applying GST before a trade discount.** If the discount is on the invoice, deduct it first. The [Discount Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) can add GST after stacked discounts.

## Tips for small businesses and freelancers

Keep the calculator open in a tab while drafting quotes, and when you are ready to bill, move the figures into the free [Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/). For B2B invoices, validate your customer's GST number first with the [GSTIN Validator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/) so the tax lands in the right place in their records.

If you sell both within your state and outside it, keep a separate column for IGST in your sales register. It makes GSTR-1 preparation and the GSTR-3B summary much easier at month end.

## A note on accuracy

This calculator does the arithmetic correctly for any rate you enter, but it cannot tell you which rate or tax type legally applies to your supply. Classification, exemptions, reverse charge and place-of-supply rules can be subtle. This guide is general information, not tax advice. For anything beyond routine billing, check the GST portal and CBIC notifications, or ask a chartered accountant or GST practitioner who knows your business.

Q: How do I calculate GST backwards from the total amount?
A: Divide the GST-inclusive total by 1 plus the rate as a decimal. For 18% GST, divide by 1.18; for 5%, divide by 1.05. The answer is the taxable value, and the difference between the total and that value is the GST included in the price.

Q: Is CGST plus SGST the same as IGST?
A: In amount, yes. On an intra-state sale at 18%, you charge 9% CGST and 9% SGST, which together equal the 18% IGST you would charge on an inter-state sale. What differs is who receives the tax and how input tax credit is set off.

Q: Which GST rates are used after the September 2025 changes?
A: From 22 September 2025, GST rates were rationalised so that most goods and services fall in 5% or 18%, with 40% for certain luxury and sin goods. Special rates such as 3% for gold remain. Rates for specific items change by notification, so confirm the current rate on the CBIC website.

Q: Should GST be calculated on the discounted price or the MRP?
A: Generally GST is charged on the transaction value, so a discount shown on the invoice at the time of sale reduces the taxable value before GST is added. Post-sale discounts follow separate conditions. If you are unsure how a particular scheme is treated, check with a GST practitioner.

Q: Why does my bill show GST to the paisa but the calculator rounds?
A: The calculator shows amounts to two decimal places, which matches paisa-level billing. Businesses often round the final invoice total to the nearest rupee and show a small round-off line. That rounding is an accounting choice and does not change the tax rate applied.

## GST Return Due Dates: GSTR-1, GSTR-3B, CMP-08 and Annual Returns

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/gst-return-due-dates-calendar/
Tool: GST Due Date Calendar (https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-due-date-calendar/)

Quick answer: Monthly GST filers file GSTR-1 by the 11th and GSTR-3B by the 20th of the following month. QRMP filers file quarterly GSTR-1 by the 13th and GSTR-3B by the 22nd or 24th, depending on their state. BISCS India's free GST Due Date Calendar builds your yearly schedule and exports it as calendar reminders.

For a regular GST taxpayer who files monthly, the two key deadlines are **GSTR-1 by the 11th** and **GSTR-3B by the 20th** of the following month. Under the quarterly QRMP scheme, GSTR-1 is due by the **13th** of the month after the quarter, and GSTR-3B by the **22nd or 24th**, depending on your state. Composition taxpayers pay through **CMP-08 by the 18th** after each quarter and file **GSTR-4 by 30 April** after the year.

These are the standard dates. The government frequently extends them by notification, so always confirm on the GST portal. The free [GST Due Date Calendar](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-due-date-calendar/) builds your full-year schedule from these rules and lets you download it as calendar reminders.

## GST due dates at a glance

| Return or payment | Who files | Standard due date |
|---|---|---|
| GSTR-1 (monthly) | Regular taxpayers filing monthly | 11th of the next month |
| GSTR-3B (monthly) | Regular taxpayers filing monthly | 20th of the next month |
| IFF (optional) | QRMP taxpayers, months 1 and 2 of a quarter | 13th of the next month |
| PMT-06 | QRMP taxpayers, months 1 and 2 of a quarter | 25th of the next month |
| GSTR-1 (quarterly) | QRMP taxpayers | 13th of the month after the quarter |
| GSTR-3B (quarterly) | QRMP taxpayers | 22nd (Category I) or 24th (Category II) |
| CMP-08 | Composition taxpayers | 18th of the month after the quarter |
| GSTR-4 | Composition taxpayers | 30 April after the financial year |
| GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C | Regular taxpayers, subject to turnover thresholds | 31 December after the financial year |
| GSTR-7 / GSTR-8 | TDS deductors / e-commerce operators collecting TCS | 10th of the next month |
| ITC-04 | Principals sending goods for job work | 25 April (annual), or 25 October and 25 April (half-yearly, turnover above ₹5 crore) |

## How to use the BISCS GST Due Date Calendar

1. Open the [GST Due Date Calendar](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-due-date-calendar/).
2. Choose the **financial year**. The current one is selected by default.
3. Pick your **filing type**: Monthly, QRMP (quarterly) or Composition.
4. If you chose QRMP, select your **state or UT of registration** so the right GSTR-3B date (22nd or 24th) is used, and decide whether to show IFF dates.
5. Tick any extras that apply: **GSTR-9/9C**, **GSTR-7** if you deduct GST TDS, **GSTR-8** if you are an e-commerce operator, and **ITC-04** if you send goods for job work.
6. Review the next due date, the count of dates in the next 30 days, and the month-by-month timeline. Dates within a week are highlighted and passed dates are marked.
7. Click **Download .ics** to add every date to Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar, with an optional reminder two days before. Or click **Copy list** to paste the schedule into an email or WhatsApp message to your accountant.

The calendar is built in your browser from built-in rules. It makes no network requests and nothing about your business is sent anywhere.

## Example: a QRMP trader in West Bengal

Sourav runs a hardware shop in Howrah with turnover well under ₹5 crore and files under QRMP. For October to December 2026, his schedule looks like this:

- 13 November 2026: IFF for October (optional, for B2B invoices)
- 25 November 2026: PMT-06 tax payment for October
- 13 December 2026: IFF for November (optional)
- 25 December 2026: PMT-06 tax payment for November
- 13 January 2027: GSTR-1 for the quarter
- 24 January 2027: GSTR-3B for the quarter (West Bengal is in Category II)

His cousin in Kochi, also on QRMP, has the same dates except GSTR-3B, which is due on 22 January 2027 because Kerala is in Category I. Both also see 31 December 2026 as the standard date for the FY 2025-26 annual return, if it applies to them.

## Which filing type applies to you?

- **Monthly:** the default for regular taxpayers, and compulsory if your aggregate turnover is above ₹5 crore.
- **QRMP:** an option for taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore. Returns are quarterly, but tax is still paid monthly through PMT-06.
- **Composition:** a simpler scheme for eligible small businesses that pay tax at a fixed rate on turnover and cannot claim input tax credit.

If you are unsure which applies, your registration details on the GST portal show your status.

## Tips to never miss a GST deadline

1. **Import the .ics file at the start of each financial year**, and again if you change filing type.
2. **Keep the two-day reminder** so you have time to reconcile purchases and collect invoices.
3. **File GSTR-1 on time even if GSTR-3B is later.** Your B2B customers rely on it for their input tax credit.
4. **Validate customer GSTINs** in your sales data before filing with the [GSTIN Validator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/).
5. **Use consistent HSN or SAC codes** on invoices; the [HSN & SAC Code Finder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hsn-code-finder/) helps.
6. **Check for extensions** on the GST portal's news and updates section a few days before each date.

## Common mistakes

- Treating QRMP as "pay quarterly". Tax for the first two months is still due by the 25th through PMT-06.
- Using the 22nd when your state is in Category II, or vice versa.
- Assuming a date that falls on a Sunday moves automatically. It does not unless notified.
- Forgetting GSTR-7 or GSTR-8 obligations if you deduct TDS or run an e-commerce platform.
- Leaving the annual return to the last week of December, when the portal is busiest.

For working out the tax itself, the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/) adds or removes GST at any rate.

## Important caution

The calendar reflects standard due dates under the regular GST rules as built into the tool. It does not track notifications, state-specific relief, holiday shifts or changes made after the tool was last updated. This article is general information, not legal or tax advice. Always confirm current deadlines, late fees and interest on the official GST portal (gst.gov.in) and CBIC notifications, and work with a GST practitioner if you are unsure about your obligations.

Q: Why is my quarterly GSTR-3B due on the 22nd and my friend's on the 24th?
A: Under QRMP, states and Union Territories are split into two groups to spread the load on the GST system. Category I, which includes Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana among others, files by the 22nd. Category II, which includes Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal among others, files by the 24th.

Q: Does the calendar include government extensions?
A: No. It shows the standard due dates under the regular GST rules. The government often extends deadlines through notifications, and dates falling on a Sunday or holiday are not shifted automatically. Always check the GST portal for any extension before relying on a date.

Q: Is filing GSTR-9 compulsory for small businesses?
A: The calendar notes that GSTR-9 is optional where aggregate turnover is up to ₹2 crore, and that the reconciliation statement GSTR-9C applies where turnover exceeds ₹5 crore. These thresholds are set by notification and have been revised before, so confirm the current position for the year you are filing.

Q: How do I add GST due dates to my phone's calendar?
A: Click Download .ics, then open the file on your phone or import it into Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar. Each due date becomes an all-day event, with an optional reminder two days before. The file is generated in your browser and contains only the dates and descriptions.

Q: What happens if I miss a GST due date?
A: Late filing usually attracts a late fee for each day of delay, and late payment of tax attracts interest. Missing returns can also block your customers' input tax credit and, over time, lead to notices or restrictions on your registration. Check the current late fee and interest rules on the GST portal or with your practitioner.

## How to Check a GSTIN: Format, Checksum and State Code Explained

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/gstin-validator-check-gst-number/
Tool: GSTIN Validator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/)

Quick answer: A valid GSTIN has 15 characters: a two-digit state code, the holder's 10-character PAN, an entity number, the letter Z and a check character calculated from the first 14. BISCS India's free GSTIN Validator checks all of this in your browser, singly or in bulk, but only the GST portal can confirm a registration is active.

To check a GST number (GSTIN), confirm it has exactly 15 characters in the right pattern and that its last character matches the official checksum. A correct GSTIN has a two-digit state code, the holder's 10-character PAN, an entity number, the letter Z and a check character. If any part is wrong, the number is either mistyped or not a real GSTIN.

The free [GSTIN Validator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/) on BISCS India runs all these checks instantly and tells you the state, the PAN and the type of holder. To confirm the business is actually registered and active, you still need the official GST portal.

## What does each part of a GSTIN mean?

Take the sample number the tool loads, **27AAPFU0939F1ZV**:

| Position | Characters | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | 27 | State/UT code: Maharashtra |
| 3–12 | AAPFU0939F | PAN of the business or person |
| 4th character of the PAN | F | Holder type: firm or LLP |
| 13 | 1 | Entity number: first registration under this PAN in the state |
| 14 | Z | Default letter for regular registrations |
| 15 | V | Check character calculated from the first 14 |

Because the PAN sits inside the GSTIN, you can see at a glance whether the number belongs to an individual (P), a company (C), a firm or LLP (F), a trust (T), an HUF (H) and so on.

## Common GST state codes

The first two digits tell you where the registration belongs. A few frequently seen codes:

| Code | State/UT | Code | State/UT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 07 | Delhi | 27 | Maharashtra |
| 09 | Uttar Pradesh | 29 | Karnataka |
| 10 | Bihar | 32 | Kerala |
| 19 | West Bengal | 33 | Tamil Nadu |
| 21 | Odisha | 36 | Telangana |
| 24 | Gujarat | 37 | Andhra Pradesh |

A few codes have history behind them. Andhra Pradesh registrations now use 37, while 28 was its code before Telangana was formed. Code 26 covers the merged Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, with 25 being the older Daman and Diu code. Ladakh uses 38, 97 is "Other Territory" and 99 is the Centre jurisdiction code. The validator names all of these, so if a supplier says they are in Gujarat but their GSTIN starts with 27, you will spot the mismatch straight away.

## How does the checksum catch typos?

The 15th character is not random. It is calculated from the first 14 using a mod-36 method: each character is turned into a number from 0 to 35, alternate positions are weighted, the results are summed in a specific way, and the remainder decides the check character.

The practical effect is that most single-character typos and many swapped characters produce a different check character. If someone types 27AAPFU0939F1ZX instead of 27AAPFU0939F1ZV, the validator reports a checksum mismatch and tells you that "V" was expected. That is often enough to catch an error before it reaches your GST return.

## How to use the BISCS GSTIN Validator

1. Open the [GSTIN Validator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/).
2. Stay on **Single GSTIN** and type or paste the number. Spaces and hyphens are ignored, and lower case is converted to capitals.
3. Read the result: valid or invalid, with the state, PAN, holder type and entity number.
4. Check the list of individual tests (length, characters, state code, PAN pattern, holder type, entity number, 14th character and checksum) to see exactly what failed.
5. For many numbers, switch to **Bulk check**, paste up to 5,000 GSTINs, filter to valid or invalid, and click **Export CSV** to save the results.

Everything runs locally in your browser with no network requests, so your customer and supplier lists stay on your device.

## When should you validate a GSTIN?

- **Before raising a B2B invoice.** A wrong GSTIN means your customer may not see the invoice correctly in their records and may not be able to claim input tax credit.
- **When onboarding a vendor.** Catch typos in vendor master data early.
- **Before filing GSTR-1.** Bulk-check your customer list to reduce errors in reported B2B supplies.
- **When cleaning a spreadsheet.** Paste a whole column, export the CSV and fix the invalid rows.

Once the number checks out, you can use it in the free [Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/) and work out tax with the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/).

## Format check vs portal verification

| Question | Format validator | GST portal search |
|---|---|---|
| Is the number correctly formed? | Yes | Yes |
| Is there a typo? | Usually detected by checksum | Shows "not found" |
| Is the registration active, cancelled or suspended? | No | Yes |
| What is the legal and trade name? | No | Yes |
| Works offline, in bulk, privately | Yes | No |

Use both: the validator for speed and bulk cleaning, and the portal's Search Taxpayer page for status and name.

## Common mistakes with GST numbers

1. **Confusing O and 0, or I and 1.** The checksum usually catches these.
2. **Using a GSTIN from the wrong state.** A business registered in several states has a different GSTIN in each; match it to the place of supply.
3. **Assuming the 14th character is always Z.** It is Z for regular registrations; a few special registration types follow different patterns and may be flagged.
4. **Relying on format alone for large transactions.** Always confirm status on the portal.
5. **Copying from a scanned invoice without checking.** OCR often misreads characters; validate after copying.

The PAN inside a GSTIN can also be checked separately with the [PAN & IFSC Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pan-ifsc-validator/).

## Important limits

The validator checks structure and the checksum only. It cannot see GST network data, so a correctly formed number might still have been cancelled, suspended or never issued. This guide is general information, not legal or tax advice. Before relying on a counterparty's registration, verify it on the official GST portal (gst.gov.in), and consult a GST practitioner if a mismatch affects your returns or input tax credit.

Q: Does a valid format mean the GST number is genuine?
A: No. A format and checksum check confirms the number is correctly built and free of typos. It cannot tell you whether the registration was actually issued, is active, or has been cancelled or suspended. For that, use the Search Taxpayer facility on the official GST portal, which shows the legal name and status.

Q: How can I find the state from a GST number?
A: The first two digits are the state or Union Territory code. For example, 27 is Maharashtra, 19 is West Bengal, 29 is Karnataka and 07 is Delhi. The validator shows the state name for every code, including older codes and special codes such as 97 for Other Territory.

Q: What does the 13th character in a GSTIN mean?
A: It shows how many registrations the same PAN holds in that state. A business's first registration in a state usually has 1, the second 2, and after 9 the letters A to Z are used. Zero is never used. A company with branches in one state under separate registrations will see different 13th characters.

Q: Can I check many GST numbers at once?
A: Yes. Switch to Bulk check and paste up to 5,000 GSTINs, one per line or separated by commas, semicolons or tabs. You can filter to valid or invalid entries, spot duplicates and export the results with reasons as a CSV file to open in Excel or Google Sheets.

Q: Is it safe to paste my customers' GSTINs into the tool?
A: The validator runs entirely in your browser using built-in rules. The numbers you paste are not uploaded or stored on a server. GSTINs are also not secret, as they appear on every tax invoice, but keeping customer lists on your own device is still good practice.

## MD5 and SHA-256 Hash Generator: Verify Files and Text

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/md5-sha256-hash-generator-checksum/
Tool: Hash Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/hash-generator/)

Quick answer: A hash generator turns text or a file into a fixed-length fingerprint, such as a 64-character SHA-256 value, that changes completely if even one byte changes. Use it to verify downloads or compare files. BISCS India's Hash Generator computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, plus HMACs, on your device without uploading anything.

A hash function turns any input, whether a word, a document or a 4 GB video, into a short fixed-length string called a hash, digest or checksum. The same input always gives the same hash. Change a single character and the hash changes completely.

That makes hashes ideal for one job above all: checking that two things are identical without comparing them byte by byte. The [Hash Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hash-generator/) on BISCS India calculates MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 for text or files, all at once, on your own device.

## What does a hash look like?

Here is the SHA-256 hash of the word `hello`, and of `Hello` with a capital H:

```text
hello  -> 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824
Hello  -> 185f8db32271fe25f561a6fc938b2e264306ec304eda518007d1764826381969
```

One letter changed, and there is no visible relationship between the two outputs. This "avalanche effect" is exactly what you want from a fingerprint.

Different algorithms produce different lengths:

| Algorithm | Output (hex characters) | Status for security |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MD5 | 32 | Broken; fine only for accidental-corruption checks |
| SHA-1 | 40 | Broken for collisions; avoid for new work |
| SHA-256 | 64 | Secure; the common default |
| SHA-384 | 96 | Secure |
| SHA-512 | 128 | Secure; can be faster on 64-bit machines |

## What are hashes used for?

- **Verifying downloads.** Software publishers list a SHA-256 checksum next to the download. If your file’s hash matches, it arrived intact and unmodified.
- **Detecting duplicate files.** Two photos or PDFs with the same SHA-256 are, for practical purposes, the same file, even if their names differ.
- **Checking a backup or copy.** Hash a large file before and after copying it to a pen drive or cloud folder to be sure nothing was corrupted.
- **Webhook and API signatures.** Payment gateways and many SaaS platforms sign webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256 so your server can prove the request is genuine.
- **Cache keys and content addressing.** Build tools often name files after the hash of their contents, so a changed file gets a new name automatically.

## How to generate a hash with BISCS India

1. Open the [Hash Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hash-generator/).
2. Choose **Text** or **File** as the input source.
3. For text, type or paste into the box. For a file, choose it or drag it in. Files up to 1 GB can be hashed, and they are read on your device, not uploaded.
4. All five hashes, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, appear together. Tick **Uppercase** if the value you are comparing against uses capital letters.
5. To verify a download, paste the publisher’s checksum into **Compare with a hash**. The matching row is highlighted, so you do not need to compare 64 characters by eye.
6. To create an HMAC instead of a plain hash, enter a value in **HMAC secret key**.
7. Copy whichever value you need.

The SHA family uses your browser’s built-in Web Crypto API, which is only available on secure (HTTPS) pages. MD5 is not part of Web Crypto, so the tool includes its own implementation.

## Why MD5 and SHA-1 are not for security

This is the point most often misunderstood. MD5 and SHA-1 still work as checksums: random corruption on a disk or network will not accidentally produce a matching hash. But both are **cryptographically broken**. Researchers can deliberately construct two different files that share an MD5 hash, and practical SHA-1 collisions have been demonstrated publicly.

That means:

- Do not rely on MD5 or SHA-1 to prove that a file has not been tampered with by someone malicious.
- Do not use them for digital signatures or certificates.
- **Never** use them, or even plain SHA-256, to store passwords.

## Hashing is not how you store passwords

A fast hash is the wrong tool for passwords precisely because it is fast. A modern graphics card can test billions of MD5 or SHA-256 guesses per second, and lists of leaked passwords make common choices trivial to find. An unsalted MD5 of a weak password can often be looked up in seconds.

Password storage needs algorithms built to be slow and salted: **Argon2id**, **bcrypt** or **scrypt**. Use the implementation your framework provides. If you are generating passwords for users, the [Password Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/) creates strong random ones, and the [Password Strength Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/) estimates how hard a password is to guess.

## Verifying a checksum: a worked example

Say you downloaded an installer, and the publisher’s site lists:

```text
SHA256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
```

Choose the file in the tool, paste that value into **Compare with a hash**, and look for the highlighted match. If no row matches, do not run the file. Download it again from the official source, and if it still does not match, report it.

On the command line, the equivalent checks are:

```text
certutil -hashfile installer.exe SHA256      (Windows)
shasum -a 256 installer.dmg                  (macOS)
sha256sum installer.deb                      (Linux)
```

## Testing a webhook HMAC

Many payment and messaging providers sign each webhook with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret from your dashboard. When your signature check fails, it helps to calculate the expected value by hand. Paste the exact raw request body into the text box, enter the secret in **HMAC secret key**, and compare the HMAC-SHA256 output with the signature header.

Mismatches are almost always caused by hashing a re-formatted body instead of the raw bytes, extra whitespace or newlines, or comparing hex against Base64. Check your provider’s documentation for which encoding they use.

## Common mistakes

- **Invisible whitespace.** A trailing newline changes the hash entirely. Text copied from a terminal or editor often has one.
- **Line endings.** Windows files use CRLF, Linux and macOS use LF. The same-looking text gives different hashes.
- **Case confusion.** `ABC123…` and `abc123…` are the same hex value. Use the **Uppercase** toggle to match.
- **Comparing different algorithms.** A 64-character value is SHA-256; a 32-character one is MD5. They will never match each other.

## Privacy

Text and files are hashed locally in your browser. Even a 1 GB file never leaves your computer, which is important when you are checking confidential documents, database exports or private keys. If you also need to encode data for transport rather than fingerprint it, see [Base64 Encode / Decode](https://biscsindia.com/tools/base64-encoder/).

Q: Can a hash be reversed to get the original text?
A: No. Cryptographic hash functions are one-way by design. However, short or common inputs such as simple passwords can be found by looking them up in huge precomputed tables or by guessing quickly, especially with fast hashes like MD5 and SHA-1. That is why fast hashes must never be used to store passwords.

Q: Is MD5 still safe to use?
A: MD5 is broken for security purposes: researchers can deliberately create two different files with the same MD5 hash. It is still acceptable for spotting accidental corruption, such as checking a file copied correctly. For anything security-related, including verifying software downloads from untrusted mirrors, use SHA-256 or stronger.

Q: How should passwords be stored if not with SHA-256?
A: Use a slow, salted password hashing algorithm designed for the job, such as Argon2id, bcrypt or scrypt. These are intentionally expensive to compute, which makes large-scale guessing impractical. A plain SHA-256 of a password, even with a salt, can be tested billions of times per second on modern hardware.

Q: Why do I get a different hash for the same text in another tool?
A: Usually the inputs differ invisibly: a trailing newline, a space, Windows CRLF line endings instead of LF, or a different character encoding. This tool hashes the exact UTF-8 bytes of what is in the box. Also check whether the other tool shows uppercase hex, which is the same value written differently.

Q: What is an HMAC and when do I need one?
A: An HMAC is a hash combined with a secret key. Only someone who knows the key can produce the same value, so it proves a message was not tampered with and came from a key holder. Payment gateways and webhooks commonly sign requests with HMAC-SHA256, which you can test here.

## HRA Exemption Calculator: How Tax-Free HRA Is Worked Out

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/hra-exemption-calculation-rules/
Tool: HRA Exemption Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/)

Quick answer: Your HRA exemption is the lowest of three amounts: the HRA you actually receive, rent paid minus 10% of basic salary plus DA, and 50% of basic plus DA in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai (40% elsewhere). BISCS India's free HRA Exemption Calculator shows all three and the taxable balance. It applies only under the old tax regime.

The tax-free part of your House Rent Allowance (HRA) is the **lowest** of three amounts, all calculated for the year:

1. The actual HRA you received from your employer.
2. Rent paid minus 10% of your basic salary plus dearness allowance (DA).
3. 50% of basic plus DA if you live in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata or Chennai, or 40% in any other city.

Whatever HRA is left above that lowest figure is taxable. The exemption is available only under the old tax regime. The free [HRA Exemption Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/) works out all three limits and highlights the one that applies to you.

## Worked example: a renter in Kolkata

Arjun works in Kolkata. His basic salary plus DA is ₹50,000 a month, his employer pays ₹20,000 as HRA, and he pays ₹18,000 a month in rent.

| Condition (annual) | Calculation | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Actual HRA received | 20,000 × 12 | ₹2,40,000 |
| Rent minus 10% of basic + DA | 2,16,000 − 60,000 | ₹1,56,000 |
| 50% of basic + DA (metro) | 6,00,000 × 50% | ₹3,00,000 |

The lowest is ₹1,56,000, so that much of his HRA is exempt. The remaining ₹84,000 is added to his taxable salary. Monthly, that is ₹13,000 exempt and ₹7,000 taxable.

Notice that if Arjun lived in a non-metro city, the third limit would be ₹2,40,000, but his exemption would still be ₹1,56,000, because rent is the binding limit. In his case, paying more rent (genuinely) would raise the exemption; moving cities would not.

## A second example: when the city limit bites

Divya works in Pune with basic plus DA of ₹40,000 a month, HRA of ₹20,000 and rent of ₹25,000.

- Actual HRA: ₹2,40,000
- Rent minus 10% of basic: 3,00,000 − 48,000 = ₹2,52,000
- 40% of basic (non-metro): ₹1,92,000

Her exemption is ₹1,92,000 and ₹48,000 is taxable. Here the 40% city cap is the lowest figure, so higher rent would not increase her exemption.

## What if you moved house or city during the year?

The three limits are worked out for the period you actually paid rent, so a mid-year move means calculating each period separately and adding the results.

Suppose Farhan's basic plus DA is ₹50,000 a month and his HRA is ₹20,000 a month all year. From April to September he rents in Pune for ₹15,000 a month; from October to March he rents in Mumbai for ₹22,000 a month.

| Period (6 months) | Actual HRA | Rent − 10% of basic | City limit | Exempt |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr–Sep, Pune (40%) | ₹1,20,000 | 90,000 − 30,000 = ₹60,000 | ₹1,20,000 | ₹60,000 |
| Oct–Mar, Mumbai (50%) | ₹1,20,000 | 1,32,000 − 30,000 = ₹1,02,000 | ₹1,50,000 | ₹1,02,000 |

His total exemption is ₹1,62,000 and the remaining ₹78,000 of HRA is taxable. To do this with the calculator, enter each period's monthly figures, choose the right city type, and take half of the annual result for each six-month block. A salary change mid-year is handled the same way.

## How to use the BISCS HRA Calculator

1. Open the [HRA Exemption Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/).
2. Choose whether you will enter amounts **per month** or **per year**.
3. Enter **basic salary + DA**. Include DA only if it counts for retirement benefits, as per your salary terms.
4. Enter the **HRA received** and the **rent paid**.
5. Pick **Metro (50%)** or **Non-metro (40%)**.
6. Read the exempt HRA per year and per month, the taxable HRA, and the table showing all three conditions with the lowest one marked.

The tool flags two common situations: if rent is zero, the full HRA is taxable, and if annual rent crosses ₹1 lakh, you will need your landlord's PAN. Everything is calculated in your browser.

## What counts as basic salary for HRA?

"Salary" for this rule means basic pay plus DA where DA forms part of retirement benefits, plus any commission fixed as a percentage of turnover. It does not include HRA itself, special allowances, bonuses or perquisites. Check your salary slip; the [Salary Slip Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/) can help you see components laid out clearly if you are structuring pay for a small team.

## Documents checklist

- Rent receipts for each month, signed by the landlord. The [Rent Receipt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rent-receipt-generator/) creates them quickly.
- A rent agreement, especially for larger rents.
- Landlord's PAN if annual rent exceeds ₹1 lakh.
- Proof of payment, such as bank transfers or UPI records.
- Your employer's declaration form for exemptions and deductions, often Form 12BB.

Submit these to your employer on time so the exemption is reflected in monthly TDS. If you miss the employer's deadline, you can usually still claim the exemption when filing your income tax return, provided you have the proof.

## Common HRA mistakes

1. **Choosing the new regime and still expecting HRA relief.** It does not apply there.
2. **Including allowances in "basic".** Only basic plus qualifying DA counts.
3. **Assuming all large cities are metros.** For this rule, only four cities get the 50% limit.
4. **Claiming for months you did not pay rent.** Calculate for the actual period of renting; if you moved mid-year, work out each period separately.
5. **Cash rent without receipts.** It makes the claim hard to support.
6. **Living in your own house in the same city.** You cannot claim HRA for rent you do not actually pay.

## Should you even claim HRA?

HRA only helps under the old regime, so the real question is which regime gives lower tax overall. Put your exemption into the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/) along with your other deductions and compare. For many people with moderate rent and few other deductions, the new regime is still cheaper.

This guide explains the standard calculation for FY 2025-26 and is general information, not tax advice. Rules, including which cities count as metros, can change, and the Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from FY 2026-27. Check the Income Tax Department's website or speak to a tax professional, especially for unusual arrangements like paying rent to relatives.

Q: Can I claim HRA exemption under the new tax regime?
A: No. The HRA exemption is one of the benefits given up under the new regime. If you opt for the new regime, the whole HRA you receive is taxable as part of your salary. Compare both regimes using your actual exemption before choosing which one to use.

Q: Which cities count as metro for HRA?
A: For the 50% limit, the rules have long named only Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. Cities such as Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune have been treated as non-metro, with a 40% limit, for FY 2025-26. Check the rules in force for later years, as they can be revised.

Q: Do I need my landlord's PAN to claim HRA?
A: If the rent you pay is more than ₹1 lakh in a year, your employer will typically ask for the landlord's PAN. Below that, rent receipts or a rent agreement are usually enough. Keep proof of payment such as bank transfers, as these help if your claim is ever questioned.

Q: Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents?
A: Many salaried people do, provided the arrangement is genuine: you actually pay the rent, ideally by bank transfer, the parent owns the house, and the parent shows the rent as income in their own tax return. Paying rent to a spouse is generally viewed with suspicion. When in doubt, take professional advice.

Q: What if my employer does not pay HRA?
A: If you do not receive HRA but pay rent, you may be able to claim a deduction under Section 80GG in the old regime, subject to its own conditions and limits. This calculator covers HRA received from an employer only, so check the 80GG rules separately.

## Hreflang Tags Explained: Set Up Hindi, Bengali and English Pages

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/hreflang-tags-multilingual-website-guide/
Tool: Hreflang Tag Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/hreflang-generator/)

Quick answer: Hreflang tags tell search engines which language or regional version of a page to show each user, such as English, Hindi or Bengali. BISCS India’s free Hreflang Tag Generator creates the head link tags and matching XML sitemap entries for every version, adds an x-default fallback and checks codes, URLs and duplicates in your browser.

Hreflang tags are small lines of code that tell search engines, "this page also exists in these other languages, and here are the addresses." Google uses them to show each searcher the version that best matches their language and region, for example sending a Bengali-speaking user to your Bengali page rather than the English one.

The [Hreflang Tag Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hreflang-generator/) from BISCS India builds the tags for you. List every language version of a page, add an x-default fallback, and it produces both HTML head tags and XML sitemap entries, with checks for the mistakes that most often break hreflang.

## When do you need hreflang?

You need hreflang only when the **same page** exists in more than one language or regional version. Typical Indian examples:

- A government-services explainer site in English, Hindi and Bengali.
- An ed-tech platform with course pages in English, Tamil and Telugu.
- A business with separate pages for India (prices in ₹) and the UAE (prices in AED).
- A news or recipes site translating its articles into several Indian languages.

You do **not** need it for a single-language site, for pages that are merely similar, or for automatic browser translation.

## How hreflang codes work

Each version gets a code made of a language and, optionally, a region:

| Code | Meaning | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| `en` | English, any region | One English version for everyone |
| `en-IN` | English for India | Separate English pages for India and other countries |
| `hi` or `hi-IN` | Hindi | Hindi version of the page |
| `bn-IN` | Bengali for India | Bengali for Indian readers (Bangladesh would be `bn-BD`) |
| `ta`, `te`, `mr`, `gu`, `kn`, `ml` | Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam | Regional language versions |
| `x-default` | Fallback | Users who match none of the listed versions |

Languages use two-letter ISO 639-1 codes and regions use two-letter ISO 3166-1 country codes. A region on its own, such as `IN`, is not valid. The generator offers more than a dozen languages, including Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia, Assamese, Urdu and Nepali, combined with regions such as India, the US, the UK, the UAE, Singapore and neighbouring countries.

## How to generate hreflang tags

1. Open the [Hreflang Tag Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hreflang-generator/). An English, Hindi and Bengali example is pre-filled so you can see the format.
2. For each version of the page, choose the **language and region** from the dropdown and enter its full **URL**.
3. Use **Add version** for more languages and the bin icon to remove one. Include the page you are currently on as well.
4. Keep **Add x-default** ticked and enter the **x-default URL**, usually your main English page or a language-picker page.
5. Read the checks. The tool warns about relative URLs, invalid codes, duplicate codes, the same URL used for two languages, and sets with fewer than two versions.
6. Copy the **HTML head tags**, or copy the **XML sitemap entries** if you manage hreflang through your sitemap.
7. Place the same complete set on every version of the page.

Everything is generated in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

## Head tags or sitemap: which method?

Both methods are supported by Google; choose one and use it consistently.

**Head tags** suit small sites. Each language version carries the full set of `link rel="alternate"` lines in its `<head>`. They are easy to check by viewing the page source.

**Sitemap entries** suit larger sites with many pages and languages. Each URL in the sitemap lists all its alternates using `xhtml:link` elements. Remember to add the `xmlns:xhtml="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"` namespace to your `urlset`. You can create the base sitemap with the [XML Sitemap Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sitemap-generator/) and add the hreflang entries from this tool.

If you use both, they must say exactly the same thing.

## What a complete set looks like
