## What should your watermark say?

The text depends on why you are marking the image:

- **Photographers and artists:** your name or studio name, optionally with the © symbol and year, such as “© 2026 Ananya Sen Photography”. Your website or Instagram handle is even more useful, because people who like the photo can find you.
- **Online sellers and home businesses:** your shop name and the platform where you sell, for example “Kolkata Kantha Store, on Instagram”. This helps when resellers copy product photos to their own listings.
- **Drafts and previews:** a plain word such as “PREVIEW”, “DRAFT” or “SAMPLE” in a tiled pattern, so a client can judge the work but cannot use it before paying.
- **ID and document copies:** the purpose, the receiver and the date, as described above.

Keep it short. Two lines is the practical maximum; anything longer becomes hard to read and starts to look like a paragraph stamped across your image.

## Tips for professional-looking watermarks

### Match the colour to the background

White with a soft shadow is readable on almost any photo. On bright, white product backgrounds, a mid-grey works better than black, which can look heavy.

### Keep it small for portfolios

Viewers come to see the photograph, not the signature. A corner mark sized around 3–5% of the image is enough to carry your name without spoiling the shot.

### Use a consistent style

If you post regularly on Instagram or run an online store, use the same text, font, position and opacity on every image. It becomes part of your brand. A simple logo-style text such as your shop name and website works well; you can design a matching logo with the [Logo Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/logo-maker/).

### Place it where cropping hurts

A mark in the far corner is the easiest to crop. Placing it slightly inwards, or over part of the subject, means cropping it out would damage the picture.

## Common mistakes

- **Opacity at 100% for a large centred mark.** The photo becomes unusable for its real purpose.
- **Tiny text on a large photo.** It looks fine in the editor but disappears when the image is viewed on a phone. Zoom out and check.
- **Watermarking a document so heavily that the receiver cannot read it.** They will simply ask for another copy.
- **Forgetting the year or website changes.** Update the default text before you start a batch.
- **Watermarking the only copy.** Always keep your original unmarked photo safely stored; the tool saves a new file, so your original is untouched.

## Does the watermark tool upload my photos?

No. The preview and the final image are both drawn using your browser’s canvas, on your own phone or computer. That matters when the photo is an ID card, a client’s unreleased product or a personal picture. The downloaded file is rendered at the original dimensions, so you do not lose resolution.

Q: Does a watermark stop people from stealing my photos?
A: No watermark makes copying impossible. A small corner mark can be cropped out, and determined people can edit out even large marks. A watermark does make casual copying less attractive and keeps your name attached when photos are shared, which is the realistic goal.

Q: What opacity should a watermark be?
A: For a corner signature, around 50 to 70 percent is readable without dominating the picture. For a tiled pattern across sensitive documents, 15 to 30 percent keeps the content readable while making reuse obvious. Check the preview at the size people will actually see.

Q: Should I watermark copies of my Aadhaar or PAN card?
A: Many people add a line such as the purpose and date when sharing ID copies, so a copy is harder to reuse for something else. Use a tiled, semi-transparent mark that does not hide your details, since the receiver still needs to read them.

Q: Can I watermark many photos at once?
A: This tool works on one photo at a time so you can position the mark carefully for each picture. The settings stay the same while you work, so for a small set you can repeat the process quickly. For PDFs, Watermark PDF stamps every page in one go.

Q: Will watermarking reduce my photo quality?
A: The watermark is drawn onto the photo at its full original size, so resolution does not change. Saving as JPG applies normal compression; keep quality high or choose PNG if you want to avoid any loss.

## Income Tax Calculator FY 2025-26: New vs Old Regime Compared

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/income-tax-calculator-new-vs-old-regime/
Tool: Income Tax Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/)

Quick answer: For FY 2025-26, the new regime taxes income above ₹4 lakh in slabs from 5% to 30%, gives salaried people a ₹75,000 standard deduction and a Section 87A rebate that makes tax nil up to ₹12 lakh of taxable income. BISCS India's free Income Tax Calculator compares this with the old regime and your deductions side by side.

For FY 2025-26 (assessment year 2026-27), most salaried people in India pay less tax under the new regime unless they claim large deductions. The new regime has wider slabs, a ₹75,000 standard deduction and a Section 87A rebate that makes tax nil when taxable income is up to ₹12 lakh. In practice, a salary of up to ₹12.75 lakh with no other income pays no tax.

The old regime has higher rates but allows deductions such as HRA, 80C, 80D and home loan interest. Which one is better depends on your numbers. The free [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/) works out both and tells you which saves more.

## What are the tax slabs for FY 2025-26?

| Taxable income | New regime rate | Old regime rate (below 60) |
|---|---|---|
| Up to ₹2.5 lakh | Nil | Nil |
| ₹2.5 lakh – ₹4 lakh | Nil | 5% |
| ₹4 lakh – ₹5 lakh | 5% | 5% |
| ₹5 lakh – ₹8 lakh | 5% | 20% |
| ₹8 lakh – ₹10 lakh | 10% | 20% |
| ₹10 lakh – ₹12 lakh | 10% | 30% |
| ₹12 lakh – ₹16 lakh | 15% | 30% |
| ₹16 lakh – ₹20 lakh | 20% | 30% |
| ₹20 lakh – ₹24 lakh | 25% | 30% |
| Above ₹24 lakh | 30% | 30% |

Under the old regime, the nil band is ₹3 lakh for those aged 60 to 79 and ₹5 lakh for those 80 and above. The new regime slabs are the same for all ages.

Other key figures used by the calculator:

- **Standard deduction:** ₹75,000 (new) or ₹50,000 (old) for salaried people and pensioners.
- **Section 87A rebate:** up to ₹60,000 if new-regime taxable income is ₹12 lakh or less; up to ₹12,500 if old-regime taxable income is ₹5 lakh or less.
- **Cess:** 4% on tax plus surcharge.
- **Surcharge:** 10% above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore, 25% above ₹2 crore, and 37% above ₹5 crore in the old regime (capped at 25% in the new regime).

## How to use the BISCS Income Tax Calculator

1. Open the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/).
2. Choose your **age band**: below 60, 60 to 79, or 80 and above.
3. Enter your **gross salary or pension** for the year and any **other income** taxed at slab rates, such as FD interest or rent.
4. Keep **I am salaried / a pensioner** ticked to apply the standard deduction.
5. Fill in your **old regime deductions**: 80C, 80D, HRA exemption, home loan interest, NPS 80CCD(1B) and others. The tool caps each at its statutory limit.
6. Read which regime saves you money and by how much, then check the side-by-side table and the slab-wise breakup for each regime.

Your salary details are processed only in your browser.

## Worked examples

**1. Salary ₹12,75,000, no other income.** New regime: 12,75,000 − 75,000 = ₹12,00,000 taxable. Slab tax is ₹20,000 (4–8 lakh at 5%) + ₹40,000 (8–12 lakh at 10%) = ₹60,000. The 87A rebate cancels it: **tax nil**. Old regime with ₹1.5 lakh 80C and ₹25,000 80D: taxable ₹10,50,000, tax ₹1,27,500 + ₹5,100 cess = **₹1,32,600**.

**2. Salary ₹13,00,000.** New regime taxable income is ₹12,25,000. Slab tax is ₹63,750, but marginal relief caps it at the ₹25,000 earned above ₹12 lakh. With cess, **tax is ₹26,000**, not ₹66,300.

**3. Salary ₹18,00,000 with heavy deductions.** Suppose HRA exemption ₹2.4 lakh, home loan interest ₹2 lakh, 80C ₹1.5 lakh, 80D ₹50,000 and NPS ₹50,000.

- New regime: taxable ₹17,25,000, tax ₹1,45,000 + cess = **₹1,50,800**
- Old regime: taxable ₹10,60,000, tax ₹1,30,500 + cess = **₹1,35,720**

Here the old regime saves about ₹15,080. Drop the HRA, home loan and NPS, and the old regime tax rises to ₹2,96,400, so the new regime wins by a wide margin.

**4. A retired person aged 65.** Suppose a pension of ₹9,00,000 plus FD interest of ₹1,50,000, with health insurance of ₹50,000 under 80D and ₹50,000 of interest deduction under 80TTB entered as "other deductions".

- New regime: 10,50,000 − 75,000 = ₹9,75,000 taxable; slab tax ₹37,500 is fully covered by the 87A rebate, so **tax is nil**.
- Old regime (60 to 79 band, ₹3 lakh nil slab): taxable ₹9,00,000, tax ₹90,000 + ₹3,600 cess = **₹93,600**.

Even with the higher senior exemption, the new regime is far cheaper here, because the rebate covers taxable income up to ₹12 lakh.

## How do you decide between the regimes?

- Add up deductions you will **actually** claim with proof, not ones you might make.
- Your HRA exemption depends on rent, salary and city; work it out first in the [HRA Exemption Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/).
- Compulsory contributions such as employee PF already count towards 80C, while voluntary ones like [PPF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ppf-calculator/) top it up to the ₹1.5 lakh limit.
- Re-run the comparison each year, because your salary and deductions change.

## Common mistakes

1. **Assuming ₹12 lakh salary is the limit.** The ₹12 lakh figure is taxable income; salaried people get the ₹75,000 deduction first.
2. **Forgetting other income.** FD and savings interest are taxable and can push you over ₹12 lakh, triggering slab tax.
3. **Claiming old regime deductions under the new regime.** Most, including 80C, 80D and HRA, are not available.
4. **Ignoring cess.** Every rupee of tax carries 4% cess.
5. **Treating capital gains like salary.** Special-rate income is outside this calculator and has its own rules.

## What the calculator does not cover

The tool is built for resident individuals for FY 2025-26. It does not handle capital gains or other special-rate income, business income computations, employer NPS contributions, losses carried forward or marginal relief on surcharge. It also uses familiar section numbers from the Income-tax Act, 1961. The Income-tax Act, 2025 took effect from 1 April 2026 for later years, with new section numbering, so rules for FY 2026-27 onwards should be checked separately.

These results are estimates to help you plan and are not tax advice. Verify your figures on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal (incometax.gov.in), and speak to a chartered accountant if your situation is complex. Once your tax is planned, the [Salary Slip Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/) can help you lay out monthly pay components clearly.

Q: Is income up to ₹12.75 lakh tax-free under the new regime?
A: For a salaried resident individual with only salary income, yes in most cases. The ₹75,000 standard deduction brings ₹12.75 lakh down to ₹12 lakh of taxable income, and the Section 87A rebate of up to ₹60,000 cancels the slab tax. Special-rate income such as certain capital gains is treated differently, so check if you have any.

Q: What is marginal relief under the new regime?
A: If taxable income is just above ₹12 lakh, the rebate is lost, which could make tax jump sharply. Marginal relief caps the tax so that it does not exceed the income above ₹12 lakh. At ₹12.25 lakh taxable, slab tax is ₹63,750 but relief limits it to ₹25,000, plus 4% cess.

Q: When does the old regime save more tax?
A: The old regime tends to win when you have large deductions and exemptions, such as HRA, home loan interest, full 80C investments, health insurance and NPS. In one example in this guide, an ₹18 lakh salary with about ₹6.9 lakh of deductions pays about ₹15,000 less under the old regime.

Q: Can I switch between the new and old regime every year?
A: Salaried individuals without business income can generally choose the regime each year when filing their return. People with business or professional income face stricter rules on switching back. Your employer will also ask for your choice for TDS purposes. Check the current rules on the Income Tax Department website before deciding.

Q: Does the calculator include surcharge and cess?
A: Yes. It adds 4% health and education cess on all tax and applies surcharge at 10%, 15%, 25% or 37% above ₹50 lakh, ₹1 crore, ₹2 crore and ₹5 crore of taxable income, with the new regime capped at 25%. It does not apply marginal relief on surcharge, so very high incomes near a threshold may see a small difference.

## Inflation Calculator: Future Cost and Value of Money in India

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/inflation-calculator-future-cost-india/
Tool: Inflation Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/inflation-calculator/)

Quick answer: Inflation raises prices at a compound rate, so future cost = today's cost × (1 + inflation)^years. At 6% a year, something costing ₹1 lakh today will cost about ₹1.79 lakh in 10 years, and ₹1 lakh received then is worth about ₹55,800 in today's money. BISCS India's free Inflation Calculator works out both directions.

Inflation is the rise in prices over time, which means the same rupee buys less each year. To see what something will cost in future, use **future cost = today's cost × (1 + inflation rate)^years**. To see what a future amount is worth today, divide instead: **today's value = future amount ÷ (1 + inflation rate)^years**.

At 6% inflation, a ₹1,00,000 expense today will cost about ₹1,79,085 in 10 years. Looked at the other way, ₹1,00,000 received in 10 years will buy only what about ₹55,839 buys now. The free [Inflation Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/inflation-calculator/) on BISCS India shows both answers and a year-by-year table.

## How inflation compounds

Inflation works like compound interest in reverse for your savings. If prices rise 6% this year, next year's 6% is applied to the already-higher price. Over a decade, ₹1 lakh of spending grows like this at 6%:

- After 1 year: ₹1,06,000
- After 5 years: about ₹1,33,823
- After 10 years: about ₹1,79,085

That is a 79% rise in ten years, even though 6% a year sounds mild. Put another way, ₹1 lakh loses about 44.2% of its purchasing power over that decade.

## How to use the BISCS Inflation Calculator

1. Open the [Inflation Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/inflation-calculator/).
2. Choose **Future cost** to see what today's expense will cost later, or **Today's value** to see what a future sum is worth now.
3. Enter the amount: **cost today** or **amount in the future**, depending on the mode.
4. Set the **inflation rate** per year. The slider covers 1% to 15%.
5. Set the number of **years**.
6. Read the result with the growth multiple, purchasing power lost and a table showing the future cost and today's value of your amount for every year.

The calculator runs entirely in your browser and needs no sign-up.

## Planning examples

| Goal | Today's cost | Inflation assumed | Years | Future cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General household expense | ₹1,00,000 | 6% | 10 | ₹1,79,085 |
| Child's annual college fee | ₹2,00,000 | 8% | 15 | ₹6,34,434 |
| Monthly living costs at retirement | ₹50,000 | 6% | 25 | ₹2,14,594 |

The last row often surprises people. A couple in Bhubaneswar who live comfortably on ₹50,000 a month today may need over ₹2.1 lakh a month for the same lifestyle in 25 years, at 6% inflation. Retirement planning that ignores this can fall badly short.

## How much is ₹1 lakh worth in future?

This table shows what ₹1,00,000 received in the future would buy in today's prices, at three inflation rates:

| Inflation rate | Worth today if received in 10 years | Worth today if received in 20 years |
|---|---|---|
| 4% | ₹67,556 | ₹45,639 |
| 6% | ₹55,839 | ₹31,180 |
| 8% | ₹46,319 | ₹21,455 |

Two things stand out. First, the difference between 4% and 8% inflation is enormous over 20 years: the same rupee amount is worth more than twice as much in one case as in the other. Second, long-dated promises such as a fixed sum from an insurance policy maturing in 20 years are worth far less than the headline suggests. Before buying any product that pays a fixed amount decades away, divide that amount by the inflation factor here to see its real value.

## Why inflation matters for your money

- **Savings in low-interest accounts** lose value in real terms if the interest is below inflation.
- **Fixed deposits** can barely keep pace once tax is deducted. Check your FD's maturity with the [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/), then convert it to today's money here.
- **Long-term goals** like education, a house or retirement need targets set in future rupees, not today's.
- **Salary hikes** below inflation mean a real pay cut, even if the number on your payslip rises.

## Is your salary hike beating inflation?

A quick real-pay check: divide (1 + hike) by (1 + inflation) and subtract 1. If Anjali's salary rises 5% in a year when prices rise 6%, her real pay change is 1.05 ÷ 1.06 − 1, about −0.94%. Her payslip shows more rupees, but they buy slightly less than last year's salary did. Over several years of below-inflation increments, the gap adds up, so it is worth running your own numbers before an appraisal conversation.

## Using inflation with investment calculators

A good habit is to work in two steps. First, use this calculator to turn your goal into future rupees. Then use the [SIP Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sip-calculator/) or [Lumpsum Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/lumpsum-calculator/) to see how much you need to invest to reach that figure. The lumpsum tool also shows a "value in today's ₹" result using an inflation rate you choose.

## Common mistakes

1. **Using today's prices for a goal 15 years away.** The target will be far too low.
2. **Applying one inflation rate to everything.** Education and healthcare costs have often risen faster than general prices.
3. **Adding inflation instead of compounding it.** 6% for 10 years is not 60%; it is about 79%.
4. **Confusing nominal and real returns.** A 10% return with 6% inflation is a real return of roughly 3.8%, not 4%, because (1.10 ÷ 1.06) − 1 ≈ 3.77%.
5. **Ignoring tax on returns.** Tax reduces what is left to fight inflation.

## Choosing a sensible rate

Over long periods, India's CPI inflation has often been in the region of 5–6% a year, but it has swung well above and below that in individual years. The RBI's inflation target is 4%, with a tolerance band of 2% either side. For personal planning, many people use 6% as a base case and test 7% or 8% for a cautious view, with higher figures for school and college fees.

## Limits of the calculator

The tool applies one steady rate to every year. Real inflation varies year to year and differs by city, household and category. The result is an illustration of scale for planning, not a forecast. This article is general information rather than financial advice; for official data, refer to the CPI releases from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and the RBI, and consider professional advice for major financial plans.

Q: What inflation rate should I use for planning?
A: There is no single right rate. Many people use around 6% for general household costs as a planning assumption, and higher rates for education and healthcare, which have often risen faster than average. Try two or three rates to see a range rather than relying on one number.

Q: What is the difference between future cost and today's value?
A: Future cost tells you how much money you will need later to buy what costs a given amount now. Today's value works the other way, telling you what a future sum can buy in current prices. The calculator has a mode for each, using the same compound formula.

Q: How does inflation affect my fixed deposit returns?
A: Your real return is roughly the interest rate minus inflation, and after tax it is lower still. If an FD pays 7% and inflation is 6%, your purchasing power grows by only about 1% a year before tax. For someone paying tax on that interest, the real return can be negative.

Q: Where can I find official inflation figures for India?
A: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is published monthly by the National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The Reserve Bank of India uses CPI inflation for its monetary policy target. Both websites publish current and historical data you can use to choose a rate.

## How to Create a GST Invoice: CGST, SGST, IGST and Format

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/create-gst-invoice-online-free/
Tool: GST Invoice Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/)

Quick answer: A GST tax invoice lists the supplier and buyer details, GSTINs, a unique invoice number and date, place of supply, HSN or SAC codes, taxable value and tax. Charge CGST plus SGST when supplier and place of supply are in the same state, and IGST when they differ. BISCS India’s free GST Invoice Generator applies this split automatically and saves the invoice as PDF.

A GST tax invoice is the bill a registered business issues when it supplies goods or services. It must show the **supplier's and buyer's details and GSTINs**, a **unique invoice number and date**, the **place of supply**, **HSN or SAC codes**, the **taxable value**, and the **tax charged**. That tax is split as **CGST + SGST** when the supplier and the place of supply are in the same state, and charged as **IGST** when they are in different states.

The free [GST Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/) builds a professional A4 invoice with these fields, applies the right tax split automatically, and lets you save it as a PDF. Your data stays in your browser.

**Note:** this guide explains general GST invoicing practice as at the time of writing. GST rules and rates change, so confirm specifics for your business on the official GST portal or with a chartered accountant.

## CGST + SGST or IGST: the core rule

The deciding question is whether the supply is **intra-state** or **inter-state**:

| Supplier's state | Place of supply | Supply type | Tax charged |
|---|---|---|---|
| West Bengal | West Bengal | Intra-state | CGST + SGST, each half the rate |
| West Bengal | Karnataka | Inter-state | IGST at the full rate |
| Delhi | Delhi | Intra-state | CGST + SGST (Delhi has its own legislature) |
| Maharashtra | Chandigarh | Inter-state | IGST |

In union territories without their own legislature, such as Chandigarh, an intra-state supply attracts **CGST + UTGST** instead of SGST.

The **place of supply** is decided by GST law. For goods it is generally where the movement of goods ends, and for many services to registered businesses it is the recipient's location. Unusual cases, such as events, transport or exports, have their own rules, so check if you are unsure.

The total tax is the same either way. Only the heads change, which affects where the tax is credited and how the buyer claims input tax credit.

## What must a GST tax invoice contain?

Under the GST invoice rules, a tax invoice should include:

- Supplier's name, address and GSTIN
- A consecutive **invoice number**, unique for the financial year, of up to 16 characters
- **Date** of issue
- Buyer's name and address, and **GSTIN if registered**
- **Place of supply** with the state name, for inter-state supplies
- **HSN** (goods) or **SAC** (services) code
- Description, **quantity** and unit
- **Taxable value** after any discount
- **Tax rate** and amount for CGST, SGST/UTGST or IGST
- Whether tax is payable on **reverse charge**
- **Signature** of the supplier or authorised signatory

The BISCS template covers each of these, and adds a tax summary by rate, the total in words, and optional bank and UPI details.

## How to make a GST invoice with the BISCS tool

1. Open the [GST Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/). A sample invoice is loaded so you can see the layout.
2. Fill in **From (your business)**: name, address, state, GSTIN, phone, email and an optional logo. A valid GSTIN sets the state automatically and is checked for format and check digit.
3. Fill in **Bill to (customer)**, including the **Place of supply**. A badge shows whether the supply is intra-state (CGST + SGST) or inter-state (IGST).
4. Set the **invoice number**, **date** and **due date**.
5. Add **items** with description, HSN/SAC, quantity, rate, discount % and GST %. Line totals update as you type.
6. Add **notes, terms**, bank details, UPI ID and the signature line text.
7. Check the **live A4 preview**, then press **Download PDF** and choose "Save as PDF" in the print dialog.

Your draft saves automatically on your device. **New invoice** keeps your business and bank details, clears the customer and items, and moves to the next invoice number.

## Worked example: same items, two customers

A Kolkata agency (West Bengal) bills three items:

| Item | Qty × Rate | Discount | Taxable value | GST rate | Tax |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Website maintenance | 1 × ₹40,000 | — | ₹40,000.00 | 18% | ₹7,200.00 |
| Training sessions | 12 × ₹1,250 | 10% | ₹13,500.00 | 18% | ₹2,430.00 |
| Printed manuals | 3 × ₹499 | — | ₹1,497.00 | 5% | ₹74.85 |
| **Total** | | | **₹54,997.00** | | **₹9,704.85** |

The rates here are for illustration. Always use the correct rate for your actual HSN or SAC code.

**Customer in Kolkata (intra-state):** CGST ₹4,852.42 + SGST ₹4,852.43. The odd paisa arises because ₹74.85 cannot be halved exactly, so the tool rounds one half and puts the remainder in the other, keeping the total exact. Invoice value ₹64,701.85, rounded off by +₹0.15 to **₹64,702**.

**Customer in Bengaluru (inter-state):** IGST ₹9,704.85. Same invoice value, **₹64,702** after rounding.

## A note on GST rates

GST rates were rationalised with effect from 22 September 2025, and most goods and services now fall in the 5% or 18% slabs, with a higher rate of 40% for certain goods. Some special rates, such as those on precious metals, also exist. The generator offers 0%, 0.25%, 3%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% and 40% so you can match the rate that applies, including for older transactions. Confirm current rates for your HSN or SAC code on the official GST sources.

## E-invoicing: when a PDF is not enough

Businesses whose aggregate turnover in any financial year exceeds the notified threshold must issue **e-invoices** for B2B supplies. At the time of writing that threshold is **₹5 crore**. E-invoicing means reporting each invoice to the government's Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an **IRN** and a signed QR code to print on the invoice.

This tool does not connect to the portal or generate IRNs. If you are above the threshold, use e-invoicing through the official portal or your accounting software, and check the latest threshold and timelines on the official e-invoice website.

## Common GST invoicing mistakes

- **Charging IGST on a local sale,** or CGST + SGST on an out-of-state one.
- **Wrong place of supply,** especially when the billing and delivery addresses are in different states.
- **Reusing or skipping invoice numbers** within a financial year.
- **Missing the buyer's GSTIN** on B2B invoices, which can block their input tax credit.
- **Applying GST before the discount** instead of on the discounted taxable value.
- **Using a tax invoice when composition or unregistered,** which is not allowed.
- **Wrong HSN/SAC or rate,** which causes mismatches in returns.

## Practical tips

- Use a number format that resets each financial year, such as `INV/2026-27/001`.
- Keep a PDF of every invoice; the browser draft is only a convenience.

- Track your filing deadlines with the [GST Due Date Calendar](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-due-date-calendar/).

A correct invoice protects both you and your customer's tax credit. Create yours with the [GST Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/), and check any doubtful rule with your tax adviser.

Q: When do I charge CGST and SGST, and when IGST?
A: Compare the supplier’s state with the place of supply. If both are in the same state, it is an intra-state supply and the GST rate is split equally into CGST and SGST, or UTGST in some union territories. If they are in different states, it is an inter-state supply and the full rate is charged as IGST. The total tax is the same either way.

Q: Does this tool generate e-invoices with an IRN?
A: No. It creates a regular tax invoice as a PDF. Businesses whose aggregate turnover exceeds the notified e-invoicing threshold, currently ₹5 crore at the time of writing, must report B2B invoices to the Invoice Registration Portal to get an IRN and signed QR code. Check the current threshold and rules on the official GST and e-invoice portals.

Q: How many digits of HSN code must I show?
A: Under the current notification, businesses with aggregate turnover up to ₹5 crore in the previous year must show at least 4-digit HSN codes on B2B tax invoices, and those above ₹5 crore must show 6 digits. Services use SAC codes. Rules can change, so confirm the current requirement on the GST portal or with your tax adviser.

Q: Can a composition dealer or unregistered business use this tool?
A: Only GST-registered regular taxpayers can issue a tax invoice and charge GST. A composition taxpayer issues a bill of supply without charging GST, and an unregistered business cannot collect GST at all. They can still use the layout as a simple bill by setting the GST rate to 0%, but should not label it or present it as a tax invoice.

Q: Where is my invoice data saved?
A: Your draft is saved only in your own browser on this device, so your business and bank details are there next time. Nothing is uploaded to a server. Download each invoice as a PDF for your records, because clearing browser data or switching devices will remove the draft.

## How to Format and Validate JSON Online (With Error Lines)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/format-validate-json-online/
Tool: JSON Formatter (https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/)

Quick answer: To format JSON, paste it into a JSON formatter, choose an indent (2 spaces, 4 spaces or tab) and copy the pretty-printed result. If the JSON is invalid, a good formatter shows the exact line and column of the error. BISCS India's JSON Formatter does all of this in your browser, so API responses never leave your device.

A JSON formatter takes a dense block of JSON, checks that it is valid, and re-prints it with consistent indentation so you can actually read it. If something is wrong, it tells you where: the line, the column and what it expected to find.

The [JSON Formatter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/) on BISCS India does three jobs in one screen: pretty-print, validate and minify. It runs entirely in your browser, which matters when the JSON you are debugging is a live API response with names, phone numbers or order details.

## What does a JSON formatter actually do?

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the format almost every web API speaks, from UPI payment callbacks to weather services. Servers usually send it minified, with no spaces or line breaks, because that saves bandwidth. That is fine for machines and miserable for people.

A formatter parses the text into a data structure and prints it back out with indentation. Here is the same object before and after:

```json
{"order":{"id":"ORD-2041","city":"Kolkata","items":[{"sku":"TEA-250","qty":2}],"paid":true}}
```

```json
{
  "order": {
    "id": "ORD-2041",
    "city": "Kolkata",
    "items": [
      { "sku": "TEA-250", "qty": 2 }
    ],
    "paid": true
  }
}
```

Because the formatter has to parse the JSON first, it doubles as a validator. If parsing fails, you get an error instead of output.

## How to format JSON with BISCS India

1. Open the [JSON Formatter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/).
2. Paste your JSON into the **Input JSON** box, drop a `.json` file onto it, or use **Upload**.
3. Choose an indent from the dropdown: 2 spaces, 4 spaces or Tab. Tick **Sort keys** if you want object keys in alphabetical order.
4. Click **Format**. The output appears on the right, along with a status line showing the type (object or array), number of keys, nesting depth and size.
5. Switch the output view to **Tree** if you want to expand and collapse nested objects instead of scrolling through text.
6. Use **Copy** or **Download** to save the result. Click **Minify** if you need the compact version instead.

The tool re-validates as you type, so you can fix an error and see the green "Valid JSON" badge appear straight away.

## How do I find the error in invalid JSON?

When parsing fails, the formatter shows a red "Invalid JSON" box with a plain-English message, the line and column, and a snippet of the offending line with a caret pointing at the problem. The **Go to error** button jumps your cursor to that character in the input.

Most JSON errors come from writing JavaScript-style objects by hand. The most common ones:

- **Trailing commas.** `[1, 2, 3,]` is valid JavaScript but invalid JSON. The message reads "Trailing comma before “]”".
- **Single quotes.** JSON strings and keys must use double quotes: `"name"`, never `'name'`.
- **Unquoted keys.** `{city: "Pune"}` must be `{"city": "Pune"}`.
- **Comments.** `//` and `/* */` are not part of JSON.
- **Line breaks inside strings.** A raw newline inside quotes is not allowed; it must be written as `\n`.
- **Special values.** `undefined`, `NaN` and `Infinity` do not exist in JSON. Use `null` or a string.
- **Two values side by side.** Pasting two JSON objects one after another, as often happens with log files, gives "Unexpected … after the end of the JSON value". Wrap them in an array or validate them one at a time.

A quick test you can run in any browser console shows the difference between JavaScript and JSON:

```js
JSON.parse('{"a": 1}');   // works
JSON.parse("{'a': 1}");   // SyntaxError: single quotes
JSON.parse('{"a": 1,}');  // SyntaxError: trailing comma
```

## Pretty-print or minify: which should you use?

| Situation | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading an API response | Pretty-print, 2 spaces | Easy to scan, compact enough on screen |
| Config file in a Git repo | Pretty-print, sorted keys | Cleaner diffs when values change |
| Sending a payload over the network | Minify | Fewer bytes per request |
| Embedding JSON in an environment variable | Minify | Must fit on one line |
| Comparing two responses | Pretty-print, sorted keys, then diff | Same order makes real changes stand out |

Sorting keys is especially useful before comparing two JSON files. Format both with **Sort keys** ticked, then paste them into the [Text Diff](https://biscsindia.com/tools/text-diff/) tool, and only genuine differences will be highlighted.

## A note on large numbers

The tool shows a warning badge, "Large numbers may lose precision", when it sees long runs of digits. This is not a bug in the formatter. Browsers store every JSON number as a 64-bit floating point value, which can only represent integers exactly up to 9,007,199,254,740,991 (2^53 − 1).

Long numeric IDs, such as some bank reference numbers or social media post IDs, can be silently rounded when parsed. If you control the API, send such IDs as strings. If you do not, be careful about copying formatted output back into a system that needs the exact value.

## Practical tips for working with JSON

- **Use the Tree view for deep data.** GST e-invoice JSON, for example, nests seller, buyer and item details several levels deep. Collapsing branches makes it much easier to find one field.
- **Keep the Sample handy.** If you are learning JSON, click **Sample** to load a small example with objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and `null`, then try breaking it to see the error messages.
- **Validate before you deploy.** A single trailing comma in a `package.json` or a translation file can break a build. Pasting the file into a validator takes seconds.
- **Convert when a spreadsheet is the real goal.** If someone asks for "this data in Excel", run the JSON through [JSON to CSV](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) instead of formatting it by hand.
- **Minify for production assets.** For whole files, the [CSS / HTML / JSON Minifier](https://biscsindia.com/tools/code-minifier/) shows exactly how many bytes you saved.

## Why formatting in the browser matters for privacy

Debugging often means pasting real data: customer records, internal API tokens inside a response, or payment webhook bodies. Many online formatters send that text to their server to process it, and you have no idea whether it is logged.

The BISCS India formatter uses your browser’s built-in `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify`. The text never leaves your device, and the page keeps working even if your connection drops after it loads. That said, if your organisation has rules about handling production data, those rules still apply.

## Limits worth knowing

The formatter handles files up to 50 MB when loaded from disk, but very large inputs will be slower to re-validate on a phone or older laptop. The tree view stops drawing after a few thousand nodes to keep the page responsive; the text output is unaffected. And because it follows the JSON standard strictly, it will not accept JSON5 or JSONC (JSON with comments) unless you remove the extra syntax first.

Q: Why does my JSON say “Unexpected token” when it looks fine?
A: The usual culprits are a trailing comma after the last item, single quotes instead of double quotes, comments, or an unquoted key. JavaScript object syntax allows some of these, but strict JSON does not. The formatter points to the line and column so you can fix the exact character.

Q: Is it safe to paste API responses with customer data into an online JSON formatter?
A: It depends on the tool. Many websites send your text to a server. The BISCS India JSON Formatter parses and formats everything with JavaScript inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded. Even so, follow your company’s data policy for production data containing personal details.

Q: Does formatting JSON change the data?
A: No. Formatting only adds or removes whitespace between tokens. Keys, values and order stay the same, unless you tick Sort keys, which reorders object keys alphabetically. Very large integers above 2^53 may lose precision because browsers store JSON numbers as 64-bit floating point values.

Q: What is the difference between pretty-printing and minifying JSON?
A: Pretty-printing adds line breaks and indentation so people can read the structure. Minifying removes all unnecessary whitespace so the file is as small as possible for sending over a network. Both versions represent exactly the same data and parse to the same result.

Q: Can I add comments to a JSON file?
A: Standard JSON has no comment syntax, so a strict parser rejects them. Some tools accept variants such as JSONC or JSON5 for configuration files, but if the file is consumed by an API or JSON.parse, remove comments or store notes in a normal string field instead.

## How to Convert JSON to CSV for Excel (Nested Data Too)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/convert-json-to-csv-excel/

Quick answer: To convert JSON to CSV, paste a JSON array of objects into a converter, which turns each object into a row and each key into a column. To convert JSON to CSV, you need JSON shaped like a list of records: an array of objects. Each object becomes one row and each key becomes a column header. Paste it into a converter, download the `.csv`, and open it in Excel or Google Sheets.

The [JSON to CSV](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) tool on BISCS India does this instantly in your browser. It also flattens nested objects, merges keys that only appear in some records, and adds a byte order mark so Excel does not garble Hindi names or the ₹ sign.

## When do you need to turn JSON into a spreadsheet?

Developers live in JSON, but managers, accountants and clients usually want Excel. Common situations include:

- Exporting orders or leads from an API so the sales team can filter them.
- Sharing a list of form submissions with someone who does not code.
- Reconciling payment gateway data against your books.
- Loading data into a tool that only accepts CSV imports.

CSV (comma-separated values) is the simplest common format both worlds understand. It is plain text, one record per line, with values separated by a delimiter.

## How the conversion works

Take this JSON array of customers:

```json
[
  { "id": 1, "name": "Asha Verma", "address": { "city": "Delhi", "pin": "110001" }, "tags": ["admin", "sales"] },
  { "id": 2, "name": "Rohan Das", "address": { "city": "Kolkata" }, "active": false }
]
```

With **Flatten nested objects** switched on, the converter produces:

```text
id,name,address.city,address.pin,tags,active
1,Asha Verma,Delhi,110001,"admin, sales",
2,Rohan Das,Kolkata,,,false
```

Notice three things. The nested `address` object became two columns using dot notation. The simple array `tags` became a single comma-separated value, quoted because it contains a comma. And `active`, which only Rohan’s record has, still gets a column; Asha’s cell is simply empty. The converter collects every key from every object, in the order it first sees them.

## Step-by-step: JSON to CSV with BISCS India

1. Open [JSON to CSV](https://biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/).
2. Paste your JSON into the left box, or click **Upload** to load a `.json` file. You can also drag a file onto the box.
3. Pick a **Delimiter**: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe.
4. Leave **Flatten nested objects (a.b.c)** ticked unless you want nested objects stored as raw JSON text in one cell.
5. Keep **Header row** ticked so the first line holds the column names.
6. Check the table under **Preview**. It shows up to the first 100 rows so you can spot problems before downloading.

## What if my JSON is not a simple array?

Real API responses are rarely a bare array. They tend to look like this:

```json
{ "status": "ok", "page": 1, "results": [ { "id": 1 }, { "id": 2 } ] }
```

The converter looks for exactly one array of objects inside the top-level object. If it finds one, it uses it and shows a note such as "Using the “results” array." If there are several such arrays, it cannot guess which one you mean, so it treats the whole object as one row. In that case, copy just the array you want into the input.

An array of arrays, such as `[[1, "a"], [2, "b"]]`, is also accepted. Each inner array becomes a row, with generic `column_1`, `column_2` headers.

## Common mistakes when converting JSON to CSV

- **Expecting deep nesting to flatten perfectly.** Arrays of objects, such as order line items, cannot be flattened into a single row without losing structure. They are written as JSON text inside the cell. If you need one row per line item, reshape the data first.
- **Opening the CSV by double-clicking without a BOM.** Excel may show `à¤…` style garbage instead of Hindi. Keep the BOM option on, or import via Excel’s Data tab and choose UTF-8.
- **Losing leading zeros.** PIN codes are safe as text in the CSV, but Excel may strip a leading zero from values like `0042` or turn long numbers like account numbers into scientific notation. Import those columns as Text in Excel.
- **Mixing delimiters and locale.** If Excel puts everything in column A, your regional settings probably expect semicolons. Re-download with the semicolon delimiter.
- **Forgetting that dates are just strings.** JSON has no date type, so dates come through exactly as written, for example `2026-03-31T10:00:00Z`. Format them in the spreadsheet afterwards.

## Choosing a delimiter

| Delimiter | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| Comma `,` | Default; Excel and Google Sheets in Indian and US locales |
| Semicolon `;` | Spreadsheets set to European locales |
| Tab | Pasting straight into a sheet; data full of commas |
| Pipe | Script-to-script transfers, legacy bank and ERP formats |

Exports of customers, employees or payments are exactly the kind of data you should not paste into random websites. This converter reads and transforms the JSON with JavaScript in your own browser. Nothing is uploaded, and the CSV is generated locally when you click download.

## Going the other way, or into Excel directly

If you later receive a CSV and need JSON for an API or a script, use [CSV to JSON](https://biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/), which also detects numbers and booleans. For converting between CSV and real `.xlsx` workbooks, the [Excel & CSV Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/excel-csv-converter/) handles the spreadsheet side.

## Tips for cleaner output

Keep key names short and consistent before converting, because they become your column headers. `customer_name` in one record and `customerName` in another will produce two separate columns. If your data comes from multiple API versions, normalise the keys first.

Finally, remember that the preview is your friend. Scroll it horizontally to check that every column you expect is there, and that nothing important ended up as a block of JSON text in a single cell.

Q: What JSON structure converts best to CSV?
A: An array of flat objects, where every object has the same keys, maps perfectly to a table: one object per row, one key per column. Nested objects can be flattened into dotted column names. Deeply nested arrays of objects do not fit a flat table well and are written as JSON text inside a cell.

Q: Why does Excel show strange characters instead of Hindi or the ₹ symbol?
A: Excel on Windows may guess the wrong text encoding when opening a CSV. Adding a UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file tells Excel the file is UTF-8. The BISCS India tool adds this by default when you download, so Devanagari, Bengali and ₹ display correctly.

Q: My JSON is an object, not an array. Can I still convert it?
A: Yes. If the object contains exactly one array of objects, such as a results or data field, the tool uses that array automatically and tells you which one it picked. Otherwise the single object becomes a one-row CSV with each key as a column.

Q: What happens to commas and line breaks inside values?
A: They are handled using standard CSV quoting. Any value containing the delimiter, a double quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes, and inner quotes are doubled. Excel, Google Sheets and most programming libraries read this format correctly.

Q: Should I use a comma or semicolon delimiter?
A: Use a comma for most cases. Choose semicolon if your spreadsheet is set to a European locale where the comma is the decimal separator. Tab is useful when pasting directly into a spreadsheet, and pipe suits data that contains lots of commas and is read by scripts.

## How to Decode a JWT Token (and Why Decoding Isn’t Verifying)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/decode-jwt-token-header-payload/
Tool: JWT Decoder (https://biscsindia.com/tools/jwt-decoder/)

Quick answer: To decode a JWT, split it at the two dots and Base64url-decode the first two parts: the header and the payload, both JSON. Decoding needs no key, which is why it never proves a token is genuine. BISCS India's JWT Decoder shows the claims, expiry in IST and algorithm, on your device without sending the token anywhere.

A JSON Web Token (JWT) is three chunks of Base64url text joined by dots: `header.payload.signature`. Decoding it means turning the first two chunks back into the JSON they came from, so you can read who the token is for, who issued it and when it expires.

The [JWT Decoder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/jwt-decoder/) on BISCS India does this instantly in your browser, converts timestamps like `exp` and `iat` into readable IST dates, and warns about expired tokens and unsafe algorithms. One thing it deliberately does not do is verify the signature, and understanding why is the most important part of working with JWTs.

## What is inside a JWT?

Here is a token split onto three lines for readability:

```text
eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9
.eyJzdWIiOiJ1c2VyXzEwMjQiLCJuYW1lIjoiUHJpeWEgU2hhcm1hIiwiZXhwIjoxNzk4NzM1NDAwfQ
.k3X1oQ...signature...
```

The first part decodes to the **header**, which says how the token was signed:

```json
{ "alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT" }
```

The second part decodes to the **payload**, a set of claims:

```json
{ "sub": "user_1024", "name": "Priya Sharma", "exp": 1798735400 }
```

The third part is the **signature**, binary data created from the first two parts and a key. It is what makes the token trustworthy, but only to someone who checks it with the right key.

## Decoding is not verifying

Anyone can decode a JWT. There is no secret involved; it is just Base64url. That has two consequences every developer should remember:

1. **The payload is public.** Never put secrets, passwords or sensitive personal data in it. Anyone who intercepts or is given the token can read it.
2. **The payload proves nothing on its own.** An attacker can write any JSON they like, encode it, and attach a fake signature. A decoder will happily show `"role": "admin"`. Only signature verification on the server reveals the forgery.

So use a decoder for **debugging and inspection**, and let your backend library, such as `jsonwebtoken` in Node.js, PyJWT in Python or your framework’s built-in middleware, **verify** every token before trusting it. Verification should check the signature, the algorithm you expect, and the `exp`, `nbf`, `iss` and `aud` claims.

## How to decode a JWT with BISCS India

1. Open the [JWT Decoder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/jwt-decoder/).
2. Paste the token into the **JSON Web Token** box. A leading `Bearer ` copied from an `Authorization` header is stripped automatically.
3. The token is shown colour-coded by part, and the **Status** card shows whether it has expired, when it expires relative to now, and the signing algorithm.
4. Read the **Header** and **Payload** cards. Standard claims are labelled in plain English, and time claims (`exp`, `nbf`, `iat`) are shown as IST dates with a relative time, alongside the raw number.
5. Use **Copy JSON** on either card to grab the decoded content for a bug report or test.

Click **Sample** to load an example token if you just want to explore.

## The standard claims, explained

| Claim | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iss` | Issuer | Who created the token, often your auth server’s URL |
| `sub` | Subject | Who the token is about, usually a user ID |
| `aud` | Audience | Which application the token is meant for |
| `exp` | Expires | Time after which the token must be rejected |
| `nbf` | Not before | Time before which the token is not valid |
| `iat` | Issued at | When the token was created |
| `jti` | Token ID | Unique ID, useful for revocation lists |

The time claims are **Unix timestamps in seconds**, not milliseconds. JavaScript’s `Date.now()` returns milliseconds, so a common bug is writing `exp: Date.now() + 3600` instead of `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600`. If you need to convert a timestamp by hand, the [Unix Timestamp Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/timestamp-converter/) shows it in IST and UTC.

## Warnings the decoder shows

- **Expired.** The `exp` time is in the past. Your server should reject this token; the client should refresh it.
- **No expiry (exp) claim.** A token that never expires is a long-lived key. If it leaks, it works forever unless you rotate the signing secret.
- **alg: none.** The token claims to be unsigned. A correct server must never accept it.
- **Five parts instead of three.** That is an encrypted JWE token. Its payload cannot be read without the decryption key, and the tool tells you so.
- **Wrong number of parts or invalid Base64.** Often a token truncated when copied from logs or a terminal.

## Common mistakes when working with JWTs

- **Storing sensitive data in claims.** Keep payloads to IDs, roles and expiry. Look everything else up on the server.
- **Trusting decoded claims in the front end for security decisions.** Hiding an admin button based on a decoded `role` is fine for convenience, but the API must enforce permissions itself.
- **Long expiry with no revocation.** Use short-lived access tokens, for example 15 minutes to an hour, plus refresh tokens.
- **Accepting any algorithm.** Configure your verifier with an explicit list such as `["RS256"]`, so an attacker cannot switch to `none` or swap an asymmetric algorithm for a symmetric one.
- **Sharing live tokens in tickets and chats.** A pasted bearer token is a working credential until it expires.

## How the decoding actually works

If you want to decode a payload in code, it is a few lines, which shows how little protection encoding provides:

```js
const payload = JSON.parse(
  new TextDecoder().decode(
    Uint8Array.from(atob(token.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/')), c => c.charCodeAt(0))
  )
);
```

`atob` needs standard Base64, so the URL-safe `-` and `_` characters are converted back first. Using `TextDecoder` keeps names in Hindi or other scripts intact. For decoding arbitrary Base64 strings rather than tokens, use the [Base64 Encode / Decode](https://biscsindia.com/tools/base64-encoder/) tool.

## Privacy

A JWT can be a live credential, so where you paste it matters. This decoder runs entirely in your browser; the token is never sent to a server or stored. If you are building tokens for a test environment, generating random user IDs with the [UUID Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/uuid-generator/) keeps test data realistic without touching real accounts.

Q: Is the data inside a JWT encrypted?
A: No, not in a standard signed JWT. The header and payload are only Base64url-encoded, so anyone holding the token can read them. Do not put passwords, Aadhaar numbers or other sensitive personal data in JWT claims. Encrypted tokens exist, called JWE, and have five parts instead of three.

Q: Does decoding a JWT verify it?
A: No. Decoding only reads the contents. Verification means recalculating or checking the signature with the correct secret or public key, and confirming claims such as exp, iss and aud. Only your server, using a maintained JWT library, should decide whether a token is trusted.

Q: Why does my token show as expired when I just logged in?
A: Check the clock on the machine that issued the token and the one checking it, because exp is compared against the current time. Also confirm the exp value is in seconds, as the standard requires. A value in milliseconds would look like a date thousands of years away, not expired.

Q: Is it safe to paste a production JWT into an online decoder?
A: A valid token is like a temporary key to an account, so treat it carefully. The BISCS India decoder works entirely in your browser and does not upload the token. Even so, prefer test tokens, and if a live token may have been exposed, revoke it or let it expire.

Q: What does alg none mean in a JWT header?
A: It means the token claims to have no signature at all. Some old libraries once accepted such tokens as valid, letting attackers forge any claims. A secure server must reject alg none and should only accept the specific algorithms it expects. The decoder flags this case with a warning.

## Keyword Density Checker: What Is a Healthy Percentage?

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/keyword-density-checker-ideal-percentage/
Tool: Keyword Density Checker (https://biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/)

Quick answer: Keyword density is the number of times a word or phrase appears divided by the total word count, shown as a percentage. BISCS India’s free Keyword Density Checker lists the most-used single words and two- or three-word phrases in your text or HTML, measures a focus keyword and flags stuffing, all inside your browser.

Keyword density tells you how often a word or phrase appears compared with the total number of words on a page. If "home loan" appears 12 times in a 1,000-word article, its density is 1.2%.

The [Keyword Density Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/) on BISCS India counts every word and phrase in your text, sorts them by frequency and checks a focus keyword against a sensible range. The useful part is not the number itself but what it reveals: repetition you did not notice, or a topic you meant to cover and barely mentioned.

## Does keyword density still matter for SEO?

Not in the way it did fifteen years ago. Modern search engines understand synonyms, related concepts and context. A page about "two-wheeler insurance" can rank for "bike insurance" without repeating that exact phrase twenty times.

What still matters:

- **The topic must be clear.** If your main subject barely appears, neither readers nor search engines will be sure what the page is about.
- **Over-repetition hurts.** Google's spam policies name keyword stuffing explicitly, and repetitive text simply reads badly.
- **Related terms help.** A guide to GST returns that never mentions GSTR-1, GSTR-3B or input tax credit is probably thin.

So use density as a diagnostic, not a target. The checker treats roughly 0.5–2.5% as a healthy range for a focus keyword, flags values above about 4% as stuffing risk, and tells you when the keyword is missing entirely.

## How to check keyword density step by step

1. Open the [Keyword Density Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/).
2. Paste your article or page copy into the box. You can also paste full HTML, or press **Upload** to load a `.txt`, `.html` or `.md` file.
3. If you pasted HTML, the **Input is HTML** option switches on automatically so tags, scripts and styles are stripped.
4. Type your **Focus keyword or phrase**, for example `gst calculator`.
5. Choose your options: ignore English stopwords, ignore Hindi stopwords, and ignore numbers.
6. Read the summary stats: words, unique words, characters, sentences and estimated reading time.
7. Check the focus keyword message, which shows how many times it appears and whether the density is low, healthy or too high.
8. Switch the table between **1 word**, **2 words** and **3 words** to see the top phrases, sort by any column, and press **Download CSV** to keep the results.

The analysis happens entirely in your browser, so unpublished drafts and client copy stay private.

## Reading the results sensibly

The top of the single-word list usually shows your main topics. If it is dominated by words like "best", "service" or your company name, the copy may be more about selling than explaining.

The two- and three-word views are often more revealing. They show the phrases you actually lean on. You might find "our company provides" twelve times, which is a sign to tighten the writing, or discover that "income tax slab" appears only once in an article meant to rank for it.

Phrases never cross sentence or comma boundaries, so the counts reflect real phrases rather than accidental word pairs.

## What the numbers mean

| Focus keyword density | What it usually means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 0% | The phrase is not used at all | Mention it naturally in the opening and a heading |
| Below about 0.5% | Light usage | Fine for long articles; add a mention if it fits |
| About 0.5–2.5% | Natural usage | Leave it alone and focus on quality |
| About 2.5–4% | Getting repetitive | Swap some instances for synonyms or pronouns |
| Above about 4% | Likely keyword stuffing | Rewrite the affected paragraphs |

These ranges are practical guidelines, not rules from Google. A 150-word product description will naturally have a higher density than a 2,000-word guide.

## Common mistakes when optimising for keywords

- **Writing for a percentage.** Adding the keyword to every sentence to "reach 2%" makes content worse.
- **Ignoring variations.** People search for "EMI calculator", "loan EMI calculator" and "how to calculate EMI". Covering these naturally is better than repeating one form.
- **Stuffing location names.** "Best plumber Kolkata, plumber in Kolkata, Kolkata plumber services" in every paragraph is a classic pattern Google's spam policies describe.
- **Counting the whole page source without stripping it.** Navigation menus, footers and cookie notices can distort the counts. Paste only the main content when you want a precise view.
- **Forgetting the title and headings.** Density only measures body text. The title tag, H1 and subheadings carry more weight for showing what a page is about.

## Tips for natural, well-covered content

- Mention the main topic early, ideally in the first paragraph.
- Use the exact phrase in one or two headings where it reads naturally.
- Answer the questions people actually ask about the topic. The [Question & Topic Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/question-generator/) can suggest them.
- Read the text aloud. If a phrase sounds repetitive, it is.
- Check readability as well as frequency. The [Readability Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/) highlights long sentences and passive voice that make content harder to follow.

Use it when you edit a draft before publishing, when you review a writer's article, or when an older page has stopped ranking and you want to see whether it still focuses on the right subject. It is also handy for comparing your page with a competitor's: paste both separately and compare which topics each covers.

For a wider check of titles, headings, image alt text and links, paste the full page HTML into the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/). For focused work on wording and repetition, the [Keyword Density Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/) gives you a quick, private view of what your content really emphasises.

Q: What is the ideal keyword density for SEO?
A: There is no official ideal figure, and Google does not rank pages by hitting a percentage. As a rough sense check, a main keyword used naturally often lands somewhere between about 0.5% and 2.5%. Much higher than that usually reads as repetitive and can look like keyword stuffing.

Q: Does Google penalise keyword stuffing?
A: Yes. Google’s spam policies specifically list keyword stuffing, meaning filling a page with keywords or numbers in an attempt to manipulate rankings. Pages doing this can rank lower or be removed. Writing naturally, with synonyms and related terms, avoids the problem.

Q: Can I check a live web page with this tool?
A: The tool does not fetch websites. Open the page in your browser, view the page source, copy all the HTML and paste it in. The checker strips tags, scripts and styles automatically and analyses only the visible text.

Q: Why are words like the and and missing from the list?
A: By default the checker ignores common English stopwords because they dominate every text and tell you nothing about its topic. Untick the stopword option if you want to see the full raw frequency list.

## What Is llms.txt and How to Create One for Your Website

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/what-is-llms-txt-how-to-create/
Tool: llms.txt Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/llms-txt-generator/)

Quick answer: llms.txt is a proposed Markdown file, placed at the root of a website, that gives AI assistants a short summary of the site and links to its most useful pages. It is an emerging, voluntary proposal rather than an official standard. BISCS India’s free llms.txt Generator builds and validates llms.txt and llms-full.txt in your browser.

llms.txt is a plain Markdown file that sits at the root of a website, at an address like `https://example.com/llms.txt`. It gives large language models (LLMs) and AI assistants a short, structured summary of the site: what it is, who it is for, and links to the pages that explain it best.

It is important to be clear from the start: llms.txt is an **emerging, voluntary proposal**, first published at llmstxt.org in 2024. It is not an official standard, it is not a ranking factor, and adding it does not guarantee that ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity will cite you. The [llms.txt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/llms-txt-generator/) from BISCS India helps you create a correct file quickly, so you can decide for yourself whether it is worth having.

## Why was llms.txt proposed?

Web pages are built for people: menus, cookie banners, scripts, adverts and sidebars surround the actual content. When an AI tool fetches a page to answer a question, all that clutter competes for its limited reading space, called the context window.

The proposal suggests a simple fix. Publish one clean Markdown file that says: here is what this site is, and here are the pages worth reading. Documentation sites for software libraries were early adopters, because coding assistants benefit from a compact map of the docs.

## What does an llms.txt file contain?

The proposed format is simple and strict about a few things:

1. **One H1 line** with the site or project name, starting with `# `.
2. **A short summary** in a blockquote, a line starting with `> `.
3. **Optional details** in normal paragraphs or bullet points.
4. **Sections** with `## ` headings, each containing a list of links in the form `- [Page title](https://full-url): short description`.
5. **An optional section called "Optional"**, placed last, for secondary links that tools may skip when they need a shorter context.

A small accounting firm in Kolkata, for example, might have a "Services" section linking to GST registration, ITR filing and audit pages, a "Guides" section with its most useful articles, and an "Optional" section with the team page and older posts.

## llms.txt vs robots.txt vs sitemap.xml

| File | Purpose | Who reads it | Controls access? |
|---|---|---|---|
| robots.txt | Crawl rules for bots | Search engines and most reputable crawlers | Requests only, voluntary |
| sitemap.xml | Complete list of URLs to discover | Search engines | No |
| llms.txt | Curated summary and key links in Markdown | Some AI tools and agents, if they choose | No |
| llms-full.txt | Full text of key pages in one file | Some AI tools and agents, if they choose | No |

llms.txt does not replace either of the other files. If you want to control which AI bots may crawl your site, that is a robots.txt job, which you can review with the [AI Crawler Access Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ai-crawler-checker/).

## How to create llms.txt with the BISCS generator

1. Open the [llms.txt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/llms-txt-generator/). Press **Sample** to see a finished example.
2. Enter your **Site or project name**. This becomes the single H1 line.
3. Write a **One-paragraph summary** of one to three sentences: what the site is, who it serves and what makes it useful. The counter tells you if it is too short or too long.
4. Add **Details** if useful, such as key terms or how your sections are organised. Avoid starting lines with `#`.
5. Under **Sections & links**, name each section and add links with a title, URL and short description. Reorder links and sections with the arrow buttons.
6. To save typing, open **Import links from URLs or sitemap XML**, paste a list of URLs or the contents of your sitemap.xml, and import them. Titles are made from the URL slugs, and you can group them by first folder.
7. Read the validation messages. The tool checks for exactly one H1, a summary, absolute URLs, duplicates, and that "Optional" is the last section.
8. Switch to **llms-full.txt** if you also want the full-text companion file, and paste page content under each link.
9. Press **Download** and upload the file to your site root.

Everything runs in your browser; nothing is fetched or uploaded. Your draft is saved in your browser's local storage so you can come back to it.

## Writing a summary AI tools can use

The blockquote summary is the part most likely to be read. Make it factual and specific:

- Say what you are and where: "BISCS India is a Kolkata-based IT services company offering web development and free browser-based tools."
- Say who it is for: small businesses, students, developers.
- Avoid marketing superlatives like "world's best". They add nothing an assistant can use.

Link descriptions follow the same rule. "GST calculator with CGST, SGST and IGST split" is more useful than "Our amazing calculator".

## Common llms.txt mistakes

- **Treating it as a ranking hack.** It is not one. Good content and normal SEO matter far more.
- **Relative links.** Every URL should be absolute, starting with `https://`.
- **Dumping every URL.** That is what a sitemap is for. llms.txt should be curated.
- **Multiple H1 headings.** The format expects exactly one.
- **Letting it go stale.** If you rename or remove pages, update the file.
- **Contradicting robots.txt.** Listing pages in llms.txt while blocking all AI crawlers sends mixed signals. Decide on your overall policy first.

## Should you bother?

For most small sites, creating llms.txt takes fifteen minutes and costs nothing, so there is little downside. For documentation-heavy sites, software products and knowledge resources, it may be genuinely useful to AI coding assistants and agents. Just keep expectations realistic: the content on your pages still does the real work.

To make that content easier for AI answer engines to quote, check it with the [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/), and keep your sitemap current alongside it with the [XML Sitemap Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sitemap-generator/). When your key pages change, reopen the [llms.txt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/llms-txt-generator/) and refresh the file.

Q: Is llms.txt an official web standard?
A: No. It is a community proposal published at llmstxt.org in 2024. It is not a W3C or IETF standard, and major search and AI providers have not formally committed to using it. Some AI tools, coding assistants and agents do read it when present.

Q: Will adding llms.txt improve my Google rankings?
A: No. llms.txt is not a Google ranking factor, and Google representatives have said publicly that Google Search does not use it. Treat it as a low-cost, optional map of your best content for AI tools that choose to read it, not as an SEO shortcut.

Q: What is the difference between llms.txt and robots.txt?
A: robots.txt tells crawlers which paths they may or may not crawl. llms.txt does not grant or block access at all. It is a human-readable and machine-readable guide that points AI assistants to the pages that best explain your site.

Q: What is llms-full.txt?
A: llms-full.txt is a companion file that contains the full text of your key pages in one Markdown document, so an assistant can read everything without following links. It is useful for documentation sites but can become long, so keep it focused.

Q: Where do I upload the llms.txt file?
A: Upload it to the root of your website so it opens at https://yourdomain.com/llms.txt, served as plain text. If you also create llms-full.txt, place it alongside at the root. On most hosts you can upload it like any other file.

## Lorem Ipsum Generator: Free Placeholder Text for Designs

Lorem ipsum is placeholder text: scrambled Latin-looking words that fill a layout before the real content exists. Designers, developers and print shops use it to see how a page looks with text in place, without readers getting distracted by what the words say.

## Where does lorem ipsum come from?

The text is derived from a passage in a Latin work on ethics by the Roman statesman Cicero. Over time, typesetters cut words and syllables from it until it became nonsense that still looks like a natural language, with a realistic mix of short and long words.

That realism is why it outlived alternatives like repeating "text text text" or "content goes here". Repeated words create obvious patterns on the page, and readable English pulls people into reading rather than judging spacing, fonts and hierarchy.

The word and character totals appear under the output, so you can match a target length, such as a 160-character meta description or a 60-word product blurb.

## When should you use placeholder text?

Lorem ipsum is the right choice when the **layout** is what you are testing. Good examples:

- **Website and app mock-ups** in Figma, Canva or plain HTML before the copy is written.
- **WordPress or Shopify theme testing**, to see how blog cards, product descriptions and footers cope with short and long text.
- **Print layouts** for brochures, menus, wedding cards and visiting cards, so the client can approve the design first.
- **Developer testing**: checking that a long paragraph wraps properly, that text does not overflow a button, and that a page still works with 10,000 words.
- **Presentation templates**, where every slide needs plausible body text.

## When real content works better

Placeholder text has real drawbacks, and experienced designers often avoid it for anything beyond early wireframes.

| Situation | Better choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Final client review | Real or near-final copy | Clients judge the content, not the boxes |
| Hindi, Bengali or other Indic layouts | Sample text in that script | Indic scripts need more line height and different fonts |
| Forms, buttons, error messages | Actual labels | Wording drives usability |
| Product pages | Real product names and prices | Lengths vary hugely, for example "Tea" vs a 70-character title |
| Pages going live | Never placeholder | Unfinished pages hurt trust and search visibility |

A practical middle ground is to use lorem ipsum for long body text, but real headings, button labels and prices from day one.

## Common mistakes with dummy text

- **Publishing it by accident.** It happens more often than you would think, especially in image alt text, meta descriptions and footer columns. Search for "lorem" before every launch.
- **Testing only the ideal length.** Real content is messy. Generate one very short and one very long version of each block to see how the design handles both.
- **Forgetting other languages.** If your site will serve Hindi or Tamil readers, Latin filler hides problems with font rendering and line breaks.
- **Copying from random websites.** Some "lorem ipsum" pages include hidden characters or odd formatting. A clean generator avoids that, and you can run any pasted text through the [Whitespace Cleaner](https://biscsindia.com/tools/whitespace-cleaner/) if needed.

## Tips for designers and developers

**Match realistic lengths.** If product descriptions on your marketplace are usually 40 to 80 words, generate 60 words rather than three full paragraphs. Use the word count below the output to check.

**Use the HTML option for templates.** With **Wrap in HTML p tags** ticked, each paragraph comes inside its own HTML paragraph element, ready to paste into a code editor or the HTML view of a content management system. The download is then saved as an `.html` file.

**Preview formatted text quickly.** Writing documentation or a README? Paste generated paragraphs into the [Markdown Preview](https://biscsindia.com/tools/markdown-preview/) alongside some headings and lists to see the full page structure.

**Check the numbers.** When a design brief says "around 300 words per section", paste your mix of real and placeholder text into the [Word Counter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/) to confirm.

## Lorem ipsum in Word, Docs and design apps

Some programs have their own shortcuts. In Microsoft Word, typing `=lorem()` on a new line and pressing Enter inserts placeholder paragraphs, and `=rand()` inserts readable English sample text instead. Design tools such as Figma and Canva offer plugins or built-in fillers too.

Those shortcuts are handy, but they tie you to one program and give you little control over length. A browser generator works the same way everywhere: on your office PC, on a client's laptop or on your phone while you are reviewing a layout. You decide the exact number of words or sentences, then paste the result into any app, email or code editor.

It also helps when several people work on one project. If the developer, designer and content writer all use the same generator with the same settings, a "three-paragraph block" means the same thing to everyone, and the mock-ups line up.

## A quick checklist before you hand over a design

- Every block of placeholder text is clearly marked as temporary in the brief.
- Headings, buttons, prices and form labels use real wording.
- Long and short versions of key blocks have both been tested.
- Any Indian-language sections have been checked with real text in that script.
- A final search for "lorem" and "ipsum" returns nothing on the live site.

When you are ready to replace the filler, open the [Lorem Ipsum Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/lorem-ipsum-generator/) one last time to compare lengths, so the real copy fits the space you designed for.

Q: What does lorem ipsum actually mean?
A: It does not mean anything as a whole. The text is a scrambled and shortened version of a passage from a Latin work on ethics by the Roman writer Cicero, with words cut and altered so it reads as nonsense. That is the point: readers are not distracted by meaning while they judge the layout.

Q: Is it fine to publish a page that still has lorem ipsum?
A: No. Live pages with placeholder text look unfinished, confuse visitors and give search engines nothing useful to index. Before launch, search your site or document for the words lorem and ipsum to catch any blocks you missed, including image alt text and meta descriptions.
