Passport-size photos are small portrait photos with fixed dimensions, most commonly 35 × 45 mm in India and many other countries. Making them yourself means cropping a good portrait to that exact shape and printing several copies on one sheet, which you then cut out.

The [Passport Photo Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/passport-photo-maker/) from BISCS India does the cropping at print resolution and lays out as many copies as fit on a 4 × 6 inch photo print or an A4 sheet, complete with cut lines. You can print at home or take the file to any photo shop.

## Which passport photo size do you need?

| Size | Pixels at 300 DPI | Commonly used for |
|---|---|---|
| 35 × 45 mm | 413 × 531 | India, UK, EU and Schengen visas, many application forms |
| 2 × 2 in (51 × 51 mm) | 600 × 600 | United States passports and visas |

Always confirm the size in the instructions of the authority you are applying to. Visa requirements are set by each country and can change.

### A note on Indian passport applications

For an Indian passport, the commonly stated requirement is a 35 × 45 mm colour photograph with a plain white background, the full face visible from the front, and neutral expression. For many applications, the photograph is captured at the Passport Seva Kendra during your appointment, but printed photos are still asked for in other situations. Rules can be revised, so check the current guidelines on the official Passport Seva website rather than relying on any third-party summary, including this one.

Printed passport-size photos are also routinely needed for school and college admissions, bank account opening, SIM cards, ID cards, visa applications, gym memberships and government forms.

## How to make passport photos step by step

1. Take a photo against a plain, light wall in good, even daylight. Face the camera directly, with shoulders visible.
2. Open the [Passport Photo Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/passport-photo-maker/) and choose the photo, drag it in or paste it with Ctrl + V.

## Printing: home printer or photo shop?

### At a photo shop

Most photo studios and print kiosks in India print 4 × 6 inch photos cheaply. Send them the sheet JPG on WhatsApp or a pen drive and ask for a normal 4 × 6 print without cropping or resizing. You get several passport photos for the price of a single print, often less than what a studio charges for a set.

### On a home printer

Use the PDF version and print on photo paper if you have it. In the print dialog:

- Set scale to **100%** or **Actual size**. Turn off fit to page.
- Choose the correct paper size and the highest photo quality setting.
- After printing, measure one photo with a ruler. It should be exactly 35 mm wide. If it is not, the printer scaled the page.

Plain paper prints are usually not accepted for official photos, so use photo paper or a lab for anything formal.

## Tips for a photo that gets accepted

- **Lighting:** face a window during the day. Avoid overhead tube lights that cast shadows under the eyes and nose.
- **Background:** a plain white or very light wall. Patterns, doors and furniture behind you will lead to rejection.
- **Expression:** neutral, mouth closed, both eyes open and looking at the camera.
- **Glasses:** many authorities now prefer no glasses. If you wear them, avoid reflections and tinted lenses.
- **Clothing:** a darker top contrasts well against a white background.
- **Recent photo:** most applications expect a photo taken within the last few months.

## Common mistakes

- **Head too small or too large.** A head that fills only half the frame or touches the top edge is a common reason for rejection.
- **Printing at the wrong scale.** A fit-to-page setting can shrink every photo by several millimetres.
- **Busy background.** This tool only fills transparent areas; it does not remove a real wall. If your background is not plain, use the [AI Passport Photo](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ai-passport-photo/) tool, which detects your face and makes the background white automatically.
- **Selfie distortion.** A phone held at arm’s length enlarges the nose. Ask someone to take the photo from about a metre or two away.
- **Using an old, low-resolution photo.** The tool needs enough pixels for a sharp 300 DPI print.

## What about digital uploads?

Online forms usually need a digital file rather than a print, often with a specific pixel size and a KB limit. Use the single photo download, then adjust it with [Resize Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/) and [Compress Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/) to match the numbers in the official notice.

## Your photo stays on your device

Cropping, sheet layout and PDF creation all happen in your browser. Your face photo is not uploaded anywhere, which is reassuring for a picture that will end up on identity documents.

Q: What is the passport photo size in India?
A: Indian passport-size photographs are generally 35 × 45 mm with a plain white background and the face clearly visible. Requirements can be updated, and different forms may add their own rules, so check the current Passport Seva guidelines or the instructions of the specific authority before you print.

## How to Generate a Strong Random Password (and Remember It)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/generate-strong-random-password/
Tool: Password Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/)

Quick answer: A strong password is long, random and unique to each account. Aim for at least 12 to 16 characters mixing letters, numbers and symbols, or a passphrase of several random words. BISCS India’s free Password Generator creates them on your device using the browser’s cryptographic random generator, so the passwords are never sent anywhere.

A strong password is **long, random and unique**. For most accounts, that means at least 12 to 16 characters mixing upper and lower case letters, numbers and symbols, or a passphrase of several random words. Most important of all, every account should have its own password.

People are poor at being random, so the best passwords are made by a computer. The free [Password Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/) creates them on your own device using your browser's cryptographic random number generator. Nothing is sent to a server, and the generated passwords are not saved.

## What makes a password strong?

Attackers rarely guess passwords one by one at a login screen. More often, they take password lists leaked from breached websites and try them elsewhere, or run fast guessing programs against stolen password databases. A strong password resists both.

- **Length.** Each extra character multiplies the number of possible passwords.
- **Randomness.** Names, dates of birth, cricket teams and keyboard patterns like `qwerty` are tried first.
- **Character variety.** Mixing cases, digits and symbols enlarges the pool for each character.
- **Uniqueness.** If one site is breached, a reused password unlocks your other accounts too.

Strength is often measured in **bits of entropy**. Each extra bit doubles the number of guesses needed. The generator shows this number and an estimated crack time for every password it makes.

## How strong is each option?

These figures come from the generator's own estimates, which assume an attacker can try 10 billion guesses a second. Real attack speeds vary widely, so treat them as a comparison rather than a promise.

| Password type | Approx. entropy | Rough time to crack |
|---|---|---|
| 8 characters, letters and digits | 48 bits | A few hours |
| 12 characters, letters and digits | 71 bits | Thousands of years |
| 16 characters, all four types | 104 bits | Far longer than the age of the universe |
| 5-word passphrase plus a number | 55 bits | Weeks |
| 7-word passphrase plus a number | 74 bits | Tens of thousands of years |

Two lessons stand out: eight characters is no longer enough, and passphrases need plenty of words.

## How to use the BISCS Password Generator

1. Open the [Password Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/). A 16-character password appears straight away by default.
2. Choose **Password** or **Passphrase** mode.
3. For a password, set the **length** (4 to 128) and tick the character types: uppercase, lowercase, numbers and symbols.
4. Tick **Exclude look-alikes** if you will read or type the password manually. It removes characters like I, l, 1, O and 0.
5. For a passphrase, choose the **number of words** (3 to 12), a separator, and whether to capitalise words and add a number.
6. Pick **how many** to generate: 1, 5, 10 or 25.
7. Press **Copy**, or use the refresh button for a new one. With several results, you can copy them all or download a .txt file.

The generator always includes at least one character from each type you select, then shuffles the result so their positions are random. Digits and symbols are colour-coded in the preview to make reading easier.

## Passwords or passphrases: which should you use?

**Random passwords** are best stored in a password manager and pasted, never typed. Use them for most website logins.

**Passphrases**, such as `Bold-River-Cake-Mint-Sail47`, are easier to remember and type on a phone keyboard. They are ideal for the few passwords you must type from memory: your computer login, your password manager's master password, or your Wi-Fi.

Because the words come from a fixed list of a few hundred common words, each word adds less strength than you might think. For anything important, use **seven or more words**.

## Common password mistakes

- **Reusing one password** across email, shopping and social media.
- **Adding a year or "@123"** to a familiar word. Attackers try these patterns first.
- **Swapping letters for symbols,** like `P@ssw0rd`. Guessing tools already account for these swaps.
- **Using personal details** such as your name, PAN, phone number, vehicle number or date of birth.
- **Saving passwords in screenshots or chat messages,** where anyone with your phone can see them.
- **Sharing OTPs or passwords** with callers claiming to be from a bank or courier. Genuine banks do not ask for them.

## A simple checklist for better account security

- Use a unique, generated password for every account.
- Store them in a reputable password manager.
- Turn on two-factor authentication for email, banking and social media.
- Change a password immediately if a service reports a breach.
- Protect your email account most of all, since it can reset everything else.
- Keep your phone's screen lock strong, because OTPs arrive there.

## When should you change a password?

Changing strong, unique passwords on a fixed schedule is no longer considered necessary by many security experts, and it often leads people to make small, predictable changes like adding 1 to the end. Instead, change a password straight away when:

- a service tells you it has suffered a data breach;
- you notice logins or activity you do not recognise;
- you shared the password with someone who no longer needs access, such as a former employee or flatmate;
- you typed it on a public or shared computer;
- you discover you have reused it on another site.

Your employer or bank may still require periodic changes. When they do, generate a completely fresh password rather than tweaking the old one.

## Practical tips for awkward websites

Some sites limit length or reject certain symbols. If a password is refused, lower the length to the site's maximum or untick symbols and add a few characters instead. When you need several passwords at once, for example while setting up accounts for a new team, generate 10 or 25 and download them, then delete the file once they are stored safely.

To test a password you already use, try the [Password Strength Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/), which also runs entirely in your browser. To share your Wi-Fi password without reading it aloud, create a Wi-Fi QR code with the [QR Code Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/qr-code-generator/). Developers who need random identifiers rather than passwords can use the [UUID Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/uuid-generator/).

Good security starts with one habit: never inventing passwords yourself. Let the [Password Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/) do it, and keep each one unique.

Q: How long should my password be?
A: For most accounts, 12 characters is a sensible minimum and 16 or more is better, especially for email, banking and password manager accounts. Length adds more strength than extra symbols. If a site limits length, use the maximum it allows and turn on two-factor authentication.

Q: Is it safe to generate passwords online?
A: It is safe when the password is created on your own device and never transmitted. The BISCS Password Generator uses your browser’s crypto.getRandomValues function and does not send or store generated passwords. Only your option choices, such as length, are remembered in your browser for convenience.

Q: Are passphrases better than random passwords?
A: Passphrases made of several truly random words are easier to remember and type, especially on phones, and can be very strong if they have enough words. Because each word comes from a limited list, you need more words for the same strength: seven or more words is a good target for important accounts.

Q: Should I use the generator for my UPI PIN or ATM PIN?
A: No. UPI and ATM PINs are short numeric codes that you set inside your bank’s app or at the ATM, and they must never be shared or typed into other websites. Choose a PIN that avoids birthdays and simple sequences like 1234 or 0000, and keep it to yourself.

Q: How should I store all these random passwords?
A: Use a reputable password manager, which stores passwords in an encrypted vault protected by one strong master password. Avoid saving them in plain notes, screenshots or WhatsApp chats. For the master password itself, a long random passphrase you can remember works well.

## How to Check Your Password Strength Without Exposing It

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/check-password-strength-safely/
Tool: Password Strength Checker (https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/)

Quick answer: A password strength checker estimates how hard a password is to guess by looking at its length, character variety and predictable patterns like words, years and keyboard runs. BISCS India’s free Password Strength Checker does this entirely in your browser, showing an entropy score, an estimated crack time and specific tips to make the password stronger.

A password strength checker estimates how hard a password would be to guess. It looks at the **length**, the **mix of character types**, and whether the password contains **predictable patterns** such as dictionary words, years, repeated characters or keyboard runs like `qwerty`. The result is usually shown as bits of entropy and an estimated time to crack.

The free [Password Strength Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/) does all of this inside your browser. What you type is not sent anywhere or stored, and the tool explains exactly what to fix.

## Why most passwords are weaker than they look

People tend to build passwords the same way: a name or word, a capital letter at the start, and a number or symbol at the end. Attackers know this. Their guessing tools try common passwords first, then words with predictable changes, then names with years attached. A password that looks complex to you can fall in seconds.

That is why the checker does not just count character types. It actively hunts for the patterns attackers try first.

## What the checker tests

- **Length.** It flags anything under 12 characters.
- **Character types.** Lowercase, uppercase, numbers and symbols.
- **Common passwords.** It compares against a list of very common passwords, including versions with letters swapped for symbols, like `p@ssw0rd`, and with a few digits added.
- **Sequences** such as `abc`, `123` or `cba`.
- **Repeats** such as `aaa` or `abcabc`.
- **Keyboard patterns** such as `qwerty`, `asdf` or `1qaz2wsx`.
- **Dictionary words and years,** including words disguised with look-alike symbols.

Each predictable part adds very little strength to the score, so `Rahul1995` is judged much weaker than nine random characters.

## How to use the Password Strength Checker

1. Open the [Password Strength Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/).
2. Type or paste a password. Use **Show** to see what you typed and **Hide** to mask it again.
3. Watch the meter move from Very weak to Very strong, with the bits of entropy shown alongside.
4. Check the **Time to crack**, **Length** and **Character pool** figures.
5. Read the **Checks** list to see which tests pass or fail.
6. Follow the **Suggestions**, which are specific to what the checker found.

For extra caution, test a password with the same structure as yours, such as a different word with the same length and pattern, rather than your exact password.

## Example results

These are the checker's own ratings for some typical passwords.

| Password | Rating | Estimated crack time | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| password123 | Very weak | Instantly | A common password with a sequence |
| P@ssw0rd | Very weak | Instantly | Common password with predictable swaps |
| qwerty12345 | Very weak | Instantly | Keyboard run plus a number sequence |
| Rahul1995 | Weak | About half a minute | Name plus a year |
| 9xT#q2Lm!vR4 | Strong | Thousands of years | 12 random characters of all types |

### A word of caution: what a checker cannot know

`Kolkata@2024` scores as Strong in the checker, because it does not recognise Kolkata as a word and only penalises the year. But a city name and a recent year are exactly what someone who knows you, or a targeted guessing list, would try. No automated checker knows your city, your children's names, your vehicle number or your PAN. If your password contains personal details, treat it as weak whatever the score says.

Likewise, the checker cannot tell whether a password has already been leaked in a data breach. A password that appeared in a breach should never be used again, however strong it looks.

## How the score is calculated

The checker first works out the **character pool**: 26 for lowercase letters, 26 for uppercase, 10 for digits and 33 for symbols, plus extra for non-English characters. A truly random character from a pool of 95 adds about 6.6 bits of entropy.

It then scans for patterns. Every character that belongs to a sequence, repeat, keyboard run, dictionary word or year is counted as adding only about 1.2 bits, because an attacker would guess that chunk as a whole rather than letter by letter. If the password matches the common-password list, the score is capped at a very low value no matter how long it is.

Finally, the bits are converted into an estimated crack time. This approach is deliberately cautious. It rewards true randomness and length, and it punishes the shortcuts people naturally use.

## How to read the strength levels

| Level | Entropy | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Very weak | Under 28 bits | Guessable almost immediately |
| Weak | 28 to 39 bits | Falls to a determined attacker quickly |
| Fair | 40 to 59 bits | Acceptable only for low-value accounts |
| Strong | 60 to 79 bits | Good for most accounts |
| Very strong | 80 bits and above | Suitable for email, banking and password managers |

## How to fix a weak password

1. **Make it longer.** Going from 8 to 16 characters adds far more strength than adding a symbol.
2. **Remove personal details** such as names, birthdays, places and phone numbers.
3. **Avoid patterns** like sequences, repeats and keyboard runs.
4. **Do not rely on symbol swaps** like @ for a or 0 for o.
5. **Make it unique,** never reused on another site.
6. **Better still, generate it.** A random password or passphrase from the [Password Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-generator/) beats anything invented by hand.

## Common mistakes when testing passwords

- **Typing a real password into an unknown website** that might send it to a server. Use tools that clearly state the check runs in your browser.
- **Trusting a high score blindly** when the password contains personal information.
- **Testing once and forgetting.** Recheck when a service reports a breach.
- **Strengthening only one account.** Your email account matters most, because it can reset all the others.

## A quick security checklist

- Unique password for every account
- At least 12 to 16 characters, or a long passphrase
- Stored in a reputable password manager
- Two-factor authentication turned on for email, banking and social media
- No passwords or OTPs shared over phone, SMS or WhatsApp

If you are curious how websites store passwords, the [Hash Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hash-generator/) shows how text is turned into a fixed fingerprint such as SHA-256. Proper password storage uses specialised slow hashing, which is one reason why stolen databases are harder to crack.

A strong password takes seconds to create and protects you for years. Check yours with the [Password Strength Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/password-strength-checker/), then replace anything that falls short.

Q: Is it safe to type my real password into a strength checker?
A: Only if the check happens entirely on your device. The BISCS checker runs in your browser and does not send or store what you type. Even so, a safer habit is to test a password with the same pattern as yours, such as the same length and structure, rather than the exact one you use.

Q: Why does P@ssw0rd show as very weak when it has symbols and numbers?
A: Because it is a well-known password with predictable swaps: @ for a and 0 for o. Guessing tools try these substitutions automatically, so they add almost no strength. The checker recognises common passwords even when letters are replaced with look-alike symbols.

Q: What does bits of entropy mean?
A: Entropy is a measure of unpredictability. Each extra bit doubles the number of guesses an attacker would need on average. Roughly, below 40 bits is weak, 60 bits and above is strong, and 80 bits and above is very strong for typical online accounts.

Q: Can a strong-scoring password still be unsafe?
A: Yes. The checker cannot know personal facts such as your name, city, pet or date of birth, or whether the password has already appeared in a data breach. A password built from those details can score well yet be easy for someone who knows you. Reusing it across sites is also risky regardless of its score.

Q: How is the crack time estimated?
A: The checker assumes an attacker can make 10 billion guesses per second, as possible in an offline attack on a stolen password database, and on average finds the password halfway through. Real speeds vary with the website’s security, so use the time as a comparison between passwords, not a guarantee.

## Edit text vs Add text vs Whiteout

| Tool | What it does | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Edit text | Covers an existing line and replaces it with your new text | Fixing typos, dates, names, numbers |
| Add text | Places new text anywhere | Filling blanks, adding notes |
| Whiteout | Draws a white box over content | Hiding stray marks or old details visually |

The key point: **Edit text and Whiteout hide content visually; they do not erase it from the file.** Someone with the right software may still be able to select or extract the covered text. For truly confidential redaction (for example, hiding an account number before sharing a statement publicly), recreate the document from its source or use dedicated redaction software.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Using Indian-language text or the ₹ sign.** The editor uses standard PDF fonts, which cover English and Western characters only. Unsupported characters are replaced with "?" when you save, and the tool warns you if this happens.
- **Treating whiteout as secure deletion.** As above, it is a visual cover only.
- **Editing a password-protected PDF.** The editor cannot open locked files. Open the PDF with its password in a reader, save an unprotected copy, and edit that.
- **Forgetting to check every page.** Scroll through the thumbnails before downloading so nothing lands on the wrong page.
- **Overwriting your only copy.** Keep the original until you have checked the edited version.

## Practical tips for neat results

- Zoom in to 150% or more when placing text on narrow form lines. It is much easier to line things up.
- Match the existing font roughly: Times for formal letters and government forms, Helvetica for modern documents, Courier for typewriter-style forms.
- Use the colour picker sparingly. Black or dark blue looks most natural on official documents.
- Duplicate an item (Ctrl+D) when you need the same text or tick in several places.
- If the PDF is a phone photo of a paper form, consider making a clean copy first with [Scan to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/), which straightens and sharpens the page.

## When should you use a different tool?

If the PDF has real form fields (you can click into boxes in a PDF reader), [Fill PDF Form](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/) is faster and fills the actual fields. If you want to rewrite whole paragraphs, convert the file with [PDF to Word](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/), edit it there, and export a fresh PDF. And if you only need to delete or reorder pages rather than change their content, a page tool is simpler.

## Privacy: your PDF stays on your device

Most free online editors ask you to upload the document to their servers. This one does not. The page loads the editing code into your browser, and from then on all rendering and saving happens on your own phone or computer. Nothing is stored after you close the tab, which is the sensible way to handle ID proofs, payslips and contracts.

The trade-off is that your device does the work. A 200-page scanned report will open more slowly on a budget phone than on a laptop, but your data never leaves your hands.

Q: Can I change the existing text in a PDF?
A: You can replace a line of existing text. The Edit text tool covers the original line with a white box and places your new text on top in a matching standard font. It is ideal for fixing a typo, a date or an amount, but it is not the same as reflowing a whole paragraph in a word processor.

Q: Does whiteout permanently delete the text underneath?
A: No. Whiteout covers content visually, but the original text can still exist in the file and may be copied or found by search. If you need to remove sensitive information for good, do not rely on whiteout alone; recreate the document or use proper redaction software.

Q: Can I type in Hindi or Bengali on a PDF?
A: Not with this editor at the moment. It uses the standard PDF fonts (Helvetica, Times and Courier), which cover English and common Western characters. Symbols such as the rupee sign and Indian scripts are replaced with a question mark when saving, so write Rs. instead of the rupee symbol.

Q: Will editing reduce the quality of my PDF?
A: No. Your additions are drawn into the original PDF, so the existing text stays selectable and vector content stays sharp. The pages are not converted into images, which also keeps the file size close to the original.

Q: Is there a page or file size limit?
A: There is no fixed limit set by the tool because everything runs in your browser. Very long or image-heavy PDFs simply need more memory, so they open more slowly on older phones. A laptop or desktop handles large files more comfortably.

## How to View and Edit PDF Metadata (Title, Author, Keywords)

BISCS India’s PDF Metadata Editor also shows the page count, PDF version and dates, and works entirely in your browser, so the document is never uploaded.

To view or edit a PDF's metadata, open the [PDF Metadata Editor](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-metadata/), load your file, change fields such as **Title**, **Author**, **Subject** and **Keywords**, and save. To strip everything before sharing, tick **Remove all metadata** instead.

The editor also shows the page count, PDF version and file size. It works in your browser, so the document is never uploaded.

## What metadata hides inside your PDFs

Open almost any PDF's Document Properties and you will find information you did not type on the page:

| Field | What it usually contains |
|---|---|
| Title | The document title, shown in browser tabs and some search results |
| Author | Often the name of the person whose computer created it |
| Subject | A short description |
| Keywords | Words to help search and filing |
| Creator | The application used, such as a word processor |
| Producer | The PDF library or printer driver that made the file |
| Created / Modified | Dates and times of creation and last change |

Most of the time nobody looks at these. But they show up in more places than you might expect: browser tab titles, file previews, document management systems and sometimes search engines.

## How to edit PDF metadata step by step

1. Open the [PDF Metadata Editor](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-metadata/) and choose your PDF.
2. Review the current values. The panel also shows pages, PDF version and file size.
3. Edit the fields you want to change. Separate keywords with commas or spaces.
4. Keep **Set "Modified" to now** ticked if the modification date should reflect your change.
5. To wipe everything instead, tick **Remove all metadata**. This clears title, author, dates, software names and the XMP metadata stream.
6. Save and download the updated PDF.

## Good reasons to change metadata

**Fix the title people see.** Share a PDF link and the browser tab says "Microsoft Word - Final_v7_JK_edits.docx". Setting a clean Title such as "Annual Report 2025–26, Sharma Textiles" looks far more professional.

**Correct the author.** A document created by a former employee or on a shared office computer may name the wrong person. Update it to the company name or the correct author.

**Help search and filing.** Firms that keep thousands of PDFs, from CA offices to architecture practices, can make documents easier to find by setting consistent titles, subjects and keywords.

**Publishing on a website.** If you publish brochures or price lists as PDFs, a meaningful Title gives search engines and visitors a clear description of the file.

## Privacy: what your PDF may be revealing

Metadata is a classic source of accidental disclosure. A proposal sent to a client may carry the name of a junior colleague as author, an internal project code in the title, or a creation date that reveals a quote was rushed together the night before. A CV exported from a template may still list the template designer as author.

Before sending documents outside your organisation, especially tenders, proposals, legal drafts and job applications, consider ticking **Remove all metadata**. The pages look exactly the same; only the hidden information goes.

Metadata is only one layer. Comments, hidden layers or text covered by shapes are part of the page content, not metadata, and this tool does not remove them.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Leaving template titles in place.** A wrong title is the most visible metadata error, because browsers show it.
- **Assuming the file name and the title are the same.** Renaming the file does not change the Title field inside it.
- **Misusing dates.** Changing Created or Modified dates to make a document seem older or newer than it is can be misleading, and for official or legal documents it may be treated as tampering. Edit dates only to correct genuine errors.
- **Editing metadata of a digitally signed PDF.** Any change to a signed file can invalidate the digital signature. Edit metadata before signing, not after.

## Checklist before sharing a document externally

- Title is clean and describes the document.
- Author is the correct person or organisation, or blank.
- Keywords and subject contain nothing internal or embarrassing.
- Or: all metadata removed in one click.
- Pages themselves checked for hidden notes and comments.

## Example: sending a quotation to a new client

Nikhil runs a small interior design studio in Ahmedabad. He prepares quotations from an old template on his office desktop and exports them to PDF. When a client opens one in their browser, the tab reads "Quote-template-2019-Ramesh", which is the name of a designer who left years ago, and the Author field shows Ramesh too.

Before sending the next quotation, he opens it in the metadata editor, sets the Title to "Quotation – 3BHK Interiors, Satellite", the Author to his studio's name, adds a few keywords for his own filing, and keeps "Set Modified to now" ticked. The client now sees a clear, professional title, and the old employee's name is gone. For proposals going to large companies, he sometimes removes all metadata instead.

## Where to see metadata on your own device

You do not need special software to check what a PDF carries. In most desktop PDF readers, open the file and look for Document Properties (often under the File menu or by pressing Ctrl+D). Browsers show the Title in the tab. On a phone, some file managers show basic details such as dates. Loading the file into the metadata editor is the quickest way to see every field at once, together with the PDF version and page count.

## Metadata and other PDF tools

Some processing steps reset or change metadata. For example, the Strong and Extreme levels in [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) rebuild the document from page images. If you care about the final metadata, make metadata edits the **last** step, after merging, compressing or watermarking.

If you are publishing a set of documents, combine this with [Add Page Numbers](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-page-numbers/) and [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/) to produce a tidy, well-labelled final file.

## Private and instant

The metadata editor reads and rewrites only the document information, so it is fast even for large files. It runs in your browser, the PDF never leaves your device, and nothing is stored once you close the tab.

Q: What is PDF metadata?
A: Metadata is information stored inside the PDF about the document itself rather than its pages: title, author, subject, keywords, the application that created it, the PDF library that produced it, and creation and modification dates. Readers show it under Document Properties, and search engines may use the title.

Q: Why does my PDF show a strange title in the browser tab?
A: Browsers display the PDF’s Title metadata instead of the file name when it exists. If the document was made from a template, the title may still say something like Untitled or an old project name. Edit the Title field to fix what people see.

Q: Should I remove metadata before sharing a PDF?
A: It is a good habit for documents going outside your organisation. Metadata can reveal the author’s name, the software used, internal file names and when the document was created or edited. Removing it takes a second and shares only what is on the pages.

Q: Does editing metadata change the content of the PDF?
A: No. The pages, text, images and layout stay exactly the same. Only the document information fields are changed. Any embedded XMP metadata is removed when saving, so every PDF reader shows the values you entered.

Q: Can I change the creation date of a PDF?
A: The editor shows the Created and Modified dates and lets you edit them, and by default sets Modified to the current time. Do not change dates to misrepresent when a document was made; for official records that can have serious consequences.

## How to Add Page Numbers to a PDF (Position, Format, Start)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/add-page-numbers-to-pdf-free/
Tool: Add Page Numbers (https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-page-numbers/)

Quick answer: To add page numbers to a PDF, open a page-numbering tool, choose the position (such as bottom centre), a format like Page 1 of N, the pages to number and the starting number, then download. BISCS India’s Add Page Numbers previews the result live and works in your browser, so your document is never uploaded.

To add page numbers to a PDF, open [Add Page Numbers](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-page-numbers/), pick a position (for example bottom centre), a format such as **Page 1 of N**, the pages to number and the starting number, then download. A live preview shows exactly where the numbers will appear before you save.

The numbers are added as real text on each page, the rest of the document is left untouched, and the PDF is processed in your browser rather than uploaded.

## Why page numbers matter more than you think

Page numbers are easy to forget until someone says "see page 14" and nobody can find it. They are especially useful for:

- **Legal and property bundles**, where lawyers and officers refer to specific pages.
- **Project reports and dissertations**, which colleges often require to be numbered.
- **Tender and bid documents**, where every page must be traceable.
- **Printed handouts**, so loose pages can be put back in order after a meeting.
- **Merged application bundles**, where the reviewer needs to navigate a long file.

## How to add page numbers step by step

1. Open [Add Page Numbers](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-page-numbers/) and choose your PDF.
2. Pick a **Position** from the six spots: top left, top centre, top right, bottom left, bottom centre or bottom right.
3. Choose a **Format**: `1, 2, 3`, `Page 1`, `Page 1 of N` or `1 / N`.
4. In **Pages to number**, leave it empty for all pages, or type a range such as `2-20` to skip a cover page.
5. Set **Start at** if the first numbered page should show something other than 1.
6. Adjust **Font size**, **Margin** (in mm) and **Colour** if needed.
7. Check the live preview, then add the numbers and download.

## Choosing a format

| Format | Looks like | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2, 3 | 7 | Books, reports, clean minimal documents |
| Page 1 | Page 7 | Letters and formal documents |
| Page 1 of N | Page 7 of 32 | Contracts, bundles, anything where missing pages matter |
| 1 / N | 7 / 32 | Presentations and handouts |

"Page 1 of N" is the most useful for legal and official papers, because the reader can immediately tell whether a page is missing.

## Skipping the cover and contents pages

Many reports start numbering after the cover and the table of contents. Suppose your PDF has a cover, two contents pages, and 40 pages of content (43 pages in total). To number the content starting at 1:

- Type `4-43` in **Pages to number**.
- Set **Start at** to `1`.

The fourth page of the file now shows "1", and the cover and contents stay clean. For the `Page 1 of N` format, note that N is the total number of pages in the PDF.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Numbers overlapping the existing footer.** Many documents already have a footer line or address. Check the preview and move the number, or increase the margin.
- **Numbering before the final page order is settled.** If you later add, remove or reorder pages, the numbers will be wrong. Finish arranging with [Organize PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/organize-pdf/) or [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/) first, then number last.
- **Tiny numbers.** A font size below about 8 points is hard to read when printed. The default is a safe starting point.
- **Bright colours on formal documents.** Grey or black looks professional. Save colour for internal drafts.
- **Margins too small for printing.** Many printers cannot print right at the edge of the paper. A margin of 10 mm or more is safer for printed documents.

## Tips for professional-looking numbering

- Bottom centre is the most common position and suits almost any document.
- For documents that will be bound on the left, bottom right or top right keeps numbers visible when pages are flipped.
- Use a slightly lighter grey than the body text so numbers do not distract.
- If you also need "Confidential" or "Draft" on every page, add a watermark with [Watermark PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/watermark-pdf/) before or after numbering.

## Example: a numbered tender bundle

An engineering firm in Pune is submitting a tender. The bid documents run to 120 pages, assembled from technical sheets, financial statements and certificates. The tender instructions require every page to be numbered and the bundle to be indexed.

The bid manager merges the files in the required order, then numbers pages 2 to 120 in the `Page 1 of N` format at bottom right, keeping the cover page clean. The index on page 2 can now refer to exact page numbers, and the evaluator can check that nothing is missing at a glance. Where a tender requires digital signing of the final file, that step comes last, after numbering, as numbering changes the file.

## Checklist before you download

- The preview shows numbers in clear space on the first page, a middle page and the last page.
- The first numbered page shows the number you expect.
- Pages that should not be numbered (cover, blank separators) are excluded in the Pages box.
- Font size is readable when printed, and the colour is suitably understated.
- The page order is final, and you will not merge or reorder after numbering.

## Numbering a merged bundle for a submission

Application bundles for scholarships, visas or court filings often combine documents that already carry their own page numbers, such as a bank statement that says "Page 2 of 6". Adding a second, document-wide number in a different corner, for example top right in the `Page 7 of 32` format, gives the reviewer a single reference system for the whole bundle. Keep it small and grey so it does not compete with the original numbers.

## Limits worth knowing

Numbers are drawn using the standard Helvetica PDF font, so the tool supports Western digits and the word "Page". It does not add Roman numerals or Indian-language numerals. It also numbers based on the page's position in the file, so it cannot read and continue an existing printed numbering scheme.

## Private and quick

Adding numbers is a light task, so even long documents finish in seconds. The PDF is opened, numbered and saved inside your browser, and nothing is uploaded to a server. Close the tab and nothing remains anywhere except the file you downloaded.

Q: How do I skip the cover page when numbering?
A: Type the pages to number in the Pages box, for example 2 to the last page, and set Start at to 1 if you want the first numbered page to show 1. Leave the box empty to number every page from the beginning.

Q: Can I use the Page 1 of N format?
A: Yes. The format options are 1, 2, 3; Page 1; Page 1 of N; and 1 / N. The total N is the number of pages in the document, which is what readers usually expect when a file is printed or shared.

Q: Will page numbers cover existing text in the footer?
A: They can if the document already has text where the number goes. Use the live preview to check, then change the position (six positions are available), increase the margin, or reduce the font size until the number sits in clear space.

Q: Can I add numbers in Hindi or other scripts?
A: The numbers are drawn with a standard PDF font, so they appear as Western digits and English words such as Page. Indian-language numerals and words are not supported in this tool at the moment.

Q: Does adding page numbers change the rest of the PDF?
A: No. The numbers are added as a small text layer on top of each page. Existing text stays selectable, images keep their quality and the file size grows only slightly.

## How to convert PDF pages to images step by step

1. Open [PDF to Images](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-jpg/) and choose your PDF.
2. Select the pages you need by clicking thumbnails, or type them in the **Pages** box (for example `1, 3-5`). Leave it empty to convert every page.
3. Choose the **Format**: JPG or PNG.
4. For JPG, set the **JPG quality** slider. The default of 85% is a good balance.
5. Choose the **Resolution**: 72, 150 or 300 DPI.
6. Convert. A progress bar shows each page being rendered.
7. Download the image, or the ZIP if you converted several pages.

## Choosing format and resolution

| Goal | Format | Resolution | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Upload a certificate under a size limit | JPG | 150 DPI | Readable text, modest file size |
| Share on WhatsApp | JPG | 150 DPI | Quick to send, clear on phones |
| Print a page as an image | JPG or PNG | 300 DPI | Enough detail for paper |
| Put a chart or table on a slide | PNG | 150 or 300 DPI | Crisp lines and text, no JPEG artefacts |
| Quick preview or thumbnail | JPG | 72 DPI | Smallest file |

DPI stands for dots per inch. A standard A4 page is about 8.3 inches wide, so at 150 DPI the image is roughly 1,240 pixels wide, and at 300 DPI roughly 2,480 pixels. Doubling the DPI roughly quadruples the number of pixels, which is why 300 DPI files are so much bigger.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Picking 300 DPI for everything.** For screen viewing and most portals, 150 DPI is plenty, and the files are about a quarter of the size.
- **Using PNG for scanned photos.** PNG is lossless, so a scanned page saved as PNG can be very large. Use JPG for scans.
- **Setting JPG quality too low.** Below about 60%, text edges start to look smudgy. If the file is too big, lower the DPI before lowering quality drastically.
- **Forgetting to unzip.** On phones, the ZIP lands in Downloads. Open your Files app and extract it before attaching images elsewhere.
- **Converting when a PDF would do.** If the portal accepts PDFs, upload the PDF itself; it keeps text sharp at any zoom.

## Meeting image size limits on portals

When a portal asks for a JPG under a certain size, the limit and the required dimensions are set by that portal, and they vary. Read the instructions next to the upload button. A workable approach:

1. Convert the page at 150 DPI as JPG with quality around 80%.
2. Check the file size.
3. If it is still too large, use the [Image Compressor](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/) to reduce it further, or the [Image Resizer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/) if the portal specifies pixel dimensions.
4. Open the final image and confirm that every line of text is legible.

## Example: a certificate for a job portal

Farhan downloaded his degree certificate as a PDF from his university's portal. The recruitment site he is applying to wants the certificate as a JPG under a stated size. He opens the converter, selects page 1, chooses JPG at 150 DPI with 85% quality and downloads the image. It is a little over the limit, so he runs it through the image compressor and lands well under it, with the registration number and seal still sharp.

## What happens to links, forms and selectable text?

An image is a flat picture of the page. Once a page is converted, its text can no longer be selected, copied or searched, clickable links stop working, and form fields become part of the picture. That is fine for sharing and previews, but keep the original PDF as your master copy. If you later need to change something, edit the PDF and convert again rather than trying to edit the image.

If you need the words from an image later, an OCR tool such as [Image to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-to-text/) can recognise them again, but it is always more accurate to work from the original PDF.

## Single page vs many pages

When you convert one page, the image downloads directly with a name based on your PDF and the page number. When you convert several, they are packed into one ZIP named after your PDF, so your Downloads folder does not fill up with dozens of separate files. On a computer, double-click the ZIP to open it; on Android, open it in the Files app and tap Extract; on an iPhone, tap the ZIP in the Files app and it unpacks into a folder beside it.

## Going the other way

Need to turn images back into a PDF? Use [Images to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/), which places JPG and PNG files on A4 or Letter pages in the order you choose. And if what you actually want is the text from a PDF rather than a picture of it, PDF to Text extracts selectable text directly.

## Privacy and performance

Rendering pages happens inside your browser using a PDF engine that loads with the page. Your file is read from your device and the images are created on your device; nothing is uploaded. Rendering many pages at 300 DPI is demanding, so a long document takes longer on a phone than on a laptop. If your phone struggles, convert fewer pages at a time or choose a lower resolution.

Q: Which resolution should I choose, 72, 150 or 300 DPI?
A: Use 72 DPI for quick on-screen previews and small file sizes, 150 DPI for most sharing and portal uploads, and 300 DPI when the image will be printed or when you need to zoom into fine text. Higher DPI means sharper images but much larger files.

Q: Should I choose JPG or PNG?
A: JPG gives smaller files and suits scanned pages and photos. PNG is lossless and keeps text and line drawings perfectly crisp, but files are larger. For a page that is mostly text or a chart, PNG looks cleaner; for upload size limits, JPG is easier.

Q: Can I convert just one page of a PDF to an image?
A: Yes. Click that page in the preview or type its number in the Pages box. Leave the box empty to convert every page. A single page downloads directly as an image, while several pages come packed in a ZIP.

Q: Why would a portal want a JPG instead of a PDF?
A: Some application forms accept only image formats for certain fields, such as a photograph, signature or a single certificate. Converting the PDF page to JPG lets you upload it there. Always check the format and size limit stated for that field.

Q: Does it work for password-protected PDFs?
A: No. A password-protected PDF must be unlocked first. Open it with the password in a PDF reader, save or print an unprotected copy, and then convert that copy to images.

## How to Extract Text from a PDF and Save It as a TXT File

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/extract-text-from-pdf-free/
Tool: PDF to Text (https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-text/)

Quick answer: To extract text from a PDF, open a PDF-to-text tool, load the file, and copy all the text or download it as a .txt file, optionally with page separators. BISCS India’s PDF to Text reads the PDF’s selectable text in your browser without uploading it. Scanned PDFs need OCR, which a separate tool provides.

To extract text from a PDF, open [PDF to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-text/), choose your file, and either click **Copy all text** or **Download .txt**. The tool reads every page and gives you the plain text, with optional "Page X of Y" separators so you know where each part came from.

It only works on text that is selectable in the PDF. If your document is a scanned image, you need OCR, which the separate [Image to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-to-text/) tool provides.

## When plain text is exactly what you need

Copying text from a PDF viewer is often painful: line breaks in odd places, columns jumbled, one page at a time. Extracting everything at once is faster when you want to:

- **Reuse content**: quote a clause from a policy, paste a paragraph into an email, or build notes from a report.
- **Search across a long document** in your favourite text editor.
- **Feed text into other tools**, such as a word counter, a translation tool or a spreadsheet.
- **Archive the words** of a document in a small, future-proof format.
- **Read on a small phone screen**, where reflowing plain text is easier than zooming into a PDF.

## How to extract text step by step

1. Open [PDF to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-text/) and choose your PDF.
2. Wait while each page is read. A progress bar shows how far it has got.
3. Look at the preview to check that the text came through.
4. Decide whether to keep **Include page separators** switched on.
5. Click **Copy all text** to paste it elsewhere, or **Download .txt** to save it.

## Digital PDF or scanned PDF?

This is the single most important thing to understand about extracting text.

| | Digital PDF | Scanned PDF |
|---|---|---|
| How it was made | Exported from Word, a website, accounting software or a bank portal | Photographed or scanned from paper |
| Can you select a word in a viewer? | Yes | No, or the whole page selects as an image |
| PDF to Text works? | Yes, accurately | No, little or no text found |
| What to use instead | — | Image to Text (OCR) |

A quick test: open the PDF and try to highlight a single word. If you can, this tool will extract it. The tool also warns you when it finds very little text, which is a strong hint the pages are scans.

## What the output looks like

The result is plain UTF-8 text. That means:

- Paragraphs come through as lines of text; bold, italics and fonts are dropped.
- Tables become rows of words separated by spaces, not neat columns.
- Headers and footers on each page (company name, page numbers) are included like any other text.
- Multi-column layouts, such as newsletters, may come out column by column or line by line depending on how the PDF was made.

If you need headings, lists and basic formatting kept, [PDF to Word](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/) is the better choice.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Trying to extract from a scan.** You will get nothing useful. Use OCR instead.
- **Expecting a perfect table.** For bank statements and price lists, plain text loses the column structure. Copy specific rows instead, or convert to Word.
- **Ignoring legacy-font Hindi PDFs.** Some older documents in Indian languages use fonts that map characters in non-standard ways, so the extracted text looks like gibberish. OCR on the page images usually works better for those.
- **Leaving separators on when pasting into a form.** The "Page X of Y" lines are helpful for reference but not for clean copy. Turn the option off before copying.
- **Assuming the text is complete.** Text inside images, such as a scanned signature block or a logo, is not extracted.

## Practical examples

**A student** has a 60-page PDF of lecture notes and wants to make flashcards. Extracting the text into a .txt file lets her search for key terms and paste definitions straight into her flashcard app.

**An office assistant** needs the exact wording of five clauses from a 40-page lease to put into an email to the landlord. Copying all the text once and picking out the clauses is quicker than copying from the PDF page by page.

**A small business owner** in Indore wants to check how often a supplier's name appears in a long contract. Extracting the text and using Find in a text editor answers it in seconds.

## Tips for cleaner text

- Turn off page separators when you need one continuous text, and on when you need to cite pages.
- After pasting, use a find-and-replace tool to remove repeated headers or footers.
- For documents with some scanned pages, extract the text here first, then run OCR only on the scanned pages.
- Save the .txt file with a meaningful name; it is tiny and easy to search later.

## PDF to Text, PDF to Word or OCR?

| You need… | Best tool |
|---|---|
| The words only, quickly, from a digital PDF | PDF to Text |
| Editable document with headings, lists and basic formatting | PDF to Word |
| Text from a scanned PDF, photo or screenshot | Image to Text (OCR) |
| Text from one specific page as a picture | PDF to Images, then OCR if needed |

For most digital documents, PDF to Text is the fastest route because there is no layout to rebuild. It reads the text the PDF already contains, so it is also exact: there are no recognition errors of the kind OCR sometimes makes with similar-looking letters and numbers.

## Is the extracted text accurate?

For a digital PDF, yes, the characters are taken directly from the file. Occasionally a PDF uses an unusual font encoding, and some characters come out wrong. Ligatures (such as "fi" printed as one symbol) and special dashes can also appear slightly differently. If the text looks wrong in places, compare with the PDF and fix those spots by hand.

## Private by default

Text extraction runs in your browser using a PDF engine loaded with the page. The document is never uploaded, so you can extract text from contracts, medical reports or bank letters without sending them anywhere. The .txt file is created on your device, and closing the tab clears everything else.

Q: Why is the extracted text empty or very short?
A: The PDF is probably a scan, where each page is a picture rather than real text. This tool reads only selectable text and tells you when very little is found. For scans, use Image to Text, which uses OCR to recognise English, Hindi and Bengali.

Q: Does PDF to Text keep tables and formatting?
A: No. The output is plain text, so bold, fonts, colours and table borders are lost, and table columns become text separated by spaces or line breaks. If you need formatting, convert the PDF to Word instead, which keeps headings, lists and basic styling.

Q: What are page separators?
A: When the option is on, the text file includes a line such as Page 3 of 12 before each page’s text. That helps you find where something came from in a long document. Turn it off if you want one continuous block of text.

Q: Can it extract Hindi text from a PDF?
A: If the PDF contains real, selectable Hindi text, it can usually be extracted. Some older Indian-language PDFs use non-Unicode legacy fonts, and their text may come out as garbled characters. In that case OCR on the page images often gives better results.

To convert a PDF to Word, open [PDF to Word](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/), choose your PDF, pick **Editable text** (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold and italic you can edit) or **Exact look** (each page as a picture), and download the `.docx` file. ## Two ways to convert, for two different needs

The most important choice is the mode. Picking the right one avoids disappointment.

| Mode | What you get | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| Editable text | Real Word text with headings, paragraphs, lists, bold and italic | You need to change wording, reuse text or update a document |
| Exact look | Each PDF page placed as an image in the Word file | You need the document to look identical, for example to add notes around it |

Editable mode deliberately simplifies complex layouts. Tables, multiple columns, text boxes and pictures are reduced to clean text, because recreating every design detail usually produces a Word file that is hard to edit. Exact look keeps appearance perfectly but the text cannot be edited.

## How to convert PDF to Word step by step

1. Open [PDF to Word](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/) and choose your PDF, or drag it into the box.
2. Pick **Editable text** or **Exact look**.
3. In Editable mode, decide whether to **Start each PDF page on a new page** in Word.
4. If the tool reports scanned pages, keep **Recognise scanned pages (OCR)** ticked and choose the **OCR language**: English, Hindi, Bengali, English + Hindi or English + Bengali.
5. In Exact look, choose **Image quality**: Standard or High.
6. Check the preview of the detected text, page by page.
7. Convert and download your `.docx` file.

## How it handles scanned PDFs

When a page has almost no selectable text, the tool marks it as scanned and tells you which pages are affected. With OCR switched on, it renders those pages and recognises the text on your device.

A few honest points about OCR:

- **The first run downloads the engine and language data** to your browser once; later runs reuse it.
- **Accuracy depends on the scan.** A clean, straight, well-lit page gives good results; a tilted phone photo with shadows gives more errors.
- **Proofread numbers and names.** OCR can confuse similar shapes, such as 0 and O, or 1 and l.
- **Choose the right language.** Ticking "English + Hindi" for a mixed document works better than English alone, but using only the languages present is faster and more accurate.

If your scans are phone photos, capturing them with [Scan to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/) first (which straightens and cleans pages) noticeably improves OCR.

## Where PDF to Word saves real time

**Updating an old document.** The original Word file of a company policy is lost, but the PDF survives. Convert it, update the clauses, and export a new PDF.

**Reusing a resume.** You have only a PDF of your CV. Convert it, edit the latest job and skills, and save again.

**Editing a rent agreement draft.** A landlord sends a PDF draft. Convert it, make your proposed changes visible in Word, and send it back for discussion.

**Hindi or Bengali office letters.** A scanned circular in Hindi needs to be quoted in a reply. OCR with the Hindi option recovers the text so you do not have to retype it.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Expecting a pixel-perfect editable copy.** No converter can perfectly turn PDF layouts into editable Word. Use Editable text for content and Exact look for appearance.
- **Converting when you only need the words.** If you just want the text, [PDF to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-text/) is quicker.
- **Skipping the proofread after OCR.** Always read through scanned-page text, particularly amounts, dates and ID numbers.
- **Trying a password-protected PDF.** Unlock it first by saving an unprotected copy with the password.
- **Converting a PDF just to fill in a form.** Fillable forms are easier with [Fill PDF Form](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/), and flat forms with Edit PDF.

## Digital PDF or scanned PDF: what to expect

| Source PDF | Text accuracy | Speed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exported from Word, Google Docs or a website | Exact, taken from the file | Seconds | Best results; headings and lists detected from font sizes and layout |
| Bank or government e-statement | Exact | Seconds | Tables become text; use Exact look if the layout matters |
| Clean office scan | Good with OCR | Slower, page by page | Proofread figures |
| Tilted phone photo saved as PDF | Variable | Slower | Rescan with a document scanner for better OCR |
| Mixed (some pages scanned) | Exact for digital pages, OCR for the rest | Depends on scanned page count | The tool lists which pages are scanned |

Headings are worked out from the relative size and weight of the text, so a well-structured digital PDF turns into a Word document with proper Heading styles. That makes it easy to generate a table of contents or reorganise sections in Word afterwards.

## Checklist after converting

- Headings came through as headings, so Word's navigation pane works.
- Lists are still lists, not lines starting with stray symbols.
- Scanned pages have been read and proofread.
- Page breaks fall where you want them.
- Any tables or images that were simplified have been fixed or recreated if needed.

## Converting back to PDF

After editing, save from Word as PDF, or use [Word to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/word-to-pdf/). Then you can merge, sign or compress the new PDF as needed.

## Privacy and performance

Everything happens on your device: the PDF is read in your browser, OCR runs locally, and the Word file is assembled without any server. Long scanned documents take a while, since each page is recognised on your own processor, and a laptop is noticeably faster than an older phone. Digital PDFs with selectable text convert in seconds.

Q: Will my PDF look exactly the same in Word?
A: In Editable text mode, the text, headings, lists, bold and italic come through, but tables, columns, text boxes and pictures are simplified, so the layout will differ. If the appearance matters more than editing, choose Exact look, which places each page as an image in the Word file.

Q: Can I convert a scanned PDF to Word?
A: Yes. Pages without selectable text are detected as scanned, and with the OCR option on (it is on by default) their text is recognised in English, Hindi, Bengali or a mix. Accuracy depends on scan quality, so proofread the result, especially numbers and names.

Q: Why is the first OCR conversion slower?
A: The first time you use OCR, the recognition engine and language data download once to your browser. After that they are reused, so later conversions start faster. Digital PDFs with selectable text do not need OCR at all and convert quickly.

Q: Does it convert tables into Word tables?
A: Not reliably. Editable mode focuses on text flow: headings, paragraphs and lists. Table content comes through as text, but borders and cell structure are simplified. For documents that are mostly tables, consider Exact look or recreating the table in Word.

Q: Is my PDF uploaded during conversion?
A: No. Reading the PDF, recognising scanned pages and building the Word file all happen inside your browser, using libraries served from this site. Your document never leaves your device, so it suits confidential files.

## How to Calculate Percentages: Formulas, Examples and a Free Tool

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/how-to-calculate-percentage-easily/
Tool: Percentage Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/)

Quick answer: To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100: 15% of 2,400 is 2,400 × 15 ÷ 100 = 360. For percentage change, divide the difference by the original value and multiply by 100. BISCS India's free Percentage Calculator handles six common percentage questions instantly.

Percentages answer one question: how big is one number compared with another, if the whole is 100? To find X% of a number, multiply the number by X and divide by 100. To find what percent one number is of another, divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.

That covers most everyday needs, from exam marks and salary hikes to sale discounts and GST. The rest of this guide shows the formulas for each situation, with worked examples you can check in the free [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/).

## What are the basic percentage formulas?

Almost every percentage problem is a rearrangement of one relationship: **part = whole × percent ÷ 100**. Knowing which of the three values you are missing tells you which formula to use.

| What you want | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| X% of a number | number × X ÷ 100 | 15% of 2,400 = 360 |
| What % is A of B | A ÷ B × 100 | 360 of 1,200 = 30% |
| Percentage change | (new − old) ÷ old × 100 | 50,000 to 65,000 = +30% |
| Increase by X% | value × (1 + X ÷ 100) | 1,000 + 18% = 1,180 |
| Decrease by X% | value × (1 − X ÷ 100) | 2,999 − 20% = 2,399.20 |
| A is P% of what | A ÷ P × 100 | 45 is 30% of 150 |
| Percentage difference | difference ÷ average × 100 | 80 and 120 = 40% |

The last row trips people up. Percentage *difference* compares two values with no "before" or "after", so it divides by their average. Percentage *change* has a clear starting point and divides by that.

## How do I use the BISCS Percentage Calculator?

The tool shows six small calculators on one page, each written as a plain sentence, so you never have to remember which formula applies.

1. Open the [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) in any browser, on a phone or computer.
2. Find the card that matches your question, such as "What is __% of __?" or "Percentage change".
3. Type your numbers into the boxes. Commas are fine, so 1,25,000 and 125000 both work.
4. Read the answer in the highlighted box. A small line beside it shows the working, for example "15% × 2,400".
5. For increase or decrease, use the toggle above the boxes to switch direction.

Results update as you type, and nothing is sent anywhere. The calculations run on your device, so salary or business figures stay private.

## Worked examples from everyday life in India

### Salary hike

Your monthly salary is ₹42,000 and you are offered an 8% increment. 8% of 42,000 is 3,360, so the new salary is ₹45,360. In the tool, use "Increase or decrease by %" with 42,000 and 8.

### Exam marks

You scored 437 out of 500. 437 ÷ 500 × 100 = 87.4%. Use "What percent is X of Y" with 437 and 500. Some universities convert CGPA to percentage using their own multiplier, so check your institution's rule for official forms.

### Sale discount

A kurta priced at ₹2,999 is on 20% off. The discount is ₹599.80 and you pay ₹2,399.20. For stacked offers like "20% + extra 10%", apply them one after the other: 2,399.20 less 10% is ₹2,159.28, which is a total discount of 28%, not 30%. The [Discount Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) handles these in one go.

### Price before GST

A bill shows ₹1,180 including 18% GST and you want the pre-tax price. The final amount is 118% of the base, so the base is 1,180 ÷ 118 × 100 = ₹1,000. Use the "X is P% of what?" card with 1,180 and 118. For full CGST and SGST splits, the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/) is quicker.

### Business growth

Monthly sales moved from ₹50,000 to ₹65,000. The change is 15,000 ÷ 50,000 × 100 = +30%. If you want the yearly growth rate over several years, a [CAGR Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/cagr-calculator/) is the right tool, because simple percentage change ignores compounding.

## Common percentage mistakes to avoid

- **Using the wrong base.** A fall from 120 to 80 is −33.33%, but a rise from 80 to 120 is +50%. Always divide by the starting value.
- **Assuming rises and falls cancel.** ₹1,000 up 50% is ₹1,500; down 50% from there is ₹750, not ₹1,000.
- **Adding stacked discounts.** "20% + 10% off" is a 28% total discount, because the second discount applies to a smaller price.
- **Mixing up percent and percentage points.** A home loan rate going from 6.5% to 7% is a rise of 0.5 percentage points, which is about 7.7% in relative terms.
- **Removing GST by subtracting 18%.** Taking 18% off ₹1,180 gives ₹967.60, which is wrong. Divide by 1.18 instead to get ₹1,000.
- **Confusing profit margin and markup.** A product bought at ₹800 and sold at ₹1,000 has a 25% markup on cost but a 20% margin on the selling price. The [Profit Margin Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/) shows both.

## Mental maths shortcuts worth knowing

You can do many percentages in your head with a few tricks:

- **10%** is the number divided by 10. 10% of 3,450 is 345.
- **5%** is half of 10%. So 5% of 3,450 is 172.50.
- **1%** is the number divided by 100. Build other rates from it: 18% is 10% + 5% + 3 × 1%.
- **Swap the numbers.** X% of Y equals Y% of X. 8% of 50 is the same as 50% of 8, which is 4.
- **25% and 50%** are a quarter and a half, and 20% is a fifth.

These are handy for quick checks at a shop counter. For anything that matters, such as an invoice, a loan comparison or official marks, confirm the figure with a calculator.

## When should you use a percentage calculator?

Mental maths is fine for round numbers. A calculator earns its place when:

- the numbers have decimals or are large, such as ₹18,47,250;
- you need to work backwards, such as finding the original price;
- you are comparing two values and need to know which to divide by;
- you want a quick check before sending a quotation, salary letter or report.

The BISCS tool also shows the working next to each answer, which makes it useful for students learning the method, not just for getting a number.

## Tips for accurate results

- Keep full precision until the final step. Rounding 33.333% to 33% early can shift a large total noticeably.
- When reporting change, say what it is relative to: "sales rose 30% compared with April".
- For money, round only the final amount to two decimal places.
- If the starting value is zero, percentage change is undefined. The tool warns you instead of showing a misleading figure.

Percentages are simple once you know which number is the whole. Bookmark the [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) for the moments when you would rather not work it out on paper.

Q: How do I calculate the percentage of marks?
A: Divide the marks you scored by the maximum marks and multiply by 100. For example, 437 out of 500 is 437 ÷ 500 × 100 = 87.4%. If your board or university uses a different method, such as best-of-five subjects or CGPA conversion, follow their official rule instead.

Q: What is the difference between percentage and percentage points?
A: Percentage points describe the simple gap between two percentages, while percentage change describes the relative change. If a loan rate moves from 6.5% to 7%, it rose by 0.5 percentage points, but that is a relative increase of about 7.7% on the original rate.

Q: Why does a 50% rise followed by a 50% fall not bring me back to the start?
A: Because the second percentage is applied to a different base. ₹1,000 rising 50% becomes ₹1,500, and a 50% fall on ₹1,500 removes ₹750, leaving ₹750. Each percentage is always a share of the value it is applied to at that moment.

Q: How do I find the original price before a percentage was added?
A: Divide the final amount by (1 + rate ÷ 100). If a price including 18% GST is ₹1,180, the original is 1,180 ÷ 1.18 = ₹1,000. In the calculator, use the “X is P% of what?” box and enter 1,180 and 118.

Q: Is the percentage calculator free and private?
A: Yes. The calculator is free to use without sign-up, and all the arithmetic happens in your browser as you type. The numbers you enter are not sent to a server, so you can use it for salary, marks or business figures without worry.
