## PPF Calculator: Public Provident Fund Maturity Over 15 Years

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/ppf-calculator-maturity-15-years/
Tool: PPF Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/ppf-calculator/)

Quick answer: A PPF calculator compounds your yearly deposits at the PPF rate over 15 years. Depositing the maximum ₹1.5 lakh every year before 5 April at 7.1% gives about ₹40.68 lakh at maturity, of which ₹18.18 lakh is tax-free interest. BISCS India's free PPF Calculator also models 5-year extensions with or without fresh deposits.

A PPF (Public Provident Fund) calculator estimates how much your account will hold after 15 years of yearly deposits. Each year, your opening balance plus that year's deposit earns interest at the PPF rate, and the interest is added to the balance. If you invest ₹1.5 lakh every year at 7.1%, the account grows to about ₹40.68 lakh after 15 years.

Of that, ₹22.5 lakh is what you put in and about ₹18.18 lakh is interest, all of it tax-free. The free [PPF Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ppf-calculator/) shows this growth year by year and lets you test 5-year extensions.

## How is PPF interest calculated?

The scheme calculates interest on the lowest balance between the 5th and the last day of each month and credits it once a year, at the end of the financial year. If you deposit before 5 April, your money earns interest for all twelve months.

The BISCS calculator assumes exactly that: one deposit at the start of each financial year. Each year it works out:

**closing balance = (opening balance + deposit) × (1 + rate ÷ 100)**

For ₹1,50,000 at 7.1%, year one ends at ₹1,60,650. Year two starts with that, adds another ₹1,50,000 and earns 7.1% on ₹3,10,650, and so on. By year 15, the interest credited for that single year is about ₹2.7 lakh.

## How to use the BISCS PPF Calculator

1. Open the [PPF Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ppf-calculator/).
2. Enter your **yearly investment**, between ₹500 and ₹1,50,000.
3. Set the **interest rate**. It defaults to 7.1%; change it to the rate currently notified.
4. Under **Extend after 15 years**, pick No, or add 5, 10, 15 or 20 years.
5. If you extend, choose whether you will **keep investing** or **stop investing** during the extension.
6. Read the maturity value, total invested and tax-free interest, and open the year-by-year table. Year 15 is highlighted so you can see the original maturity point.

The tool runs locally in your browser, so your savings plan stays on your device.

## What can PPF grow to? Worked examples at 7.1%

| Plan | Total invested | Maturity value | Interest earned |
|---|---|---|---|
| ₹50,000 a year for 15 years | ₹7.50 lakh | ₹13.56 lakh | ₹6.06 lakh |
| ₹1.5 lakh a year for 15 years | ₹22.50 lakh | ₹40.68 lakh | ₹18.18 lakh |
| ₹1.5 lakh a year for 20 years (5-year extension, deposits continue) | ₹30.00 lakh | ₹66.58 lakh | ₹36.58 lakh |
| ₹1.5 lakh for 15 years, then 5 more years without deposits | ₹22.50 lakh | ₹57.33 lakh | ₹34.83 lakh |

The extension rows show where PPF really shines. Five extra years with deposits add about ₹26 lakh to the maturity value, more than the extra ₹7.5 lakh you invest. Even without new deposits, the existing balance grows by about ₹16.6 lakh in those five years.

## PPF rules worth knowing

- **Deposit limits:** minimum ₹500 and maximum ₹1,50,000 per financial year.
- **Tenure:** the account matures after 15 full financial years, and can then be extended in 5-year blocks.
- **Tax treatment:** interest and maturity are tax-free; deposits qualify for Section 80C in the old regime only. You can compare regimes in the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/).
- **Rate changes:** the government notifies small savings rates quarterly.
- **Liquidity:** loans and partial withdrawals are allowed only after certain years and within limits, so treat PPF as long-term money.

Because these rules are set by the government and can change, confirm current details with India Post, your bank or the National Savings Institute before acting.

## Why tax-free interest matters

A PPF rate can look similar to an FD rate, but the comparison changes after tax. FD interest is taxed every year at your slab rate. For someone in the 30% slab, adding 4% cess, a 7% FD keeps only about 4.8% after tax. PPF interest at 7.1% is tax-free, so the full amount stays in the account and compounds.

Over 15 years, that gap compounds into a large difference. This is why PPF remains popular with salaried people in higher tax brackets who want a guaranteed-return component in their savings, even though the money is locked in for a long time. For people with income below the taxable limit, the tax advantage matters less, and liquidity may matter more. If you are comparing options, run the deposit through the [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/) and then reduce the interest by your tax rate to compare fairly.

## Tips to get more from your PPF

1. **Deposit early in the year.** Paying by 5 April each year earns interest for twelve months rather than fewer.
2. **If you deposit monthly, pay by the 5th.** A deposit on the 6th misses that month's interest.
3. **Do not skip the minimum.** Missing the ₹500 minimum makes the account inactive until you regularise it with a penalty.
4. **Decide on extension before maturity.** Extending with deposits requires a timely request under the scheme rules.
5. **Use PPF as the stable part of a portfolio.** For higher-risk, higher-potential growth, compare with a [SIP Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sip-calculator/) estimate.

## Common mistakes

- Depositing more than ₹1.5 lakh in a year, expecting extra interest.
- Assuming the 80C deduction applies under the new tax regime.
- Planning on a single rate for 15 years without testing a lower one.
- Treating PPF like a savings account and expecting easy withdrawals in the early years.

## Limitations and a quick caveat

The calculator assumes one deposit before 5 April every year and the same rate throughout. If you deposit in instalments or later in the year, your actual balance will be a little lower. The real rate will change over 15 years, sometimes up and sometimes down.

This article is general information, not financial or tax advice. For the authoritative rules and the current rate, check India Post, the Ministry of Finance notifications or your bank, and confirm tax treatment with the Income Tax Department or a tax professional.

Q: What is the maximum I can deposit in PPF in a year?
A: The limit is ₹1,50,000 per financial year across your own PPF account and any account you hold for a minor child, and the minimum is ₹500. Deposits above the limit do not earn interest and are not eligible for a tax deduction. Check the current rules on the India Post or National Savings Institute website.

Q: Why should I deposit before 5 April?
A: PPF interest for each month is calculated on the lowest balance between the 5th and the last day of that month. A deposit made by the 5th of April earns interest for all twelve months of the financial year. A deposit made later in the year misses interest for the months before it.

Q: What happens when my PPF account completes 15 years?
A: You can close the account and withdraw the full balance, or extend it in blocks of five years. During an extension you can continue depositing or stop, and the balance keeps earning interest either way. The form and deadline for choosing an extension with deposits are set by the scheme rules.

Q: Is PPF interest really tax-free?
A: Yes, PPF interest and the maturity amount are exempt from income tax. Deposits qualify for a deduction under Section 80C within the ₹1.5 lakh limit, but only if you choose the old tax regime. Under the new regime, there is no 80C deduction, though the interest and maturity remain tax-free.

Q: Is the PPF interest rate fixed for 15 years?
A: No. The government reviews small savings rates every quarter, and the rate in force applies to your whole balance for that period. The calculator uses one rate throughout, so treat its result as an estimate and try a slightly lower rate to see a cautious outcome.

## Profit Margin vs Markup: How to Calculate Both (With Examples)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/profit-margin-vs-markup-calculator/
Tool: Profit Margin Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/)

Quick answer: Profit margin is profit as a percentage of the selling price, while markup is profit as a percentage of cost. An item bought for ₹750 and sold for ₹1,000 has a 25% margin but a 33.33% markup. BISCS India's free Profit Margin Calculator works out both, or finds the selling price for a target margin or markup.

Profit margin and markup both describe profit, but against different bases. **Margin** is profit as a share of the selling price: (price − cost) ÷ price × 100. **Markup** is profit as a share of the cost: (price − cost) ÷ cost × 100.

Buy a product at ₹750 and sell it at ₹1,000, and you make ₹250 profit. That is a **25% margin** but a **33.33% markup**. Mixing these up is one of the most common pricing errors in small businesses. The free [Profit Margin Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/) shows both numbers side by side.

## Margin and markup formulas

| Measure | Formula | ₹750 cost, ₹1,000 price |
|---|---|---|
| Profit | Price − Cost | ₹250 |
| Margin | Profit ÷ Price × 100 | 25% |
| Markup | Profit ÷ Cost × 100 | 33.33% |
| Price from margin | Cost ÷ (1 − margin) | 750 ÷ 0.75 = ₹1,000 |
| Price from markup | Cost × (1 + markup) | 750 × 1.3333 = ₹1,000 |

Because margin uses the bigger number (price) as its base, it is always smaller than markup for the same profit.

## How to use the BISCS Profit Margin Calculator

1. Open the [Profit Margin Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/).
2. Pick a mode:
   - **Cost & price** to find margin and markup from known figures.
   - **Price from margin** to find the selling price for a target margin.
   - **Price from markup** to find the selling price for a target markup.
3. Enter the **cost price**, plus the selling price, desired margin or desired markup.
4. Optionally enter a **quantity** to see total revenue and total profit for a batch.
5. Read the profit, margin, markup and price. If the price is below cost, the tool shows the loss per unit and a warning.

All calculations run in your browser, so your costing never leaves your device.

## The classic pricing mistake

Ritu runs a small home-décor shop in Jaipur. A lamp costs her ₹700. She wants a 30% margin, so she adds 30% to the cost and prices it at ₹910.

But ₹210 profit on a ₹910 price is a margin of only about **23.08%**. To get a true 30% margin she needs to price at 700 ÷ 0.70 = **₹1,000**. On 200 lamps a year, the difference is ₹18,000 of profit she thought she was earning.

## Quick margin-to-markup conversion

| Target margin | Markup needed |
|---|---|
| 10% | 11.11% |
| 20% | 25% |
| 25% | 33.33% |
| 33.33% | 50% |
| 50% | 100% |

The formula is **markup = margin ÷ (1 − margin)**, using decimals. For example, a 40% margin needs 0.40 ÷ 0.60 = 66.67% markup.

## Example: the real margin on a marketplace sale

Margins shrink quickly when you sell online. Here is a hypothetical product sold through a marketplace, with all figures excluding GST:

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Selling price | ₹1,000 |
| Product cost | ₹600 |
| Marketplace commission (15%) | ₹150 |
| Shipping | ₹60 |
| Payment collection fee (2%) | ₹20 |
| **Profit** | **₹170** |

Looking only at product cost, the margin seems to be 40%. Once commission, shipping and fees are added to the cost (₹830 in total), the margin is 17%. To get this in the calculator, enter ₹830 as the cost price and ₹1,000 as the selling price. Returns, packaging and advertising would reduce it further, so build them in when you set prices. Commission and fee rates differ by platform and category, so use the figures from your own seller agreement.

## Margins for service businesses

Freelancers and agencies can use the same idea with time as the cost. If a designer's monthly costs, including their own target salary, come to ₹90,000 and they bill about 120 hours, each hour costs ₹750. Pricing at ₹1,000 an hour gives a 25% margin. Choosing **Price from margin** with ₹750 as cost shows the hourly rate needed for any target margin.

## When to use margin and when to use markup

- **Use markup** when you set prices from cost, for example a trader adding a fixed percentage to purchase price.
- **Use margin** when you look at profitability, compare products or talk to lenders and investors, since financial statements report margins on sales.
- **Use both** when negotiating with distributors and retailers, who may quote "margin" but mean markup. Always confirm which one is meant.

## What happens when costs rise?

If your supplier raises the cost from ₹750 to ₹800 and you keep the price at ₹1,000, your margin drops from 25% to 20%. To restore a 25% margin, the new price is 800 ÷ 0.75 = ₹1,066.67. Checking this every time a purchase price changes keeps small cost increases from silently eating your profit.

## Pricing tips for small businesses

1. **Price before GST.** Work out margin on the taxable value, then add GST with the [GST Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/).
2. **Include all variable costs.** Packaging, shipping, marketplace commission and payment gateway fees all reduce profit per unit.
3. **Plan for discounts.** If you run a 20% sale, a 25% margin almost vanishes. Test sale prices with the [Discount Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) and recheck the margin here.
4. **Know your break-even.** At a selling price equal to cost, margin is 0%. Anything less is a loss.
5. **Review regularly.** When supplier prices rise, recalculate before your margin quietly erodes.

## Common mistakes

- Treating markup as margin, as in Ritu's example.
- Calculating margin on GST-inclusive prices, which overstates revenue.
- Forgetting returns, damage and unsold stock when estimating real profit.
- Expecting a 100% margin to be possible; it is not, because profit cannot exceed the price.
- Using percentage figures without checking them against actual rupees. The [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) helps with quick checks.

## Limits of the calculator

The tool works per unit using the cost and price you provide. It does not allocate overheads, account for taxes on profit or model volume discounts. Its margin is therefore closest to a gross margin unless you build overheads into the cost.

This guide is general information to help with pricing arithmetic, not accounting or tax advice. For statutory accounts, GST treatment of discounts and schemes, or business valuation, consult a chartered accountant, and confirm GST rules on the GST portal or CBIC website.

Q: How do I find the selling price for a target margin?
A: Divide the cost by (1 minus the margin as a decimal). For a 30% margin on a cost of ₹700, the price is 700 ÷ 0.70 = ₹1,000. Adding 30% to cost gives only ₹910, which is a margin of about 23%. The calculator's Price from margin mode does this for you.

Q: Can profit margin be more than 100%?
A: No, not for a positive price. Margin is profit divided by price, and profit can never exceed the price, so the margin is always below 100%. Markup, on the other hand, can be any size: buying at ₹100 and selling at ₹300 is a 200% markup but a 66.67% margin.

Q: Should I include GST when calculating margin?
A: For a GST-registered business, calculate margin on prices excluding GST, because the GST you collect is passed on to the government after adjusting input tax credit. If you are not registered and cannot claim input credit, the GST you pay on purchases is part of your cost.

Q: Is this gross margin or net margin?
A: The calculator gives a margin on whatever cost you enter. If you enter only the purchase or production cost, the result is close to gross margin. To estimate net margin, include a share of overheads such as rent, salaries, delivery, payment fees and marketing in the cost per unit.

## Creating a UPI payment QR code

A UPI QR code lets customers pay you by scanning with any UPI app. The format and rules for UPI payment QR codes are set by the **National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)**, which runs UPI. The BISCS tool creates a standard UPI payment link containing:

- **UPI ID (VPA)**, such as `shopname@okbank`. This is required.
- **Payee name**, shown to the payer.
- **Amount**, optional. Leave it blank so the payer can type any amount, or fill it for a fixed fee.
- **Note**, optional, such as "Class 10 tuition – November".

### Before you print a UPI QR code

1. **Verify the UPI ID** letter by letter. One wrong character sends money to someone else, or nowhere.
2. **Scan it with your own UPI app** and check the name that appears is yours or your business's.
3. **Make a small test payment,** such as ₹1, and confirm it reaches the right bank account.
4. **Keep a fixed-amount code** only for fixed fees. For a shop counter, a code without an amount is more flexible.

A self-made UPI code is fine for small sellers, tutors and personal collections. If you need business features like instant payment alerts, settlement reports or a sound box, use the merchant QR issued by your bank or payment provider.

### Safety tip for customers and sellers

You **never** need to scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN to **receive** money. The PIN is only for sending. Fraudsters sometimes send a QR code claiming it will credit a refund or prize. Do not scan it. Shop owners should also check from time to time that nobody has stuck a different QR code over theirs.

## Wi-Fi QR codes for home and business

Enter your **network name (SSID)**, **password** and **security type** (usually WPA/WPA2/WPA3). Tick **Hidden network** if your router does not broadcast its name. Guests scan the code with their phone camera and connect without typing a long password. Print it for a guest room or café table, and make a new one whenever you change the password.

## Error correction, size and colours explained

QR codes contain extra data so they still scan if part of the code is damaged or covered.

| Level | Recovers up to | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Low (L) | About 7% | Clean screens, maximum data |
| Medium (M) | About 15% | Most everyday uses |
| Quartile (Q) | About 25% | Printed items that may get scuffed |
| High (H) | About 30% | Codes with a logo or rough handling |

Higher levels make the pattern denser, so keep the content short where you can. A long URL produces a crowded code; a short link scans more easily.

**Colours:** dark modules on a light background scan best. The tool warns you if the contrast is low or if you have chosen light modules on a dark background, which some apps cannot read.

**Margin:** keep a clear border, called the quiet zone, of about four modules around the code. The default setting does this.

## Common QR code mistakes

- **Not testing before printing** hundreds of flyers or standees.
- **Printing too small,** especially on visiting cards. Test at the final size.
- **Low contrast colours,** like light grey on white or brand colours that are too similar.
- **Oversized logos** covering too much of the pattern.
- **Long URLs with tracking clutter** that make the code dense. Shorten them or remove unnecessary parameters.
- **Typos in a UPI ID or Wi-Fi password,** which make the code useless or, worse, misdirect payments.

## Practical tips

- Add a short line of text beside the code, such as "Scan to pay" or "Scan for menu", so people know what to expect.
- Use SVG for large prints like banners, so edges stay crisp.
- If you want to measure scans from a campaign, add UTM tags to your link with the [UTM Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/utm-builder/) before creating the code.
- For products and inventory, a linear barcode from the [Barcode Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/barcode-generator/) may suit scanners better.
- Add your UPI ID to bills made with the [GST Invoice Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/) so customers have it in writing too.

QR codes are one of the simplest ways to connect paper to phones. Create yours with the [QR Code Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/qr-code-generator/), test it once, and it will keep working for as long as the content stays valid.

Q: Do QR codes from this generator expire?
A: No. The generator makes static QR codes: the information is stored inside the pattern itself, not on a server. The code works for as long as the content is valid, for example as long as the website or UPI ID exists. There are no scan limits or subscriptions.

Q: Is a UPI QR code from this tool safe to use for my shop?
A: It creates a standard UPI payment link that UPI apps can read. Before printing it, scan it with a UPI app and check that the correct name appears, then make a small test payment. For business features such as payment alerts, settlement reports or a soundbox, use the merchant QR provided by your bank or payment provider.

Q: Do I need to scan a QR code to receive money?
A: No. You never need to scan a QR code or enter your UPI PIN to receive money. A UPI PIN is only entered when you send money. If someone asks you to scan a code or enter a PIN to “receive” a payment or refund, it is a scam.

Q: Can I add my logo to the QR code?
A: Yes. Upload an image as a centre logo and set its size from 10% to 30% of the code. The generator automatically switches to the highest error correction level so the code can still be read with part of it covered. Always test-scan before printing.

Q: What size should a printed QR code be?
A: A common rule of thumb is that the code should be at least about one tenth of the scanning distance, and not smaller than roughly 2 cm across for close-up scanning. A code on a poster read from a metre away should be around 10 cm wide. Download the 2048 px PNG or the SVG for print.

## Random Number Generator: Fair Picks in Any Range, With No Repeats

Quick answer: To get a random number, set a minimum and maximum and let a generator pick a value where every number has an equal chance. BISCS India’s free Random Number Generator uses your browser’s cryptographically secure randomness with unbiased sampling, and can produce up to 10,000 numbers, with or without repeats, as whole numbers or decimals.

A random number generator picks numbers from a range so that every value has an equal chance. Set a **minimum** and **maximum**, choose **how many** numbers you want and whether **repeats** are allowed, and the generator does the rest. A number between 1 and 100, for example, has exactly a 1% chance of being any particular value.

The free [Random Number Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/random-number-generator/) uses your browser's cryptographically secure random source with unbiased sampling, so the results are fair and nothing is sent to a server.

## What can you use random numbers for?

- **Classroom activities,** such as picking a roll number to answer a question.
- **Games** that need dice in unusual sizes, like a 20-sided or 100-sided die.

- **Decisions,** when two options are equally good and you just need to choose.

## How to use the BISCS Random Number Generator

1. Open the [Random Number Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/random-number-generator/).
2. Enter the **Minimum** and **Maximum**. Both are included in the range.
3. Choose **Whole numbers** or **Decimals**, and for decimals set the decimal places (1 to 10).

One-tap presets cover common needs: **1–6 (dice)**, **1–10**, **1–100**, **Lottery 6 of 49**, **PIN (4 digits)** and **OTP 6 digits**. They fill in the settings and generate straight away.

## What makes a random number generator fair?

Two things matter: the **source** of randomness and the **method** used to turn it into a number in your range.

**The source.** Many simple generators use a fast formula that is fine for animations but predictable if you know its starting point. This tool uses the browser's `crypto.getRandomValues`, a cryptographically secure source designed to be unpredictable.

**The method.** A common shortcut is to take a big random number and use the remainder after dividing by the size of the range. When the big number's range does not divide evenly, some results come up slightly more often. This tool uses **rejection sampling**: it discards the few values that would cause that bias and draws again. Every number in your range therefore has exactly the same chance.

For unique numbers, it either shuffles the whole range and takes the first few, or keeps drawing and skips anything already picked. Both give every combination an equal chance.

## Worked examples

### Picking 3 winners from 250 tickets

Number the tickets 1 to 250. Set minimum 1, maximum 250, how many 3, and leave repeats off. Each ticket has a 3 in 250 chance, or 1.2%, of being among the winners.

### Audit sampling

You want to check 30 out of 1,200 invoices. Generate 30 unique numbers between 1 and 1,200, sort them smallest first, and pull those invoices from your register. Random selection avoids the unconscious bias of picking "easy" ones.

### Lottery-style odds

The **6 of 49** preset picks six unique numbers from 1 to 49. There are 13,983,816 possible combinations, so any one ticket has about a 1 in 14 million chance of matching all six. No pattern, "hot" number or previous result changes that.

### Decimal values for testing

To create sample prices between ₹10 and ₹500, choose Decimals with 2 places, set the range, and generate 50 values.

## Running a transparent lucky draw

Fairness also means people can see it is fair:

1. **Publish the rules first:** the range, how many winners, and whether one person can win twice.
2. **Number entries openly,** such as by token or registration order, and share the list.
3. **Generate on a big screen** or projector in front of everyone.
4. **Record the result** with a screenshot or the downloaded list.
5. **Agree a backup rule** in advance, such as drawing again if a winner is absent.

## Common mistakes

- **Allowing repeats in a prize draw,** so one ticket wins twice.
- **Forgetting the range is inclusive.** 1 to 10 includes both 1 and 10.
- **Expecting patterns to "even out" quickly.** Short runs of random numbers often look clumpy; that is normal.

- **Dropping leading zeros** for PINs and codes, so 0042 becomes 42.
- **Asking for more unique numbers than the range holds.** The tool will tell you how many exist.

## RD Calculator: Recurring Deposit Maturity Value Explained

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/rd-calculator-recurring-deposit-maturity/
Tool: RD Calculator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/rd-calculator/)

Quick answer: An RD calculator adds up the growth of every monthly instalment, each compounded quarterly for the time it stays deposited. Saving ₹5,000 a month for 5 years at 7% gives about ₹3,59,664, including ₹59,664 interest. BISCS India's free RD Calculator shows the maturity value, interest earned and a year-by-year balance.

A recurring deposit (RD) lets you save a fixed amount every month and earn a fixed interest rate, like a fixed deposit paid in instalments. Its maturity value is the sum of every instalment plus the interest each one earns while it sits in the account, usually compounded quarterly.

If you deposit ₹5,000 a month for 5 years at 7%, you put in ₹3,00,000 and receive about ₹3,59,664 at maturity. The free [RD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rd-calculator/) on BISCS India works this out for any amount, rate and tenure, and shows how the balance grows each year.

## How is the RD maturity amount calculated?

Think of an RD as many small FDs opened one month apart. For a tenure of n months and annual rate r, the instalment paid in month k stays deposited for (n − k + 1) months, which is (n − k + 1) ÷ 3 quarters. Its value at maturity is:

**instalment × (1 + r ÷ 400)^((n − k + 1) ÷ 3)**

The calculator adds this up for every month from the first to the last. That is how Indian banks typically describe RD interest: quarterly compounding applied to each instalment for the time it is held.

The practical result is that early instalments earn far more than late ones. In a 60-month RD, the first ₹5,000 earns interest for five full years, while the last ₹5,000 earns for just one month.

## How to use the BISCS RD Calculator

1. Open the [RD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rd-calculator/).
2. Enter the **monthly deposit**. The slider covers ₹100 to ₹2 lakh.
3. Set the **interest rate** per year offered for your RD tenure.
4. Enter the tenure in **years and months**, anywhere from 1 month to 50 years.
5. Read the maturity amount, total deposited and interest earned, with a chart comparing deposits and interest.
6. Open the year-by-year table to see the balance at the end of each year.

It all runs in your browser, so there is nothing to sign up for and nothing is sent to a server.

## Worked examples

| Monthly deposit | Rate | Tenure | Total deposited | Maturity value | Interest |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹5,000 | 7% | 1 year | ₹60,000 | ₹62,311 | ₹2,311 |
| ₹2,000 | 6.5% | 3 years | ₹72,000 | ₹79,649 | ₹7,649 |
| ₹5,000 | 7% | 5 years | ₹3,00,000 | ₹3,59,664 | ₹59,664 |

The interest in the first row may look small next to an FD at the same rate. That is because the average rupee in an RD is deposited for only about half the tenure. A ₹60,000 FD for a year at 7% would earn more, but you would need the whole ₹60,000 on day one.

## RD or FD for the same money?

Compare like with like. Suppose you can save ₹60,000 over the next year.

- **As an RD:** ₹5,000 a month for 12 months at 7% gives about ₹62,311.
- **As an FD:** if you already had ₹60,000 today, a one-year FD at 7% compounded quarterly would give about ₹64,312.

The FD earns more because the whole amount is invested for the full year. But that is not really a fair choice if the money arrives from your salary month by month. An RD is the fixed-return way to invest money you do not have yet; an FD is for money you already have. Many families use both: an FD for an emergency fund or a bonus, and an RD for steady monthly saving towards a specific expense.

## When does an RD make sense?

- **Saving towards a known expense** such as school fees due next April, a Diwali purchase or an insurance premium.
- **Building a habit.** A standing instruction from your salary account turns saving into something automatic.
- **Low risk tolerance.** The return is fixed at the start, so market moves do not affect it.
- **Short horizons.** For goals one to three years away, the certainty of an RD often matters more than squeezing out extra return.

For longer goals, compare an RD with a [SIP Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sip-calculator/) estimate, keeping in mind that SIP returns are not guaranteed. For tax-free long-term saving, a PPF account is another option; see the [PPF Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ppf-calculator/).

## Checklist before opening an RD

- Confirm whether the rate quoted is for your exact tenure; rates can differ by a few months either side.
- Ask what happens if you miss an instalment, and how late payments are charged.
- Check premature closure rules and the penalty rate.
- Set the instalment date a few days after your salary credit to avoid a failed debit.
- Remember the interest is taxable, so plan for tax in your return.
- If you also hold FDs at the same bank, add up the expected interest; TDS thresholds apply to your total deposit interest there.

## Mistakes to avoid

1. **Treating the maturity value as "returns".** Most of it is your own money. In the 5-year example, the gain is ₹59,664 on ₹3 lakh deposited.
2. **Comparing an RD rate directly with an FD's maturity.** Use the same total money and timeline when comparing. The [FD Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fd-calculator/) helps with the lump-sum side.
3. **Choosing too long a tenure.** If you might need the money early, premature closure usually reduces the rate.
4. **Ignoring inflation and tax.** At typical slab rates, the post-tax return on an RD can be close to inflation.

## Limits of this estimate

The tool follows the standard quarterly-compounding method most banks describe, but individual banks and the Post Office scheme can differ in detail: the exact compounding schedule, how a final part-quarter is handled and rounding at each step. Small differences of a few rupees from your bank's statement are normal.

Use the result for planning, not as a commitment from any bank. This article is general information rather than financial advice. Confirm the current RD rate and terms with your bank or India Post, and check TDS rules on the Income Tax Department website.

Q: How is RD interest calculated in banks?
A: Banks treat each monthly instalment like a small deposit that earns interest from the day it is paid until maturity, compounded quarterly. The first instalment earns interest for the full tenure and the last one for only a month. The maturity value is the sum of all these individual amounts.

Q: What happens if I miss an RD instalment?
A: Most banks charge a small penalty for a late instalment, and after several missed instalments they may close the account and pay interest only on what was deposited. The exact rules differ by bank and by Post Office scheme, so read the terms before you open the account.

Q: Is RD interest taxable and is TDS deducted?
A: Yes. RD interest is taxed at your income tax slab rate, and banks may deduct TDS if your total deposit interest with them crosses the yearly threshold. You can submit Form 15G or 15H if eligible. Report the interest as income from other sources in your return.

Q: Is a recurring deposit better than a SIP?
A: They serve different purposes. An RD gives a fixed, known return and suits short-term goals or money you cannot risk. A mutual fund SIP may grow more over long periods but its value can fall. Many people use an RD for goals a year or two away and SIPs for longer goals.

## Readability Checker: Flesch Score, Grade Level and Fixes

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/readability-checker-flesch-score-guide/
Tool: Readability Checker (https://biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/)

Quick answer: A readability checker measures how easy text is to read using formulas based on sentence length and word length, such as Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid grade level. BISCS India’s free Readability Checker shows six scores, highlights long sentences, possible passive voice and adverbs, and suggests fixes for your target audience, all in your browser.

A readability checker estimates how easy a piece of writing is to read. It looks at things you can measure, mainly how long your sentences are and how long your words are, and turns them into scores such as Flesch Reading Ease or a school grade level.

The [Readability Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/) from BISCS India gives you six standard scores at once, highlights the sentences and phrases that make text harder, and suggests specific fixes for the audience you choose. It runs in your browser, so drafts stay private.

## Why readability matters online

People skim on the web, often on a phone, between other tasks. Short sentences and familiar words are understood faster and abandoned less often. That is true for a product description, a government scheme explainer or an email to clients.

Clear writing also helps machines. Search engines and AI assistants extract and summarise passages; a crisp 18-word sentence is far easier to quote correctly than a 50-word sentence with three clauses. Readability is not a direct Google ranking factor as far as Google has said, but it shapes how people and answer engines use your content.

## What the scores mean

| Score | What it measures | Good target for the web |
|---|---|---|
| Flesch Reading Ease | 0–100; higher is easier, from sentence and syllable length | 60+ for general readers |
| Flesch-Kincaid grade | US school grade needed to follow the text | Around 7–9 |
| Gunning Fog | Grade estimate weighted by complex words | Below 12 |
| SMOG | Grade estimate from polysyllabic words (needs 3+ sentences) | Below 10–12 |
| Coleman-Liau | Grade from letters per word and sentences | Around 8–10 |
| ARI | Grade from characters per word and words per sentence | Around 8–10 |

The Flesch result also gets a plain label, from "Very easy" through "Plain English" to "Very difficult", with a note on who can read it comfortably.

All these formulas use English syllable and character counts, so treat them as guides rather than exact measurements, and use them for English text.

## How to check readability step by step

1. Open the [Readability Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/). A short sample is loaded so you can see how it works.
2. Paste your article, product description or email into the box.
3. Choose a **Target audience**: general public, students (school) or professionals. Each has its own target score and grade.
4. Read the **Flesch Reading Ease** result, its label and whether it is on target, close or below.
5. Review the stats: grade levels, reading time, words, sentences, paragraphs, words per sentence, long sentences and approximate passive voice count.
6. Read the **Suggestions**. They tell you, for example, that your average sentence length is 26 words and should come down to 15–20.
7. Scroll to **Highlighted text** to see long sentences (26–35 words), very long sentences (35+), possible passive voice and adverbs marked in colour.
8. Edit your text and watch the scores update as you type.

Nothing you paste leaves your device.

## Practical ways to improve a score

**Split long sentences.** Look for "and", "which", "because" and semicolons; they are natural breaking points. Two 15-word sentences beat one 30-word sentence.

**Choose everyday words.** "Use" instead of "utilise", "help" instead of "facilitate", "about" instead of "approximately". In Indian business writing, phrases like "kindly do the needful" or "please revert back" can usually be replaced with a direct request.

**Define jargon once.** "Input tax credit (ITC)" the first time, then ITC. Readers outside your field will thank you.

**Prefer active voice.** "We will send your invoice today" is shorter and clearer than "Your invoice will be sent today".

**Cut filler adverbs.** "Very", "really" and "actually" rarely add meaning. A stronger verb often does the job.

**Use structure.** Headings, short paragraphs and bullet lists do not change the formulas much, but they make text far easier to read.

## A before-and-after example

Here is a typical sentence from a service page: "Our organisation is committed to facilitating the timely completion of all statutory compliance requirements for our esteemed clients, thereby ensuring that penalties and interest are avoided." It is 28 words long, uses several four- and five-syllable words, and ends in passive voice.

A clearer version: "We file your returns on time, so you avoid penalties and interest." That is 12 words, active, and says the same thing in plain English. Make a handful of edits like this across a page and the Flesch score typically rises noticeably, while the message becomes more convincing, not less.

Paste both versions into the checker to see the difference in grade level and highlights for yourself.

## Common readability mistakes

- **Chasing a perfect 100.** Text written only in three-word sentences sounds childish. Mix short and medium sentences for a natural rhythm.
- **Ignoring the audience.** A tax guide for chartered accountants can be denser than one for first-time ITR filers. Pick the right audience setting.
- **Trusting every highlight.** Passive voice and adverb detection are approximate; some flags will be fine as they are.
- **Checking non-English text.** The scores are designed for English and will be misleading for other languages.
- **Editing out precision.** Never remove necessary legal or technical terms just to raise a score; explain them instead.

## When to use the checker

Run it on landing pages, blog posts, help articles, product descriptions and important emails before sending. It is especially useful for content aimed at a broad Indian audience, where many readers use English as a second or third language and plain sentences make a real difference.

For keyword balance in the same draft, use the [Keyword Density Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/). To see whether the text is structured well for AI answers, try the [GEO Content Analyzer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/geo-content-analyzer/), and for a quick count of words and characters, the [Word Counter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/).

Good writing is rewriting. Paste your next draft into the [Readability Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/), fix the longest sentences first, and read it aloud once before you publish.

Q: What is a good Flesch Reading Ease score?
A: Higher scores mean easier text. A score of 60 or more is plain English that most adults read comfortably, and is a sensible target for websites. Scores of 70–80 suit blogs and help pages, while professional or technical content often lands between 45 and 60.

Q: Is readability a Google ranking factor?
A: Google has not said that it uses readability formulas for ranking. Clear writing still matters because people understand and stay with it, and well-structured, plain sentences are easier for search engines and AI assistants to summarise and quote accurately.

Q: Does the readability checker work for Hindi or Bengali text?
A: The formulas and syllable estimates are designed for English, so scores for Hindi, Bengali or other languages are not meaningful. The checker is best used for English and Indian English content. For other languages, focus on short sentences and simple words.

Q: Why is my grade level so high?
A: Grade formulas rise with long sentences and words of many syllables. Splitting sentences over 25 words, replacing jargon with everyday words and defining technical terms usually brings the grade down quickly without dumbing down the content.

Q: Is passive voice always wrong?
A: No. Passive voice is useful when the actor is unknown or unimportant, as in the form was submitted. Too much of it makes writing vague and wordy. The checker’s passive-voice detection is approximate, so review each highlight rather than changing every one.

## Regex Tester: Test JavaScript Regular Expressions Live

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/regex-tester-javascript-patterns-india/
Tool: Regex Tester (https://biscsindia.com/tools/regex-tester/)

Quick answer: A regex tester lets you type a regular expression and instantly see what it matches in sample text, including capture groups and the result of a replacement. BISCS India's Regex Tester uses the JavaScript regex engine, supports all flags, and includes presets for Indian mobile numbers, PAN, GSTIN, IFSC and PIN codes, all running in your browser.

A regex tester is a scratchpad for regular expressions. You type a pattern, paste some sample text, and every match lights up as you type, with its position and capture groups listed underneath. It turns regex writing from guesswork into a quick feedback loop.

The [Regex Tester](https://biscsindia.com/tools/regex-tester/) on BISCS India uses the JavaScript regex engine built into your browser, supports every standard flag, previews replacements, and comes with ready-made patterns for things Indian developers validate all the time: mobile numbers, PIN codes, PAN, GSTIN and IFSC.

## What is a regular expression?

A regular expression (regex) is a compact pattern that describes text. `\d{6}` means "six digits". `[A-Z]{5}` means "five capital letters". Combine pieces and you can find, validate or reshape text in ways that would take dozens of lines of ordinary code.

Here is the pattern the tester uses for an Indian PIN code:

```text
\b[1-9][0-9]{5}\b
```

Read left to right: a word boundary, a digit from 1 to 9 (PIN codes never start with 0), five more digits, and another word boundary so it does not match the middle of a longer number.

## How to test a regex with BISCS India

1. Open the [Regex Tester](https://biscsindia.com/tools/regex-tester/).
2. Type your pattern in the **Regular expression** box, between the slashes. You can also paste a full literal such as `/\d+/gi`, and the flags are picked up automatically.
3. Tick the flags you need: **g** (global), **i** (ignore case), **m** (multiline), **s** (dotAll), **u** (unicode) and **y** (sticky).
4. Paste text into **Test string**. Matches are highlighted in alternating colours so neighbouring matches are easy to tell apart, and a badge shows the count.
5. Check **Match details** for each match’s position and capture groups, including named groups. **Copy matches** copies every match, one per line.
6. To transform text, type a replacement in the **Replace** box using `$1`, `$<name>` or `$&`, and see the result immediately. **Copy result** grabs the output.

If the pattern has a syntax error, such as an unclosed bracket, the error message appears in place of the highlights.

## Ready-made patterns for Indian data

The **Common patterns** menu loads a preset pattern with the right flags. These are useful starting points:

| Preset | Pattern | Matches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indian mobile number | `[6-9]\d{9}` with an optional +91 or 0 prefix | 98XXXXXXXX, +91 98XXXXXXXX, 098XXXXXXXX |
| PIN code | `\b[1-9][0-9]{5}\b` | 700001, 560034 |
| PAN | `\b[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z]\b` | ABCDE1234F |
| IFSC code | `\b[A-Z]{4}0[A-Z0-9]{6}\b` | Four letters, a zero, six characters |
| Date (DD/MM/YYYY) | Day, month and year with `/`, `-` or `.` | 31/03/2026 |

There are also presets for email addresses, URLs, ISO dates with named groups, IPv4 addresses, hex colours and hashtags.

Remember that a format check is not proof of validity. A PAN regex cannot tell whether a PAN was issued, and a GSTIN has a check digit that a regex cannot compute. For those, use a dedicated checker such as the [GSTIN Validator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/) or the [PAN & IFSC Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pan-ifsc-validator/).

## Tip: test a whole list at once

When you are building a validation pattern for a form field, paste a list of real-looking values into the test string, one per line, including the ones that should fail. For a mobile number field, that might be a correct ten-digit number, one with +91, one with a space in the middle, a landline with an STD code and a nine-digit typo.

Then anchor the pattern with `^` and `$` and tick **m (multiline)**, so each line is tested as a separate value. You can see at a glance which lines match and which do not. Keep the list somewhere handy; when someone reports that a valid number was rejected, add it to the list and re-test before changing the pattern.

## Understanding the flags

- **g (global)** finds all matches instead of stopping at the first.
- **i (ignore case)** treats `a` and `A` as the same.
- **m (multiline)** makes `^` and `$` match at the start and end of each line, not just the whole text. Essential when testing a list of values, one per line.
- **s (dotAll)** lets `.` match line breaks too.
- **u (unicode)** treats characters outside the basic range, such as emoji, as single characters and enables `\p{…}` property escapes. For example, `\p{Script=Devanagari}+` with the `u` flag matches Hindi words.
- **y (sticky)** only matches at the exact current position. Mostly useful for writing tokenisers.

## Capture groups and replacement: a practical example

Suppose you have dates written as `31/03/2026` and need them in ISO format, `2026-03-31`, for a database import. Use this pattern with the **g** flag:

```text
(\d{2})/(\d{2})/(\d{4})
```

And this replacement:

```text
$3-$2-$1
```

Each pair of brackets captures a piece, numbered from left to right. Named groups make this more readable:

```js
const re = /(?<d>\d{2})\/(?<m>\d{2})\/(?<y>\d{4})/g;
'Due 31/03/2026'.replace(re, '$<y>-$<m>-$<d>');  // "Due 2026-03-31"
```

For simple literal swaps across a whole document, the [Find and Replace](https://biscsindia.com/tools/find-and-replace/) tool may be quicker.

## Common regex mistakes

- **Forgetting anchors when validating.** `\d{6}` matches inside `1234567`. To validate a whole field, use `^\d{6}$`.
- **Unescaped dots.** `.` means "any character". To match a literal full stop, as in a domain name, write `\.`.
- **Greedy matching.** `".+"` on `"Pune" and "Nagpur"` matches everything from the first quote to the last. Use the lazy `".+?"` to stop at the first closing quote.
- **Escaping twice or not at all in code.** In a JavaScript string, `"\d"` loses its backslash. Use a regex literal `/\d/` or write `"\\d"` in strings.
- **Catastrophic backtracking.** Patterns like `(\w+)+$` can freeze on long inputs that almost match. Keep quantifiers simple and test with long, non-matching text.
- **Trying to parse HTML or JSON with regex.** Use a real parser. Regex is great for extracting simple tokens, not nested structures.

## Privacy and limits

The tester runs your pattern against your text inside the browser; nothing is uploaded. To keep the page responsive, it stops highlighting after 5,000 matches and lists the first 500 in the details table. And because it uses the JavaScript engine, a pattern that works here may need small changes for Python, Java or a database.

Q: Which regex flavour does this tester use?
A: It uses your browser’s JavaScript (ECMAScript) regex engine, the same one used by Node.js and front-end code. Most syntax is shared with Python, Java and PCRE, but there are differences, for example in lookbehind support in older engines, possessive quantifiers and some flags. Test in your target language before relying on edge cases.

Q: Why does my regex match only the first occurrence?
A: Without the g (global) flag, JavaScript stops after the first match. Tick global to find every match. Note that with g, methods like test and exec remember their position through lastIndex, which can cause surprising results when you reuse the same regex object in code.

Q: Is there a regex that fully validates an email address?
A: Not a practical one. The official email address rules are very permissive, so any short regex will either reject some valid addresses or accept some invalid ones. Use a simple pattern to catch obvious typos, then confirm the address by sending a verification email.

Q: Can a regex verify that a PAN or GSTIN is genuine?
A: No. A regex checks only the format, such as five letters, four digits and a letter for PAN. It cannot tell whether the number was actually issued. GSTINs also include a check digit that a regex cannot calculate. Use a proper validator and, for compliance, the official government portal.

Q: What does catastrophic backtracking mean?
A: Some patterns with nested repetition, such as (a+)+ followed by something that fails, make the engine try an enormous number of combinations, so it freezes on certain inputs. This can be exploited to slow down servers. Avoid nested quantifiers on overlapping patterns and test with long non-matching strings.

## Common mistakes when de-duplicating lists

- **Duplicate pages.** It happens when you scan the same sheet twice or merge overlapping files.
- **Sensitive pages.** Sharing a property document with a contractor? Drop the pages with family details or financial information.
- **Cover pages and adverts.** Some e-statements include promotional pages that only bulk up the file.

## How to remove pages step by step

1. Open [Remove PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/) and choose your PDF.
2. Wait for the page thumbnails to load.
3. Click each page you want to remove. Selected pages are marked clearly, and a counter shows how many will go.
4. Alternatively, type the pages in the **Pages to remove** box, such as `1, 3, 10-12`. The thumbnails stay in sync with what you type.
5. Read the status line: it tells you how many pages the new PDF will have.
6. Click **Remove pages** and download the new file.

## Remove, extract or split: which do you need?

These three tools overlap, so pick the one that matches how you think about the job.

| Your situation | Best tool |
|---|---|
| "I want everything except these few pages" | Remove PDF Pages |
| "I only need these few pages" | [Extract PDF Pages](https://biscsindia.com/tools/extract-pdf-pages/) |
| "I want this document cut into several files" | [Split PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/) |
| "I want to delete some pages and reorder the rest" | [Organize PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/organize-pdf/) |

Removing two pages from a 50-page file is faster here; keeping two pages out of 50 is faster with Extract.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Confusing printed page numbers with PDF positions.** If page 1 of the PDF is a cover, the page printed as "3" might be the fourth page in the file. Go by the thumbnails, not the numbers in the footer.
- **Deleting a page with a signature or stamp.** Some agreements are only valid with every signed page attached. Check before removing anything from a legal document.
- **Not checking the result.** Open the downloaded file and scroll through it quickly. It takes ten seconds and avoids sending an incomplete document.
- **Overwriting the only copy.** The tool never changes your original, but if you then delete the original from your phone yourself, the removed pages are gone for good.

## Removing pages before a portal upload

When an application portal limits file size, removing unnecessary pages is often the easiest way to get under the limit without lowering quality. A scanned page can easily be several hundred KB, so dropping three blank pages may be all you need.

Limits differ from portal to portal (and sometimes between documents on the same portal), so read the specific instructions. If the file is still too big after removing pages, use [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) on the result.

## A note on sensitive information

Removing a page really removes it: the new PDF is built only from the pages you keep, so the deleted pages are not hidden inside. That makes page removal a safer way to withhold information than covering it with a white box.

However, information on the pages you keep stays as it is. If a page you need contains one sensitive line, such as a full account number, removing the page is not an option. In that case, recreate the document from its source, or use proper redaction software that permanently removes the text.

## Example: cleaning up a scanned property file

Meera in Hyderabad scanned her flat's purchase documents on the office copier to send to a bank for a top-up loan. The copier was set to double-sided, so the 18-page bundle came out as 36 pages, with a blank or near-blank back after most sheets. It also picked up the copier's own cover sheet as page 1.

She opens the PDF, clicks page 1 and each blank back page while scanning the thumbnails, and the counter shows 19 pages selected. The status line says the new PDF will have 17 pages. That does not match the 18 sheets she scanned, so she looks again and spots that she clicked one page with a faint stamp on it. She deselects it, the count becomes 18, and she downloads a file that is half the original size.

That small check, comparing the final page count with what you expect, is the best habit you can build with this tool.

## Tips for working faster

- Zoom out in your browser (Ctrl and minus) to see more thumbnails at once in long documents.
- Use ranges for patterns. To drop the last ten pages of a 60-page file, type `51-60`.
- If every other page is blank (a common double-sided scanning result), list them as ranges or click them one by one; then confirm the count before saving.
- On mobile, tapping thumbnails is usually quicker than typing.

## Private by design

The PDF is opened by a library running inside your browser tab. Selecting pages, building the new file and saving it all happen on your device, and nothing is uploaded or stored on a server. The first visit downloads the tool's code; after that, the processing needs no internet connection at all.

Q: Can I delete pages from a PDF without Adobe Acrobat?
A: Yes. A browser-based tool can remove pages without any paid software. Open the PDF, select the pages to delete and download the result. It works on Windows, Mac, Android and iPhone in any modern browser, with no installation or account.

Q: Can I undo a page deletion?
A: The tool creates a new file and leaves your original PDF untouched on your device. If you removed the wrong page, simply start again from the original. That is also why it is a good habit to keep the original until you have checked the new version.

Q: Why can’t I remove all pages?
A: A PDF needs at least one page to be a valid document, so the tool asks you to keep at least one. If you want to discard the entire file, just delete it from your device instead.

Q: Does removing pages make the PDF smaller?
A: Usually, yes. The removed pages and their images are not copied into the new file, so the size drops roughly in proportion. Removing a few scanned pages from a large document can noticeably reduce the size before you upload it.

Q: How do I select many pages quickly?
A: Type them in the box using commas and hyphens, for example 1, 4-9, 15. The thumbnails update to match. You can also click thumbnails directly, which is easier when you are spotting blank or duplicate pages by eye.

## Rent Receipt Generator for HRA Claims: Format and Rules

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/rent-receipt-format-hra-claim/
Tool: Rent Receipt Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/rent-receipt-generator/)

Quick answer: To create rent receipts for an HRA claim, enter the tenant and landlord names, property address, monthly rent, payment mode and the months covered, then print the receipts for your landlord to sign. BISCS India’s Rent Receipt Generator makes up to 36 monthly receipts, two per A4 page, with landlord PAN and a revenue stamp box.

A rent receipt is a simple document in which your landlord confirms that they received a stated amount of rent from you for a particular month and property. Salaried employees in India use them mainly to claim House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption, by submitting them to their employer or keeping them as proof for their tax return.

The fastest way to create them is with a generator: enter the details once, choose the months, print, and get your landlord to sign. Here is how, and what the rules expect.

## What should a rent receipt include?

A receipt that most employers accept has:

- the **tenant's name**;
- the **landlord's name**, and **PAN** where required;
- the **address of the rented property**;
- the **rent amount**, in figures and words;
- the **month or period** covered;
- the **payment mode** (cash, UPI, bank transfer or cheque) and a reference number if available;
- a **receipt number** and **date**;
- the **landlord's signature**, and a revenue stamp where applicable.

## How to make rent receipts online

1. Open the [Rent Receipt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rent-receipt-generator/). Sample data shows how a finished receipt looks.
2. Enter the **tenant name**, **landlord name**, **landlord PAN** (if applicable), landlord address and the **property address**.
3. Enter the **monthly rent** and choose the **payment mode**. Add a cheque number or UPI/UTR reference if you like.
4. Pick the **From** and **To** months, for example April to March for a full financial year.
5. Choose the receipt date (first or last day of each month), a receipt number prefix and starting number, and the place.
6. Tick **Show revenue stamp box** if needed.
7. Click **Print / Save as PDF**, or **Download all as one PDF** for a ready-made file.

Receipts are laid out two per A4 page with a cut line between them, so twelve months fit on six sheets. Up to 36 receipts can be generated at once. The summary panel shows the total rent for the period and flags missing PAN or cash payments that need a stamp.

## How HRA exemption works

HRA exemption is available **only under the old tax regime**. Under the new regime, which is now the default, HRA received is fully taxable and rent receipts do not reduce your tax.

Under the old regime, the exempt part of HRA is the lowest of:

1. the actual HRA you received;
2. rent paid minus 10% of salary (Basic plus DA);
3. 50% of salary if you live in a city classed as a metro for this purpose, or 40% elsewhere.

The list of metro cities is set by the tax rules, and has traditionally been Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai; check the current list for the year you are claiming. You can work out your exempt amount with the [HRA Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/) and compare the two regimes with the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/).

## When is the landlord's PAN required?

Employers generally ask for the landlord's PAN when the **annual rent exceeds ₹1,00,000**, roughly ₹8,333 a month. The generator warns you if your rent crosses this level without a PAN, and checks that the PAN you enter has the right shape (five letters, four digits, one letter).

If your landlord genuinely does not have a PAN, a signed declaration from them saying so is usually accepted. You can check the format of a PAN with the [PAN & IFSC Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pan-ifsc-validator/), though that only confirms the pattern, not that the PAN belongs to your landlord.

## Do you need a revenue stamp?

It is common practice, and many employers expect it, to affix a **₹1 revenue stamp** on a rent receipt when the rent is **paid in cash and exceeds ₹5,000**, with the landlord signing across the stamp. The tool shows a reminder in that situation.

Stamp duty on receipts is governed by stamp law, and practice varies, so if your HR team or tax adviser asks for something different, follow them. Payments by bank transfer or UPI leave their own trail, which is the stronger evidence in any case. Revenue stamps are usually sold at post offices.

## Common mistakes that get HRA claims questioned

- **Receipts that do not match your bank statement.** If you pay by UPI, the receipts should show the same amounts.
- **Missing landlord signature.** An unsigned receipt is just a printout.
- **Wrong property address.** It should be the house you live in, not your permanent address.
- **Claiming HRA for a house you own and live in.** HRA is for rented accommodation.
- **Rent paid to your spouse.** Tax authorities generally do not accept this.
- **Round figures with no rental agreement** for high rents. Keep the agreement, especially if rent is substantial.
- **Choosing the new regime and still submitting receipts.** They will not reduce tax under that regime.

## Tips for tenants

- **Pay by bank transfer or UPI** where possible. It is the easiest proof that rent was actually paid.
- **Generate the whole year at once** and get them signed together, rather than chasing the landlord every month.
- **Keep scanned copies.** Many employers want digital proofs uploaded to a portal; scan signed receipts and combine them into one file with [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/) if needed.
- **Missed the employer deadline?** Under the old regime, you can usually still claim the exemption when filing your income tax return, so keep the receipts and agreement safe.
- **Rent to parents** can be valid if a parent owns the home, the rent is genuinely paid, and the parent declares it as income.

## Is the rent receipt generator private?

Yes. The [Rent Receipt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rent-receipt-generator/) creates the receipts and the PDF in your browser. Names, PAN and address are saved only as a draft on your device, so you can come back next year and change the dates, and they are not sent to BISCS India.

Remember that the receipts must reflect rent you actually paid. Creating receipts for rent that was not paid, to reduce tax, is not allowed and can lead to penalties.

Q: When do I need my landlord’s PAN for HRA?
A: Employers generally require the landlord’s PAN when the rent you pay is more than ₹1,00,000 in a financial year, which is about ₹8,333 a month. If the landlord does not have a PAN, a signed declaration from them to that effect is usually accepted. Check your employer’s proof submission guidelines.

Q: Is a revenue stamp required on a rent receipt?
A: It is common practice, and many employers expect it, to affix a ₹1 revenue stamp on a rent receipt for a cash payment above ₹5,000, with the landlord signing across the stamp. Stamp requirements come from stamp duty law, so ask your HR or tax adviser if you are unsure. Bank transfers carry their own record.

Q: Can I claim HRA under the new tax regime?
A: No. The HRA exemption is available only if you choose the old tax regime. Under the new regime, which is the default, HRA received is fully taxable, so rent receipts do not reduce your tax. Compare both regimes with an income tax calculator before deciding which suits you.

Q: Can I pay rent to my parents and claim HRA?
A: Generally yes, if the parent owns the house, the rent is genuinely paid, ideally by bank transfer, and the parent reports it as income in their tax return. Rent paid to a spouse is usually not accepted. Keep receipts, bank records and a rental agreement in case of questions.

Q: Does the landlord have to sign every receipt?
A: Yes. A receipt is the landlord’s acknowledgement that they received the rent, so each monthly receipt should carry the landlord’s signature. Print the receipts, have them signed, and scan the signed copies if your employer wants digital proof.

A good resume is clear, honest and easy to scan, both for a recruiter who spends a short time on it and for the software many companies use to sort applications. You can build one in under an hour: pick a simple template, write a focused summary, list your experience with concrete achievements, add education and skills, and download it as a PDF.

This guide explains how to use the BISCS India builder, then covers the practical questions Indian job seekers ask most: what an ATS-friendly resume really means, how a fresher's CV differs from an experienced one, and what to leave out.

## How to make a resume with the BISCS Resume Builder
