## What does "ATS-friendly" actually mean?

An applicant tracking system (ATS) is software that companies and job portals use to collect, store and search applications. Many systems pull text out of your resume to fill in fields and let recruiters search by keywords. If the software cannot read your resume properly, a recruiter searching for "Tally" or "React" may never see you.

You do not need tricks to pass an ATS. You need a resume that is simple to read for both machines and people:

- **Use a single-column layout** for the safest parsing. In the builder, Classic and Minimal are single-column; Modern uses a side column, which many systems handle but some do not.
- **Use standard section headings** like "Experience", "Education" and "Skills" rather than creative labels.
- **Keep contact details in the main body**, not in a page header or an image.
- **Use real text, not images of text.** The PDF from the builder contains selectable text.
- **Match the wording of the job description** where it honestly applies. If the post says "accounts payable", use that phrase rather than only "vendor payments".
- **Avoid graphics for skills.** Rating bars and dots look neat but mean little to software. The builder's skill levels are optional for that reason.

The builder's checklist covers these points and others: a headline under your name, a summary of 25 to 90 words, at least two bullets per job, numbers in at least half your bullets, six or more relevant skills, dates on every job, and no photo.

## Fresher vs experienced: how should the resume differ?

| Area | Fresher or recent graduate | Experienced professional |
|---|---|---|
| Length | One page | One to two pages |
| Section order | Summary, Education, Projects, Internships, Skills | Summary, Experience, Skills, Education |
| Main evidence | Projects, internships, certifications, college roles | Achievements in past jobs, with numbers |
| Education detail | Degree, college, year, marks or CGPA if good | Degree, college, year; marks usually not needed |
| Summary focus | Skills and the role you want | Years of experience, specialism, key results |

### Tips for freshers

- **Lead with what you can prove.** A final-year project, an internship, a hackathon or a certification shows more than a list of subjects.
- **Describe projects like jobs.** What you built, the tools you used, and the result.
- **Include 10th and 12th marks only if asked** or if they are strong; many employers now focus on the degree.
- **Avoid generic objectives** like "seeking a challenging position in a reputed organisation". Write two lines about the role you want and what you bring.

### Tips for experienced candidates

- **Write achievements, not duties.** "Reduced month-end closing from 7 days to 4 by automating bank reconciliation" beats "Responsible for bank reconciliation".
- **Use numbers where they are true**: ₹ values, percentages, team sizes, turnaround times.
- **Trim older roles.** Jobs from 10 or more years ago need only a line or two.
- **Explain gaps briefly if asked**, but you do not need to justify every month on the page.

## What should you leave out of a resume?

Indian resumes often carry details that recruiters do not need and that can invite bias. Unless an employer or a government form specifically asks, leave out:

- **Date of birth and age**
- **Marital status, religion, caste and father's name**
- **Full residential address** (your city is enough)
- **Aadhaar, PAN or passport numbers**, which are sensitive identifiers
- **A photo**, for most private-sector roles
- **Current and expected salary**, which belong in the application form or conversation
- **"References available on request"**, which is assumed
- **The declaration paragraph**, unless requested
- **Hobbies that say nothing**, like "listening to music"; keep only interests that add something relevant

Government, PSU and some overseas applications have their own required formats. Always follow the employer's instructions over general advice.

## Common resume mistakes

- **Typos in your email or phone number.** Check them twice; a recruiter cannot call a wrong number.
- **An unprofessional email address.** Create a simple one with your name if needed.
- **One resume for every job.** Adjust your summary and skills for each application.
- **Dense paragraphs.** Use short bullets, ideally under two lines each.
- **Inconsistent dates and formatting.** Pick one date style, such as "Jun 2023", and use it everywhere.
- **Exaggeration.** Background checks are common, and interviews quickly expose inflated claims.

## Finishing touches

Before you send it, convert any certificates into a single file with [Merge PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/) if the employer asks for them together, and keep your resume file small with [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) if a portal has an upload limit. If an employer wants a formal passport-size photo separately, the [Passport Photo Maker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/passport-photo-maker/) can prepare one.

Your details stay on your device throughout. The [Resume Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/resume-builder/) creates the PDF and Word files in your browser, and nothing is uploaded to BISCS India.

Q: Should I put my photo on my resume in India?
A: For most private-sector jobs, no. A photo adds nothing to your qualifications, takes space and can confuse some applicant tracking systems. Add one only when the employer specifically asks for it, as some government, aviation, hospitality or modelling applications do. The builder’s photo field is optional for that reason.

Q: Is a one-page resume necessary?
A: For freshers and people with under about five years of experience, one page is usually enough and easier to read. Experienced professionals can use two pages if every line is relevant. The builder shows an estimated page count and page-break guides so you can see where the content falls.

Q: PDF or Word: which format should I send?
A: Send a PDF unless the job post asks for Word. PDFs keep your layout the same on every device. Some recruiters and job portals prefer .docx because they edit or parse it, so the builder offers both. Name the file clearly, for example Priya-Sharma-Resume.pdf.

Q: Do I need a declaration at the end of my resume?
A: Most private companies do not need one. The line ‘I hereby declare that the above information is true’ is a habit from older formats and government applications. If a specific employer or government form asks for it, add it using the custom section; otherwise use the space for achievements.

Q: Is my resume data stored online?
A: No. Your draft is autosaved in your browser’s storage on this device only, and the PDF and Word files are created in the browser. BISCS India does not receive your details. Use Export to save a backup file, because clearing browser data or switching devices removes the saved draft.

## Reverse Text: Write Backwards, Flip Words or Go Upside Down

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/reverse-text-backwards-upside-down/
Tool: Reverse Text (https://biscsindia.com/tools/reverse-text/)

Quick answer: To reverse text, paste it into a text reverser and choose whether to flip the characters, the word order, each word, or the order of lines. BISCS India’s Reverse Text tool also makes upside-down text and keeps emoji, accents and Hindi conjuncts intact, all processed privately in your browser.

Reversing text means flipping it so it reads backwards. Depending on what you need, that could be the characters ("India" becomes "aidnI"), the order of words, the letters inside each word, or the order of lines in a list. A reverse text tool does any of these instantly.

Most people use it for fun, such as puzzles, mirror-style captions or upside-down social posts, but flipping line order is also a genuinely useful clean-up trick for lists and logs.

## Five ways to reverse text

The BISCS India [Reverse Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/reverse-text/) tool offers five modes. Here is what each does to the same sentence.

| Mode | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Characters | Namaste India | aidnI etsamaN |
| Word order | Namaste India | India Namaste |
| Each word | Namaste India | etsamaN aidnI |
| Line order | Line 1 / Line 2 / Line 3 | Line 3 / Line 2 / Line 1 |
| Upside down | Namaste India | ɐᴉpuI ǝʇsɐɯɐN |

**Word order** keeps each line separate, so a multi-line poem has its words flipped line by line rather than being jumbled together. **Each word** keeps punctuation and spacing where they were and flips only the letters within words.

## How to reverse text online

1. Open the [Reverse Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/reverse-text/) tool.
2. Paste or type your text in the left box.
3. Choose a mode: **Characters**, **Word order**, **Each word**, **Line order** or **Upside down**.
4. The reversed text appears on the right straight away.
5. Click **Copy** to paste it into WhatsApp, Instagram or a document, or **Download** to save it as a text file.

**Use as input** sends the output back to the left box. That lets you combine modes, for example reversing line order and then reversing each word.

## Why emoji and Hindi need careful handling

Here is a detail most reversers get wrong. Many characters you see on screen are actually made from several hidden pieces:

- **Hindi and other Indic scripts** combine consonants with vowel signs (matras) and the halant to form conjuncts like "क्ष" or "स्ते".
- **Emoji with skin tones** are a base emoji plus a modifier, and family or flag emoji join several symbols together.
- **Accented letters** can be a plain letter plus a separate accent mark.

A simple tool reverses these pieces individually. The result is matras floating on the wrong letter, emoji splitting into two, and accents landing on spaces. The BISCS tool reverses whole visible characters, known as grapheme clusters, so each one stays intact. "नमस्ते" reversed keeps "स्ते" as a unit rather than scattering its parts.

Bear in mind that reversing Hindi by visible characters still produces text that does not read as Hindi. It just avoids broken symbols.

## Fun and practical uses

**Social media and messages.** Upside-down or backwards captions grab attention on Instagram stories, WhatsApp statuses and gaming profiles. For more styles like bold, script and bubble letters, try the [Fancy Text Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fancy-text-generator/).

**Puzzles and classroom activities.** Teachers write spelling words backwards for children to decode, and quiz hosts use reversed names as clues. Palindromes, words that read the same both ways like "malayalam" or "level", are easy to check: reverse the characters and compare.

**Flipping lists and logs.** Bank statements, chat exports and server logs are often shown newest first. Reversing line order puts them in date order without needing a spreadsheet. If the lines need true sorting rather than flipping, use [Sort Lines](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sort-lines/).

**Testing software.** Developers use reversed and upside-down strings to test how forms, databases and fonts cope with unusual Unicode characters.

## Common mistakes

- **Expecting a mirror image.** Character reversal does not mirror letter shapes. An "R" stays an "R" facing the normal way. Upside-down mode uses look-alike symbols, which is the closest text can get.
- **Using it for anything important.** Reversed text is hard for everyone to read, and screen readers cannot make sense of it. Do not reverse phone numbers, addresses or instructions.
- **Thinking it hides information.** Reversed text is not encryption. Anyone can flip it back in seconds with the same tool.
- **Mixing up word order and line order.** If your output still has the lines in the same sequence, you probably chose Word order. Switch to Line order to flip the list itself.

## Tips for upside-down text

Upside-down mode reverses the order of lines and characters and swaps each letter for a Unicode look-alike, such as "ɐ" for "a" and "ʎ" for "y". Numbers and common punctuation like "?" and "!" are flipped too.

- It looks best in short phrases. Long paragraphs become tiring to read.
- Some look-alike characters depend on the font. Check how it appears on the platform before posting.
- Capital letters have fewer good look-alikes, so lower case often looks neater.
- Letters outside A to Z, including Hindi, stay unchanged in this mode.

## Try it: a palindrome check in four steps

Palindromes make a nice classroom or quiz activity, and the tool turns checking them into a quick game.

1. Type a word or phrase such as "malayalam", "nitin" or "never odd or even".
2. Choose **Characters** mode.
3. Compare the output with the input. "malayalam" comes back unchanged, so it is a palindrome.
4. For phrases, ignore spaces and capitals when comparing. "never odd or even" reversed is "neve ro ddo reven", which matches once the spaces are removed.

Children enjoy finding their own examples, and it is a gentle way to talk about letters, spelling and patterns. You can also try number palindromes like dates written as 12022021, or vehicle registration numbers with a symmetrical sequence.

## Is the reversed text stored anywhere?

No. All five modes run in your browser, so the text you enter is not uploaded or saved by BISCS India. Close the tab and it is gone. For tidying up the result, such as removing extra spaces after flipping words, run it through the [Whitespace Cleaner](https://biscsindia.com/tools/whitespace-cleaner/).

Q: Why does reversed Hindi text look broken in some tools?
A: Hindi letters are often built from several Unicode code points, such as a consonant plus a vowel sign or a half letter. Simple reversers flip those pieces separately, which detaches vowel signs. The BISCS tool reverses whole visible characters, called grapheme clusters, so conjuncts and matras stay together.

Q: Is upside-down text real text or an image?
A: It is real text. Each letter is swapped for a Unicode character that looks like an upside-down version, such as ɐ for a and ǝ for e, and the order is reversed. You can paste it into most apps, but some characters may look slightly different depending on the font.

Q: Can I reverse the order of lines in a list?
A: Yes. Choose Line order and the last line becomes the first, without changing the text inside each line. This is handy for flipping a chat export, a log file or a list that was entered newest first.

Q: Can reversed text be used as a password trick?
A: It is not a good idea. Writing a common word backwards adds almost no security, because password-cracking tools try reversed words automatically. Use a long random password from a password generator instead, stored in a password manager.

Q: Will screen readers read reversed or upside-down text?
A: Not meaningfully. Reversed text is read as nonsense, and upside-down characters may be skipped or announced as symbols. Keep these effects for fun posts and puzzles, and avoid them for important information such as contact details or instructions.

## How to Create a robots.txt File (With Free Generator)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/create-robots-txt-file-guide/
Tool: Robots.txt Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/robots-txt-generator/)

Quick answer: A robots.txt file sits at the root of your website and tells crawlers which paths they may or may not crawl. BISCS India’s free Robots.txt Generator builds the file from presets and custom rules, adds your sitemap URL, checks for common syntax errors and lets you download it ready to upload.

A robots.txt file is a plain text file at the root of your site that gives crawlers instructions about which parts of the site they may visit. It is one of the first files Googlebot requests, and a small mistake in it can hide an entire website from search.

The [Robots.txt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/robots-txt-generator/) from BISCS India builds the file for you from simple choices: a default policy, quick presets, custom rules and your sitemap URL. It checks each line as you go and explains what search engines will and will not do with it.

## What does a robots.txt file actually do?

Robots.txt is a set of polite requests, not a lock. Well-behaved crawlers like Googlebot and Bingbot read it and follow the rules. Badly behaved scrapers ignore it.

The file uses a few simple directives:

- `User-agent:` names the crawler a group of rules applies to. `*` means all crawlers.
- `Disallow:` lists a path that crawler should not fetch.
- `Allow:` makes an exception inside a disallowed folder.
- `Sitemap:` gives the full URL of your XML sitemap.

A simple, healthy file for a small business site often has just four lines: `User-agent: *`, then `Disallow: /admin/` and `Disallow: /cart/`, and finally `Sitemap: https://www.example.com/sitemap.xml`. In other words, every crawler may visit everything except the admin and cart areas, and here is the sitemap.

## What robots.txt cannot do

This is where many site owners go wrong, so it is worth being clear:

| You want to | Use robots.txt? | Better approach |
|---|---|---|
| Stop crawlers wasting time on cart or search pages | Yes | Disallow those paths |
| Keep a page out of Google results | No | Add a `noindex` meta tag and let Google crawl it |
| Hide private documents | No | Password protection or server-level restrictions |
| Remove a page already indexed | No | noindex, or the removals tool in Search Console |
| Tell crawlers where your sitemap is | Yes | Add a `Sitemap:` line |

The robots.txt file itself is public. Anyone can open it in a browser, so listing a "secret" folder in it actually advertises that folder.

## Should you block AI crawlers?

The generator includes an optional preset that blocks several AI-related crawlers: GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended, anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot. Whether you should use it depends on what you want.

Some points to weigh:

- **These rules are voluntary.** Reputable AI companies say their crawlers respect robots.txt, but it is not an enforcement mechanism.
- **Google-Extended is not a search crawler.** It is a control token that tells Google whether your content may be used for training and grounding its Gemini models. Blocking it does not affect how your site ranks in Google Search.
- **Blocking can reduce visibility in AI answers.** If you want ChatGPT, Perplexity or similar tools to cite your pages, blocking their crawlers works against that goal.
- **Bot names change.** Companies add and rename user agents, so review the list now and then against each company's official documentation.

To check how an existing file treats these bots, paste it into the [AI Crawler Access Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ai-crawler-checker/).

## Common robots.txt mistakes

- **Leaving `Disallow: /` live after launch.** Developers often block staging sites and forget to change the rule when the site goes live.
- **Blocking CSS and JavaScript folders.** Google needs these to render your pages. Old advice to block `/wp-includes/` or `/assets/` can hurt how Google sees your site.
- **Paths without a leading slash.** `Disallow: admin` is unclear; use `Disallow: /admin/`.
- **Using robots.txt to fix duplicate content.** Use canonical tags instead, so Google can still see and consolidate the pages.
- **Relative sitemap URLs.** The `Sitemap:` line must be a full URL. The tool checks this.
- **Wrong file name or location.** It must be lowercase `robots.txt` at the domain root.

## Tips for WordPress and online shops

WordPress creates a virtual robots.txt automatically. If you upload a real file, it replaces the virtual one, so make sure it includes everything you need. The admin preset in the generator blocks `/wp-admin/` while still allowing `admin-ajax.php`, which some themes and plugins rely on.

For WooCommerce or other shops, blocking cart, checkout and account pages saves crawl effort for the pages that matter. Faceted filter URLs (colour, size, price) can create thousands of near-duplicate pages; disallowing the filter parameters can help, but test carefully so you do not block category pages you want ranked.

## After you upload the file

Open `https://yourdomain.com/robots.txt` in a browser to confirm it is live. In Google Search Console, the robots.txt report shows the version Google fetched and any parsing problems.

Then make sure the sitemap you referenced actually exists. If you do not have one yet, the [XML Sitemap Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/sitemap-generator/) can create it from a list of URLs. To confirm individual pages are not set to noindex by mistake, run them through the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/).

A good robots.txt is usually short. Build yours in the [Robots.txt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/robots-txt-generator/), keep it simple, and revisit it whenever your site structure changes.

Q: Does robots.txt stop a page from appearing in Google?
A: Not reliably. robots.txt controls crawling, not indexing. A blocked URL can still be indexed if other sites link to it, usually without a description. To keep a page out of search results, allow crawling and add a noindex meta tag instead.

Q: Where should the robots.txt file be placed?
A: At the root of the domain, so it opens at https://yourdomain.com/robots.txt. Each subdomain needs its own file. A robots.txt placed in a subfolder is ignored by crawlers.

Q: Does Google follow Crawl-delay?
A: No. Googlebot ignores the Crawl-delay line. Bing and Yandex have historically respected it. If Google is genuinely overloading your server, there are other ways to manage this, such as temporarily returning 503 or 429 responses, explained in Google’s crawling documentation.

Q: Should I block AI crawlers like GPTBot?
A: It depends on your goals. Blocking them may keep future content out of some AI training or AI search features, but well-behaved bots follow robots.txt voluntarily, and blocking Google-Extended does not affect your Google Search ranking. Decide deliberately rather than by default.

Q: Can a wrong robots.txt harm my SEO?
A: Yes. A single line such as Disallow: / in the group for all user agents blocks every compliant crawler from your entire site. Always review the final file and test important URLs in Google Search Console’s robots.txt report after uploading.

## Roman Numerals Explained: Rules, Chart and Easy Conversion

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/roman-numerals-chart-and-converter/
Tool: Roman Numerals (https://biscsindia.com/tools/roman-numeral-converter/)

Quick answer: Roman numerals use seven letters, I (1), V (5), X (10), L (50), C (100), D (500) and M (1,000), added together from largest to smallest, with a smaller letter before a larger one meaning subtraction. So 2026 is MMXXVI and 1947 is MCMXLVII. BISCS India’s free converter works both ways for 1 to 3,999.

Roman numerals write numbers with seven letters: **I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1,000**. You read them from left to right and add the values, except when a smaller letter comes before a larger one, which means subtract. So **VI** is 6, **IV** is 4, and **2026** is **MMXXVI**.

The free [Roman Numerals](https://biscsindia.com/tools/roman-numeral-converter/) converter turns any number from 1 to 3,999 into Roman numerals and back, and shows a breakdown of each part so you can learn the pattern.

## Where do we still use Roman numerals?

Roman numerals are far from dead. In India you see them every day:

- **School classes** such as Class VIII, Class X and Class XII.
- **Sections and parts of documents**, like Part III of the Constitution of India on Fundamental Rights.
- **Preface pages** of books, numbered i, ii, iii before the main chapters begin.
- **Clock and watch faces**, often with IIII instead of IV for design reasons.
- **Names of kings and popes**, sequels and event editions.
- **Years** on monuments, film credits, wedding invitations and tattoos.

## The Roman numeral chart

| Symbol | Value | Subtractive pair | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | 1 | IV | 4 |
| V | 5 | IX | 9 |
| X | 10 | XL | 40 |
| L | 50 | XC | 90 |
| C | 100 | CD | 400 |
| D | 500 | CM | 900 |
| M | 1,000 | | |

Those six subtractive pairs are the only ones allowed in standard form. Learn them and you can write any number up to 3,999.

## The rules in plain language

1. **Write from largest to smallest.** MDC is 1,000 + 500 + 100 = 1,600.
2. **Repeat a symbol up to three times** to add it: III is 3, XXX is 30, CCC is 300.
3. **Never repeat V, L or D.** VV is not 10; use X.
4. **Subtract only with the six pairs above.** I before V or X, X before L or C, C before D or M.
5. **Only one smaller symbol** can come before a larger one. 8 is VIII, not IIX.

## How to use the Roman Numerals converter

1. Open the [Roman Numerals](https://biscsindia.com/tools/roman-numeral-converter/) converter.
2. Type a whole number from 1 to 3,999 in the **Number** box, or a numeral in the **Roman numeral** box. The other box fills in instantly.
3. Check the **Breakdown** table, which splits the result into parts, for example 2026 = MM (2 × 1000) + XX (2 × 10) + V (5) + I (1).
4. Use the **Reference** chart if you are learning the symbols.
5. Press **Copy** to copy the numeral for your document or design.

If you enter something that is not a valid standard numeral, such as IIII or LXXXX, the tool explains what is wrong and suggests the standard form. Everything runs in your browser.

## Worked examples: converting years and numbers

### 1947 to Roman numerals

Split it by place value: 1000 + 900 + 40 + 7.

- 1000 = M
- 900 = CM
- 40 = XL
- 7 = VII

Result: **MCMXLVII**.

### 2026 to Roman numerals

2000 + 20 + 6 = MM + XX + VI = **MMXXVI**.

### 1999, the classic trap

It is tempting to write MIM (1000 − 1 + 1000), but I can only be placed before V or X. The standard form is 1000 + 900 + 90 + 9 = M + CM + XC + IX = **MCMXCIX**.

### Reading MDCCCLVII

M (1000) + D (500) + CCC (300) + L (50) + V (5) + II (2) = **1857**.

### More quick examples

- 14 = XIV
- 49 = XLIX (not IL)
- 90 = XC
- 444 = CDXLIV
- 3,999 = MMMCMXCIX, the largest standard numeral

## How to read any Roman numeral, step by step

Converting from Roman numerals back to a normal number is just as mechanical:

1. Write down the value of each letter underneath it. For MCMXC: 1000, 100, 1000, 10, 100.
2. Move from left to right. If a value is smaller than the one after it, subtract it; otherwise add it.
3. Here, M adds 1000. C is smaller than the next M, so it subtracts 100. M adds 1000. X is smaller than the next C, so it subtracts 10. C adds 100.
4. Total: 1000 − 100 + 1000 − 10 + 100 = **1990**.

With practice you start to see pairs like CM and XC as single chunks, which makes reading much faster.

## Handy reference: tens and hundreds

Most numerals are built from these three ladders, so they are worth memorising:

- **Units:** I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX
- **Tens:** X, XX, XXX, XL, L, LX, LXX, LXXX, XC
- **Hundreds:** C, CC, CCC, CD, D, DC, DCC, DCCC, CM

To write any number up to 3,999, take the thousands as M, MM or MMM, then pick one item from each ladder. For 2,748, that is MM + DCC + XL + VIII = **MMDCCXLVIII**.

## Common Roman numeral mistakes

- **Using IL for 49 or IC for 99.** The correct forms are XLIX and XCIX.
- **Writing IIII for 4** outside of clock faces. In text, use IV.
- **Repeating V, L or D,** such as VV or LL.
- **Putting two smaller symbols before a larger one,** such as IIX for 8.
- **Trying to write zero or negative numbers.** The Roman system has no zero.
- **Mixing up D and M,** which is easy when reading quickly on a building or certificate.

## Tips for designers and writers

- For tattoos, invitations and engravings, convert with a tool and double-check the result before it becomes permanent.
- Use a serif font for a classic look, and keep letter spacing even so each symbol is clear.
- When numbering sections, be consistent: either Roman throughout (I, II, III) or Arabic (1, 2, 3).
- For dates, you can write each part separately, such as XV · VIII · MCMXLVII for 15 August 1947.

## Why the Roman system faded

Roman numerals are fine for labels but awkward for arithmetic. Try multiplying XLVII by XIX without converting first. The decimal place-value system with zero, which developed in India and later spread through the Arab world to Europe, made calculation far easier, and it is the system the world uses today.

To spell out numbers for cheques and invoices, try [Number to Words](https://biscsindia.com/tools/number-to-words/). And for fun with fancy lettering on social posts, the [Fancy Text Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/fancy-text-generator/) offers many styles.

Roman numerals take a few minutes to learn and a lifetime to stop noticing. When you need a correct conversion quickly, the [Roman Numerals](https://biscsindia.com/tools/roman-numeral-converter/) converter has you covered.

Q: How do you write 2026 in Roman numerals?
A: 2026 is MMXXVI. Break it into 2000 + 20 + 6. Two thousand is MM, twenty is XX and six is VI. Put them together from largest to smallest to get MMXXVI.

Q: Why is 4 written as IV and not IIII?
A: Standard Roman numerals use subtractive notation: placing I before V means 5 minus 1. It keeps numbers shorter and avoids repeating a symbol four times. Some clock faces still show IIII for four, which is a long-standing design tradition, but IV is the standard form.

Q: Is there a Roman numeral for zero?
A: No. The Roman system had no symbol for zero and no way to write negative numbers. That is why the converter accepts whole numbers from 1 upwards. Zero as a number with its own symbol came from the Indian number system.

Q: Why does the converter stop at 3,999?
A: With the standard seven symbols and the rule that a symbol repeats at most three times, the largest number you can write is MMMCMXCIX, which is 3,999. Larger values historically used a bar over a letter to multiply it by 1,000, but there is no single standard for that.

Q: Why is MIM not accepted for 1999?
A: Standard subtraction only allows I before V and X, X before L and C, and C before D and M. So 1999 must be written as 1000 + 900 + 90 + 9, which is MCMXCIX. Shortcuts like MIM or IL for 49 are not standard and the converter flags them.

Rotating a photo turns it around its centre, usually by 90° or 180°, while flipping mirrors it from left to right or top to bottom. Together they fix the most common annoyances with phone pictures: sideways shots, upside-down scans, reversed selfies and slightly crooked horizons.

The [Rotate & Flip Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/) tool from BISCS India does all of this with single clicks, plus a fine straightening slider. It works in your browser, so your photo never leaves your device.

## Why do photos end up sideways in the first place?

When you take a picture, your phone records which way it was held. Rather than rotating the pixels, many phones save them in the sensor’s natural orientation and add a small piece of metadata, the EXIF orientation tag, telling apps how to display it.

Your gallery app reads that tag and shows the photo correctly. But some websites, older desktop programs, document portals and print kiosks ignore it. The result: a photo that looked fine on your phone appears sideways after upload.

The fix is to save a fresh copy with the correct orientation built into the pixels rather than left as a hint in the metadata. The BISCS India tool reads the orientation tag when it opens your photo, so if the preview already looks upright you can simply download it. If it is still sideways, the picture was genuinely taken that way and needs a rotate.

## How to rotate or flip an image

1. Open [Rotate & Flip Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/) and choose a photo, drag it in, or paste it with Ctrl + V.
2. Use **Rotate left** or **Rotate right** to turn it by 90°, or **Rotate 180°** for upside-down images.
3. Use **Flip horizontal** to mirror it left to right, or **Flip vertical** to mirror it top to bottom.
4. If the horizon or a document edge is slightly tilted, drag the **Straighten (fine angle)** slider, which moves in half-degree steps between −45° and +45°.
5. Check the output size shown under the preview. Choose the format and quality if you want something other than the original format.
6. Press **Reset** to start again at any point, or download when you are happy.

|---|---|---|

## Straightening a crooked photo the right way

A small tilt, even two or three degrees, makes buildings look like they are leaning and the sea look like it is draining off one side of the frame. To straighten:

- Find a line that should be level or vertical: a horizon, a door frame, the edge of a table, the top of a document.
- Move the slider until that line is parallel with the edge of the preview.
- Because the picture has turned, the corners of the frame now contain empty space. Use [Crop Image](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/) to trim those angled edges away.

Fine rotation resamples the pixels, so there is a very slight softening. For exact 90° turns and flips there is no such loss.

## Practical uses in everyday life

- **Documents for upload.** A photographed Aadhaar card, mark sheet or rent agreement that appears sideways on a portal looks careless and may be harder for the reviewer to read. Rotate it upright before converting it with [JPG to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/).
- **Scanned PDFs.** If the problem is a page inside a PDF rather than an image, [Rotate PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-pdf/) fixes pages without converting them.
- **Mirror selfies.** Your name on a T-shirt or a shop sign behind you reading backwards is a giveaway. One horizontal flip fixes it.
- **Product photography.** Online sellers sometimes need left- and right-facing versions of the same product image for a layout. Flipping gives you both in seconds.
- **Old family photos.** Scans of prints are often slightly crooked on the scanner bed. Straighten, crop and then improve them with the [Photo Enhancer](https://biscsindia.com/tools/ai-photo-enhancer/).

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Flipping when you meant to rotate.** A flipped portrait looks subtly wrong because faces are not perfectly symmetrical, and any text becomes mirrored. If you only wanted the photo upright, use rotate.
- **Rotating a photo that only looks wrong in one app.** If it appears correctly in your gallery but sideways on one website, the website is ignoring the orientation tag. Open it here and check the preview before turning it, or you may end up rotating it twice.
- **Straightening without cropping.** The angled empty corners look odd in the final image.
- **Mirroring photos with logos or text for official use.** Mirrored certificates and ID documents will not be accepted.
- **Repeated JPG saves.** Rotate once, from the original, rather than saving and re-rotating a JPG many times.

## Is it private?

Yes. All the turning, flipping and straightening happens on your device using your browser’s canvas. The image is not sent anywhere, so it is fine for personal photos and documents. On older phones, very large photos may take a moment longer to save, simply because the work is done locally.

Q: Why does my photo appear sideways after uploading it?
A: Phones often store the picture in one orientation and add a small EXIF tag telling apps to turn it. Some websites ignore that tag, so the photo shows sideways. Rotating it properly and saving a new copy bakes the correct orientation into the pixels themselves.

Q: What is the difference between rotating and flipping?
A: Rotating turns the whole picture around its centre, like turning a printed photo on a table. Flipping mirrors it, so the left side becomes the right side or the top becomes the bottom. Text reads backwards after a horizontal flip, which is how you spot a mirrored selfie.

Q: Why do my selfies look reversed and how do I fix it?
A: Many front cameras show a mirror image in the preview, and some also save it that way. Writing on clothes or signs then appears backwards. Use Flip horizontal once to mirror the photo back so it matches how other people see you.

Q: Does rotating a photo lose quality?
A: Turning by exact 90 degree steps or flipping moves pixels without blending them, so the picture stays sharp. Small straightening angles require the pixels to be resampled, which softens the image very slightly. Saving as JPG also applies normal compression, so keep quality high.

## Why PDFs end up sideways

Sideways pages are a nuisance with many causes:

- **Phone scans.** Your phone guessed the orientation from how you held it, and guessed wrong.
- **Scanners and copiers.** A document placed the wrong way on the glass comes out upside down.
- **Landscape pages in portrait documents.** Spreadsheets and charts printed in landscape appear sideways inside a report.
- **Mixed bundles.** Merging several files can bring together pages with different orientations.

A reviewer, examiner or bank officer who has to tilt their head to read your documents is not off to a good start. Fixing orientation takes seconds.

## Example: a GST notice reply bundle

A small trader in Surat is replying to a notice and has to attach invoices, a ledger extract and bank statements. The ledger was printed in landscape and scanned, so those six pages are sideways, while the invoices were photographed upside down on a desk.

## Does rotation affect printing?

Yes, in a good way. Printers follow the rotation saved in the file, so a correctly rotated PDF prints upright without you fiddling with print settings. Landscape pages that you leave in landscape will print sideways on a portrait sheet, which is usually what you want for wide tables. If you rotate them to portrait instead, the table will be printed across the narrow side of the paper and may become small, so think about whether the document is mainly for screen reading or for print.

## What about pages that are slightly tilted?

Rotate PDF turns pages in exact steps of 90 degrees. It cannot straighten a photo taken at a slight angle, where the text runs a few degrees off horizontal. For that kind of problem, the fix is at the scanning stage: use a scanner app that corrects perspective, such as Scan to PDF, and capture the page again. A crisp, straight page is far easier to read than a tilted one, and it also compresses better.

## Checklist before you download

- Every page reads upright when you scroll through the preview.
- Landscape tables are oriented the way you intend for screen or print.
- No page was accidentally turned twice.
- You still have the original file, in case you need to start again.

## Privacy and speed

Rotation is a light operation, so even long documents finish almost instantly. It runs entirely in your browser: the file is read from your device and the rotated copy is saved back to it. Nothing is uploaded, which matters when the pages are bank statements, invoices or identity documents.

Q: Why does my PDF go back to sideways after I rotate it in a viewer?
A: Most PDF viewers only rotate the display for that session; they do not change the file. To make the rotation stick for everyone who opens the document, you need to save a rotated copy with a tool like Rotate PDF.

Q: Can I rotate only some pages?
A: Yes. Click the pages you want in the preview, or use the quick select buttons for odd or even pages, then press Left, Right or 180°. If nothing is selected, the rotation applies to all pages.

Q: Does rotating a PDF reduce its quality?
A: No. The tool changes the page’s rotation setting instead of redrawing it, so text remains selectable and images stay as sharp as in the original. The file size stays virtually the same.

Q: How do I fix a whole document scanned upside down?
A: Open the file, make sure no pages are selected, and press 180°. Every page turns the right way up. Download the result, and it will open correctly in any PDF reader or upload portal.

## Salary Slip Generator: Payslip Format with PF, ESI and PT

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/salary-slip-format-pf-esi-professional-tax/
Tool: Salary Slip Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/)

Quick answer: A salary slip lists an employee’s monthly earnings, such as Basic and HRA, minus deductions like EPF, ESI, professional tax and TDS, to show net pay. BISCS India’s Salary Slip Generator calculates these from your figures, handles loss-of-pay days, shows employer contributions and prints a professional payslip as a PDF from your browser.

A salary slip, or payslip, is the monthly statement an employer gives an employee showing how their pay was worked out: the earnings, each deduction, and the net amount credited to the bank. For employees it is proof of income for loans, rental agreements and visas. For employers, especially small businesses, it is a basic record-keeping duty.

The BISCS India generator does the arithmetic and layout for you, but it helps to understand what every line means. That is what most of this guide covers.

## What is on a typical Indian salary slip?

A complete payslip has four parts:

1. **Employer and employee details**: company name and address, employee name, ID, designation, department, date of joining, PAN, UAN and bank account (usually only the last few digits).
2. **Attendance**: days in the month, paid days and loss-of-pay (LOP) days.
3. **Earnings and deductions**, side by side, with totals.
4. **Net pay**, in figures and in words, and space for signatures.

Some employers also show employer contributions to PF and ESI, which helps employees understand their cost to company (CTC).

## Salary components explained

### Earnings

| Component | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Basic | The core fixed salary | Usually the base for PF and often for gratuity |
| Dearness Allowance (DA) | Inflation-linked allowance | Common in government and some private jobs; usually counts for PF |
| House Rent Allowance (HRA) | Help with rent | Tax exemption depends on your tax regime and rent paid |
| Conveyance or transport allowance | Travel to work | Tax treatment has changed over the years; check current rules |
| Special allowance | Balancing figure in the salary structure | Fully taxable |
| Bonus, overtime, incentives | Variable pay | Shown only in the months paid |

### Deductions

**Employees' Provident Fund (EPF).** The employee contributes 12% of PF wages, usually Basic plus DA. The statutory wage ceiling is ₹15,000 a month, so many employers calculate PF on a maximum of ₹15,000, which caps the employee share at ₹1,800. Employers and employees may agree to contribute on the full wage instead. The employer also contributes 12%, of which 8.33% (on wages up to ₹15,000) goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme and the rest to the PF account.

**Employees' State Insurance (ESI).** At the time of writing, ESI applies to employees with gross monthly wages up to ₹21,000 (₹25,000 for persons with disability) in covered establishments. The employee pays 0.75% of gross wages and the employer 3.25%. ESI is assessed over six-month contribution periods, so an employee who crosses the limit mid-period may continue to contribute until it ends.

**Professional tax (PT).** A state tax on employment, deducted by the employer. Each state sets its own slabs, some states do not levy it at all, and the Constitution caps it at ₹2,500 per person per year.

**Income tax (TDS).** The employer estimates your annual tax under your chosen regime and deducts a share each month.

**Other deductions**: salary advances, loan recoveries, canteen charges and similar items.

## Professional tax: the West Bengal slab

The generator includes the West Bengal monthly slab, as currently implemented in the tool:

| Monthly salary | Professional tax |
|---|---|
| Up to ₹10,000 | Nil |
| ₹10,001 to ₹15,000 | ₹110 |
| ₹15,001 to ₹25,000 | ₹130 |
| ₹25,001 to ₹40,000 | ₹150 |
| Above ₹40,000 | ₹200 |

It also offers simplified slabs for Maharashtra and Karnataka, a manual entry option for other states, and a "No professional tax" option for states such as Delhi that do not levy it. Rates are revised from time to time, so verify the current slab with your state's commercial tax or professional tax department before issuing slips.

## How to create a salary slip

1. Open the [Salary Slip Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/). Sample data loads so you can see a complete slip.
2. Enter **company details**, and optionally upload a logo and choose an accent colour.
3. Enter **employee details**: name, ID, designation, department, PAN, UAN, bank account digits and date of joining.
4. Choose the **pay month**, and enter any **LOP days**. Tick "Reduce earnings for LOP days" to pro-rate pay.
5. Add **earnings**. Tick **PF wage** for the components that count towards PF, usually Basic and DA.
6. Set the **deductions**: EPF (with or without the ₹15,000 cap), ESI, the professional tax state, TDS and any other deductions.
7. Check the preview, then click **Download PDF** and choose "Save as PDF" in the print dialog.

To issue slips for several months at once, use **Print several months** and pick a range, such as a financial year. Months other than the selected pay month assume full attendance, so adjust any month with LOP separately.

## A worked example

Take the sample: Basic ₹15,000, HRA ₹7,500, conveyance ₹1,600 and special allowance ₹5,900, for a gross of ₹30,000 in Kolkata.

- EPF: 12% of ₹15,000 (Basic only) = ₹1,800
- ESI: not applicable, as gross is above ₹21,000
- Professional tax (West Bengal, ₹25,001 to ₹40,000): ₹150
- Net pay before TDS: ₹30,000 − ₹1,800 − ₹150 = ₹28,050

If the employee had two LOP days in a 30-day month with pro-rating on, each earning would be reduced by 2/30 before deductions are worked out.

## Common payslip mistakes

- **Counting HRA or special allowance as PF wages.** That inflates the deduction; follow your organisation's PF policy.
- **Applying ESI above the limit**, or forgetting it for a low-paid employee.
- **Using the wrong state's PT slab** for an employee who works in another state.
- **Net pay that does not match the bank credit.** Slips should reflect what was actually paid.
- **Missing PAN or UAN**, which employees need for tax filing and PF tracking.

## Important: rules change, so verify

This tool uses EPF at 12% with the ₹15,000 wage ceiling, ESI at 0.75% and 3.25% up to ₹21,000 gross, and simplified PT slabs. India's new labour codes also change how "wages" are defined for PF and other purposes, which can affect salary structures. Check current rates and how they apply to your organisation with your payroll adviser, the EPFO and ESIC websites, or your state tax department.

A payslip must reflect salary genuinely paid. Making slips for income that does not exist, for a loan or visa, is fraud.

## Related tools and privacy

Employees can check the tax side of their salary with the [Income Tax Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/) and work out exempt HRA with the [HRA Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/hra-calculator/). Tenants claiming HRA will also need rent receipts, which the [Rent Receipt Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/rent-receipt-generator/) creates.

Salary data is sensitive. The [Salary Slip Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/salary-slip-generator/) works in your browser, saves your draft only on your device, and does not send employee details to BISCS India.

Q: How is the EPF deduction on a salary slip calculated?
A: The employee contributes 12% of PF wages, which usually means Basic plus Dearness Allowance. Many employers apply the statutory wage ceiling of ₹15,000 a month, which caps the employee share at ₹1,800. Contributions on a higher wage are allowed by choice. Tick PF wage only for the components your employer counts.

Q: When does ESI apply to an employee?
A: At the time of writing, ESI covers employees whose gross monthly wages are up to ₹21,000, with a higher limit of ₹25,000 for persons with disability. The employee pays 0.75% and the employer 3.25% of gross wages. Coverage is decided per contribution period, so check the ESIC rules for mid-period salary changes.

Q: What is the professional tax slab in West Bengal?
A: As built into this tool, the West Bengal monthly slab is nil up to ₹10,000, ₹110 for ₹10,001 to ₹15,000, ₹130 for ₹15,001 to ₹25,000, ₹150 for ₹25,001 to ₹40,000 and ₹200 above ₹40,000. State rates can change, so confirm with the state’s commercial tax department.

Q: Is a salary slip from an online generator valid?
A: A payslip is valid when it is issued by the employer and reflects salary actually paid. The generator only helps employers and small businesses format slips correctly. Creating payslips for salary that was not paid, for loans or visas, is fraud. Banks often cross-check slips with bank statements and Form 16.

Q: Why are employer PF and ESI shown separately?
A: Employer contributions are part of the cost to company but are not deducted from the employee’s pay, so they do not affect net salary. Showing them in a separate box helps employees understand their CTC. The tool splits employer PF into the pension share of 8.33% and the provident fund share of 3.67%.

## How to Scan Documents to PDF with Your Phone Camera (Free)

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/scan-documents-to-pdf-phone-camera/
Tool: Scan to PDF (https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/)

Quick answer: To scan documents to PDF with your phone, open a browser-based scanner, capture each page with the camera or upload photos, check the detected corners, apply a filter such as Enhanced or Black and white, and download one PDF. BISCS India’s Scan to PDF needs no app and processes every page on your device.

To scan a document to PDF with your phone, open [Scan to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/), tap **Scan with camera**, capture each page, check the automatically detected corners, choose a filter such as **Enhanced** or **B&W**, and download one PDF. No app to install, and the pages never leave your phone.

You can also upload photos you have already taken. The scanner finds the edges of the paper, straightens the perspective so the page looks flat, and cleans up the background.

## Why a scanner beats a plain photo

A normal phone photo of a document has problems: the page is skewed, the table shows around the edges, shadows darken one side, and the paper looks grey or yellow. A scanner fixes all of these:

- **Edge detection** finds the four corners of the paper.
- **Perspective correction** turns a tilted shot into a flat, rectangular page.
- **Filters** whiten the background and sharpen text.
- **Page sizing** snaps pages that are nearly A4 to an exact A4 shape.

The result looks like it came from an office scanner and is far easier to read, print and upload.

## How to scan a document step by step

1. Open [Scan to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/) on your phone (or a laptop with a webcam).
2. Tap **Scan with camera** and allow camera access. Or choose **Upload photos** to use existing images.
3. Hold the phone above the page with all four corners visible, in good even light. If your phone supports it, a flash button appears for dark rooms, and a flip button lets you switch cameras.
4. Capture each page. Captured pages appear in a grid.
5. Select a page to check its detected corners. Drag the handles (with the magnifier to help) if any corner is off.
6. Choose a **Filter**: Original, Enhanced, Gray or B&W. Apply it to one page or all pages.
7. Drag pages to reorder them, and rotate any that are sideways.
8. Choose the **PDF page size** (A4, Letter or Fit image), **JPEG quality** and a **File name**.
9. Download as a PDF, or as JPG images in a ZIP.

## Choosing a filter

| Filter | Effect | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Original | No colour change, just straightened | Photos, colourful certificates, ID cards where colour matters |
| Enhanced | Brighter background, sharper text, colour kept | Most everyday documents, receipts, letters with coloured stamps |
| Gray | Removes colour, keeps tones | Forms and printed pages where colour is irrelevant |
| B&W | High-contrast black and white | Typed text, notes, pages to be printed or OCR'd |

Enhanced is the default because it suits most documents. If a portal or office specifically asks for black-and-white copies, use B&W or Gray.

## Scanning ID documents and certificates

Indians scan Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, driving licences, mark sheets and caste or income certificates for countless applications. A few pointers:

- **Scan both sides** of cards as separate pages, front first.
- **Use Original or Enhanced** so photos and holograms remain recognisable.
- **Check portal requirements.** Each portal sets its own format and size limit, and some want a JPG rather than a PDF. Read the instructions next to the upload field.
- **Reduce size if needed.** Lower the JPEG quality slider before downloading, or compress afterwards with [Compress PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/).
- **Consider DigiLocker first.** For documents issued through DigiLocker, the official digital copy may be accepted and is cleaner than any scan.

Because processing happens on your device, the images of your ID never pass through a third-party server.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Poor light.** Shadows and dim rooms cause blur and grey pages. Daylight near a window, without direct sun on the page, works best.
- **Low contrast background.** White paper on a white bedsheet is hard to detect. Use a dark table or floor.
- **Cutting off corners.** If a corner is outside the frame, detection fails and part of the page is lost.
- **Using B&W for photos.** Faces and coloured seals turn harsh. Use Original or Enhanced for these pages.
- **Very high quality for portal uploads.** A 95% JPEG quality multi-page PDF can exceed small upload limits. Try 70–85%.

## Page shape and size options

The **Shape** setting controls how the straightened page is proportioned. **Auto** snaps pages that are close to A4 to an exact A4 shape, which tidies up small measurement errors; **A4 ratio** always uses A4 proportions; **As measured** keeps the exact shape detected, which is better for receipts, ID cards and other non-A4 items.

The **PDF page size** then decides the paper size inside the PDF: A4 for Indian offices and portals, Letter for US recipients, or Fit image to make each PDF page exactly the size of the scan. For a mix of an A4 form and a small ID card, A4 with As measured keeps the card's natural proportions, scaled to fit and centred on an A4 page. If you need the card printed at its real size, print the JPG at actual size instead.

## Scan to PDF or Images to PDF?

If your photos are already clean and straight (for example screenshots or images from a flatbed scanner), [Images to PDF](https://biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/) is quicker and keeps the original image quality. If you are photographing paper on a table, the scanner's edge detection and filters make a much bigger difference.

## After scanning: what next?

Scanning is often the first step in a workflow:

- Need the text? Run the scan through [Image to Text](https://biscsindia.com/tools/image-to-text/), or convert it with [PDF to Word](https://biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/), which can OCR scanned pages in English, Hindi and Bengali.
- Need to sign it? Open the PDF in Sign PDF.
- Need to combine it with other documents? Use Merge PDF.

## Example: a rental agreement in the evening

Arvind in Kolkata signs a rental agreement on paper and needs to email a copy to his company's HR the same evening for HRA records. He places the six pages one by one on his dark dining table, scans them with the camera under the ceiling light, uses Enhanced for all pages, fixes one corner the scanner misjudged, and downloads a single A4 PDF. It looks like an office scan, and it never left his phone until he attached it to his email.

## Privacy and performance

The camera feed, edge detection, perspective correction and filters all run in your browser, with heavy image work done in a background worker so the page stays responsive. Nothing is uploaded. Processing many high-resolution pages can take a few seconds each on older phones; the grid shows each page's progress as it is cleaned up.

Q: Do I need to install an app to scan documents?
A: No. The scanner runs in your phone’s browser and uses the camera after you allow access. It works on Android and iPhone, and on laptops with a webcam. If the camera is not available, you can upload photos you have already taken instead.

Q: Is it safe to scan Aadhaar or PAN cards this way?
A: The photos and the PDF are processed entirely on your device and are not uploaded, which is safer than tools that send images to a server. Still, share ID copies only where needed, and consider marking the purpose on the copy with a watermark.

Q: Which filter should I use?
A: Enhanced suits most documents: it brightens the background and sharpens text while keeping colour. Gray removes colour for a neutral look. B&W gives high-contrast pages ideal for typed text. Original keeps the photo as captured, which suits photographs and colourful certificates.

Q: Why are the corners detected wrongly?
A: Edge detection needs contrast between the paper and the background. A white page on a white table or busy patterned surface can confuse it. Place the document on a darker, plain surface, or drag the corner handles to the right spots yourself.

Q: Can I scan multiple pages into one PDF?
A: Yes. Capture each page in turn; they collect in a grid where you can reorder them, rotate any page, fix corners or change filters. When you download, all pages are combined into a single PDF, or you can save them as JPG images in a ZIP.

## Schema Markup Generator: Create JSON-LD Without Coding

URL: https://biscsindia.com/blog/schema-markup-generator-json-ld-guide/
Tool: Schema Markup Generator (https://biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/)

Quick answer: Schema markup is structured data, usually written as JSON-LD, that tells search engines exactly what a page describes, such as a business, product or article. BISCS India’s free Schema Markup Generator builds valid JSON-LD from a simple form for ten common types, flags missing required fields and lets you copy or download the script.

Schema markup is a small block of code that describes your page in a language search engines understand precisely. Instead of guessing that "₹1,499" on a page is a price, Google reads a `price` property inside a `Product`. The most common format is JSON-LD, a script that sits in your HTML without changing how the page looks.

The [Schema Markup Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) on BISCS India writes that JSON-LD for you. You choose a type, fill in a form, and copy a ready-to-paste script, with warnings for missing required fields.

## What schema types can you create?

The generator covers ten types that most small and medium websites actually need:

| Type | Best for | Possible benefit |
|---|---|---|
| Local Business | Shops, clinics, CA firms, coaching centres, restaurants | Clear name, address, phone and opening hours for search and maps |
| Organization | Company home or about page | Logo and official profiles linked to your brand |
| Website (with search) | Home page | Helps Google show your preferred site name |
| Product | Single product pages | Price, availability and genuine ratings in results |
| Article / Blog post | Blog posts and news | Headline, image, author and dates understood correctly |
| Breadcrumbs | Any page deep in your site | Readable breadcrumb path instead of a raw URL |
| Event | Workshops, webinars, concerts, fests | Date, venue and ticket information |
| Person | Author or professional profile pages | Connects a person to their work and profiles |
| FAQ page | Pages with visible Q&As | Limited rich results today (see below) |
| How-to | Step-by-step guides | Rich results retired by Google, still valid markup |

The Local Business type offers sub-types such as ProfessionalService, Store, Restaurant, MedicalBusiness, FinancialService, LegalService and EducationalOrganization, so you can be specific about what you do.

## How to generate schema markup step by step

1. Open the [Schema Markup Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/).
2. Pick a **Schema type** from the dropdown, for example Local Business.
3. Fill in the fields. Required fields are marked, and hints explain formats such as the two-letter country code `IN` or opening hours like `Mo-Fr 10:00-19:00`.
4. For list-based types (FAQ questions, breadcrumb levels, how-to steps), use **Add** to create rows and the arrow button to reorder them.
5. Watch the **JSON-LD** panel update live, and read the messages underneath. Errors must be fixed; warnings are advice.
6. Press **Copy** for the full `<script type="application/ld+json">` block, **Copy JSON only** if your CMS wraps it for you, or **Download** to save it as a file.
7. Paste it into your page, publish, and test the URL in Google's Rich Results Test.

The tool runs entirely in your browser, so business details you are still finalising are never sent to a server.

## Which rich results can you still get today?

Search features change, so it is worth being realistic. Google has retired or restricted several rich results in recent years:

- **FAQ rich results** were restricted in 2023 to well-known, authoritative government and health sites. Most business sites no longer get the expandable questions in search results.
- **How-to rich results** were removed in 2023.
- **The sitelinks search box** was retired in late 2024, although WebSite markup is still useful for site names.

The markup itself remains valid schema.org vocabulary. Other search engines and AI systems may still read it to understand your content, so it is not wasted, but do not add FAQ or how-to schema expecting a visual change in Google.

Types that commonly still produce visible features include Product (price, availability, ratings), Breadcrumbs, Event, Article and Local Business details. Eligibility is never guaranteed: Google decides whether to show them.

## Local business schema for Indian businesses

Local Business markup is the most valuable starting point for a shop or service in an Indian city. A few practical points:

- **Use your full address**, including street, city, state and PIN code. The generator warns you when the street address is missing.
- **Match your Google Business Profile exactly.** The same name, address and phone number everywhere builds trust.
- **Add latitude and longitude** if you know them. You can copy them from Google Maps by right-clicking your location.
- **Use the international phone format**, such as `+91 98XXXXXXXX`.
- **List real social profiles** under sameAs: your Facebook page, LinkedIn company page or Instagram account.
- **Set the price range** with something simple like ₹₹ if you want to signal affordability.

## Common schema markup mistakes

- **Marking up content that is not on the page.** If the FAQ questions or product price in your JSON-LD are not visible to visitors, Google treats it as misleading.
- **Fake or self-written reviews.** The generator reminds you that ratings must come from real customers shown on the page. This is one of the quickest ways to get a manual penalty.
- **Currency symbols in the price.** Prices must be plain numbers like `1499`, with the currency set separately as INR. The tool reports this as an error.
- **Relative URLs.** Images and page URLs should be absolute, starting with `https://`.
- **Several conflicting blocks.** Two plugins each adding an Organization block with different names confuses search engines. Check your final HTML with the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/), which lists the structured data types it finds.
- **Never updating it.** If your prices, hours or event dates change, the schema must change too.

## Tips for getting more from structured data

Start with the pages that matter most for enquiries: your home page (Organization or Local Business plus WebSite), your main service or product pages, and your contact page. Add Breadcrumbs on deeper pages so results show a readable path.

For deeper entity work, such as linking an author to their LinkedIn profile and publications, the [Entity & Author Schema Builder](https://biscsindia.com/tools/entity-schema-builder/) creates connected Organization and Person markup. If you have a page of genuine questions and answers, the [FAQ Schema Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/faq-schema-generator/) builds the visible HTML and matching JSON-LD together so they always agree.

Structured data is a quiet piece of SEO hygiene: it will not transform a weak page, but it removes guesswork for search engines. Build your first block in the [Schema Markup Generator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) and test it before you publish.

Q: Does schema markup improve Google rankings?
A: Structured data is not a direct ranking boost. It helps search engines understand your page and can make it eligible for rich results such as product prices, ratings, event dates and breadcrumbs, which can improve how your listing looks and how many people click it.

Q: Is FAQ schema still worth adding?
A: Google limited FAQ rich results in 2023 to well-known, authoritative government and health websites, so most sites will no longer see them. The markup is still valid schema.org and can help other search engines and AI systems understand question-and-answer content, as long as it matches visible text.

Q: Where do I put JSON-LD on my page?
A: Paste the script block into the page’s HTML, either in the head or the body. Google reads it in both places. On WordPress, use a plugin or a header-scripts field rather than editing theme files directly.

Q: Can I add star ratings to my product schema?
A: Only if the ratings come from real customers and are visible on the same page. Writing your own reviews or marking up ratings that visitors cannot see breaks Google’s structured data guidelines and can lead to a manual action.

Q: How do I test my schema markup?
A: Use Google’s Rich Results Test to see whether the page is eligible for rich results, and the Schema.org validator for general syntax checks. After publishing, Google Search Console reports structured data errors under its enhancements sections.

## How to Use a Scientific Calculator Online: Trig, Logs and Powers

With a good online one, you can type a whole expression, such as `2sin(30)+√16`, and get the answer (5, in degree mode) in one step.

| Function | Keys or typing | Example |
|---|---|---|

## How to use it, step by step

## Worked examples

### Height of a building with trigonometry

Standing 40 m from a building, you measure the angle to the top as 35°. Height = 40 × tan(35°). In DEG mode, type `40*tan(35)` to get about **28.01 m**.

### Pythagoras

A right triangle has sides 3 and 4. The hypotenuse is `√(3^2+4^2)` = **5**. The angle opposite the side of 3 is `tan⁻¹(3/4)`, about **36.87°**.

### Compound growth

₹1,00,000 growing at 7% a year for 5 years becomes `100000*(1.07)^5`, about **₹1,40,255.17**. For full investment projections, a dedicated SIP or lumpsum calculator is more practical, but this is a handy check.

### Logs

`log(1000)` gives 3 and `ln(e)` gives 1. To find a log in any base, divide: log₂(64) is `log(64)/log(2)` = 6.

### Factorials and combinations

The number of ways to choose 3 students from 10 is 10! ÷ (3! × 7!). Type `10!/(3!*7!)` to get **120**.

## Order of operations, explained

The calculator follows standard maths rules, often taught as BODMAS:

1. **Brackets** first.
2. **Powers and roots**, worked from right to left, so `2^3^2` is 2^9 = 512.
3. **Multiplication and division**, left to right.
4. **Addition and subtraction**, left to right.

A minus sign in front of a power applies after the power, so `−3^2` is −9. If you mean (−3)², type `(−3)^2` to get 9. You can also write implied multiplication such as `2π` or `3(4+5)`.

## Common mistakes on scientific calculators

- **Wrong angle mode.** sin(30) is 0.5 in degrees but about −0.988 in radians. Check DEG/RAD first.
- **Missing brackets.** `1/2π` is read as (1/2) × π, about 1.571, while `1/(2π)` is about 0.159. Add brackets when in doubt.
- **Confusing log and ln.** log is base 10; ln is base e.
- **Taking logs of zero or negatives.** These are undefined, and the calculator tells you so.
- **tan(90°).** It is undefined, and the calculator says so instead of showing a huge number.
- **Factorials of decimals.** n! here needs a whole number from 0 upwards.

## Degrees or radians: which should you use?

Angles can be measured in two units. A full circle is 360 degrees, or 2π radians, so 180° equals π radians and 1 radian is about 57.3°.

Use **DEG** for school geometry, surveying, construction, navigation and most problems where an angle is given with a degree sign. Use **RAD** for calculus, physics formulas involving angular speed or oscillation, and anything where angles are written in terms of π, such as sin(π/6).

The setting changes how sin, cos and tan read their input, and how the inverse functions return their answer. If you switch mid-calculation, recalculate the steps that involved angles. A quick sanity check: in DEG mode, sin(90) should be exactly 1.

## How memory and history save time

Long problems often need a few separate results combined. Instead of writing them on paper:

- Calculate the first part and press **M+** to add it to memory.
- Calculate the next part and press **M+** again, or **M−** to subtract it.
- Press **MR** to insert the stored total into a new expression, and **MC** to clear it.

A small **M** badge appears on the display while memory holds a value. The history panel keeps your last 20 calculations for the session, and **Ans** always holds the latest answer, so `Ans*1.18` adds 18% to whatever you just worked out.

## Tips for students and professionals

- Use the history to double-check a multi-step homework answer without retyping.
- Store intermediate results with **M+** when you need to add several results together.
- Results are shown to 12 significant digits. Round only your final answer, as your syllabus or report requires.
- For exams, practise on the model of physical calculator your exam allows, since online tools are usually not permitted in the hall.

When you need percentage questions with the working shown, the [Percentage Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) is clearer. For mean, median and standard deviation of a data set, use [Average & Statistics](https://biscsindia.com/tools/statistics-calculator/). And to switch between binary, octal and hexadecimal, try the [Number Base Converter](https://biscsindia.com/tools/number-base-converter/).

A scientific calculator is only as accurate as the expression you give it. With the angle mode set and brackets in place, the [Scientific Calculator](https://biscsindia.com/tools/scientific-calculator/) handles the rest in your browser, privately and instantly.

Q: Why does sin(30) give −0.988 instead of 0.5?
A: The calculator is in radian mode. sin(30) in radians is about −0.988, while sin(30°) in degrees is 0.5. Switch the DEG/RAD toggle at the top of the display to DEG for school geometry and most practical angle problems, and to RAD for calculus and physics formulas written in radians.

Q: What is the difference between log and ln?
A: log is the common logarithm, base 10, so log(1000) is 3. ln is the natural logarithm, base e (about 2.71828), so ln(e) is 1. Many science formulas use ln, while pH, decibels and the Richter scale use base-10 logs.

Q: Can I use this calculator in an exam?
A: Online calculators are generally not allowed in board, university or competitive exams. Each exam body sets its own rules on which physical calculators, if any, are permitted. Use the online tool for study and homework, and check your exam’s instructions for what you may bring.

Q: How does the percentage key work?
A: The % key divides the number before it by 100. So 200 × 18% is read as 200 × 0.18, which gives 36. For percentage change, reverse percentages and similar problems, the dedicated Percentage Calculator shows the working more clearly.

Q: Is the expression I type sent to a server?
A: No. The calculator parses and evaluates your expression in your browser using its own safe parser, so nothing is uploaded. Your history is kept only while the page is open.

## WebM or MP4: which do you need?

Browsers record using the formats they support natively. Most produce **WebM**, usually with the VP9 or VP8 video codec and Opus audio. Some newer browsers can produce **MP4** directly.

A quick explanation of the terms: the **container** (WebM, MP4) is the file wrapper, and the **codec** (VP9, H.264) is how the pictures are actually compressed inside it. WebM plays well in Chrome, Firefox, Edge and VLC, and on YouTube. MP4 with H.264 is the safest choice for WhatsApp, PowerPoint, iPhones and older smart TVs.

The **Convert to MP4** button re-encodes your recording to H.264 on your own computer. The first time, it downloads a video engine of about 32 MB, which your browser then caches. For other formats, or to pull out just the audio as MP3, use the [Video Converter & MP3](https://biscsindia.com/tools/video-converter/).

## Tips for clear, professional recordings

- **Record a tab or window, not the whole screen,** unless you need to switch apps. It avoids accidentally showing WhatsApp Web, email previews or other private notifications.
- **Turn on Do Not Disturb** in Windows or macOS before you start, for the same reason.
- **Zoom the browser to 125% or more** when recording web pages, so text is readable on a phone.
- **Use a headset microphone if you can.** Laptop microphones pick up fan noise and room echo. Speak a little slower than normal.
- **Write three bullet points before you hit record.** Short, planned videos are far more useful than long, wandering ones.
- **Keep the webcam bubble small** and in a corner that does not cover buttons you will click.
- **Close heavy tabs and apps.** Recording and encoding use your processor, and a slow laptop may drop frames if it is also running many other things.

## Common problems and fixes

- **"This browser does not let websites record the screen."** You are probably on a phone or tablet, or using an older browser. Switch to a desktop browser.
- **No sound in the recording.** Check that **Record system / tab sound** was ticked and that you ticked "share audio" in the browser’s dialog. If you shared a whole screen on a Mac, try sharing the specific tab instead.
- **Microphone or camera blocked.** Click the camera or lock icon in the address bar and allow access, then try again. Make sure another app such as Zoom or Teams is not holding the camera.
- **Recording is shorter than expected.** If you clicked **Stop sharing** or closed the shared window, recording ends automatically.
- **Choppy video.** Lower your screen resolution, close other apps, or record a single tab instead of the whole screen.

## Privacy

Your recording is captured and encoded by your own browser and stays in that tab until you download it. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account, and no watermark is added. Remember to respect other people’s privacy too: get consent before recording meetings or calls that include others.
